Vbi verò primùm coeperunt aperiri oculi icтorum hominum, vt videant superna illa, ac vitam illam cœlestem; tum quidem obliti omnium rerum icтarum, incipiunt appetere illas res cœlestes, ac immortalitatem illam, quæ futura est in altera vita, qua vt potiantur, nihili faciunt omnem sitim; omnē famem quæ contingit in ista vita, mortem denique ipsam libenter ferunt, vt post hanc vitam, viuant beatam illam vitam in cœlis cum Domino suo in sempiternum. Mulier ista voluit quidem leuari omnibus molestiis huius vitæ, leuari siti, leuari fame, leuari labore itandi ad fontem Iacobi, nimirum nondum videns illa superna ac cœlestia: sed cui datum est semel illa intueri, tum is libenter omnia perfert in hac vita, vt beatam illam in cœlis tandem adipiscatur.
units.tr: Yet again her words indicate that she did not understand what sort of water it was. For when she says, that I may not thirst, nor come here to draw, it clearly shows that she understood it to be a bodily and temporary water, not unlike the water of Jacob's well, perhaps even better, by which that bodily thirst would be quenched and the woman could be relieved of the labour of coming to Jacob's well. We all wish to be blessed, all to be immortal; for God made us for this very purpose, that we should live for ever. Hence from the creation onward all men, even by natural instinct, constantly desire that immortality for which they were originally made. But if they are not enlightened by the Holy Spirit of God, they seek only some earthly happiness, and they want to remain always in the present life, even with misery and the greatest lack of all things; they want to live on in the earth perpetually, and think of departing only reluctantly. But when the eyes of such men begin to be opened, so that they see those higher things and that heavenly life, then, forgetting all these things, they begin to desire those heavenly things and that immortality which is to come in the other life. To obtain it they count every thirst as nothing, they gladly bear every hunger that befalls them in this life, and finally they bear death itself, so that after this life they may live that blessed life in heaven with their Lord for ever. That woman indeed wanted to be relieved of all the troubles of this life, relieved of thirst, relieved of hunger, relieved of the labour of going to the well of Jacob, not yet seeing those higher and heavenly things. But he to whom it has been given once to behold them gladly endures all things in this life, so that at last he may attain that blessed life in heaven.

units.la: 16 Dicit ei Iesus, Vade, voca virum tuum, & veni hûc.
units.tr: 16 Jesus said to her, Go, call your husband, and come here.

units.la: 17 Respondit mulier, & dixit ei, Non habeo virum. Dicit ei Iesus, Bene dixisti, Non habeo virum.
units.tr: 17 The woman answered and said to him, I have no husband. Jesus said to her, You have said well, I have no husband.

units.la: 18 Quinque enim viros habuisti: & nunc quem habes, non est tuus vir. Hoc verè dixisti.
units.tr: 18 For you have had five husbands, and the one you now have is not your husband. This you have said truly.

units.la: HAc parte dialogi, Christus omisso sermone de aqua illa viua, iam excitata illius aquæ aliqua in muliere siti & appetitione, eò redit unde exorsus est, nempe ad instituendam mulierem in notitia veri Messiæ: sic enim ratus est fore, vt frustra loquatur ei plura de aqua illa viua, déque rebus spiritualibus, non demonstrato prius Messia, in quo sunt omnes hæ res spirituales, & extra quem nihil earum inuenitur. Quòd si enim seriò premeret nos conscientia peccati, frustra loqueretur quis nobis de remissione peccati, ac pollicere- tur gratiam ac vitam, nisi ostenso prius Mediatore, in quo solo placata est ira Dei aduersus peccata nostra. Eminus, fateor, demōstranda est illa vita, tanquam felicitas nostra, vt nos ad eam quærendam alliciamur, sed ea iam digito quasi demonstrata, veniendum est continuò ad Christum qui solus est via ad vitam, & sine quo neque iustitia, neque vita est vlla. Philosophi multa scripserunt, de officiis, de honesto, iusto, & aliis id genus moralibus, interea Christi nunquam meminerunt, quia eum non cognouerunt. Quo factum est vt doctrina illa Philosophorum nūquam potuerit esse efficax ad instituendū vel vnum aliquem in vera virtute morali, quia sine fide in Christo, in quo sunt omnes virtutes, & ex quo hauriendæ sunt, ne Philosophorum quidem ipsorum quisquam particeps esse vnquam potuit. Ego enim nihil fecerim simulachra ista duntaxat virtutum, quæ in ethnicis hominibus apparuerunt, sine interna cordis regeneratione ac purgatione, quę non fit nisi per fidem in Christum, cui sit omnis honor & gloria. Amen.
units.tr: In this part of the dialogue, Christ sets aside his talk about that living water. Having stirred up in the woman some thirst and desire for that water, he returns to where he began, namely to instructing the woman in knowledge of the true Messiah. For he judged that it would be pointless to speak to her more about that living water and about spiritual things before the Messiah had been shown, since all these spiritual things are in him, and they cannot be found apart from him. For if the awareness of sin weighed on us seriously, it would be pointless for anyone to speak to us of the forgiveness of sins and to promise grace and life, unless the Mediator had first been shown, in whom alone the wrath of God against our sins is appeased. I admit that the life to come must be set before us from afar, as our happiness, so that we are drawn to seek it. But once it has been pointed to, as it were with a finger, we must go straight on to Christ, who alone is the way to life, and without whom there is neither righteousness nor life at all. The philosophers wrote much about duties, about what is honourable, just, and other such moral matters, yet they never mentioned Christ, because they did not know him. Hence that teaching of the philosophers could never be effective in training anyone, even one man, in true moral virtue, because without faith in Christ, in whom all virtues are and from whom they must be drawn, not one of the philosophers themselves could ever have been a partaker. For I would call those virtues mere images, which appeared in the heathen, apart from the inward regeneration and cleansing of the heart, which is brought about only through faith in Christ, to whom be all honour and glory. Amen.

units.la: Interea autē temporis dum se innotescere facit mulieri, simul excitat conscientiam peccati illius, (nempe fornicationis) in quo tum iacebat misera absque vlla conscientia, absque vllo dolore, vt vna eadémque opera & remedium peccati ac miseriæ demonstraret, & excitaret miseram ad remedium illud persequendum; Eo enim sumus omnes ingenio, vt nunquam velimus quęrere Christum nisi impulsi sensu aliquo miseriæ ac indigentiæ nostræ. Qui valent, non egent medico, sed male affecti, inquit Christus. Venite ad me omnes qui fatigati & onerati estis, & ego faciam vt requiescatis. Quotquot igitur Christum prædicant, Christi exemplo hoc discant, nempe quo tempore alliciunt homines ad fidem, proposita illa suauitate, quæ est in Christo, eodem tempore exstimulādos esse ipsos peccati ac miseriæ suę sensu ad Christum amplectendū. Nam hæ duæ partes doctrinæ semper coniungendæ sunt, doctrina miseriæ & doctrina misericordiæ in Christo Iesu, cui sit omnis honor & gloria: Amen.
units.tr: Meanwhile, while he makes himself known to the woman, he at the same time stirs up the awareness of her sin (namely, fornication), in which the wretched woman then lay without any awareness and without any sorrow. In one and the same work he shows the remedy for sin and misery, and stirs the wretched woman to pursue that remedy. For we are all so made that we never want to seek Christ unless we are driven by some sense of our misery and need. Those who are well, says Christ, have no need of a physician, but those who are ill. Come to me, all you who are weary and heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Therefore, whoever preaches Christ should learn this from Christ's example: at the same time that he draws people to faith by setting before them the sweetness that is in Christ, he must also stir them, by a sense of their sin and misery, to embrace Christ. For these two parts of doctrine must always be joined together, the doctrine of misery and the doctrine of mercy in Jesus Christ, to whom be all honour and glory. Amen.

units.la: Conscientia mulieris excitatur.
units.tr: The woman's conscience is stirred.

units.la: 9 Dicit ei mulier, Domine, video te Prophetam esse.
units.tr: 19 The woman said to him, Lord, I see that you are a prophet.

units.la: 20 Patres nostri in hoc monte adorauerunt: Et vos dicitis Hierosolymis esse locum illum vbi oportet adorare.
units.tr: 20 Our fathers worshipped on this mountain, and you say that Jerusalem is the place where men ought to worship.

units.la: 21 Dicit ei Iesus, Mulier, crede mihi, venit tempus quando neque in monte hoc, neque Hierosolymis adorabitis Patrem.
units.tr: 21 Jesus said to her, Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.

units.la: 22 Vos adoratis quod nescitis, nos adoramus quod scimus, quia salus ex Iudaeis est.
units.tr: 22 You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, for salvation is of the Jews.

units.la: 23 Sed venit hora & nunc est, quum veri adoratores adorabunt Patrem Spiritu ac veritate, etenim Pater tales quaerit qui ipsum adorent.
units.tr: 23 But the hour is coming, and now is, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for the Father seeks such people to worship him.

units.la: 24 Deus est Spiritus: & qui adorant eum, oportet ut Spiritu ac veritate adorent.
units.tr: 24 God is Spirit, and those who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.

units.la: EX revelatione hac extraordinaria tum anteacte tum praesentis vitae ipsius, mulier prophetam eum & extraordinarium hominem deprehendit, atque ita paulatim ad cognitionem Messiae deducitur. Non enim simul ac semel sed certis quibusdam gradibus Christus cognoscitur. Patres nostri adoraverunt. Mulier cum deprehendisset eum Prophetam esse & plusquam vulgarem aliquem hominem, statim movet quaestionem de loco adorationis: Essetne locus adorationis in illo monte, cuius nomen fuit Garizim, an vero Hierosolymis. Patres nostri adorarunt, inquit, in hoc monte; ex quo relinquit colligendum eum esse adorationis locum proprium. De loco sciendum, quod in eo Sanaballath Cuthaeus templum extruxit permissu Alexandri Macedonis, post victoriam Ifficam, ibique summum pontificem constituit Manassem generum suum. Tum subiungit sententiam Iudaeorum de loco adorationis. Vos autem, inquit, dicitis Hierosolymis esse locum adorationis. Mulierцyлa ista, etsi leuicula & scortatrix, non omnino tamen ignara fuit controversiae illius in religione quae tum agitabatur inter Samaritanos & Iudaeos de loco adorationis. Quotusquisque est, quaeso, virorum apud nos etiam eorum, qui aliquid videri volunt, ut de mulierculis & de vulgo hominum nihil loquar, qui novit aliquid in controversiis his quae agitantur hodierno die inter nos & aduersarios, vel qui animum advertat ad eas, vel denique qui putet ad se aliquid pertinere controversias.
units.tr: From this extraordinary revelation, both of his past and of his present life, the woman perceives him to be a prophet and an extraordinary man, and so she is gradually led to the knowledge of the Messiah. For Christus is not known all at once, but by certain steps. Patres nostri adoraverunt. When the woman had perceived that he was a prophet and more than an ordinary man, she at once raises the question of the place of worship: whether the place of worship was on that mountain, called Gerizim, or rather in Jerusalem. "Our fathers worshipped," she says, "on this mountain," from which she leaves it to be inferred that it was the proper place of worship. As for the place, it should be known that Sanballat the Cuthite built a temple there, with the permission of Alexander the Macedonian, after the Issic victory, and there he appointed Manasseh, his son-in-law, as high priest. Then she adds the Jews' view about the place of worship: But you, she says, say that Jerusalem is the place of worship. This little woman, though light and a harlot, was not entirely ignorant of that controversy in religion which was then being carried on between the Samaritans and the Jews concerning the place of worship. How few men there are among us, I ask, even among those who wish to seem to be somebody (not to speak of women and the common people), who know anything of the controversies that are being argued today between us and our opponents, or who pay attention to them, or who at last think that the controversies concern them at all.

units.la: {y} Iosephus, Antiq. lib. II. lias illas de rebus maximis, vt sunt iustitia & vita æterna? Imò verò si quando incidunt in sermones de hisce rebus, annon audimus eos quasi aliud agentes & conteptim de iis loqui, vt Festus ille præses Romanus dum Agrippę regi exponeret controuersiam illam quæ tum agitabatur inter Paulum & Iudæos, Nullum, inquit, crimen obiiciebant eorum quæ ego suspicatus eram, sed quæstiones quasdam de suasuperstitione habebant aduersus eum, & de quodam Iesu defuncto, quem affirmauit Paulus viuere. Sic ex nostris hominibus non pauci sunt non minus prophani quam Festus homo ethnicus, qui non minus nunc pro iudicio habent religionem quàm tunc Festus. Quòd si quæstio fiat de hereditate terrena, vel eius portiuncula aliqua, mirum est quàm grauiter de iis rebus & cogitent & loquantur homines, & quàm metuât ne ipsis earum rerum vel tantillum præripiatur. Sin quæstio fiat de iustificatione impij, de æterna illa ac cælesti hæreditate, tum dici non potest quàm securi sint istarum rerum,& quàm leuiter, quasi hæ nihil ad ipsos pertineant, de iis loquantur, facileque patiantur iustitiam illam Christi totam, & vitam illam quæ est per eam, sibi totam ab aduersariis eripi. Dum expendo mecum & dicta & facta hominum, facilè deprehendo non esse istarum rerum sensum aliquem in cordibus. Quid enim? si cogitarent prædicationem gratiæ Christi aliquid serij esse, & serio hoc agi in Ecclesia, ac non potius pro more tantùm & perfunctorie, an, inquam, tum raperent ad se illud fere totum quo oporteret ali Ministros verbi Dei? Sed tempus veniet, cùm videbunt nihil fuisse serium aut graue in vita, præter ista, quæ nunc tam ludicra & leuia videntur esse, & ista agenda fuisse præcipuè in hac vita. Mulier deinde postquam cognouit Christū prophetam esse, Messiam enim nondum cognouit, statim consuluit eum de eo quod ipsam anxiam & suspe- tam tenuit. Quotusquisque est nostrorum hominum quasi incidat in eum, qui notitiam aliquam habet in mysterio Christi, interroget eum de re quapiam quæ ad vitam illam alteram pertineat, de iustitia coram Deo, de regeneratione, de vita æterna? Quòd si valetudinarius aliquis incidat in eum qui Medicinam profiteatur, tum nullus est modus quærendi de remedio. Si qui litigat incidat in Iurisperitum, tum nullum facit quærendi modum. At si incidat in eum qui notitiam aliquam habeat in mysterio Christi, tum nullum verbum fit. Quòd si sentiant homines spiritualem hunc, quo tam grauiter laborant, morbum, & viderent peccatum suum, cuius pondere deprimuntur ad inferos vsque, profecto tum non minus quærerent de remedio huius mali, quàm solent querere de remedio morborum corporis. Sed fit nescio quomodo vt etiam in tanta luce, nullus tamen sit sensus peccati, nullus sensus mortis. Quo rursus fit vt nemo quærat de remedio mali omnium grauissimi. Sed tempus erit cum sentient homines peccati sui grauitatem, metuendum autem ne id fiat postquam tempora ista refrigerationis praeterierint.
units.tr: {y} Josephus, Antiq. lib. II. Do they not, when such matters as righteousness and eternal life come up in conversation, hear them as if they were talking of something else, and speak of them with contempt? Just as that Roman governor Festus, when he explained to King Agrippa the controversy then being carried on between Paul and the Jews, said: "They had no charge against him of the kind I had supposed, but had certain questions against him about their own superstition, and about one Jesus, who had died, whom Paul affirmed to be alive." So among our own people there are not a few who are no less profane than the heathen Festus, and who now regard religion no less as a matter of opinion than Festus did then. If a question arises about an earthly inheritance, or some small part of it, it is remarkable how seriously men think and talk about those things, and how anxious they are lest even the smallest part of them be snatched away. But if the question is about the justification of the sinner, about that eternal and heavenly inheritance, then one cannot say how carefree men are about such things, and how lightly they talk of them, as if they had nothing to do with them, and how easily they allow the whole righteousness of Christ, and the life that comes through it, to be torn from them entirely by their opponents. As I weigh in my mind both the words and the deeds of men, I easily perceive that there is no sense of these things in their hearts. For what? If they thought that the preaching of the grace of Christ was something serious, and that this was seriously pursued in the Church, and not merely as a custom and in a perfunctory way, would they, I ask, then snatch up almost the whole of what ought to support the ministers of the Word of God? But the time will come when they will see that nothing in life was serious or weighty except those things which now seem so trifling and light, and that these were to be done chiefly in this life. Then, after the woman has learned that he is a prophet (for she does not yet know him to be the Messiah), she at once consults him about what troubles and torments her. How few of our people, when they come upon one who has some knowledge of the mystery of Christ, ask him about any matter pertaining to that other life, about righteousness before God, about regeneration, about eternal life! If a sick man meets a doctor who practises medicine, there is no limit to his asking about a remedy. If a man who is in a lawsuit meets a lawyer, then he asks without limit. But if he meets one who has some knowledge of the mystery of Christ, then no word is spoken. But if men would feel this spiritual disease, under which they labour so grievously, and would see their sin, by whose weight they are pressed down even to hell, then surely they would ask no less about the remedy for this evil than they are accustomed to ask about remedies for bodily diseases. But somehow, even in such great light, there is still no sense of sin, no sense of death. Hence again it comes about that no one asks about the remedy for the most grievous evil of all. But the time will come when men will feel the weight of their sin, though it is to be feared that this will happen only after these times of cooling have passed.

units.la: Redeo ad mulierem. Nunc demum quærit mulier de loco adorationis. Annon acquieuit in illo adorationis loco, quem iam à multo tempore frequetauit cum aliis Samaritanis? Hoc profecto argumento est, animum mulieris nunquam plane conquieuisse in idololatrico suo cultu. Idololatrae & superstitiosi nunquam prorsus acquiescunt in idolo ac superstitione sua. Papistae animus nunquam acquiescit, scio, in idolo ac superstitione sua. Iactet licet cum muliere ista superstitiosa patrum templa, altaria, & alia quae sunt inventa hominum; tamen hisce omnibus cor ipsis non constabilitur. Bonum est, inquit author ad Hebraeos, cor constabiliri gratia, non cibis, quibus non sunt adiuti, qui in ipsis versati sunt. Quibus verbis innuit cor hominis constabiliri non rebus illis externis, non traditionibus ac inventis hominum, sed gratia Dei, & Euangelio hoc gratiae. Fieri quidem potest, vt quantisper quis manet excaecatus & quasi consopitus, gaudet ad tempus tantisper videatur ipsi idolum esse aliquid, & ipse videatur sibi in idolo acquiescere. Verum iam vbi excitatus est ex lethali illo sopore, videbit idolum suum ludibrium esse, imo vt homo dormiens quadiu dormit putat somnium aliquid esse, & placet sibi in somnio suo, at iam excitatus ex somno euanescit somnium, iamque vidit somnium illud suum nihil esse. Idoli nihil est aliud praeter somnium dormientis hominis. Haec-
units.tr: I return to the woman. Only now does she finally ask about the place of worship. Had she not already settled into that place of worship, which she had frequented for a long time along with the other Samaritans? This is surely evidence that the woman's mind had never truly come to rest in her idolatrous worship. Idolaters and superstitious people never fully rest in their idol and superstition. The mind of the Papists, I know, never rests in their idol and superstition. Let this superstitious woman boast as much as she likes of the temples, altars and other human inventions of the fathers; yet her heart is not steadied by any of them. The author to the Hebrews says, It is good that the heart be steadied by grace, not by foods, by which those who have been occupied with them have not been helped. By these words he indicates that the human heart is steadied not by external things, nor by human traditions and inventions, but by the grace of God and the Gospel of this grace. It is indeed possible that, for as long as a man remains blinded and as it were lulled to sleep, he rejoices for a time, and for a time it seems to him that his idol is something, and he seems to himself to rest in his idol. But once he has been roused from that deadly sleep, he will see that his idol is a mockery. Just as a sleeping man, for as long as he sleeps, thinks his dream is something and takes pleasure in his dream, but once he is awake the dream vanishes and he sees that his dream was nothing, so an idol is nothing but the dream of a sleeping man.

units.la: Hactenus fuit quæstio mulieris ; ad quam deinde re- spondet Christus, Mulier, crede mihi, venit hora quando ne- que in hoc monte, neque Hierosolymis adorabitis Patrem. Christus respônso suo, primum tollit omne discrimen locorum in quibus adoretur Deus, neque delectum facit aliquem vel montis Garizim, vel Hierosolymorum, licet ante Christi manifestationem fuerit ibi locus adorationis proprius Deut.12.1. & deinceps. Quò autem id magis persuadeat mulieri, Mulier, crede mihi, inquit. Tam difficile fuit & arduum in principio inducere homines ut crederent venisse iam tempus Messiæ & renouationis ac restitutionis omnium rerum per eum. Nota, Christus non statim respondit ad id quod quæsitum est à muliere de loco adorationis, esset ne ille penes Samaritanos, an verò penes Iudæos? Verùm, cùm haberet ante oculos, non quidem id, ut stabiliret Iudaismum, quem iam cepit abrogare aduentu suo, neque ut efficeret mulierem ex Samaritana Iudæam: verùm ut ex Samaritana Christiana efficeret. Ideóque respondit primùm id quod res erat, non esse iam amplius discrimen locorum, sed adorationi & cultui diuino omnem ex æquo locum adventu Christi sanctificatum. Nobis qui laboramus in verbo id propositum esse debet, ut quoscunque homines Christianos efficiamus. Ideóque quoties aduersarij mouent quæstionem, & gloriantur suo more de rebus externis Ecclesiæ & aliis huiusmodi, nostrum est, exemplo Christi, his rebus silentio prætereitis, de spiritualibus ipsis respondere; ut de iustitia Christi, quæ nostra fit per imputationem, de regeneratione, de vita æterna. Iohannes Baptista, cùm quærerent Pharisæi de causa & authoritate qua ipse baptizaret, & posset iustam causam reddere baptismi sui, non tamen reddidit; sed extenuato baptismo & ministerio suo, ad Christum conatus est comperducere, eum sibi loagè præferens. Ego, inquit, baptizo aqua, sed in medio vestrum stat quem vos nescitis. Ita nobis faciendum : non respondendum perpetuò ad ista externa, quorum illi nullum modum faciunt, sed demonstranda sunt vel inuitis & recusantibus spiritualia ista, quæ nos tradimus ac docemus, ut sunt Christus, iustitia ipsius, regeneratio, vita æterna, ad hoc, ut si fieri possit, miseri isti adducantur tandem aliquando vt videant ea & credant.
units.tr: So far was the woman's question; to it Christ then replies: Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor at Jerusalem. In his reply Christ first removes all distinction of places in which God is worshipped; he chooses neither Mount Gerizim nor Jerusalem, although before the manifestation of Christ there was a proper place of worship there, Deut. 12.1 and following. Yet in order to persuade the woman the more, he says, Woman, believe me. It was so difficult and hard at the beginning to bring men to believe that the time of the Messiah had come, and of the renewal and restoration of all things through him. Note that Christ did not answer at once the question the woman asked about the place of worship, whether it was among the Samaritans or among the Jews. But, keeping in view not so much the establishing of Judaism, which by his coming he had already begun to abolish, nor the making of a Samaritan woman into a Jewess, but the making of a Samaritan woman into a Christian, he answered first what the matter really was: that there is no longer any distinction of places, but that by the coming of Christ every place has been equally sanctified for worship and divine service. For us who labour in the Word, this must be our aim, that we make Christians of whomever we can. Therefore, whenever our adversaries raise the question and boast in their usual way about the external things of the Church and other things of that kind, it is our part, following the example of Christ, to pass over these things in silence and to answer about spiritual things themselves, such as the righteousness of Christ, which becomes ours by imputation, regeneration, and eternal life. When the Pharisees asked John the Baptist about the cause and authority by which he baptized, and about what would be a just reason for his baptism, he did not give one; but, diminishing his baptism and ministry, he sought to lead them to Christ, placing him far above himself: I baptize with water, but in the midst of you stands one whom you do not know. So we too must act: we should not always reply to these external matters, to which they make no end, but we must set forth those spiritual things which we teach and preach, such as Christ, his righteousness, regeneration and eternal life, so that, if it can be done, these wretched men may at last be brought to see them and believe.

units.la: Vos adoratis. Ante absolutam resposionem suam (subiata enim differentia locorum & externo ac carnali cultu,continuò stabiliendus fuit cultus spiritualis, & eius mentio facienda) verùm ante absolutam responsionem, & eam responsionis partem quæ est de spirituali cultu,medio loco inseruit iustam responsionem ad quæstionem à muliere factam, Iudæorúmque in cultu & adoratione præfert Samaritanis. Vos adoratis quod nescitis, nos adoramus quod scimus. Iudæi adorârunt quod sciuerunt, quia ex præscripto verbi diuini adorârunt. Nam qui ex præscripto verbi Dei non adorat, adorat quod nescit.
units.tr: You worship. Before his full reply (for once the difference of places and external and carnal worship had been removed, spiritual worship had at once to be established and mention made of it), and before the part of the reply that concerns spiritual worship, he inserted in the middle a proper answer to the question put by the woman, and he prefers the Jews to the Samaritans in worship and adoration. You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know. The Jews worshipped what they knew, because they worshipped according to the prescription of the divine Word. For whoever does not worship according to the prescription of the Word of God worships what he does not know.

units.la: Neque enim bonæ intentiones Papistarum, quas præteruunt inuentionibus & adorationibus suis contra verbū Dei, vnquam efficient vt sciant miseri quod adorant, aut vnquam excusabunt idololatricum illum cultum. Dicat licet se adorare Deum creatorem cœli & terræ, Patrem Domini nostri Iesu Christi, non tamen efficient vnquam vt Deum cognoscant, quem non ex mente Dei, sed ex sensu suo colunt,& quem in imagine adorant, hoc est, vt Apostolus loquitur, cuius gloriam mutárunt in effigiem imaginem mortalis hominis,&c. Ita enim olim Samaritani adorârunt præter alios deos à se excogitatos,verum illū Deum Israëlis. Nihilominus dicit Christus eos quod nescirent adorare: quia non ex præscripto verbi ipsius ipsum adorârunt. Quia salus ex Iudeis est. Ratio differentiæ inter Iudæos & Samaritanos in cultu & adoratione. Est autem quia salus ex Iudæis est, hoc est, doctrina & verbum salutare tantum est nunc in Iudaica Ecclesia: Et ab ea Ecclesia tàtum in reliquos omnes populos deriuatur. Alludit, vt videtur, ad locum Esaiæ, quo introducit gentes sese inuicem hortantes ad ascendendum in montem Iehouæ, in domum Dei Iacobi, hoc est, ad adiungendum sese Ecclesiæ, quæ tunc Iudæ finibus conclusa fuit. Ratio ibidem addita est, Nam Sione prodiit doctrina, & verbum Iehouæ Hierosolymis, hoc est, quia verbum in Dei Ecclesia durat xat est,& ab ea deriuatur in alios omnes quicunque volunt eius participes fieri. Ecclesia enim est columna & stabilimentum veritatis. Hic quæstio instituitur de vera Ecclesia visibili, sitne illa Samaritana, an vero Iudaica: Respondet Christus Iudaicam esse veram illam visibilem, non autem Samaritanam. Docet autem veram esse Iudaicam ex nota verae ac salutaris doctrinae quae tum tantum in Iudaea fuit, & quae ex Iudaea in reliquas gentes fuit derivanda. Nam cum haec diceret Christus, nondum erant abdicati Iudaei, neque adhuc plane desierant esse Ecclesia Dei. Vide igitur quae sunt notae verae visibilis Ecclesiae: Successiones-ne illæ & universalitas, & alia quae afferunt Papistae? An vero verbum Dei pure praedicatum, & Sacramenta sincere administrata?
units.tr: For the good intentions of the Papists, which they put forward for their inventions and their worship contrary to the Word of God, will never make these wretched people know what they worship, nor will they ever excuse that idolatrous worship. Let them say that they worship God, the creator of heaven and earth, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ; yet they will never bring it about that they know the God whom they worship not according to the mind of God but according to their own sense, and whom they worship in an image, that is, as the Apostle says, who changed his glory into the likeness of an image of mortal man, and so on. For so the Samaritans of old worshipped, besides other gods devised by themselves, the true God of Israel. Nevertheless Christ says that they worshipped what they did not know, because they did not worship him according to his own prescribed Word. For salvation is of the Jews. This is the reason for the difference between the Jews and the Samaritans in worship and adoration. Now the meaning of for salvation is of the Jews is that the doctrine and saving Word are now only in the Jewish Church, and from that Church alone are they derived to all other peoples. He seems to allude to the passage of Isaiah in which he introduces the nations exhorting one another to go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob, that is, to join themselves to the Church, which was then confined within the borders of Judah. A reason is added in the same place: For from Zion goes forth the doctrine, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem, that is, because the Word endures in the Church of God alone, and is derived from it to all others who wish to become partakers of it. For the Church is the pillar and ground of the truth. Here the question is raised about the true visible Church, whether it is the Samaritan or the Jewish. Christ answers that the true visible Church is the Jewish one, and not the Samaritan. He teaches, however, that the Jewish is the true one, from the mark of true and saving doctrine, which at that time was in Judea alone, and which was to be derived from Judea to the other nations. For when Christ said these things, the Jews had not yet been cast off, nor had they yet altogether ceased to be the Church of God. See, then, what are the marks of the true visible Church: are they those successions and that universality, and the other things the Papists allege? Or rather, the Word of God purely preached and the Sacraments sincerely administered?

units.la: Sed venit hora. Sic obiter inseruit responsionem factam quaestioni de adorationis loco: Nunc redit ad superiorem responsionem inceptam quidem versu 21. sed interruptam ac interpellatam vers. 22. Nunc igitur ut prius sustulit omne discrimen locorum adorationis, simulque illum omnem cultum externum; ita nunc stabilit spiritualem ac verum cultum. Venit hora, inquit, & nunc est, cum veri adoratores adorabunt Patrem in spiritu ac veritate: Hoc est, cultu non externo, legali ac carnali: (Unde mandatum carnale dictum est, quo praescribitur hic cultus) sed interno, vero & sincero. Nam veritatem interpretor sinceritatem cordis, cui opponitur dolus: nisi mavis veritatem opponere umbris ac caeremoniis legalibus. Ratio duplex subiecta est; prior est a Dei voluntate. Etenim Pater tales quaerit qui ipsum adorent. Posterior est a Dei natura, Deus est Spiritus, ex quibus illud concludit, quod qui adorant eum, oporteat Spiritu & veritate id faciant. Vide ut statim postquam attigit obiter illud responsum factum ad id quod quaesiuit mulier, statim, inquam, redeat ad prius illud responsum quod inceptum erat vers. 21. Quo quidem exemplo suo nos docet Christus, si ita sumus ut attingamus illa externa & corporalia, in quibus adversarii toti sunt, non manendum esse diutius in his, sed inde redeundum ad magis utilia & spiritualia.
units.tr: But the hour is coming. Thus in passing he inserted his answer to the question about the place of worship. Now he returns to the earlier reply, which had begun at verse 21 but was interrupted and broken off at verse 22. So now, as before, he has removed every distinction of places of worship and at the same time all external worship; so now he establishes spiritual and true worship. The hour is coming, he says, and now is, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth: that is, not in external, legal and carnal worship (for which reason this worship as prescribed is called a carnal commandment), but in inward, true and sincere worship. For I understand truth as the sincerity of the heart, to which deceit is opposed; unless you prefer to take truth as opposed to the shadows and legal ceremonies. A twofold reason is added: the first is from the will of God: For the Father seeks such as worship him. The second is from the nature of God: God is Spirit, from which he concludes that those who worship him must do so in spirit and truth. See how, having touched in passing upon the answer given to the woman's question, he returns at once, I say, to the earlier answer that had begun at verse 21. By this example Christ teaches us that, if we are at some point touching on those external and bodily matters in which our adversaries are wholly absorbed, we must not remain in them any longer, but must return from there to what is more useful and spiritual.

units.la: Sed quod ex hoc loco praecipue discimus, hoc est, Ac primum quidem exemplo mulieris, omnes natura propendere ad externum & carnalem cultum: Quod cum viderent Papistae, cultus genus adinuenerunt prorsus externum ac carnale, & religionem penitus confutam ex crassis cæremoniis partim prophanarum gentium, partim Iudæorum consarcinauerunt. Indeque factum est, vt mundū natura sua tam procliuem ad istiusmodi cul-tum post fe vniuersum traxerint. Exemplo Christi deinde discimus, non esse indulgendum corruptæ actraf-fæ hominum naturæ,sed oculos pariter & animos auel-lendos ab his externis ad fpiritualiū cōtemplationē.Iu-dæis quidē cōcessus fuit adeoq; mādatus externus & cę-remonialis cultus,ita tamen vt internus & spiritualis cū eo coniūgi necesse fuerit.Neq;enim,vt hoc obiter dicā, ideo dictum est à Domino nunc demum venisse horam & tempus spiritualis cultus, ac fi non extiterit omnino ante hoc tempus in Iudaico populo spiritualis iste cultus,sed comparatè intelligendus est locus.Si enim compares cultum illum Iudæorum cum cultu Christianorum hominum, qui totus est spiritualis, ille Iudæorum cultus videtur non esse nisi externus & carnalis, cum tamen habuerint in illis cæremoniis suis tam multiplicibus Iudæi cultum suum internum ac spiritualem, ad quem Prophetæ semper eos sunt adhortati. Ut tigitur redeam ad id unde sum digressus, licuit quidem Iudæis externum & carnalem cultum exercere, quibus adumbratus duntaxat fuit Christus vmbris illis legalibus: At Christianorum cultus prorsus simplex ac spiritualis debet esse, neque oculi eorum trahendi sunt ad externas istas pompas & externa oblectamenta,quæ passim videre est in templis Papisticis,neque aures demulcendæ organis illis musicis, quæ in templis eorum passim sonat: sed aures occupandæ sunt in audiendo dūtaxat Dei verbo. Oculi non in aliis externis videndis,quàm in iis quę instituit Dominus noster Iesus Christus, symbolis visibilibus, Baptismo & Cœna Domini. Externa alia non agnosco, quæ quò plura sunt ab hominibus inuenta & in Ecclesiam Dei inuecta,eò longius abstrahimur à contemplatione Christi ipsius,& quæ in eo sunt, rerum spiritualium. Quare facessant hinc Papistæ cum pompis suis & spectaculis plus quàm theatricis: Nos autem,qui in Christi regno volumus viuere, magis magisque delectemur cultu simplici ac spirituali. Non enim, vt loquar quarcum Apostolo, accessimus ad mòtem tractabile, &c. hoc est, ad res terrenas, materiatas & tractabiles, cuiusmodi fuit mons Sina, ad quem tum olim accessit populus Israël: Verùm nos accessimus ad Hierusalem cœlestem, ad myriades Angelorum, concentum & concionem primogenitorum, qui conscripti sunt in cœlis, & Iudicem vniuersorum Deum, & spiritus iustorum consecratorum, & ad noui testamenti Mediatorem Iesum, & sanguinem aspersionis præstantiora loquente quàm loquerĕtur sanguis Abel, hoc est, accessimus ad res omnes spirituales eásque gloriosissimas, ad quas videndas oculis mentis semper nobis connitendum est in hac vita, tantisper dum iis plenè perfectéque fruamur in aduentu Domini nostri Iesu Christi, cui sit omnis honor & gloria, Amen.
units.tr: But what we chiefly learn from this passage is, first of all from the example of the woman, that all people by nature lean toward external and carnal worship. Seeing this, the Papists devised a kind of worship that is utterly external and carnal, and they patched together a religion, wholly refuted, out of the gross ceremonies partly of profane nations and partly of the Jews. Hence they have drawn the whole world after them, since the world by its nature is so prone to this kind of worship. Next, from Christ's example we learn that the corrupted nature of man is not to be indulged, but both eyes and minds must be torn away from these external things to the contemplation of spiritual things. The Jews indeed were granted, and even commanded, external and ceremonial worship, yet in such a way that internal and spiritual worship had to be joined with it. For, to say this in passing, it is not for this reason that the Lord said that now at last the hour and time of spiritual worship has come, as if this spiritual worship had not existed at all among the Jewish people before this time; the place must rather be understood comparatively. For if you compare that worship of the Jews with the worship of Christian men, which is wholly spiritual, that worship of the Jews seems to be nothing but external and carnal, although the Jews, in those many ceremonies of theirs, also had their internal and spiritual worship, to which the Prophets always exhorted them. So to return to where I digressed: it was indeed lawful for the Jews to practise external and carnal worship, in which Christ was only foreshadowed by those legal shadows. But the worship of Christians must be utterly simple and spiritual, and their eyes must not be drawn to those external pomps and external delights which are everywhere to be seen in Papist temples, nor their ears soothed by those musical instruments which everywhere sound in their temples; rather, ears are to be occupied in hearing the Word of God alone. Eyes are to be occupied with no external things other than those which our Lord Jesus Christ instituted, the visible signs, Baptism and the Lord's Supper. I acknowledge no other external things; the more of these men have invented and brought into the Church of God, the further we are drawn away from contemplating Christ himself and the spiritual things that are in him. Therefore let the Papists depart hence with their pomps and spectacles, more than theatrical; but we, who wish to live in the kingdom of Christ, should delight more and more in simple and spiritual worship. For, to speak with the Apostle, we have not come to a mountain that may be touched, etc. That is, we have not come to earthly, material and tangible things, such as Mount Sinai, to which the people of Israel once came. But we have come to the heavenly Jerusalem, to myriads of angels, to the gathering and assembly of the firstborn who are enrolled in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of the just made perfect, and to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling, which speaks better things than the blood of Abel. That is, we have come to all spiritual things, and those most glorious, which we must always strive in this life to see with the eyes of the mind, for so long until we enjoy them fully and perfectly at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, to whom be all honour and glory, Amen.

units.la: 25 Dicit ei mulier, Scio Messiam venturum (qui dicitur Christus) quum venerit ille, nobis annuntiabit omnia.
units.tr: 25 The woman said to him, I know that the Messiah is coming (who is called Christ). When he comes, he will tell us all things.

units.la: 26 Dicit ei Iesu, Ego is sum qui loquor tibi.
units.tr: 26 Jesus said to her, I am he who speaks to you.

units.la: AVdita innouatione cultus & adorationis, statim subit recordatio Messiæ, quia plerique omnes in aduentu Messiæ expectabant rerum omnium insignem aliquam mutationem. Dicit itaque mulier, Scio Messiam venturum, qui Græcè dicitur Christus. Hæc verba videntur inserta ab Euangelista, quibus interpretatur Hebraicam Messiæ vocem. Messias enim Hebreis est, Christus Græcis, Vnctus Latinis; de qua voce iam antea à nobis dictum est. Cùm venerit ille, nobis annuntiabit omnia, Nempe quæ ad cultum & religionem spectant. Dicit ei Iesus, Ego is sum qui loquor tibi. Christus multis rationib. ac modis iam inde à dialogismi huius principio, conatus est excitare memoriam Messiæ; huc enim videntur pertinere omnia quæ ab eo dicta sunt, quod loquutus est de aqua viua, cuod dixit ei omnia quæcunque fecit, quod denique de Spirituali cultu & reparatione rerum omnium. Non citius autem recordatur mulier Messiæ, eúmque desiderare incipit, quàm prodit se Christus eū se esse. Deus noster omnibus modis conatur nos Christi seruatoris memores reddere, & cuius profecto non nisi dissicillimè recordantur homines, vt exemplo huius mulieris discimus, quæ tam tardè, & non nisi post longum sermonem vltrò citroque habitum, Messiæ recordatur: Nam occupationes huius vitæ obruunt memoriam Christi. Non citius aute eius reminiscimur, ipsumque cum desiderio aliquo sentimus, quàm ipse nobis respondeat, & adesse nobis aliquo modo significet: Etsi enim non exhibeat nobis nunc visibilem suam præsentiam, vt tum olim mulieri isti, tamen non minus efficaciter præsens est etiam nūc cordibus nostris, quàm tunc fuit oculis mulieris. Unde enim, quæso, est hoc gaudium quod sentimus, hæc pax qua tranquillantur cōscientiæ nostræ? Non aliunde profectò quàm à Christi illa præsentia in cordibus nostris. Quem cùm non vide-rimus, diligimus; quem cùm nunc non cernamus, ei tamen credentes exultamus gaudio ineffabili ac gloriosò. Sed tempus aderit, neque longè ab hinc abest, cùm desiderantes Dominū, videbimus eum præsentem ac viva voce respondentem nobis se adesse: Hoc enim ipsum desiderium Christi, quod pij omnes sentiunt in se, in tot tamen confusionibus & perturbationibus omnium rerum argumento est, non longè abesse illud tempus, quo Dominus venturus est ad iudicandum mundum. Dedit aliquando illud sui desiderium vel gemens in cordibus piorum hominum qui illum in primo suo aduentu exertis capitibus expectârunt. Cùm igitur nūc in postremis hisce temporibus det suis desiderium sui ingens, argumento est eum festinare & accelerare aduentum illum suum gloriosum. Beati quotquot expectant & desiderant cum suspiriis illustrem illum aduentū Domini. Deinde mulier hæc, vt colligi potest ex verbis ipsius, expetebat innouationem cultus ac religionis, & nouam aliquam reuelationem, ideóque factum vt Messiam desideraret. Quare non ita tranquillatus animus eius & confirmatus fuit in superstitione Samaritanorū, quin meliorem cultum & optauerit & expectauerit. Imò Iudæi ipsi, quorum religio à Deo ipso erat præscripta; non tamen ea fuerunt contenti; verùm cùm umbras haberent, corpus ipsum expetiuerunt: ideóque author ad Hebræos affirmat sacrificia illa vetera & legalia à Deo ipso præscripta non purgasse conscientiam peccati: Argumentum
units.tr: When the renewal of worship and of adoration is mentioned, the memory of the Messiah immediately comes to mind, because almost all people expected some notable change of all things at the coming of the Messiah. So the woman says, I know that the Messiah is coming, who is called Christ in Greek. These words seem to have been inserted by the Evangelist, to interpret the Hebrew word Messiah. For the Hebrews say Messiah, the Greeks say Christ, and the Latins say Anointed; of this word we have already spoken earlier. When he comes, he will tell us all things, namely those things that pertain to worship and religion. Jesus said to her, I am he who speaks to you. From the beginning of this dialogue Christ has in many ways and by many means tried to awaken the memory of the Messiah; for to this seem to belong all the things he has said, that he spoke of living water, that he told her all that she had done, and finally that he spoke of spiritual worship and the restoration of all things. But the woman no sooner remembers the Messiah and begins to long for him than Christ reveals that he is the one. Our God in every way seeks to make us mindful of Christ the Saviour, and yet men remember him only with great difficulty, as we learn from the example of this woman, who remembers the Messiah so slowly, and only after a long conversation held back and forth. For the cares of this life overwhelm the memory of Christ. Nor do we remember him sooner, or feel some longing for him, than he himself answers us and signifies in some way that he is present with us. For although he does not now show us his visible presence, as he did once to that woman, yet he is no less effectively present now in our hearts than he was then to the woman's eyes. For whence, I ask, comes this joy that we feel, this peace by which our consciences are calmed? Surely from nothing other than Christ's presence in our hearts. Whom, though we have not seen, we love; though now we do not see him, yet believing in him we exult with joy unspeakable and full of glory. But the time will come, and it is not far off, when, longing for the Lord, we shall see him present and he will answer us with his living voice that he is here. For this very longing for Christ, which all the godly feel within themselves amid so much confusion and disorder of all things, is a sign that the time is not far off when the Lord will come to judge the world. At other times that longing for him has been sensed, even groaned for, in the hearts of godly people who waited for him with heads lifted up at his first coming. Therefore, since now in these last times he gives his people so great a longing for himself, it is a sign that he is hastening and accelerating that glorious coming of his. Blessed are all who expect and desire with sighs the illustrious coming of the Lord. Further, this woman, as can be gathered from her own words, was seeking a renewal of worship and religion and some new revelation, and therefore it came about that she desired the Messiah. Hence her mind was not so calmed and confirmed in the superstition of the Samaritans that she did not both wish for and expect a better worship. Indeed the Jews themselves, whose religion God himself had prescribed, were not content with it; but since they had shadows, they longed for the body itself. Therefore the author to the Hebrews affirms that those old and legal sacrifices, prescribed by God himself, could not purge the conscience of sin. Argument

units.la: Quomodo id fiat.
units.tr: How this comes about.

units.la: Heb.1.10. tum adducit crebram illam eorum repetitionem atque iterationem, quæ satis indicauit ipsorum imperfectionem. Quare ante aduentum Christi, vel nulla fuit planè religio, vel nulla fuit perfecta. Verùm perfectademum religionem ac voluntatis diuinæ reuelationem primus in mundum introduxit Iesus Christus: Quod confirmat vel conscientiæ eorum, quotquot sunt quorum aperti sunt oculi, vt videant hanc lucem ac reuelatione longè clarissimam. Nam ita in ea toti acquiescunt vt nihil amplius desiderent in hac vita, nullam reuelationem clariorem; ita contenti sunt Christi illo sacrificio semel oblato, vt nullum sacrificium præterea requirant. Quod vtinam animaduerterent tandem Papistæ, qui quotidie sacrificant, quasi imperfectum esset illud Christi vnicum sacrificium, & infinitas vanitates quotidie affuunt puritati ac simplicitati Euangelij, acsi illa esset mutila & manca sine illis accessionibus.
units.tr: Heb. 1.10. He then adduces their frequent repetition and iteration of the same sacrifices, which sufficiently showed their imperfection. Hence before the coming of Christ there was either no religion at all, or no perfect one. But it was Jesus Christ who first brought perfect religion and the revelation of the divine will into the world. This is confirmed even by the consciences of all those whose eyes have been opened to see this light, which is by far the clearest revelation. For they rest so wholly in it that they desire nothing more in this life, and seek no clearer revelation; they are so content with Christ's sacrifice, offered once for all, that they require no other sacrifice. Would that the Papists, who sacrifice every day, would at last take note of this, as if Christ's one sacrifice were imperfect, and as if countless vanities were added every day to the purity and simplicity of the Gospel, as though it were maimed and lame without those additions.

units.la: 27 Interea verò venerunt eius discipuli, & mirati sunt quòd cum muliere loqueretur. Nemo tamen dixit, Quid quæris, aut, quid loqueris cum ea?
units.tr: Meanwhile his disciples came back, and they marvelled that he was speaking with a woman. Yet no one said, "What are you seeking?" or "Why are you speaking with her?"

units.la: 28 Reliquit ergo hydriam suam mulier, & abiit in vrbem, dixitque eius loci hominibus,
units.tr: The woman then left her water jar and went off into the city, and said to the people there,

units.la: 29 Venite, videte hominem, qui dixit mihi quæcunque feci: num iste est Christus ille?
units.tr: "Come, see a man who told me everything I have ever done. Could this be the Christ?"

units.la: 30 Exierunt ergo ex vrbe, & venerunt ad eum.
units.tr: So they went out of the city and came to him.

units.la: HActenus fuit communicatio illa inter Christum & mulierem, nunc est commemoratio eius quod incidit in finem illius communicationis: Interuenerunt discipuli Christi, qui iam antea missi fuerunt in vrbem vt emerent cibos; Mirantur illi quòd cum vili & abiecto muliere loqueretur. Illud imprimis admiratione omnium dignum est, quòd Deus demittat se ad conferendos sermones cum abiectissimo & vilissimo quoque. Nemo enim est qui tam vilescit mundo, quin eum sermone dignetur Deus. Nemo etiam est qui tam contemptus est in oculis suis ipsius, quin postquam iam aperti sunt oculi ad videndam suam ipsius fœditatem, Deus eum sustineat intueri & affari. Nullum peccatum adeo graue, adeo horribile est, vt excludat præsentiam Dei, si semel amplexus fueris illud Christi sacrificiu, semélque aspersus fueris illo sanguine, qui adeo pretiosus est in oculis Dei. Sed hoc non caret vitio, quod discipuli, & si reuerentia quadam, fateor, magistri sui, ad id inducti sint, quod, inquam, non conscij conditionis suæ ipsorum pristinæ, qui ex nihilo facti sunt aliquid, in quo materia non minor, adeoque etiam maior erat admirationis, non, inquam, conscij conditionis suæ, non potuerunt satis mirari Dominum respexisse vilem illam & abiectam mulierem. Sic se res habet, & sic natura comparatum est, vt nemo sit omnium nostrum qui videat sortem ac vilitatem suam: indeque est quod se magni faciat quisque, velitque se apud homines in pretio esse & plurimi fieri ac laudari, etiam si quæ in ipso sunt vitia. At vero quæ in aliis sunt labes & maculæ, eas perspicacissimè intueatur, damnet ac ægre ferat si qui indignus abiectúsque ac vilis videtur, is in honore sit apud alios. Hæc est communis nostrum omnium natura. Conandum igitur vt omnes nos primùm omnium peruideamus nosipsos ac vilitatem nostrum ipsorum, vt qui mirari velit, miretur Domini respexisse se omniū mortalium infimum, dicatque apud se, Quis sum ego, Domine, vt me digneris hoc loco & hoc honore? Consideratio ista vilitatis nostræ cum admiratione gratiæ Dei provocat nos ad assiduam gratiarum actionem. Gratias ago ei qui me robustum effecit, id est, Christo Iesu Domino nostro, qui me fidelem duxerit, &c. Hæc Paulus de se. Sed unde exiit gratiarum ista actio? Vide quæ subiicit: Qui prius erat blasphemus, & persecutor & iniuriosus: hæc est consideratio vilitatis & indignitatis suæ, non sine admiratione diuinæ gratiæ.
units.tr: Thus far was that conversation between Christ and the woman. Now comes the record of what happened at the end of it. Christ's disciples returned, those who had been sent earlier into the city to buy food. They marvel that he was speaking with a woman so lowly and despised. Above all, this deserves the wonder of everyone: that God stoops to converse with the most abject and vile of persons. For there is no one so worthless in the world that God does not deign to speak with him. Nor is there anyone so despised in his own eyes that God cannot bear to look upon him and address him, once his eyes have been opened to see his own foulness. No sin is so grave, so horrible, that it shuts out the presence of God, if only you have embraced that sacrifice of Christ and been sprinkled with that blood, which is so precious in the eyes of God. But it is not free of fault that the disciples, although, I grant, they were led by a certain reverence for their master, did not, I say, being unaware of their former condition, the condition of those who were made something out of nothing, a matter that called for no less, indeed even greater, wonder, could not sufficiently marvel that the Lord had regarded that vile and abject woman. So things stand, and so nature has ordained it, that none of us sees his own lowliness and vileness. Hence each person makes much of himself and wishes to be held in esteem among men and to be greatly valued and praised, even when there are faults in him. Yet whatever blemishes and stains are in others, he looks at most keenly, condemns, and takes ill; if someone seems unworthy, abject and vile, he resents that such a man should be honoured among others. This is the common nature of us all. We must therefore strive first of all to see clearly ourselves and our own vileness, so that whoever wishes to wonder may wonder that the Lord has regarded him, the lowest of all mortals, and say to himself, "Who am I, Lord, that you should deign to look on me in this place and with this honour?" This consideration of our vileness, together with wonder at the grace of God, moves us to constant thanksgiving. I give thanks to him who has strengthened me, that is, to Christ Jesus our Lord, who counted me faithful, etc. Thus Paul speaks of himself. But whence came that thanksgiving? See what he adds: who was before a blasphemer, and a persecutor, and injurious. This is the consideration of his own vileness and unworthiness, not without wonder at divine grace.

units.la: Nemo tamen dixit. Miranti quidem sunt discipuli quòd Christus alloqueretur tam vilem mulierem, non tamen ausi sunt efferre quod cogitarunt. Multa sunt quæ nos cogitamus, & illa quidem indigna aduersus maiestatem & prouidentiam Dei, quantisper non sumus plenè regenerati. Atque hoc sentimus in nobis ipsi sæpè, non a'bsque magno dolore, qui etiam Paulo miserabilem hanc vocem expressit, Miser ego homo, quis me eripiet ex isto corpore mortis? Quid hic faciendum sit discimus exemplo discipulorum Christi: Reprimendæ sunt ac strangulandæ quasi in pectore impiæ huiusmodi cogitationes omnes, quæ indignæ sunt quæ in lucem proferantur, cauendumque ne aperte violemus sacrosanctam illâ maiestatem. Hoc ita fiet, si imbuatur animus noster reuerentia aliqua Dei, & opinione veritatis atque iustitiæ ipsius: ita enim fiet, vt reluctantes dicamus impuris istis cogitationibus, Compescite vos, Deus meus iustus est, Deus meus verus est, &c.
units.tr: Yet no one said. The disciples indeed marvelled that Christ spoke with so vile a woman, but they did not dare to voice what they were thinking. We think many things, and indeed unworthy things, against the majesty and providence of God, for as long as we are not fully regenerated. We often feel this in ourselves, not without great grief; it even drew from Paul this pitiful cry: Wretched man that I am, who will deliver me from this body of death? What we should do here we learn from the example of Christ's disciples. All such impious thoughts, which are unworthy to be brought to light, must be repressed and strangled, as it were, in the breast, and we must take care not to violate that most holy majesty openly. This will happen if our mind is imbued with some reverence for God, and with the conviction of his truth and justice. For so we will say, struggling against those impure thoughts, "Be silent! My God is just, my God is true," etc.

units.la: Reliquit ergo hydriam. Redit Euangelista ad mulierem, ostenditque quodnam effectum operata sit in muliere illa, de qua dictum est, Messiæ reuelatio. Reliquit, inquit, hydriam suam mulier. Paulo ante magni-fecit fontem illum Iacobi, magni fecit vas illud suum quo hausit aquam ex fonte. Nunc vero vbi primùm audiuit de Messia, eúmque præsentem intuita est, horum obliuiscitur. Qui magni faciunt terrestria ita, meliora non nouerunt; qui toti affixi sunt & alligati huic mundo, diuitiis huius mundi, gloriæ huius mundi, etsi millies dixerint se scire Christum, se scire cœlos; tamen non credidero. Nam si quis vel leuiter gustauerit quàm benignus sit Dominus, illud gignat necesse est in eo tam admirabilem mutationem, vt qui paulo ante totus addictus fuit hisce rebus, iam liber ac solutus feratur supra hos cœlos, & ista omnia inferiora despiciat quasi ex alto: imò sese ipse negct, nihilque faciat suum ipsius dedecus, vt Dominus glorificetur. Dixit mihi, inquit mulier, omnia quæcunque feci. Ecce nō puduit eam diuulgare sua etiam peccata, vt Dominus iustificaretur in veritate verbi sui, quo quasi mulierem accusauit scortationis. Sic Dauid, Conuertor, inquit, vt iustificeris in sermonibus tuis, & tu purus sis quando iudicas. Quòd si tam leuis aspectus Christi tantum pariat gaudium, quantum erit gaudium tum cùm videmus eum sicuti est? Putant vulgò hi, qui toti sunt in his inferioribus, in gloria, in voluptatibus, in diuitiis huius mundi: putant, inquam, non posse se cœlos assequi, nisi simul his crassis reb' quibus hic se oblectãr, fruantur, eásque secum quasi in cœlos auferant. Putat diues non esse cœleste gaudium sine diuitiis suis: Putat libidinosus non consistere cœleste gaudium sine libidine sua: Putat ambitiosus non esse cœlós sine gloria huius mundi. Sed, miser, si daretur tibi semel introspicere in illud gaudium cœlorum quod in Christo reconditū est, citiùs dicto obliuiscereris istorum omnium, iamque amplius non caperes voluptatem ex his quibus etiam propter necessitatem huius vitæ carere non potes. In resurrectione, respondet Christus Sadducæis, neque ducunt vxores, neque nuptum dantur, sed sunt vt Angeli Dei in cœlo. Quibus verbis significat incorruptos fore ac gloriosos tanquam Angelos, deposita tota hac infirmitate quæ nunc est, nihilóque magis quàm ipsos Angelos opus habituros istis rebus terrenis & crassis, quæ ad hanc mortalem conditionem sunt necessaria. Et abiit in vrbem. Non statim contulit se domum, vt quod concepit gaudium ex Messia conspecto apud se reseruaret, atque id aliis non communicaret, sed vt eius loci homines ac gentiles suos ad Christum adduceret, vt & ii percepti gaudij fierent socij. Fides in Christum habet perpetuò comitem charitatem: fides enim per charitatem operatur. Qui Christum semel ipse apprehendit corde, eundem libenter impertit aliis, neque fieri potest, quin de eo verba faciat apud alios. Credidi, & ideo locutus sum. Nō necesse est perpetuò, vt qui de Christo loquatur, non loquatur de eo, nisi ex suggestu in publico hominum cœtu. Loquendum de Christo omnibus, in omni loco, in omni tempore. Quod si qui duo peregrè abeant in locū vel regionem aliquam vbi commoraturi sunt, & sedem suam locaturi, ij ferè sermones suos habent de regione illa, de moribus, de commoditatibus eius. De regionibus autem per quas iter faciunt, nihil aut parum admodum loquuntur. Quòd si nostri homines emiterentur ad cœlestem illam patriam, sicuti vulgò iactitant; Quis enim tam sœdus adulter, qui non prædicet se iter ad cœlos corripere? Quis tam crudelis homicida, qui non dicat se eòdem tendere? & sic de cæteris. Verùm si seriò cogitarent illuc se conferre, certè oportet eos vel semel interdiu aut noctu, vel loqui vel meditari de cœlis. iis quos iactitant, neque ita occupari cogitationes eorum in vanitatibus, & voces eorum in solis rebus huius mundi, in convitiis, in blasphemiis, in aliis huiusmodi: quæ satis superqueargunt animum non esse attentum ad illa cœlestia. Paulus postquam de gloriosa illa futura resurrectione dixisset: Consolamini, inquit, alij alios iis sermonibus. Meditationes & sermones de cœlis ac supernis, impossibile est separari à fide & spe vitæ & cœlorum: Immo hos vius habent, inchoant & alunt vitam illam cælestem tanquam perdum ea plenè perfruantur. Venite & videte. Hæc est concio multi-s, quam habuit apud cives{?} suos, venite & videte hor-, qui dixit mihi quæcunque fe-ci: Num iste est Christus? Num Christus sit necne vos ipsi iudicate. Hoc autem certò scio eum dixisse mihi omnia quæcunque feci, & totius vitæ meæ conditionem, præteritæ, præsentis in peccato, mihi exposuisse. Similiter loquitur cæcus ille à natiuitate, postea cap. 9. 25. &c. An peccator sit nescio. Vnum scio, me, cum cæcus fuerim, nunc videre. Certum autem est magis inclinasse mulierem in eam sententiam quòd esset Messias. Nisi enim Messiæ fuisset aliqua apprehensio, profectò non extitisset ea in corde lætitia, quæ non exurgit nisi ex fide in Christum Iesum. Quemadmodum idem ille cæcus paulò post eodem capite Christum non esse peccatorem conuincit: Scimus Deum peccatores non audire, sed si quis Dei cultor est & voluntatem eius exequitur, hunc audit. Deus autem hunc audiuit, tantumque opus antea inauditum per eum præstitit: Ergo is peccator non est. Videmus in hoc exemplo mulieris, quanta cum infirmitate sæpe prædicent Christum, etiam ministri Dei, quàm mediocri cum actione, quàm parua etiam nonnunquam cum persuasione cordis & παῤῥησίᾳ, quantis cum dubitationibus, ac anxietatibus animi, sicuti Paulus de se ait, Fui ego cum infirmitate & timore ac tremore multo apud vos: Neque oratio mea & prædicatio mea versata est in persuasorijs humanæ sapientiæ verbis. Vide rursus exemplo infirmæ huius mulieris quàm efficaciter operari soleat Deus in cordibus hominum per infirmitatem nostram. Exiuerunt, inquit, ex vrbe, & venerunt ad eum. Ita Deus in infirmitate ministrorum suorum sæpe efficax est per Spiritum suum, vt ap-
units.tr: So she left her water jar. The Evangelist returns to the woman and shows what effect the revelation of the Messiah had upon her. The woman, he says, left her water jar. A little before, she had prized that well of Jacob, and prized the vessel with which she drew water from the well. But now, as soon as she heard of the Messiah and saw him present, she forgets these things. Those who set great store by earthly things do not know better things; those who are wholly fixed and bound to this world, its riches and its glory, will not, I believe, be credited even if they have said a thousand times that they know Christ and know heaven. For if anyone has even lightly tasted how gracious the Lord is, this must necessarily produce in him so wonderful a change that the one who a little before was wholly given over to these things is now carried free and loosed above the heavens, and looks down on all these lower things as from on high; indeed he denies himself and counts nothing his own shame, so that the Lord may be glorified. He told me, said the woman, everything that I have done. See, she was not ashamed to publish even her own sins, so that the Lord might be justified in the truth of his word, by which he, as it were, accused the woman of fornication. So David: I turn, he says, that you may be justified in your words, and be pure when you judge. But if so slight a sight of Christ brings such joy, how great will the joy be when we see him as he is? Those who are wholly given over to these lower things, to pleasures, to riches of this world, commonly suppose, I say, that they cannot attain heaven unless they enjoy these gross things in which they delight here, and carry them off with them into heaven. The rich man thinks there is no heavenly joy without his riches; the lustful man thinks there is no heavenly joy without his lust; the ambitious man thinks there is no heaven without the glory of this world. But, wretched man, if it were granted you once to look into that joy of heaven which is laid up in Christ, you would forget all these things in a moment, and you would no longer take pleasure in those things which you cannot even do without for the necessities of this life. In the resurrection, Christ answers the Sadducees, they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like the angels of God in heaven. By these words he signifies that they will be incorrupt and glorious, like angels, having laid aside all this present weakness, and that they will need these earthly and gross things, which are necessary for this mortal condition, no more than the angels themselves do. And she went away into the city. She did not at once betake herself home to keep to herself the joy she had conceived from seeing the Messiah, and not share it with others; she brought the people of that place and her own kinsfolk to Christ, so that they too might become partners in the joy she had received. Faith in Christ always has love as its companion: faith works through love. Whoever has truly laid hold of Christ in his heart gladly imparts him to others, nor can it be otherwise than that he speaks of him to others. I believed, and therefore I have spoken. It is not necessary that whoever speaks of Christ always speak of him from a pulpit before a public assembly. Everyone must speak of Christ, in every place and at every time. When two men go abroad to some land or region where they are to stay and settle, their talk is for the most part about that region, its customs and its advantages; but of the lands through which they travel they say little or nothing. But if our people were hastening toward that heavenly homeland, as they commonly boast, who is so foul an adulterer that he would not declare he is hastening toward heaven? Who is so cruel a murderer that he would not say he is heading there too? And so on for the rest. Yet if they were seriously thinking of going there, they would surely speak of heaven, or at least meditate on it, once a day, by day or by night, instead of their thoughts being so taken up with vanities and their words only with the things of this world, with abuse, with blasphemies, and with other such things, which are quite enough to prove that their minds are not attentive to those heavenly things. After Paul had spoken of that glorious resurrection to come, he said: Comfort one another, he says, with these words. Meditations and talk about heaven and the things above cannot be separated from faith and hope of life and heaven; indeed they have this use: they begin and nourish that heavenly life, so that we may fully enjoy it. Come and see. This was the sermon he gave among his fellow citizens: Come and see a man who told me everything that I have done. Is this not the Christ? Judge for yourselves whether he is Christ or not. This I know for certain: he told me everything that I have ever done, and laid out before me the whole state of my life, past and present, in sin. The blind man from birth speaks similarly, later in chapter 9, verses 25 and following: Whether he is a sinner I do not know. One thing I know: that whereas I was blind, now I see. It is certain, however, that the woman was rather inclined to think that he was the Messiah. For unless there had been some apprehension of the Messiah in her, surely there would not have arisen in her heart that joy, which arises only from faith in Christ Jesus. Just as that same blind man, a little later in the same chapter, proves that Christ is not a sinner: We know that God does not hear sinners, but if anyone is a worshipper of God and does his will, him he hears. But God did hear him, and by him performed a work so great and unheard of before. Therefore he is not a sinner. We see in this example of the woman how greatly, with what weakness, ministers of God too often preach Christ, with how mediocre an effect, how small at times even with conviction of heart and boldness [παῤῥησίᾳ], with what doubts and anxieties of mind; as Paul says of himself: I was with you in weakness and in fear and much trembling. Nor did my speech and my preaching consist in persuasive words of human wisdom. Again, see from the example of this weak woman how effectively God is wont to work in the hearts of men through our weakness. They went out, he says, of the city, and came to him. Thus God, often effective through the Spirit in the weakness of his ministers, so that it may appear that the work is not of man, nor of the natural faculties that are in man, but of God himself, so that the excellence of the power may be of God and not of us, so that he who glories may glory in the Lord.

units.la: {1} 1. Thes. 4. 18. pareat opus esse non hominis, aut facultatum naturalium quae in homine sunt, sed ipsius Dei, vt eius virtutis praestantia sit Dei, & non ex nobis, vt qui gloriatur, in Domino glorietur, Cui sit omnis honor & gloria, Amen.
units.tr: 1 Thess. 4.18. It appears that the work is not of man, or of the natural faculties that are in man, but of God himself, so that the excellence of this power is God's and not ours; so that "he who glories, let him glory in the Lord." To whom be all honour and glory, Amen.

units.la: 31 Interim autem rogabant eum discipuli, dicentes, Rabbi, comede.
units.tr: Meanwhile the disciples were asking him, saying, Rabbi, eat.

units.la: 32 Ille autem dixit eis, Ego cibum habeo quem vescar, quem vos non nostis.
units.tr: But he said to them, I have food to eat that you do not know.

units.la: 33 Dicebant ergo discipuli alij ad alios, Num quis attulit ei vt vesceretur?
units.tr: So the disciples said to one another, Has anyone brought him something to eat?

units.la: SEquitur communicatio quaedam inter Christum & Sipsius discipulos habita interea dum Samaritani ad eum veniunt. Qua communicatione Christus primum instituit discipulos suos in ea sollicitudine & cura qua ipse habet lucrandi animas hominum: deinde hortatur discipulos ad serium studium & diligentiam in vocatione sua, & in demetenda messe Domini. Quod ad primum, dicit, Interim autem rogabant: Hoc est, interea tempori dum Samaritani ad Christum venire festinant, vicissim; Christus eos expectat & a cibo abstinet: quod tamen Domini consilium ignorarunt discipuli; ideoque rogabant eum vt cibum caperet, quasi vero hoc ea praecipue agendum esset: Neque enim discipuli intellexerunt quid ei ex officio incumberet, neque dum satis spirituales erant, sed sapiebant adhuc magis ea quae erant huius mundi, quam superna illa ac coelestia. Quorum oculi nondum sunt illuminati ad videndum Deum, Christum & illa spiritualia ac coelestia, putant illi nihil serio ac sedulo agendum in hac vita, nisi quod ad hanc vitam tolerandam pertinet, nisi hoc, vt edamus, bibamus, dormiamus, opes congeramus, honores venemur, aliaque id genus tori incumbamus: Atque ideo fit, vt sic decepti opinione occupentur in vita praecipue, & distrahantur iis rebus; quibus etiam occupabuntur plerique omnes in aduentu illo Domini secundo, edent, bibent, vxores ducent, & nuptum dabunt, quemadmodum fiebat diebus Noae. Sed, o oppressionem illam & angustiam quae in illo die eos occupabit. Vt autem haec vnic
units.tr: What follows is a certain conversation between Christ and his disciples, held while the Samaritans are coming to him. In this conversation Christ first instructs his disciples in that concern and care with which he himself seeks to win the souls of men; then he exhorts the disciples to earnest zeal and diligence in their calling and in reaping the Lord's harvest. As to the first, he says, Meanwhile the disciples were asking him. That is, in the meantime, while the Samaritans are hurrying to come to Christ, in turn Christ waits for them and abstains from food. Yet the disciples did not know this purpose of the Lord, and so they asked him to take food, as if this were especially what ought to be done then. For the disciples did not understand what duty lay upon him, nor were they yet spiritual enough, but still savoured more of those things which are of this world than of those supernal and heavenly things. Their eyes are not yet enlightened to see God, Christ and those spiritual and heavenly things. They think nothing is to be done earnestly and diligently in this life except what pertains to enduring this life: that is, that we eat, drink, sleep, heap up wealth, hunt after honours, and devote ourselves to other things of that kind. And so it happens that being thus deceived by opinion, they are occupied in life above all, and distracted by those things. By these same things most people will be occupied at that second coming of the Lord: they will eat, drink, take wives and give in marriage, as was done in the days of Noah. But oh, the oppression and distress that will overtake them on that day! But as they do these things only,

units.la: Matth. 24. 37.38. nicèagunt, & in his sunt ipsi : ita quantum in se est o-mnes alios huc inuitant, ac inuitos sæpe trahunt, nunc rogando,vt discipuli Christum rogárunt: nùc verò blasphemando,vt illi ex gentibus, cùm initio qui conuersi fuerunt ad Christum non concurrerent ad eandem lu-xus profusionem. Adeo periculosum sit piis versanti in hoc mundo, & ipsi electi non nisi difficulter seruentur. Sed videamus quid ad hoc respondeat Christus. Ille autem dixit us, Ego cibum habeo. Significat nunc se etiam ve-sci cibi quodam genere, quod ab ipsis ignoretur. Intelli-git autem huius cibi nomine, vt ipse exponit postea, opus patris sui ad quod faciendum missus est in hunc mundum. In exemplo Christi hoc est quod obseruamus: Qui oculos habent aliqua ex parte illuminatos ad videndum coelestia, & ea quæ pertinent ad regnum Dei, illi quidem statuunt apud se nihil agendum serio in tota vita, præter illa coelestia: ideóque & ipsi hæc agunt vnicè, alia autem omnia obiter, & tamen ea ipsa agunt in Dei gloriam. Siue editis, siue bibitis,siue quid faci-tis, omnia facite in Dei gloriam. Ipsi igitur hæc agunt vnicè, & alios pertrahunt & inuitant ad videndum, quæ ipsi vident, sine vlla vatione fieri possit. Paulus per-petuo in vita spectabat non ea quæ cernuntur, sed ea quæ non cernuntur negligebat. Ideóque eadem illa, quantum per ipsum fieri potuit, aliis conatus est de-monstrare. Si resurrexistu, inquit, cum Christo, superna quærite, vbi Christus est ad dextram Dei sedens: superna cura-te non terrestria: Nam mortui estis, & vita vestra abscondita est cum Christo in Deo. Et profecto is potest commodissi-mè aliis cœlos demonstrare qui ipse prior vidit eos: Atque eos demum solos decet loqui de Christo, déque eius beneficiis, qui ipsi priores Christum & viderunt ac senserunt. Deinde videmus in his Christi verbis,& in hoc Christi exemplo, pios, vbi semel datum est iis inspicere illa cæleltia, euehi longè supra omnes hos cœlos, & supra istos qui perpetuò hæret in cœno huius mundi, quantùmuis sapientes, quantùuis gloriosi esse videantur, & ista omnia desuper quasi spectare,nihiliq; facere vel sapientiam huius mundi, vel nobilitatem & gloriā nobilium, intuentes in illam sapientiam & gloriā quæ
units.tr: Matth. 24. 37.38. They act in the same way, and are caught up in these things themselves. So far as they can, they invite all others to join them, and often drag the unwilling along: sometimes by asking, as the disciples asked Christ, and sometimes, indeed, by blaspheming, as those from the Gentiles did when, at the beginning, those who had been converted to Christ did not run to the same riotous extravagance. So dangerous is it for the godly to live in this world, and even the elect are only with difficulty kept safe. But let us see how Christ answers this. But he said to them, I have food to eat. He now signifies that he also feeds on a certain kind of food that is unknown to them. He means by the name of this food, as he himself explains afterwards, the work of his Father, for the doing of which he was sent into this world. In Christ's example we observe this: those who have their eyes in some measure enlightened to see heavenly things, and those things which belong to the kingdom of God, decide that nothing else in their whole life is to be done seriously except those heavenly things. Therefore they do these things alone, and do all other things only in passing, yet they do those very things for the glory of God. Whether you eat, or drink, or do anything else, do all things for the glory of God. So they alone do these things, and draw and invite others to see what they themselves see, as far as this can be done without any loss. Paul, throughout his life, looked not at the things that are seen, but disregarded the things that are not seen. Therefore he tried, as far as it could be done through him, to show those same things to others. If you have risen, he says, with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God: care for the things that are above, not for the things that are on earth. For you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. And truly he can most fittingly show the heavens to others who has himself seen them first; and it is fitting that those alone speak of Christ and of his benefits who first saw and felt Christ themselves.
