Ergo denuntiat eiectionem e domo Dei. q.d. quamuis ad tempus videamini in speciem filij in domo Dei, tamen serui estis: & eiiciendi e domo Dei suo tempore, nisi resipueritis. Alludit autem ad conditionem servi quæ est in familia & domo heri sui. Ad tempus servus est filio similis, fruitur quoque privilegiis filij, imperat in domo.
units.tr: But consider what the Lord immediately declares against these slaves of sin: "The slave," he says, "does not remain in the house forever." Therefore he threatens their expulsion from the house of God. As if to say: although for a time you seem, in appearance, to be children in the house of God, nevertheless you are slaves, and unless you repent, you will be cast out of the house of God in due time. He alludes, moreover, to the condition of a slave, who is in the household and house of his master. For a time the slave is like the son, he also enjoys the privileges of the son, and he commands in the house.

units.la: {y} Matth. 7. 16. Ioan. 3. domo heri sui omniaque gubernat: Sed cum ventum est ad hæreditatem diuidendam, tum eiicitur e domo, cumque omnibus innotescit eum seruum esse & fuisse: ita se res habet in domo Dei. Hypocrita aliquis manet in Ecclesia Dei visibili ista tanquam filius, gaudetque priuilegiis filij, participat verbo simul & sacramentis: sed cum ventum est ad hæreditatem, nulla ei portio attributa est signatur, sed e domo eiicitur. Hoc docuit iam olim exemplum Ismaelis, qui quatuordecim circiter annos vixit in familia Abrahæ, quæ tum fuit Ecclesia visibilis, tanquam filius & hæres, sed se prodidit tandem cum iustum hæredem Isaacum persequutus est. Tum autem quid dicit Scriptura? Eiice ancillam & filium eius, non enim hæres erit ancillæ filius cum filio liberæ.
units.tr: {y} Matth. 7. 16. Ioan. 3. and governs everything in his master's house. But when the time comes to divide the inheritance, then he is cast out of the house, and it becomes known to all that he is and has been a slave. So it is in the house of God. A hypocrite remains in the visible Church of God like a son, enjoys the privileges of a son, and shares in the Word and the sacraments at the same time. But when the time comes for the inheritance, no portion is assigned to him, but he is cast out of the house. The example of Ishmael taught this long ago: he lived for about fourteen years in the family of Abraham, which was then the visible Church, as a son and heir; but he revealed himself at last, when he persecuted the rightful heir, Isaac. What then does Scripture say? "Cast out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman shall not be heir with the son of the free woman."

units.la: Quare cautiores debemus esse ex inspectis huiusmodi exemplis, nunquam- que contenti si exterius tantum videamur esse filij. Verum interna illa libertas filiorum semper nobis exploranda est. Multi enim in Ecclesia latent hypocritæ, qui sibiipsis ad tempus imponunt, quique tandem eiiciendi sunt in tenebras exteriores. Quare quisque excutiat animum, quæratque sibi testimonium veri filij. Sequitur deinde mirigatio huius denuntiationis, qua proponit iis modum, quo in libertatem vindicentur. Est autem, si filius eos in libertatem vindicarit. Sed priusquam ad modum descendat, conditio filij quæ sit in domo Patris sui ostendit, idque allusione facta ad conditionem filiorum terrestrium. Est autem ea, filius terrestris & hæres rei paternæ, nullo unquam tempore eiicitur e domo, sed patri succedit in familia, ac hereditate suo tempore fruitur. Ita filius Dei Iesus Christus perpetuo manet in domo Patris sui, hæreditate illa cœlesti fruitur in perpetuum, ita ut ad eam participandam, nemini pateat aditus, nisi per eum. Solus enim hæres est proprie, neque hæreditatis pars aliqua ad alium spectat, quia is solus est filius naturalis, quod si vel angeli, vel homines participes fiant hereditatis istius, id per eum continget, quia solus est hæres. Hic nota: Antequam, ut dixi, proponat modum, quo vindicadi sint isti in libertatem, quæ quidem est per filium, conditionem filij subiungit in familia Patris sui, quænam sit ea, idque in eum finem, ut
units.tr: Therefore we ought to be more cautious, taking note of examples of this kind, and never to be content if we seem to be sons only outwardly. Rather, that inward liberty of the sons must always be examined by us. For many hypocrites lie hidden in the Church, who deceive themselves for a time, and who at last must be cast out into outer darkness. Therefore let each person search his own mind, and seek for himself the testimony of a true son. Next follows the means of this warning, by which he sets before them the way in which they may be set free. It is, however, "if the Son sets you free." But before he descends to the means, he shows the condition of the son who is in his Father's house, and he does so by an allusion to the condition of earthly sons. This is it: an earthly son, the heir of his father's estate, is never cast out of the house at any time, but succeeds his father in the family and enjoys the inheritance in due time. So the Son of God, Jesus Christ, remains forever in the house of his Father, enjoys that heavenly inheritance for ever, so that no one has access to share in it except through him. For he alone is the heir in the proper sense, and no part of the inheritance belongs to another, because he alone is the natural Son; and if either angels or men become sharers in that inheritance, this will happen through him, because he alone is the heir. Here note: before, as I said, he sets forth the way by which those men are to be set free, which is indeed through the Son, he adds the condition of the son in his Father's house, what it is, and this for the purpose that

units.la: LL consideratā conditione filij credant fieri posse vt per eum liberentur. Ita faciendum nobis est perpetuò, quoties proponitur aliquod beneficium in Christo. Iam primum ipse Christus proponendus est, natura eius, & tota eius gloria: Atque ita demum fiet, vt nihil sit tam credituum difficile, quod non credant hominies futurum, si semel penitus in eum oculis fidei descenderint. Contrà autem, quod plerique non credant se per eum consequuturos tot tantaque beneficia, in causa est, quòd non videant Christum, ipsius personam atque conditionem omnem. Hæc etiam causa est cur mundus alio confugiat quàm ad eum, & in inuentis hominum quaerat sibi salutem. Hæc causa fuit cur initio Iudæi non contenti solo Christo coniungebant ieiuna illa elementa & hominum traditiones: idèoque Apostolus huc deducit Colossenses vt videant in eo esse abscondita omnes thesauros cognitionis & sapientiæ, & in eo inhabitare omnem plenitudinem deitatis corporaliter. Conditione filij proposita, ad modum liberationis descendit. Si, inquit, vos filius, &c. Hoc sequitur necessario exitio posito, filius manet in domo Dei in æternum, & accepit omnem potestatem in cœlo & in terra. Hinc sequitur quod si filius liberauerit vos, vel si visum fuerit ei vos in libertatem asserere, Vos vero liberi eritis. Vera enim libertas est per eum solum qui potest liberare; Potest autem cum maneat in domo Patris sui in æternum. Quare concludit ex conditione filij veram libertatem eorum, quos ipse liberauerit. Veram dicit, comparatione libertatis carnalis, quam illi soli intellexerunt, hanc autem capere non potuerunt, nam spiritualia quæque vere talia sunt. Panis quidem hic terrestris est, sed vere panis est ille, qui è cœlo descendit. Libertas hæc carnalis est quidem libertas, sed vera libertas est illa spiritualis: siue qualitatem eius spectes, est enim gloriosa: siue quantitatem & magnitudinem, superat enim infinitis partibus corporalem illam etiam regiam: siue denique durationem, est enim æterna, cùm ista sit momentanea.
units.tr: having considered the condition of the son, they may believe it possible that they can be set free through him. So we must always do this whenever some benefit in Christ is set forth. First of all Christ himself must be presented, his nature and his whole glory. And so at last it will come about that nothing is so hard to believe that men will not believe it possible, once they have descended with the eyes of faith fully into him. On the contrary, the reason why most people do not believe that they will obtain through him so many and so great benefits is that they do not see Christ, his person and his whole condition. This is also the reason why the world flees to anything other than him, and seeks its salvation in the inventions of men. This was the reason why at the beginning the Jews, not content with Christ alone, joined to him those weak elements and the traditions of men. Therefore the Apostle leads the Colossians to this point, that they may see that in him are hidden all the treasures of knowledge and wisdom, and that in him dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily. Having set out the condition of the son, he now descends to the manner of liberation: "If the Son," he says, "sets you free," etc. This follows necessarily from the position that the Son remains in the house of God forever, and has received all power in heaven and on earth. Hence it follows that if the Son has set you free, or if it has seemed good to him to assert you in liberty, you will indeed be free. For true liberty is only through him who alone can set free; and he can, since he remains in his Father's house forever. Therefore he concludes from the condition of the Son the true liberty of those whom he himself has set free. He calls it true in comparison with carnal liberty, which those men alone understood but could not grasp, for all spiritual things are truly such. This bread here is indeed earthly, but that bread which comes down from heaven is truly bread. This carnal liberty is indeed liberty, but that spiritual liberty is true liberty: whether you look at its quality, for it is glorious; or at its quantity and magnitude, for it surpasses by infinite degrees even that bodily royal liberty; or finally at its duration, for it is eternal, whereas the other is momentary.

units.la: Est enim, vt ait Paulus, æternum pondus excellenter excellentis gloriæ. Est gloria & ea quidem excellenter excellens, est præterea pondus excellenter excellentis gloriæ, est denique nique æternum pondus excellenter excellentis gloriæ. Sed hoc quoque attingendum, quòd dicat filium nos liberare: Liberat nos filius primùm sanguine suo, dum liberat à reatu peccati & à pœna. Estque hæc liberatio nihil aliud quàm remissio peccati. Liberat deinde Spiritu suo à reliquiis istis peccati inhærentis: Estque hæc liberatio nihil aliud quàm regeneratio siue sanctificatio corruptæ huius naturæ. Modo hoc liberationis propositο,cos ad se quidem allicit, vt in ipsum credant, etsi nõ aperte fidem ab aliis requirat: non enim dicit, Si vos credideritis in filium,&c.
units.tr: For, as Paul says, an eternal weight of glory, exceedingly excellent. It is glory, and indeed glory that is exceedingly excellent; it is moreover a weight of exceedingly excellent glory; and finally it is an eternal weight of exceedingly excellent glory. But this also must be noted, that he says the Son sets us free. The Son sets us free first by his blood, when he frees us from the guilt of sin and from its punishment, and this deliverance is nothing other than the remission of sin. Then he frees us by his Spirit from those remnants of indwelling sin, and this deliverance is nothing other than the regeneration, or sanctification, of this corrupt nature. By this promise of deliverance he indeed draws them to himself, so that they believe in him, although he does not openly demand faith from them. For he does not say, "If you believe in the Son," etc.

units.la: 37 Scio vos semen Abrahæ esse, sed studetis me interficere, quia sermo ille meus non habet locum apud vos.
units.tr: 37 I know that you are the seed of Abraham, but you seek to kill me, because my word has no place among you.

units.la: 38 Ego loquor quod vidi apud Patrem meum, & vos facitis quod vidistis apud patrem vestrum.
units.tr: 38 I speak what I have seen with my Father, and you do what you have seen with your father.

units.la: HActenus refutauit assertionem eorum, probauitque affirmantem partem, nempe seruos illos esse: Nunc ad argumenta ipsorum respondet, nominatim verò ad argumentum illud seminis Abrahæ, quòd nimirum essent eius semen ac filii: primùm cum iis agit per concessionem, sed ironicam, Scio, inquit, vos semen Abrahæ esse. Tum sequentia verba destruunt quod concessum est, sed studetis, inquit, me trucidare. Factum hoc ex diametropugnat, cum iis qui verè sunt filij Abrahæ, quos Christus maximè intelligit hoc loco. Similis huic locutio ista est, qua quis respondet ostentanti nomen Christiani, Ecclesiæ, fidei, &c. Scio quidem te talem esse, sed tamen homicida, adulter, sacrilegus es, &c. Paulus, Rom. 2. 17. & deinceps, ita egit cum Iudæis, primùm cõcedendo illos titulos, de quibus gloriati sunt, deinde corrigendo quod dictum & concessum. Proculdubio autem Deus hodierno die irridet è cœlis professionem iistorum hominum, siue Papistæ illi sint, siue hypocritæ Christiani. Causam affert cùm studeant ipsum trucidare: Quia, inquit, sermo meus, &c. Ratio est ex eo quòd denegent locum sermoni ipsius ac veritati. Ergo deducit ejus ad fundamentum odij aduersus personam ipsius concepti, nempe odium veritatis, quam ipse prædicabat & gestabat coram mundo. Persequutio omnis ministrorum verbi certum habet fundamentum veritatis illius quam ipsi prædicant, odium. Quicquid prætexant demum isti, siue Papistæ, siue hypocritæ Christiani, omnes denique qui vel ludibrio habent, vel persequuntur aliquo modo Dei seruos, omnes, inquam, citra exceptionem, oderunt veritatem eam quam ipsi profitentur. Paulus petit vt pij precentur pro ipso, vt eripiatur à proteruis & scelveratis hominibus, non enim, inquit, omnium est fides. q.d. Non enim omnes amplectuntur veritatem Christi: Ideóq; me, qui veritatis illius præconem, intereptû cuperent. Ego loquor quod vidi. Obiici potuit; Atquis ille sermo tuus, quę nos ampleƈti oportet? Respondet, ac eos ad ipsius fontē deducit, nempe Patrē, quóque magis conspiciatur sermonis illius dignitas, ex-plicat comparatione factorū ipsorum; q.d. Non est ille quidē similis factis vestris, quorum origo est diabolus. Sed videnda sunt singillatim verba. Duo sunt quæ competunt in Christum, eo quod in summa Patris sit ab æterno: hoc est, modo plane admirabili coniunctus cum Patre, in vna eademque essentia. Primum est quod videat ipsum Patrem, ac solus videat proprie & per se: Nō quòd patrem viderit quisquam, nisi is qui est à Deo, hic vidit Patrem Iohan. 6. 46. Creaturæ eum vident, sed in imagine Filij. Deinde videat quæcunque in Patre sunt arcana ac mysteria, ac socius est consiliorum eius omnium ab æterno: videat denique omnia eius opera, Pater diligit Filium ac demonstrat ei quæ facit omnia, &c. Iohan. 5. 20. Ab hac proprietate Filius dicitur Patris sapientia, quod omnia Patris sapiat ac cognoscat accuratè; id quod sonat verbum quod est apud Danielem 8. 13. Vbi angelus eum מלמד appellat. Tum est alterum quod in Filium cupetit, nepe quòd cum videat omnia, quo vult tempore, quibus vult creaturis, qua vult mensura eloquatur ea. Ab hac proprietate dicitur λόγος sermo. & apud Danielé c. 8. 13. codé sensu המדבר. Vtrumque hoc positū est isto loco, vbi dicit, Ego loquor quod vidi apud Patrem meum. Nā videt hic Filius pariter & loquitur. Sed loquitur quod videt apud Patrem. Hic Patre facit authorē sermosermonum suorum. Filiis diaboli idem ascribit in hac comparatione: nam & ipsi quoque faciunt quod viderunt apud Patrem suum, quod vel ex eo apparet quod facta eius imitentur omnes. Vident itaque eū quodammodo præcū- te ipsis exemplo suo: verbi gratia, homicidæ videntur eum quodammodo priorem homicidium perpetrantē, & exē- plum eius sunt secuti. Imò hic est plus quiddam quàm nudus aspectus, sentiunt enim cum penitus in corde a- gentem & eos agitantem. Ideòque Apostolus spiritus meminit qui agit in filiis infidelitatis: & dicit adductum Deum. Antichristi fore ex efficacia Satanæ. Nota hoc loco: dū- bitantes de verbo suo Christus ad ipsius authorem de- ducit, simulque ad factorum suorum Patrem, ut nimi- rum commonstratis his quasi fontibus lubentius am- plecterentur ipsius sermonem, ut qui Deum authorem habeat: & à malefactis abstinerent, ut quæ diabolum au- thorem habeant. Pessimi quique deducēdi sunt ad ipsos fontes bonorum & malorum, admonendiqué sunt Deum authorem esse eius quod ipsi tamen oderunt, & è con- tra diabolum authorem esse eius quod tamen ipsi amat tantopere, ut audito Dei nomine alliciantur ad hoc, ut si fieri possit amplectantur id quod bonum est Deóque gra- tum: contra vero, diaboli nomine audito, deterreantur à facinoribus suis. Nemo enim omnium est qui se prosi- teatur diabolum sequi velle. Præsertim autem ita cum hypocritis agendum est, commonstrandúsque est iis ipsorum Pater, cùm illi pessima quæque facta sua, Dei, religionis, Christi denique ac fidei nominibus atque ti- tulis, tanquam fuco quodam obducto, colorent. Quam- obrem detrahenda hæc larua, ut diabolum authorē esse eorum appareat.
units.tr: Hitherto he has refuted their assertion and proved the affirmative part, namely that they are slaves. Now he answers their arguments, and in particular that argument about the seed of Abraham, that they are his seed and children. First he deals with them by way of concession, but an ironical one: "I know," he says, "that you are the seed of Abraham." Then the following words overturn what was conceded: "but you seek," he says, "to slay me." This fights directly against those who are truly the children of Abraham, whom Christ chiefly has in view here. A similar way of speaking is this, by which someone answers a man who boasts of the name of Christian, of the Church, of the faith, etc.: "I know indeed that you are such a one, but nevertheless you are a murderer, an adulterer, a sacrilegious man," etc. Paul, Rom. 2.17 and following, dealt in this way with the Jews: first by conceding the titles in which they gloried, and then by correcting what was said and conceded. Without doubt God today mocks from heaven the profession of those men, whether they be Papists or hypocritical Christians. He gives the reason when they seek to slay him: "because," he says, "my word," etc. The reason is that they deny his word and the truth a place. Therefore he traces this back to the foundation of the hatred conceived against his person, namely hatred of the truth, which he himself preached and bore before the world. Every persecution of the ministers of the Word has as its certain foundation hatred of that truth which they preach. Whatever pretexts these men put forward, whether Papists or hypocritical Christians, in short all who in any way mock or persecute God's servants, all of them, I say, without exception, hate the truth that they themselves profess. Paul asks that the godly pray for him, that he may be rescued from unreasonable and wicked men: "for not all," he says, "have faith." That is, "For not all embrace the truth of Christ; therefore they wish to seize me, who am the herald of that truth." "I speak what I have seen." It could be objected: "But what is that word of yours which we ought to embrace?" He answers, and leads them back to its source, namely the Father; and so that the dignity of his word may be seen more clearly, he explains it by comparison with their deeds, as if to say: "It is not like your deeds, whose origin is the devil." But the words must be considered one by one. There are two things that belong to Christ, because he is in the bosom of the Father from eternity, that is, joined with the Father in a manner altogether wonderful, in one and the same essence. The first is that he sees the Father himself, and alone sees him properly and of himself. "Not that anyone has seen the Father, except he who is from God; he has seen the Father" (John 6.46). Creatures see him, but in the image of the Son. Second, he sees all the hidden things and mysteries that are in the Father, and from eternity he is the partner of all his counsels; finally he sees all his works: "The Father loves the Son and shows him all the things that he does," etc. (John 5.20). From this property the Son is called the wisdom of the Father, because he accurately knows and understands all the things of the Father; this is what the word in Daniel 8.13 means, where the angel calls him מלמד [melammed, teacher]. Then there is the other thing that is ascribed to the Son, namely that, since he sees all things, he speaks them at what time he wills, to what creatures he wills, and in what measure he wills. From this property he is called λόγος [logos], word, and in Daniel 8.13 with the same sense המדבר [hammedabbēr, the speaker]. Both of these are set forth in this passage, where he says, "I speak what I have seen with my Father." For the Son here both sees and speaks equally, but speaks what he sees with the Father. Here he makes the Father the author of his words. In this comparison he ascribes the same to the children of the devil: for they too do what they have seen with their father, as appears from the fact that all imitate his deeds. Thus they see him in a certain way going before them by his example; for instance, murderers seem in a way to see him committing murder first, and they have followed his example. Indeed there is something more here than bare sight, for they feel him acting and driving them in the depths of the heart. Therefore the Apostle makes mention of the spirit who works in the sons of unbelief, and says that God has allowed the coming of Antichrist to be by the efficacy of Satan. Note here: Christ, when they doubt his word, traces it back to its author, and at the same time to the Father of their deeds, so that, having these as it were springs displayed, they might more willingly embrace his word, as having God for its author, and abstain from evil deeds, as having the devil for their author. The worst men are to be led back to the very springs of good and evil, and they are to be warned that God is the author of what they nevertheless hate, and on the contrary that the devil is the author of what they nevertheless love so greatly that, when the name of God is heard, they are drawn to embrace, if it were possible, what is good and pleasing to God; but on the contrary, when the name of the devil is heard, they are deterred from their wicked deeds. For there is no one at all who professes that he wishes to follow the devil. Especially, however, must one deal in this way with hypocrites, and their Father must be shown to them, since they colour all their most wicked deeds with the names and titles of God, religion, Christ and finally faith, as if with some dye spread over them. Therefore this mask must be torn away, so that it may appear that the devil is their author.

units.la: 39 Responderunt & dixerunt ei, Pater noster Abrahamus est. Dicit eis Iesus, Si filij Abrahami essetis, opera Abrahami faceretis.
units.tr: 39 They answered and said to him, Abraham is our father. Jesus says to them, If you were children of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham.

units.la: 40 Nunc autem quaeritis me trucidare, hominem qui veritatem vobis locutus sum, quam audivi à Deo: hoc Abrahamus non fecit.
units.tr: 40 But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth, which I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.

units.la: 41 Vos facitis opera Patris vestri. Itaque dixerunt ei, Nos excscortatione non sumus geniti, unum patrem habemus, nempe Deum.
units.tr: 41 You do the works of your father. So they said to him, We were not born of fornication; we have one father, namely God.

units.la: Nihil de factis suis loquuntur, quae tamen dixit a diabolo patre esse: ea non defendunt, sed praetextu illum nominis Abrahami retinent mordicus. Hoc ingenium est hypocritarum, cum facta sua ipsis exprobrantur, praetereunt ea silentio, perpetuo autem ad nomina & titulos confugiunt, & laruam illam qua se induunt, & praeclara quaeque nomina pro viribus retinent. Nam usque adeo sunt excaecati, ut vel sola haec nomina, caeremonias, caeteraque id genus externa, meritoria esse putent. De vera fide in Christum, de operibus illius fidei testimoniis, nihil interea solliciti. Si filij Abrahami.
units.tr: They say nothing about their own deeds, although he has said that they are from the devil their father; they do not defend these, but cling stubbornly to the pretext of the name of Abraham. This is the habit of hypocrites: when their deeds are thrown in their faces, they pass them over in silence, and always take refuge in names and titles, and hold on as best they can to that mask they put on and to every splendid name. For they are so blinded that they think these names alone, ceremonies and the other things of that kind, which are external, are meritorious. Meanwhile they are not at all concerned about true faith in Christ, or about the works that witness to that faith. "If you are children of Abraham..."

units.la: Christus respondet ad illum praetextum nominis Abrahami, eumque iis detrahere conatur hoc argumento, ab operibus eorum sumpto. Si filij Abrahami essetis, opera Abrahami faceretis. At non facitis opera Abrahami: Ergo &c. Assumptionem probat: Studetis inquiens, me interficere. Ne autem existimarent illud leve esse at nullius ponderis, addit se hominem esse qui veritatem ipsis loquutus, hoc est hominem veracem, ac propterea bene de iis meritum: ut qui veritatem quam audierat a Patre annuntiarit. Tum assumit, At Abraham nihil huiusmodi fecit: hinc sequitur, Ergo non facitis opera Abrahae. Sed pro eo habet aequipollens, Vos facitis opera Patris vestri.
units.tr: Christ answers the pretext of Abraham's name and tries to strip it from them with this argument, drawn from their works: "If you were the children of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham. But you do not do the works of Abraham; therefore..." He proves the minor premise: "You seek," he says, "to kill me." Lest they think this a slight matter of no weight, he adds that he is a man who has told them the truth, that is, a truthful man who has therefore deserved well of them, since he has announced the truth he heard from the Father. Then he assumes: "But Abraham did nothing of the kind; hence it follows, therefore you do not do the works of Abraham." Instead of this he puts an equivalent: "You do the works of your father."

units.la: Nota, Christus dum conatur iis detrahere laruam illam nominis Abrahami, obiicit sua ipsorum opera, quae cum operibus Abrahae comparat, ad hoc ut ex operibus ipsorum eos convincat: sic faciendum hodierno die cum hypocritis. Gloriatur illi quidem in his externis, in nomine hominis Christiani, fidei, Evangelii: quare nihil promoueris si his nominibus agas cum iis: concedenda sunt ista omnia, idque Christus fecit supra: itc Paulus, Rom. 2. Verum externa ista oppugnanda sunt per opera, tanquam totidem testimonia hominis vere Christiani, veraeque fidei, & ex operibus convincendi sunt. Nam haec sola restat agendi cum hypocritis ratio; quam etiam sequetur ipse Deus in iudicio illo novissimo: nam mundum ex operibus iudicabit. Proculdubio hoc futurum est propter pter hominum hypocrisin, qui de externis his plus satis gloriari solent. Notandum vero hoc est, quod dum ostendit opera ipsorum no esse Abrahae operibus similia, non contentus sit, ea ipsorum opera in genere nominare, verum ad speciem descendat, specialeque homicidij malum in medium proferat: ita nobis agendum cum hypocritis nostri temporis, in medium afferenda sunt particularia eorum facta. Verbi gratia, hoc homicidium, hoc tempore perpetratum, illud adulterium, &c. Hoc, inquam, faciendum est Christi exemplo, cum ad conuictionem conscientiae plurimum valeat. Est enim conscientia certorum quorundam & peculiarium facinorum, non autem factorum in genere. Itaque dixerunt ei. Nihil adhuc ad opera obiecta respondent: verum illud arcte tenent se ex Abrahamo, adeoque Deo ipso esse, ac pro absurdo habent, & conuitij loco ducunt quod negeret eos ex Abrahamo esse. At enim, inquiunt, ex fornicatione nati essemus, si, quod dicis, Abraha non esset Pater noster, sed alios haberemus Patres: de terrenis parentibus, non spiritualibus, sine dubio loquuntur. Nam Abrahamum tanquam terrenum Patre obiiciunt toto hoc loco, gloriantur-que quod ex eo carnaliter sint oriundi. Idenim satis esse putabant ad religionem, pietatem, ad haec ut essent filij Dei, ad vitam aeternam assequendam, denique ad omnia. Ergo ita ratiocinantur: Abraham non esset Pater, si ex fornicatione geniti essemus. At non sumus nati ex fornicatione. Quare Abraham est Pater. Verum altius aspirant sibique arrogat titulum magis gloriosum: Vnum, inquiunt, Patrem habemus, nempe Deum ipsum. Nam, ut dixi, satis esse putabant, ad hoc ut filij Dei & essent & dicerentur, si Abrahae carnales filij essent. Id apparet ex Rom. 9. 8. quo etiam loco contrarium docet Apostolus, Non, inquit, qui filij carnis, ij filij Dei, sed qui sunt filij promissionis censentur in semine. Obserua hoc loco non nisi aegerrime agnoscere hypocritas sua mala opera, neque tamen cum obiiciuntur ad ea respondere: sed perpetuo ad titulos suos & gloriosa nomina transfugere. Atque etiam altiora quaeque sibi arrogare: interea autem queri de iniuria, si forte negentur iis de quibus ipsi glorientur. V. g. Si negetur ipsos vere Christianos esse, in numero verò fidelium esse, &c. Hoc verò non est hic prætereundum quod non defendant illum suum aduersus Christum conatū: ex quo apparet conuictos eos fuisse apud conscientias suas, quòd malus fuerit ac peruersus ipsorum aduersus Dominū conatus. Obserua igitur, licet velint videri hypocritæ nihil attendere ad opera obiecta; tamē conuincuntur conscientiæ eorum sæpenumerò quòd inala sint, etiam interea dum gloriantur de titulis ac nominibus suis rebusque externis. Sed quid ad hæc Christus?
units.tr: Note that when Christ tries to strip away the mask of Abraham's name, he sets against them their own works and compares them with the works of Abraham, so that he may convict them by their works. This is how we must deal with hypocrites today. They boast indeed of these outward things, of the name of Christian, of faith, of the Gospel; so you will achieve nothing if you argue with them by these names. All these must be conceded, and Christ did this above, as did Paul in Romans 2. But these outward things must be assailed by works, as so many proofs of a truly Christian man and true faith, and they must be convicted by their works. For this is the only way left of dealing with hypocrites, and God himself will follow it at that last judgment, for he will judge the world by works. This will undoubtedly happen because of the hypocrisy of men, who are wont to boast more than enough of these outward things. It must be noted, however, that when he shows that their works are not like the works of Abraham, he is not content to name their works in general, but descends to the particular and brings forward the specific evil of murder. So we must deal with the hypocrites of our own time: their particular deeds must be brought forward. For example, this murder committed in this time, that adultery, and so on. I say this must be done after Christ's example, since it greatly helps to convict the conscience. For conscience is of certain and particular deeds, not of deeds in general. And so they said to him. They make no reply yet to the works objected, but hold firmly to the claim that they are from Abraham, and so from God himself; they count it absurd, and take it as an insult, that he should deny they are of Abraham. "Indeed," they say, "we would be born of fornication if, as you say, Abraham were not our father, but we had other fathers." They are undoubtedly speaking of earthly parents, not spiritual ones. For they object to Abraham as their earthly father throughout this passage, and they boast that they are carnally descended from him. For they thought this enough for religion and piety, for being the sons of God, for attaining eternal life, and in short for everything. So they reason thus: "Abraham would not be our father if we had been born of fornication. But we are not born of fornication. Therefore Abraham is our father." But they aspire higher and claim for themselves a more glorious title: "We have one Father," they say, "namely God himself." For, as I said, they thought it enough, in order both to be and to be called sons of God, that they were the fleshly sons of Abraham. This appears from Romans 9:8, where the Apostle teaches the contrary: "It is not the children of the flesh," he says, "who are the children of God, but those who are the children of the promise are counted as the seed." Observe here that hypocrites acknowledge their evil works only with the greatest reluctance, and even when they are objected to, they do not answer them, but always flee to their titles and glorious names. They even claim for themselves the loftiest things, and meanwhile complain of injury if they are denied the things in which they glory: for example, if it is denied that they are truly Christians, or are among the number of the faithful, and so on. Nor should it be passed over here that they do not defend that attempt of theirs against Christ, from which it appears that they were convicted in their consciences that their attempt against the Lord was evil and perverse. Observe, therefore, that although hypocrites want to seem to pay no attention to the works objected, yet their consciences are very often convicted that these are evil, even while they boast of their titles and names and outward things. But what does Christ say to this?

units.la: 42 Dixit ergo iis Iesus, Si Deus Pater vester esset, diligeretis me: ego enim à Deo prodij & adsum, nec enim à me ipso veni, sed ille me misit.
units.tr: 42 Jesus therefore said to them: "If God were your Father, you would love me; for I came forth from God and am here; for I did not come of myself, but he sent me."

units.la: 43 Quare loquutionem istam meam non agnoscitis? nempe quoniam non potestis audire sermonem meum.
units.tr: 43 "Why do you not understand my speech? Because you cannot hear my word."

units.la: 44 Vos ex patre diabolo estis, & cupiditates patris vestri vultis explere. Ille fuit homicida à principio, & in veritate non perstitit: non est enim veritas in eo. Quotiescunque loquitur mendacium, de suo loquitur, quia mendax est, & pater ille mendacij.
units.tr: 44 "You are of your father the devil, and you want to fulfil the lusts of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning, and did not stand in the truth, for there is no truth in him. Whenever he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own, because he is a liar and the father of lies."

units.la: ET hanc quoque Dei ipsius laruam quam obtendunt, Eiis detrahere conatur etiam argumento ab operibus & moribus eorum. Nam vrget perpetuò moralem legē. Si Deus Pater vester esset, diligeretis me. Si autem ab iis fortè obiiceretur: At cur te diligeremus? Respondet, Ego enim à Deo prodij & adsum. Hoc non de generatione, sed de missione Filij accipiendū, vt verba sequentia docent. Nec enim: Ratio est & explicatio superiorum verborum. At hæc sunt quæ respondet Christus. Ex quo nota, Querantur licet & tumpantur hypocritæ, tamen resistendum perpetuò, & detrahenda iis larua est, obiectis continuò malis ipsorum operibus, dicendumque cum Iacobo, Ostende mihi fidem ex operibus tuis. Notandum verò & loco isto & superiori, quo dictum est, studetis me interficere, hominem qui veritatem vobis loquutus sum, sup. vers. 40. His locis non obiicit simpliciter quòd ipsum studeant interficere,
units.tr: This mask of God himself, which they put forward, he also tries to strip from them, by an argument drawn from their works and conduct. For he presses the moral law continually: "If God were your Father, you would love me." But if they should perhaps object, "But why should we love you?", he answers, "For I came forth from God and am here." This is to be taken not of generation but of the mission of the Son, as the following words show: "For I did not come of myself." This is the reason and explanation of the preceding words, and it is what Christ answers. From this note: however much hypocrites complain and swell with pride, we must nonetheless resist them continually, and their mask must be stripped away by continually objecting their evil works, and we must say with James: "Show me your faith by your works." It must also be noted, both in this place and in the earlier one where it was said, "You seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth" (above, verse 40), that in these places he does not object simply that they seek to kill him,

units.la: Ad instantiam Iudaeorum, se Dei filios dicentium, Christi respondet.
units.tr: Christ answers the Jews who say that they are the sons of God.

units.la: Iacob. 2. 18. cere,& quòd ipsum non diligant, sed quòd se talem, vt-pote à Deo missum,cum sermone veritatis, studeant interficere,ac talem non diligant: quod quidem longè gratius est, quàm si simpliciter, vt hominem,velex vulgo aliquem studerent interficere. Graue enim est hominem occidere, sed hominem à Deo missum interficere grauius.
units.tr: James 2:18. but that they seek to kill him as one sent by God with the word of truth, and that they do not love such a one. This is far more grievous than if they had simply sought to kill him as a man, or as some common person. For it is grave to kill a man, but to kill a man sent by God is graver.

units.la: Ergo ita exaggeratum est eorū factum. Hypocritis no-stri temporis idé plane obiiciendum; Odistis homines à Deo missos, contumeliosi estis ac iniurij in eos qui ve-ritatem sunt loquuti. Hoc ad aggrauandum eorum sa-čta pertinet, ne putent sibi rem esse cum hominibus sim-pliciter, dum in Ministros verbi sic & blasphemi & iniurij sunt. Sed pergant,si velint:sentient demū non fuisse sibi rem cum personis hominum tantùm,sed cum legatis Dei quem ipsi tam turpiter violârunt. Quare loquutionem. Manent adhuc ignari eorum quæ loquutus est Dominus,ideóque vrget eius rei causam:q.d.Quę causa est curme loquentem non intelligatis magis, quàm si ignota aliqua lingua vos alloquerer? Tum ipse respon-sionem subiicit:Quia non potestis. Causa est contumacia & malicia,qua non sustinuerunt eum loquentem audire, vt & ipsi dixerunt,Quis potest ipsum audire? sup.cap.6.60.Quare videmus hic ignorantiam cum aliqua malicia semper coniunctam.Neque enim ignorantia est aliqua tam simplex, quin aliquā contumaciam habeat coniunctam.
units.tr: So their deed is thus magnified. The very same must be objected to the hypocrites of our time: you hate men sent by God, you are insolent and unjust towards those who have spoken the truth. This pertains to aggravating their sin, so that they may not think they have to do merely with men. For in being so blasphemous and unjust towards the ministers of the Word, they are dealing with men. But let them go on if they wish: they will at last feel that they have had to do not merely with the persons of men, but with the envoys of God, whom they have so shamefully violated. "Why do you not understand my speech?" The disciples remain ignorant of what the Lord has said, and so he presses the cause of this matter, as if to say: What is the reason that you do not understand me, speaking more than if I were addressing you in some unknown tongue? Then he himself adds the answer: "Because you cannot." The cause is their obstinacy and malice, by which they did not endure to hear him speaking, as they themselves said: "Who can hear him?" (above, ch. 6, verse 60). Hence we see here ignorance always joined with some malice. For no ignorance is so simple that it does not have some obstinacy joined with it.

units.la: Ignorantiam Gentium aliquis fortasse excusaret, vt simplicem ininimèque malitiosam, vt quibus nihil de Deo in Christo prædicatum & annuntiatum vnquam fuerit. At Paulus ignorantiam gentiū tribuit induratione cordis ipsarum. Propter ignorantiam ,inquit,quæ est in ipsis,ex obduratione cordis eorum.Item,Rom.1.28.Præsertim autem ignorantia eorum,qui clarâ lucem intuentur, eneumax est,cuiusmodi est Papistarum, qui vsque adeo obstinati manent hodierno die, & veritatem tam acriter oppugnant. Cuiusmodi etiam est nostrorū homi-num,qui puritatem Euangelij nobiscum profitentur, nihil tamen intelligunt, semper discunt,nihil proficiunt. Quamobrem exemplo Christi hoc loco vrgendi sunt omnes isti & eò pertrahendi, vt causam ignorantiæ suæ, contumaciam suam & cordis obstinationē ipsi sentiant,
units.tr: Someone might perhaps excuse the ignorance of the Gentiles as simple and not at all malicious, since nothing about God in Christ was ever preached or announced to them. But Paul ascribes the ignorance of the Gentiles to the hardening of their hearts: "Because of the ignorance that is in them, from the hardness of their heart" (Eph. 4.18); likewise Rom. 1.28. Yet the ignorance of those who gaze upon the clear light is especially inexcusable, such as that of the Papists, who remain so obstinate to this very day and oppose the truth so fiercely. Such also is that of some of our own people, who profess the purity of the Gospel along with us, yet understand nothing, are always learning and never make progress. Therefore, following Christ's example, all such people must be urged at this point and drawn on until they feel for themselves the cause of their ignorance, their stubbornness and the obstinacy of their heart,

units.la: Eph. 4.18. & fel illud amaritudinis quod in corde penitus latet quasi degustent, vt si fieri possit vitam suá emendent atque corrigant.
units.tr: Eph. 4.18. and taste, as it were, the gall of bitterness that lies hidden deep in the heart, so that, if it can be done, they may amend and correct their lives.

units.la: Vos ex Patre. Ex contumacia illa colligit veram originem generis eorum; illi gloriati sunt de Abrahamo Patre: at Dominus diabolum patrem esse colligit, atque subiratus; vt discamus, cōtumacia illa atque obstinatio ne maximè commoueri ad iram Dominum. Pij quique inter argumentādum & conferendum sermones de veritate cū obstinatis, non possunt æquo animo ferre contumaciam istam eorū, qui veritatem etiam agnitam tā impudenter oppugnant. Ex contumacia igitur & impatientia audiendi infert eos ex diabolo patre esse, & id quidem merito. Nam contumacia & obstinatio cordis
units.tr: You are of your father. From that stubbornness he infers the true origin of their kind. They boasted of Abraham as their father, but the Lord concludes that the devil is their father, and he does so in anger, so that we may learn that the Lord is deeply moved to wrath by such stubbornness and obstinacy. All pious people, when arguing and conferring with obstinate men about the truth, cannot bear with equanimity the stubbornness of those who so shamelessly oppose even the truth they have acknowledged. Therefore, from their stubbornness and their impatience in hearing, he infers that they are of the devil as their father, and rightly so. For stubbornness and obstinacy of heart

units.la: ex efficacia Satanæ est. Quòd si Euangelium nostrum, (inquit Paulus) tectum est, in quibus Deus huius sæculi excæcauit mentes, &c. Addo præterea efficaciam Satanæ in eo sitam esse imprimis, vt excæcet atque obduret aduersus veritatem hominum corda: nam obduratis semel aduersus veritatem hominum animis, facilè consequitur quodcunque vult malum, vt homicidia, vt scortationes, & id genus alia. Ideoque Paulus dicit adventum Antichristi, qui obcæcaturus est mundum. fore ex efficacia Satanæ. Et Elymam magum, hominem aduersus veritatem obsirmatum, vocat filium diaboli. Et excæcationem tribuit Deo huius sæculi. Ex quibus locis apparet hoc esse primum & præcipuum effectum Satanæ in hominibus, vt ipsos obduret obsirmétque aduersus Dei veritatem. Et cupiditates. Persistit in proxima complexione, & argumento generaliori, sumpto ab eorum plena persectaque obedientia diabolo præstita, confirmat eos filios esse ipsius, quasi in hunc modum argumentetur: Eius estis filij cuius cupiditates vultis explere: at diaboli cupiditates vultis explere: Ergo &c. Propositio manifesta est, nam natura quærunt omnes parentum voluntate perficere, iisque ante omnia placere. In assumptione intelligendum quid sit illud, facere cupiditates diaboli, tū velle eas facere: nam ista differunt. Facere igitur cupiditates diaboli non est parere illi simpliciter, & facere quæ ipse vult, eo interea quasi eminus inspectante. Verū est
units.tr: come from the efficacy of Satan. But if our gospel is hidden, (says Paul), it is hidden among those in whom the god of this world has blinded the minds, etc. I add further that the efficacy of Satan lies chiefly in this, that he blinds and hardens human hearts against the truth. For once human minds are hardened against the truth, whatever evil he wishes readily follows, such as murders, fornications and other things of that kind. Therefore Paul also says that the coming of Antichrist, who is about to blind the world, will be from the efficacy of Satan. And he calls Elymas the magician, a man hardened against the truth, a son of the devil. And he attributes the blinding to the god of this world. From these passages it appears that this is the first and chief effect of Satan in men: that he hardens them and makes them obstinate against the truth of God. And the desires. He persists in the closer connection and in a more general argument, drawn from their full and complete obedience rendered to the devil, and confirms that they are his sons, reasoning in this way: You are the sons of him whose desires you wish to fulfil; but you wish to fulfil the desires of the devil; therefore etc. The major premise is plain, for by nature all seek to carry out the will of their parents and above all to please them. In the minor premise one must understand what it means to do the desires of the devil, namely to wish to do them, for these differ. To do the desires of the devil, then, is not simply to obey him and do what he wants while he watches from a distance. Rather it is

units.la: Cupiditates Satanæ quomodo impii explere discuntur. est ipso impulsore & efficaciter agente in cordibus facere, quod ipse vult. Non secus atque facere voluntatem Dei est ductu spiritus Dei ea facere. Atque haec est pars miseriae nostrae, & poenae quae insecuta est in hac vita lapsum primorum parentum, nempe spiritualis illa servitus Satanae, quam nunquam in hac vita plane exuent etiam regeniti. Faciunt enim malum & cupiditatem diaboli: verum, vt ait Apostolus, nolentes faciunt. Hoc est, non plane assentientes libidini eius, nempe ea parte voluntatis, quae regenita est. At vero reprobi & non renati faciunt malum & volentes faciunt, vt hic loquitur, id est tota voluntate, totoque impetu. Nihil enim est in iis quod malo resistat. Idcoque hi demum sunt qui proprie dicuntur filij, vel potius servi diaboli. Nota igitur, a contumacia speciali, nimirum malo quo arguit eos diaboli filios, pergit ad vniuersum malum & ad omne genus iniustitiae, inde etiam arguens eos esse diaboli filios: quo significat eos qui semel obdurati sunt plane, in omni re addictos esse libidini Satanae, & in omnibus facere voluntatem eius.
units.tr: How the wicked are taught to fulfil the desires of Satan. It is to do what he wants with him as the instigator, effectively working in their hearts. Just as to do the will of God is to do those things under the guidance of the Spirit of God. And this is part of our misery, and of the punishment that followed the fall of our first parents in this life: namely that spiritual slavery to Satan, which even the regenerate never fully cast off in this life. For they do the evil and the desire of the devil, yet, as the Apostle says, they do it unwillingly. That is, not fully assenting to his lust, namely by that part of the will which is regenerate. But the reprobate and the unregenerate do evil and do it willingly, as he puts it here, that is, with their whole will and whole impulse. For there is nothing in them that resists evil. Hence these are the ones who are properly called sons, or rather slaves, of the devil. Note, then, that from stubbornness, specifically the evil by which he proves them to be sons of the devil, he goes on to all evil and every kind of injustice, thereby also proving them to be sons of the devil. By this he signifies that those who have once been fully hardened are given over entirely to the lust of Satan, and in all things do his will.

units.la: Ille fuit homicida. Quo demonstret illud generale, summit sibi duo particularia mala, in quibus faciunt quod concupiscit diabolus, homicidium & infidelitatem. Primum itaque occurrit homicidium. Ab initio. Hoc dictum est, non respectu ipsius Satanae, sed hominis: q.d. in prima statim creatione hominis, antequam propagaretur, ipsum interfecit tam corpore quam anima: effecit vt incurreret poenam illam mortis vtriusque. Nota ad demonstrandum generale sumpsit sibi hoc particulare potissimum & primum, quod vt Satan erat homicida in initio, ita & illi. Ex quo apparet imaginem diaboli vel maxime positam esse in homicidio, & homicidam qui delectatur sanguinis effusione diabolum patrem maximè referre, eique servum esse addictissimum. Viderint hoc homicidae isti quibus abundat haec nostra natio hodierno die. Neque perstitit in veritate. Hoc est alterum particulare, infidelitas: nam ita interpretor haec verba, idque adductus apodosi & applicatione quae est sequenti versu. Ergo non perstitit in veritate, neque perstitit in fide in veritatem: sed infidelis & perfidus euasit. verba clare indicant eum stetisse aliquando in veritate,sed non per-stitisse, id quod Iudas in Epistola sua aperte loquitur, nam dicit diabolos non seruasse originem suam vers.6.
units.tr: He was a murderer. By this he shows the general point. He takes two particular evils in which they do what the devil desires: murder and unbelief. First, murder presents itself. From the beginning. This was said not with respect to Satan himself but to man: that is, in the very first creation of man, before the human race was propagated, he killed him both in body and in soul, bringing it about that he incurred that penalty of death of both kinds. Note that to demonstrate the general, he took to himself this particular, chiefly and first, namely that just as Satan was a murderer from the beginning, so are they. From this it appears that the image of the devil is especially placed in murder, and that a murderer who delights in the shedding of blood very closely resembles the father devil, and is most thoroughly devoted to him as his servant. Let those murderers, of whom this nation of ours abounds today, see to it. Nor did he stand in the truth. This is the second particular, unbelief, for I interpret these words so, and I am led to this by the apodosis and the application that follows in the next verse. Therefore he did not persist in the truth, nor did he persist in faith in the truth, but became unbelieving and treacherous. The words clearly indicate that he once stood in the truth but did not persist in it, which Jude plainly says in his Epistle, for he says the devils did not keep their own origin (v. 6).

units.la: Atque ita refellitur hæresis Manichæorum de duobus principiis Deo & diabolo. Vt autem disputationem hanc paulò altius exordiar: Angeli initio creati erant boni, sed nõ immutabiles (hoc enim solius Dei proprium est immutabilem esse) Verum mutabiles, & variis motibus, pro variis obiectis sese offerentibus, obnoxij, mutabiles etiam in deterius. Itaque in ipso lapsus eorum momento Deo eos non sustentante, neque noua gratia confirmante, (neque enim cuiquam debet aliquid, & iusta causa suberat, vt nimirum locus esset prædestinationi ipsius) Deo, inquam, eos non confirmante, lapsi sunt. Quis autem fuerit aut qualis angelorum lapsus nos non curiosius indagabimus. Hic Iohannes eum vocat defectorem à fide & veritate in infidelitatem & perfidiam. Iudas Apostolus dicit eos reliquisse domicilium suum, hoc est, stationem, vt videtur, ipsis designatam, ad hoc vt Deo ministrarent. Sed in hoc non inquiro equidem curiosius: certum enim id est, post primum lapsum insequutam horrendam corruptionem naturæ ipsorum, imprimis autem maliciam (nam hæc ipsis qualitatem maximè inculcat scriptura, hinc etiam nomen diaboli est sumptum, Satanásque, siue diabolus, dictus est) maliciam, inquam, in Deum, & propter Deum in homines. Atque hæc fuit prima lapsus eorum pœna, inde detrusos esse in inferos, ibíque reseruatos in vinculis caliginis ad plenam damnationem testes sunt Petrus & Iudas. Sed hæc mittamus. Videamus secundum Particulare, infidelitatem in Deum eiusque veritatem. Nota igitur in quibus sica fit natura diaboli maximè, nempe in homicidio & malicia in homine, & malicia in Deum ipsiúsque veritatem. Quare in quibus hæc duo maxima mala reperiuntur, illi maximè referunt diabolum, & ad imaginem ipsius factus sunt, adeo vt non opus sit aliam quærere imaginem diaboli, quàm infidelem & homicidam hominem. Hæc autem duo coniungo: nam qui homicida est, cuiusmodi sunt ex nostris quamplurimi, illi quoque infideles sunt, & hostes veritatis Dei, quicquid
units.tr: And so the heresy of the Manichaeans concerning two principles, God and the devil, is refuted. But to begin this disputation somewhat more deeply: the angels were created good at the beginning, but not immutable (for to be immutable is proper to God alone), rather mutable, and subject to various movements according to the various objects presenting themselves, and mutable even for the worse. Thus at the very moment of their fall, God not sustaining them and not confirming them by new grace (for he owed nothing to anyone, and there was a just cause, namely that there might be room for his predestination), God, I say, not confirming them, they fell. Who the angels' fall was, or what kind of fall it was, we will not inquire into too curiously. Here John calls him a deserter from faith and truth into unbelief and treachery. Jude the Apostle says they left their dwelling, that is, their station, as it seems, assigned to them so that they might minister to God. But I do not inquire into this too curiously, for this is certain: after the first fall there followed a horrible corruption of their nature, and above all malice (for Scripture especially impresses this quality on them; hence the name devil is also taken, and he is called Satan or devil), malice, I say, against God and, on account of God, against men. And this was the first punishment of their fall: that they were thrust down into hell and kept there in chains of darkness for full damnation, as Peter and Jude witness. But let us set these aside. Let us see the second particular, unbelief towards God and his truth. Note, then, in what things the nature of the devil is most of all made manifest: namely in murder and malice against man, and in malice against God and his truth. Therefore those in whom these two greatest evils are found most resemble the devil and are made in his image, so that there is no need to seek another image of the devil than an unbelieving and murderous man. I join these two, for whoever is a murderer, as very many of ours are, is also unbelieving and an enemy of God's truth, whatever they may at last profess.

units.la: {y} Ioan. 8. quid demum profiteantur, diabolus enim ipse prius defecit à veritate quàm homicida euasit. Verbis sequentibus immoratur in explicatione secundi specialis, perfidiæ nimirum diaboli: docet enim aliquando defecisse ex præsenti ipsius conditione, qua nimirum, neminimum quidem veritatis in ipso est; sed totus est mendax & dolo plenus. Ex hoc aliud quiddam deducit, nempe quoties mendacium loquitur, de suo cum loquitur, hoc est, loqui ex ingenio suo, quod naturale est sibi facere, suum enim & quod ex sese depromptit, non autem quod alias accepit, profert. Tum rationem & causam huius rei repetit, quia mendax est, &, quod amplius est, pater est mendacii. Nam vt ab initio homicida fuit, ita ab initio mendacium suo occiderit primos illos homines, nólsque in iis omnes citra exceptionem. Nota; Arguit ex præsenti Satanæ conditione, ex mendaciis & dolis quibus plenus est, tanquam ex effectis, defectione eius à veritate. Ergo defectionem à veritate Dei sequitur omnis animi depravatio: nihil enim in illo homine sani esse potest, nihil sinceri, in quo non est veritas Dei persidem inhabitans. Quare semper retinenda nobis est illa Dei veritas, vt per eam sanctificetur cor nostrum, & imbuamur aliis virtutibus; quæ sine ea vere esse nequaquam possunt.
units.tr: {y} John 8. For the devil himself fell away from the truth before he became a murderer. In the words that follow, he dwells on the explanation of the second specific point, namely the devil's perfidy. For he teaches that the devil has fallen away from his present condition, in which there is not the least trace of truth in him, but he is wholly a liar and full of deceit. From this he draws out something further, namely that whenever he speaks a lie, he speaks it from his own resources, that is, he speaks from his own nature, which is natural to him, for he utters what is his own and comes from himself, not what he has received from elsewhere. Then he gives the reason and cause of this: because he is a liar, and, what is more, the father of lies. For just as from the beginning he was a murderer, so from the beginning he destroyed those first men by a lie, and all of them in them without exception. Note: he argues from Satan's present condition, from the lies and deceits with which he is full, as from effects, to his defection from the truth. Therefore every corruption of the mind follows from defection from the truth of God. For nothing sound and nothing sincere can be in that man in whom the truth of God does not dwell. Therefore we must always hold fast to that truth of God, so that our heart is sanctified by it and we are imbued with the other virtues, which cannot truly exist without it.

units.la: 45 Vos autem, quia ego veritatem dico, non creditis mihi.
units.tr: 45 But because I tell you the truth, you do not believe me.

units.la: 46 Quis ex vobis arguit me de peccato? Si veritatem dico, quare vos non creditis mihi?
units.tr: 46 Which of you convicts me of sin? And if I tell the truth, why do you not believe me?

units.la: 47 Qui ex Deo est, verba Dei audit, propterea vos non auditis, quia ex Deo non estis.
units.tr: 47 He who is of God hears God's words; therefore you do not hear them, because you are not of God.

units.la: Hoc versu est apodosis sive applicatio duorum illorum specialium, homicidij & infidelitatis, quæ diaboli attributa sunt. Applicat autem infidelitatem illam nominatim incredulis Iudæis. Nam homicidas non semel suprà appellauit. Vos, inquit, non creditis mihi, & quamobrem? quia veritatem dico. Notanda hic causa quæ innuit incredulitatem cum malitia coniunctam. Est enim etiam infidelitas quædam cum ignorantia,cuiusmodi fuit illa Pauli: Ignorans, inquit, faciebam, fidei expers. Ergo infidelitas eius fuit ex ignorantia, quam sequitur misericordia Dei: Ideo dicit, Misertus est mei. At malitiosa ista & pertinax infidelitas non facile impetrat veniam, quia est cum cognitione veritatis, ideoque ipsius maliciosa oppugnatione. Propterea dixit Dominus Pharisaeis, Si caeci essetis, non haberetis peccatum. Nunc vero dicitis videmus, itaque peccatum vestrum manet: Manet, inquam, non sublatum & remissum ex Dei misericordia. Quis ex vobis arguet me de peccato? occurrendo autem gloriatur & provocat eos ad tentandum crimen, si quid habeant quod adversum ipsum dicant. vid. Rom.8.33. peccatum hoc loco est mendacium in specie sine falsa doctrina, ut apparet ex verbis proxime sequentibus. Si veritatem dico, &c. Et cap. 9.31. Scimus Deum non audire peccatores, hoc est medaces & falsos doctores, ut satis ostendit illius loci argumentum. Sed unde nam haec gloriatio? ex fiducia quadam animi oportet ea proficisci. At unde fiducia? ex conscientia bona proculdubio. Conscientia enim bona efficit fiduciam, fiducia autem gloriationem. Paulus gloriatur in hunc modum, Mihi vero pro minimo est, quod a vobis diiudicer aut ab humano iudicio, imo nec meipsum diiudico. Sed unde haec gloriatio? gloriationis fundamentum proximis verbis subiicit, Nullus enim rei mihi sum conscius. Christi exemplo requiritur in omni Pastore ut cum fiducia gloriari possit tum cum ei res est cum obstinato & ingrato populo. Neque oportet eum expectare dum accusetur ab alio, verum oportet prius prorem provocare ad accusationem. Quid sibi vult illud? Requiritur in eo homine conscientia bona, quod bona fide functus sit ministerio suo. Quod de Ministro verbi dico, id de omnibus intelligo qui aliquo sunt loco. Nam omnibus res est cum ingrato mundo. Vi-dendum ergo cuique in quocumque officio, ut possit merito gloriari adversus ingratum mundum: alioqui non est illo munere, quodcunque illud demum sit, dignus. Verum quidem est eam perfectionem in terris non reperiri quae efficiat hic, quam dicimus, conscientia, ac proinde fiduciam. Sed hic confugiendum est ad eum, qui perfectus
units.tr: In this verse is the apodosis, or application, of the two specific points which are attributed to the devil, murder and unbelief. He applies that unbelief by name to the unbelieving Jews. For he had already called them murderers more than once. "You do not believe me," he says, "and why? Because I tell the truth." Here the cause that points to unbelief joined with malice is to be noted. For there is also a certain unbelief joined with ignorance, such as that of Paul: "Ignorant as I was," he says, "I did it," lacking faith. So his unbelief arose from ignorance, which is followed by the mercy of God; hence he says, "I obtained mercy." But that malicious and stubborn unbelief does not easily obtain pardon, because it is held together with knowledge of the truth, and therefore it is a malicious opposition to it. For this reason the Lord said to the Pharisees, "If you were blind, you would have no sin. But now you say, 'We see'; therefore your sin remains." It remains, I say, not taken away and forgiven by the mercy of God. "Which of you convicts me of sin?" By running ahead he boasts and challenges them to try the charge, if they have anything to say against him. See Rom. 8.33. Sin in this place is a lie in the form of false doctrine, as appears from the words that immediately follow: "If I tell the truth," etc. And in chapter 9.31: "We know that God does not hear sinners," that is, liars and false teachers, as the argument of that passage sufficiently shows. But whence does this boasting come? It must spring from a certain confidence of mind. But whence the confidence? Undoubtedly from a good conscience. For a good conscience produces confidence, and confidence produces boasting. Paul boasts in this way: "But it is a very small thing to me that I should be judged by you or by human judgment; indeed I do not even judge myself." But whence this boasting? He gives the foundation of the boasting in the words that follow: "For I am conscious of nothing against myself." By the example of Christ, it is required of every minister that he be able to boast with confidence when he has to deal with a stubborn and ungrateful people. Nor must he wait until he is accused by another, but he must first challenge the accuser. What does that mean? A good conscience is required in such a man, that he has discharged his ministry in good faith. What I say of the minister of the Word, I understand of all who hold any office. For all have to do with an ungrateful world. Therefore each man, in whatever office, must see to it that he may rightly boast against the ungrateful world; otherwise he is not worthy of that office, whatever it may be. It is true that such perfection as produces this conscience which we speak of, and consequently this confidence, is not to be found on earth. But here we must take refuge in Him who is perfect

units.la: Quid in Christi servis praecipue requiratur.
units.tr: What is especially required in the servants of Christ.

units.la: in sermonem Christi, si efficaciam sermonis Christi quae quantaque sit consideremus. Verbum Christi dixit Petrus supra 6.68. esse verbum vitae aeternę, Verba vitæ æternæ habes, inquit. Verbum autem vitæ est, quia spiritus est eodem cap. verf. 63. Verba quæ ego loquor vobis Spiritus sunt & vita sunt. Vita igitur sunt, quia spiritus sunt, hoc est, coniunctam habent Spiritus Dei potentiam, qui iis vtitur tanquam efficaci instrumento ad excitandam in cordibus fidem & nouam vitam. Neque enim putandum est verba Dei nuda & ieiuna duntaxat verba esse, cuiusmodi sunt hominum etiam eloquentissimorum, quæ nihil plane possunt ad solidam cordis atque effectuum immutationem; sed verba Dei virtutis ac potentiæ plena sunt. Ideoque Apostolus ait, Regnum Dei non est situm in verbis etiam difertissimis (cuiusmodi erat verba illa Pseudo-apostolorum illorum Corinthiorum) sed in Spiritus virtute. Verum quidem id est, sermonem crucis humilem esse, atque in speciem abiectam, sed sermo crucis, inquit Paulus, iis qui seruantur potentia Dei est. Et materia illius sermonis vilis admodum videtur mundo, vtpote homo crucifixus, sed Christus crucifixus, ait Apostolus, vocatis est Dei potentia & sapientia. Demum hoc intelligunt qui id re ipsa experti sunt. Sentiunt ij dum prædicatur hoc verbum excitari in se nouam vitam, seseque ex morte ad vitam resurgere.
units.tr: in the word of Christ, if we consider what the efficacy of the word of Christ is and how great it is. Peter, above in 6.68, called the word of Christ the word of eternal life: "You have the words of eternal life," he says. And the word is a word of life because it is spirit, as in the same chapter, verse 63: "The words that I speak to you are spirit and are life." Therefore they are life because they are spirit, that is, they have joined to them the power of the Spirit of God, who uses them as an effective instrument for arousing faith and new life in hearts. For we must not think that the words of God are bare and empty words only, such as those of even the most eloquent men, which can do nothing at all towards a solid change of heart and of conduct; but the words of God are full of virtue and power. Therefore the Apostle says, "The kingdom of God does not consist in words," even the most eloquent (such as were the words of those false apostles of the Corinthians), "but in the power of the Spirit." It is indeed true that the word of the cross is humble and in appearance despised, "but the word of the cross," says Paul, "is the power of God to those who are being saved." And the matter of that word seems to the world very worthless, namely a crucified man; but "Christ crucified," says the Apostle, "is the power and wisdom of God to those who are called." At last those understand this who have experienced it in fact. They feel, while this word is preached, a new life being stirred up in them, and themselves rising from death to life.

units.la: 52 Dixerunt ergo ei Iudæi, Nunc agnoscimus te damonium habere. Abrahamus mortuus est, & Prophetæ: & tu dicis, Si quis sermonem meum seruauerit, non gustabit mortem in æternum.
units.tr: 52 The Jews therefore said to him, "Now we know that you have a demon. Abraham is dead, and the prophets too; yet you say, 'If anyone keeps my word, he shall never taste death.'"

units.la: 53 Num tu maior es Patre illo nostro Abrahamo, qui mortuus est? etiam Prophetæ mortui sunt, quem tu teipsum facis?
units.tr: 53 "Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets also died. Whom do you make yourself out to be?"

units.la: Iudæi indurantur etiam ad promissionem vitæ propositam, non minus quam ad exprobrationem miseriæ, vt intelligas imprimis difficile atque arduum, indurarum semel hominis animum & cor quasi præclusum emollire atque aperire. Sed videamus quid sit quod colligant ex Christi hac promissione; Nunc nimirum costo Iesu,cùm natura fimus filij iræ & diaboli filij. At adoptio hæc non est inefficax ad mutandam naturam nostram,nósque iterfus quasi gignendos. Vnde & ab hac noua generatione filij Dei appellamur. Iohannes enim in hûc modum definit filios Dei : Qui, inquit,non ex sanguine,neque ex libidine carnis,neque ex libidine viri,sed ex Deo geniti sunt. Iam verò hic modus est nascendi quem nos adumbrabimus. Deus per Spiritum suum sanctum nos gignit,supr.cap.3.3.& deinceps. Opus autem est ad hanc generationem femine aliquo,ex quo nascimur, non secus atque fit in naturali generatione. Renati sumus,inquit Petrus, non ex femine mortali,sed immortali per sermonem Dei viui & manentis in æternum: Ergo ex Deo esse est ex eo nasci per Spiritum & verbum. Hinc sequitur non mirum esse,si qui ex Deo sunt expetant sibi illud verbum,ad perficiendam nimirum regenerationem istam quæ numquam in hac vita tota simul ac semel absoluitur. Petrus ait,Expetite lac illud sincerum sermonis, ut per illud adolescatis, si quidem gustatis quod benignus sit Dominus. Quibus postremis verbis significat quod qui semel Christi suauitatem in verbo ipsius gustarunt, in perpetuo expetant illud lac verbi sincerum, vt per illud adoleseat. Idem Petrus, cùm multitudo discipulorum defecisset à Domino,interrogatus cum cæteris à Domino, Num & vos vultis abire? Respondet, Domine ad quem ibimus, verba vitæ æternæ habes. Gustauit enim suauitatem illius verbi: Petrus itaque noluit vnquam à latere Domini discedere. Iohannes Baptista significauit immensum gaudium suum conceptum ex hoc verbo audito,cùm dixit, Amicus sponsi qui stat & audit eum gaudio gaudet propter vocem sponsi, hoc ergo gaudium meum impletum est. Sentit nimirum semel quàm suaue esset hoc verbum sponsi. Itaque mirifico eius porrò audiedi gaudio tenebatur. Atque hæc de generali hoc fundamento rationis. Hinc sequitur, quòd cùm ipsi nolint audire verbum illud, eos ex Deo non esse Infidelitas & odium verbi Dei, reprobatio nis signū. Quare Dominus dum infidelitatem illam contumacem intuetur, descendit altius in naturam eorum, quam videtnō esse sanctificatam Dei participatione. Ex nulla enim relalia magis cognosces naturam non sanctificatam, quàm ex infidelitate, & odio verbi diuini. Promptu enim
units.tr: The Jews are hardened even against the promise of life set before them, no less than against the reproach of their misery. So you may understand, first of all, how difficult and arduous it is to soften and open a human mind and heart once it has been hardened and, as it were, shut. But let us see what they gather from this promise of Christ. Surely, they say, since by nature we are children of wrath and children of the devil, this adoption is not powerful enough to change our nature and, as it were, to beget us anew. Hence we are also called sons of God by this new generation. For John defines the sons of God in this way: "Who," he says, "were not born of blood, nor of the desire of the flesh, nor of the desire of man, but were born of God." Now this is the manner of birth that we shall outline. God begets us by his Holy Spirit (see above, chap. 3, vers. 3 and following). Moreover, for this regeneration some seed is needed, from which we are born, just as happens in natural generation. "We have been born again," says Peter, "not of mortal seed but of immortal, through the word of the living God, which abides for ever." So to be of God is to be born of him through the Spirit and the word. From this it follows that it is no wonder if those who are of God long for that word, since it is by that word that this regeneration is brought to completion, which is never fully and at once finished in this life. Peter says, "Long for the pure milk of the word, so that by it you may grow, if indeed you have tasted that the Lord is kind." By these last words he means that those who have once tasted the sweetness of Christ in his word should continue to long for the pure milk of the word, so that they may grow by it. Peter again, when a multitude of disciples had fallen away from the Lord, was asked by the Lord along with the rest, "Do you also wish to go away?" He answers, "Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life." For he had tasted the sweetness of that word; therefore Peter was never willing to leave the side of the Lord. John the Baptist showed the immense joy he had conceived from hearing this word, when he said, "The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice; this my joy therefore is fulfilled." He surely felt once how sweet this word of the bridegroom was; and so he was held by a wonderful joy in hearing him further. And this is enough about this general ground of reasoning. From this it follows that, since they themselves are unwilling to hear that word, they are not of God; unbelief and hatred of the word of God are a sign of reprobation. Therefore the Lord, looking upon that stubborn unbelief, goes deeper into their nature, which evidently has not been sanctified by participation in God. For you will know a nature that is not sanctified from nothing more surely than from unbelief and hatred of the divine word.

units.la: Iohan.7.66 &c. enim est iudicare eū, qui non delectatur verbo Dei audiendo, eum, inquam, nihil cum Deo commune habere, neque dum sanctificatū esse. Plura sunt, fateor, argumenta & indicia naturæ sanctificatæ, sed nullum est isto certius, nempe si quis sincerè diligat verbum Dei. Quod si quis non diligat verbum Dei, ideoque nullo modo delectetur, sed gaudeat potiùs tenebris & ignorātia, is profecto sanctificatus non est, ne si forte sanctitatem planè angelicam præterexat. Id faciunt obstinati Papistæ hodierno die. Sunt etiam apud nos qui bene alioqui & civiliter viuunt, qui tamen nullo desiderio verbi tenentur; istos homines nunquā ego sanctificatos dixerim, neque eorū virtutes esse existimarim, sed virtutū vmbras dunxat & simulachra, cūm sine sanctificatione & participatione diuinæ naturæ nulla posset esse vera virtus.
units.tr: For it is easy to judge that the man who takes no delight in hearing the word of God has nothing in common with God and is not yet sanctified, I say. There are, I admit, many arguments and indications of a sanctified nature, but none is more certain than this: whether someone sincerely loves the word of God. But if someone does not love the word of God, and therefore takes no delight in it at all, but rather rejoices in darkness and ignorance, he is certainly not sanctified, even if he should somehow be wholly angelic in holiness. Obstinate Papists do this in our own day. There are also among us some who otherwise live well and decently, yet are held by no desire for the word; I would never call such people sanctified, nor do I think their virtues are virtues at all, but only shadows and images of virtue, since without sanctification and participation in the divine nature no true virtue can exist.

units.la: 48 Responderunt ergo Iudæi & dixerunt ei, None bene dicimus te Samaritanum esse, & dæmonium habere?
units.tr: 48 The Jews answered and said to him, "Do we not say well that you are a Samaritan and have a demon?"

units.la: 49 Respondit Iesus, Ego dæmonium non habeo, sed honoro Patrem meum, & vos contumelia afficitis me.
units.tr: 49 Jesus answered, "I do not have a demon; but I honour my Father, and you dishonour me."

units.la: 50 Ego verò non quæro gloriam meam: est qui quærat & iudicet.
units.tr: 50 "But I do not seek my own glory; there is one who seeks it and judges."

units.la: 51 Amen, amen dico vobis: si quis sermonem meum seruauerit, mortem nō conspiciet in æternum.
units.tr: 51 "Amen, amen, I say to you: if anyone keeps my word, he shall never see death."

units.la: Rritati iam obiiciunt eum Samaritanum esse, hoc est, ut verba sequentia exponunt, correptum fallaci & erroneo aliquo spiritu, instar Samaritanorum. Vide nunc magis insaniunt quam prius. Antea quidem paulò modò contendebant se filios Abrahæ, Filios Dei esse. Nunc maliciosè insurgunt aduersus Dominum, vt fac videas quanto magis agis cum indurato, tanto magis euadere induratū. Nullus enim est modus peccādi, vbi quis semel incepit maliciosè peccare in lucem. Tantum mali est in induratione & excæcatione vel semel inchoata. At, inquis, provocati sunt illi quidem verbis Christi acerrimis. Obiecit enim filios diaboli esse, eósque à Deo plané seperauit. At, inquam, id merita est, idque postulauit eorum contumacia, quæ nisi aperiatur penitus à fundamento suo & insito naturæ principio, profecto nunquam futurum est vt curetur. Hic est enim primus gradus ad salutem, agnitio miseriæ nostræ & naturæ huius corruptissimæ, quam qui non cognouit ex parte certè aliqua, is profecto ne vnum quidem passum confecit in via salutis. Sed quid est quod obiiciunt? nempe vulgare quoddam conuitium, vulgò enim si quando voluerunt Iudæi grauare quemquam magna aliqua infamia, Samaritanum dixerunt, hoc est impurum hominem & corruptum in notitia veritatis. Nihil igitur habent quod de quo tanquam speciali aliquo crimine ipsum accusent. Obtrauit enim illis os iam supra; sed tamen non prorsus tacent: vt scias contumacibus nunquam defuturam materiam, qua sese magis indurent, & quam obiiciant aduersus pios quosque & eos maxime qui lucem ipsis præferunt. S. Minister verbi hodierno die non minus innocens sit quàm Angelus, nunquam tamen deerit nostris hominibus vel accusandi, vel conuiciandi, vel detractandi materia. Quæ potius quàm nulla sit, obiicient dæmonium habere. Non sunt ignotæ nobis istorum voces, sed Christus passus est ante nos hæc omnia. Respondit Iesus. Respondens Dominus non conuitiu conuitio compensat, sed modestè negat quod obiecerunt per conuitium. Negationis autem reddit rationem à contrario ipsius facto. Ego, inquit, dæmonium non habeo. Qui honorat Patrem, is necesse est non habeat dæmonium: At ego honoro Patrem: Ergo, &c. Quid sit honorare Patrem Dominus ipse ostendit in illa oratione ad Patrem suum, de qua postea cap. 17. 4. Ego glorificaui te in terra. Tum quid hoc sit docet verbis sequentibus: Opus consummauì quod dedisti mihi vt facerem. Opus intelligit redemptionis humanæ, in qua perficienda ipse se exinaniuit, summisit, & factus est obediens Patri vsque ad mortem, mortem autem crucis. Nulla enim vnquam creatura sic humiliauit se sub manu Patris, vt Filius. Nota igitur, qui verè honorat Deum, is necesse est non corripiatur à mendaci spiritu. Hæc enim nota est veri doctoris, si quis in doctrina sua quærat Dei gloriam in solidum: vt è contra nota est falsi doctoris, si quis in doctrina sua quaerat se potius quam Deum: is profecto verus doctor esse non poterit. Unde has notas verae falsaeque doctrinae dedit Dominus supra cap.7.18. Qui a semetipso loquitur, gloriam quaerit: Qui autem quaerit gloriam eius qui misit ipsum, hic verax est, & iniustitia non est in eo. Subiicit deinde factum eorum contrarium suo facto, factum, inquam, indignissimum. Indignissimum enim est ignominia afficere eos qui Deum sincere glorificant. Et tamen qui ignominiosi sunt maxime, & indignis quibusque modis tractantur in hoc saeculo, ii sunt qui maxime student Deo placere, qui, inquam, sese humiliant, seipsos abnegare studeant, ut Deum suum glorificent. Idcirco fatigamur, inquit Paulus, & probris afficimur, quod speremus in Deo vivo. Et Petrus dicit a prophanis hominibus blasphematos fuisse initio Christianos, qui more solito ad eundem luxus excessum cum iis non concurrebant. Optimus quisque apud nos & sanctissimus a filiis huius saeculi irridetur & blasphematur.
units.tr: Now they provoke him by calling him a Samaritan. That is, as the following words explain, they mean that he is seized by some deceitful and erroneous spirit, like the Samaritans. See how they now rage more than before. A little earlier they were insisting that they were sons of Abraham and sons of God. Now they maliciously rise up against the Lord, so that you may see how the more you deal with a hardened man, the more hardened he becomes.
