For it is the nature of the godly that, although they understand that it will go ill for them, they care nothing for it so long as they may do good to the Church. So Paul, when he knew that bonds and affliction awaited him at Jerusalem, when he was about to go up thither, said: "Yet I count not my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy." Moreover, from this time we see that Christ deliberately wished, by giving this example of humility in the sight of the disciples, to close his life and, as it were, the last act of his life; so that what they saw last they might most of all imitate throughout their whole life. For he no longer wished to perform any miracle at the end, but by commending this example of humility he signified that he wished us to have humility rather than the gift of miracles, and that those are more the imitators of Christ who follow his humility than those who work miracles and things beyond the ordinary course.

units.la: Sciens Iesus Patrem omnia. Redit ad occasiones: éstque hæc tertia & vltima facti occasio, siue causa potiùs. Significatur his verbis, Christum securo fuisse animo quòd ad res suas attinebat. Ex quo factum est, vt curam discipulorum & aliorum in se susceperit. Ad hoc vt sit aliorum & posterorum seria cura, nō satis est, si eos diligamus, nisi etiam nosipsi simus securo animo, certíqs salutis nostræ ipsorum; neque Pater etsi filium suum vnicum quàm maximè diligat iam extremam agens animam, eius tamen curam habet, nisi ipse securo sit animo, persuasùmque habeat bene sibi fore post vitam istâ. Hinc verba illa Iacobi ad filios suos, hinc Dauidis ad Salomonem filium, quem heredem regni reliquit. Omnis quicunque velit hortari, admonere, consolari, opus habet, vt ipse ea in se sentiat, ad quæ alios mouet atque excitat. Sic Dauid primùm, deinde post eum Paulus, Cre lidi, inquit, ideo loquutus sum. Surgit à cœna. Singulæ partes humilitatis huius ita inducuntur, vt & nihil reliquisse Christum ad perfectam humilitatem videas, & ipse quasi in rem præsente introducaris, & oculis propemodum videas Christum surgentem, &c. vt & ipse licet cum discipulis Christi, non videris oculis tuis & coram Christum sese humiliantem, tamen tam viua ista hypothesi moueris ad eandem cum discipulis humilitatem, quoties legis vel audis ista à Spiritu sancto tam ad viuum expressa.
units.tr: "Jesus, knowing that the Father had given all things." He returns to the occasions; and this is the third and last occasion of the deed, or rather cause. These words signify that Christ was of a secure mind as regards his own affairs. From this it followed that he took upon himself the care of the disciples and of others. For there to be a serious care for others and for posterity, it is not enough that we love them, unless we ourselves also have a secure mind and certainty of our own salvation and theirs. Nor does a father, even though he loves his only son most greatly, have care for him while he is breathing his last, unless he himself is secure in mind and persuaded that it will go well with himself after this life. Hence those words of Jacob to his sons, hence David's words to Solomon his son, whom he left as heir to the kingdom. Whoever wishes to exhort, admonish or console, must himself feel in himself those things to which he moves and stirs others. "So David first, and after him Paul: 'I have therefore spoken'" (cf. 2 Cor. 4). "He riseth from supper." The individual parts of this humility are so set forth that you see Christ leaving nothing out of perfect humility, and you are introduced as if you were present at the matter, and you almost see with your eyes Christ rising from supper, and so on. So that, although you are not with the disciples and do not see with your own eyes Christ humbling himself in front of you, nevertheless you are moved by this lively picture to the same humility as the disciples, whenever you read or hear these things so vividly expressed by the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 6 Venit ergo ad Simonem Petrum: qui dixit ei, Domine, tu mihi lavas pedes!
units.tr: 6 So he came to Simon Peter, who said to him, Lord, are you washing my feet?

units.la: 7 Respondit Iesus & dixit ei, Quod ego facio tu nescis nunc, cognosces autem postea.
units.tr: 7 Jesus answered and said to him, What I am doing you do not understand now, but you will understand afterwards.

units.la: 8 Dicit ei Petrus, Non lavabis pedes meos in æternum. Respondit ei Iesus, Nisi lavero te, nihil mecum habebis commune.
units.tr: 8 Peter says to him, You shall never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, If I do not wash you, you will have no share with me.

units.la: 9 Dicit ei Simon Petrus, Domine, non solum pedes meos, sed etiam manus & caput.
units.tr: 9 Simon Peter says to him, Lord, not only my feet but also my hands and my head.

units.la: 10 Dicit ei Iesus, Ei qui lotus est, non opus est nisi ut pedes lavet, sed est purus totus: & vos puri estis, sed non omnes.
units.tr: 10 Jesus says to him, He who has bathed has no need except to wash his feet, but is wholly clean; and you are clean, but not all of you.

units.la: 11 Noverat enim eum a quo prodebatur, propterea dixit, Non estis puri omnes.
units.tr: 11 For he knew who was to betray him; therefore he said, You are not all clean.

units.la: PRimum aggreditur Simonem Petrum. Ipse autem quodammodo eum repellit hac voce, Tu mihi lavas pedes! Verba significat rei indignitatem, quod ipse indignus sit cuius pedes lavet Dominus. Modestiam igitur aliquam indicant & humilitatem hominis, nisi obedire Domino esset vera humilitas, obedire, inquam, etiam cum accidunt quæ nobis indigna ac indecora alioqui videntur, illud scientes perpetuò, omnia ex eius voluntate fieri. Quod ego facio. Hæc verba simplicem obedientiam nobis commendant, etiamsi ignoremus causam factorum Dei & ad concilium rerum earum quæ fiunt non advocemur. Neque enim subditi recusant obedientiam principi suo, quod non statim omnes subditos princeps vocet ad concilium, & cum iis causas factorum communicet & mandatorum suorum. Neque figmentum dicit fictori, ut Paulus loquitur, Cur me talem fecisti? An igitur homuncio responsare Deo creatori? Cognosces autem postea. Nam facti rationem redditurus est statim absoluto facto. Qui præstant Deo simplicem obedientiam, neque statim curiose requirunt in causas factorum Dei, ipsi patientiæ suæ & obedientiæ fructum decerpunt hunc nimirum, ut Deus tandem, si opus sit, iis huiusmodi causas communicaturus sit, ita ut iam inspectis causis utpote bono suo & Dei ipsius gloria, non vellent quidem iam etsi in optione rem haberent, & res integra esset, aliter factum. Non tamen laudabis. Excusari aliquo modo potuit prima ista recusatio Petri: at vero postquam respondit Dominus, rationem facti statim postea exponendam esse, cum iam non acquiescit dicto quomodo potest excusari? Et annon modestia illa, quae videbatur, conversa est in pertinaciam? Ita solet fieri de modestia quae est contra voluntatem Dei, dum homines contra Dei voluntatem volunt videri modestiores. Si porro urgeantur reuocenturque ad Dei voluntatem, iam manifesto voluntatis suae pertinaciam & obstinationem animi sui produnt. Papistae volunt videri ex submissione animi invocare Angelos & sanctos defunctos, at cum ab errore revocantur, tum plane arguunt non submissionem animi veram, sed, ut Paulus ait, honorem animi inflati sensu carnis. Deinde in toto suo cultu fictitio volunt submissi ac humiles conspici, sed hypocritae sunt & lupi in pelle agnina, id quod summa ista omnium Europae Ecclesiarum perturbatio & diuexatio plus satis ostendit, neque patiuntur se ab inuentionibus suis & figmentis abduci. Mira est in omnibus rebus voluntatis humanae peruersitas, quae tum demum se prodit, cum ad normam voluntatis diuinae reducuntur, φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς est inimicitia aduersus Deum.
units.tr: First he approaches Simon Peter. But he himself, in a way, pushes him back with these words, "You are washing my feet!" The words express the unworthiness of the thing: that he is not worthy to have the Lord wash his feet. They therefore indicate a certain modesty and humility on the man's part; but true humility would be to obey the Lord, obey, I say, even when things happen that otherwise seem to us unworthy and unseemly, always knowing that everything comes about by his will. What I am doing. These words commend to us a simple obedience, even though we do not know the cause of God's acts and are not called into the counsel of the things that are done. For subjects do not refuse obedience to their prince because the prince does not call all his subjects at once into his council and share with them the reasons for his acts and commands. Nor does the thing formed say to the former, as Paul puts it, "Why have you made me thus?" Is a little man to answer back to God his Creator? You will understand afterwards. For he will give an account of his acts as soon as the act is finished. Those who render to God a simple obedience, and do not at once inquire curiously into the causes of God's acts, reap the fruit of their patience and obedience, namely this: that God, if need be, will in the end share such causes with them, so that once they have seen the causes, as belonging to their own good and the glory of God himself, they would not wish, even if they had the choice and the matter were still open, that it had been done otherwise. Not yet will you praise. That first refusal of Peter could be excused in some way; but after the Lord answered that the reason for the act would be explained afterwards, how can he be excused, since he no longer assents to the word? And has that modesty which seemed to be there not been turned into obstinacy? This commonly happens with a modesty that is against the will of God, when men want to appear more modest in opposition to the will of God. If they are further pressed and called back to the will of God, they then plainly reveal the obstinacy of their will and the stubbornness of their mind. The Papists want to seem, out of humbleness of mind, to invoke angels and departed saints; but when they are called back from their error, they plainly show that their humbleness of mind is not true, but, as Paul says, the honour of a mind puffed up by the sense of the flesh. Again, in all their made-up worship they want to be seen as humble and lowly, but they are hypocrites and wolves in sheep's clothing, as that great upheaval and disturbance of all the Churches of Europe sufficiently shows, and they do not allow themselves to be drawn away from their inventions and fictions. Wondrous is the perversity of the human will in all things, which shows itself most clearly when it is brought back to the rule of the divine will: the mind of the flesh [φρόνημα τῆς σαρκὸς] is enmity against God.

units.la: Nisi tamen. His verbis subiudicatur hoc Christi factum non tantum exemplum esse huius humilitatis, sed etiam signum quoddam ac symbolum lotionis illius & ablutionis peccatorum per sanguinem Christi & per Spiritum sanctum. Necesse igitur est, qui velint partem aliquam in Christo habere, per Christum sordes eorum abluantur. Qua in re vehementer errant homines ac decipiuntur. Putant enim posse immundis pedibus cum Christo vna ambulare, & pollutatis ac foedatis manibus sanguine & rapina, cum Christo tamen vna versari. Sic Simon magus cuius cor positum erat in felle amaritudinis & in nexu iniustitiae, putabat se tamen parte ac sortem habere in negotio Christi. Sed quid huic Petrus? Non est tibi, inquit, pars neque sors in hoc negotio. Falluntur tamen hac re peccatores: ideo Apostolus, Neque fornicatores, neque idololatrae, neque maechi, &c. hareditariò possidebunt regnum cælorum. Significat igitur decipi homines peccatores eo, quod cum summe peccent, putent tamen sibi in cælis locum reliquum esse. Tum ibidem subiicit Apostolus: Et hæc erat nonnulli, sed abluti estis, sed sanctificati estis, &c. Quibus verbis significat, non nisi ablutos prius locum habituros in cælis, hoc est, ut ipse exponit, iustificatos sanguine Christi, & sanctificatos Spiritu sancto. Videmus etiam his Christi verbis contemptum signi vel symboli à Deo instituti homines è cælis excludere. Neque id mirum, cum contempto signo conculcetur pariter sanguis ille fœderis, & ignominia afficiatur Spiritus Dei sanctus. Denique non est prætereundum quòd acerbè excipiat Petrum hoc responso Dominus. Nam Dominus cum benignis benignum se exhibet, & cum peruersis luctatur. Offenditur autem Deus pertinacia quàm maximè.
units.tr: Unless indeed. By these words it is shown that this act of Christ is not only an example of this humility, but also a certain sign and symbol of that washing and cleansing of sins through the blood of Christ and through the Holy Spirit. It is necessary, therefore, that those who wish to have some part in Christ have their filth washed away through Christ. In this matter men greatly err and are deceived. For they think that they can walk with Christ with unclean feet, and still be with Christ with hands defiled and stained with blood and plunder. So Simon Magus, whose heart was set in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity, thought nonetheless that he had a part and lot in the work of Christ. But what did Peter say to him? You have, he said, neither part nor lot in this matter. Sinners are nonetheless deceived in this respect; therefore the Apostle says, Neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, etc. will inherit the kingdom of heaven. He signifies, therefore, that sinners are deceived in this, that although they sin most grievously, they nevertheless think that a place in heaven is still left for them. Then the Apostle adds in the same place: And such were some of you, but you were washed, but you were sanctified, etc. By these words he signifies that only those who have been washed beforehand will have a place in heaven, that is, as he himself explains, those justified by the blood of Christ and sanctified by the Holy Spirit. We see also from these words of Christ that contempt for a sign or symbol instituted by God shuts men out of heaven. Nor is this surprising, since, when the sign is despised, that blood of the covenant is equally trampled underfoot and the Holy Spirit of God is put to shame. Finally, it must not be passed over that the Lord receives Peter harshly with this answer. For the Lord shows himself kind to the kind, but wrestles with the perverse. God is displeased above all by obstinacy.

units.la: Non solùm pedes. Nunc demum perterrefactus superiori comminatione acquievit Petrus, neque amplius resistit. Nimirum non leui de causa patitur se velli à Christo, qui iam degustasset quàm benignus esset Dominus, ut ipse in Epistola sua loquitur. Qui enim semel adhæserunt Domino, quidlibet potius patientur priusquam se ab eo diuelli patiantur: & quoties audiunt aliquid de separatione, toties eum ut infans matrem interminantem arctius amplectuntur. Cùm dixisset Dominus discipulis, An vos quoque me derelinquetis? Respondet Petrus, ad quem abibimus: nam verba vitæ æternæ habes. Tum ibidem qua fide adhæserit Christo egregia confessione indicauit, Credimus, inquit, & agnoscimus te esse Christum illum filium Dei viuentis. At iis qui Christum nondum sapuerunt, leue videtur esse & stultum ac ridiculum, si obiiciatur iisdem à Christo dicutur ac ridiculum? Quoties ...
units.tr: Not only the feet. Now at last Peter, terrified by the earlier threat, yields and no longer resists. Assuredly he allows himself to be pulled away by Christ not for a slight reason, for he had already tasted how gracious the Lord is, as he himself says in his Epistle. For those who have once clung to the Lord would sooner suffer anything than suffer themselves to be torn away from him; and whenever they hear anything about separation, they embrace him all the more tightly, as a child embraces its mother when she threatens it. When the Lord had said to the disciples, Will you also leave me? Peter answers, To whom shall we go? For you have the words of eternal life. Then in the same place he showed by an outstanding confession the faith by which he had clung to Christ: We believe, he says, and acknowledge that you are that Christ, the Son of the living God. But to those who have not yet tasted Christ, it seems a light and foolish and ridiculous thing, if it is put to them... Christ said... ridiculous? How often...

units.la: Quod tamen Petrus ... Fit tamen, vt qui insigni peccati sensu afficiuntur, ipsis videatur se plane totos esse corruptos, & opus ipsis esse noua ablutione omnium sordium, iustificatione, sanctificatione. Dauid petit ablui ita, acsi nulla sui parte ablu-tus iam esset: multum laua me ab iniquitate mea. & Paulus etiam regenitus, tamen se carnalem vocat, venditum vtsubiiceretur peccato. Et postea eodem capite, Miser ego homo, quis me liberabit ex corpore mortis huius? Verum tamen verbis quae eo loco sequuntur continuo sese colligit, ac gratias agit Deo in Christo quod ipsum iam eripuerit.
units.tr: Yet Peter... It happens, however, that those who are affected by a deep sense of sin seem to themselves to be wholly corrupted, and to need a new washing away of all filth, justification, sanctification. David asks to be washed as though no part of him were yet clean: Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity. And Paul, though regenerate, still calls himself carnal, sold to be under sin. And later in the same chapter: Wretched man that I am, who will deliver me from the body of this death? Yet in the words that follow in that place he at once collects himself and gives thanks to God in Christ, who has already rescued him.

units.la: Pedum nomine hic intelliguntur peccati inhaerentis reliquiae. Ex his verbis colligi potest iustificatum iam in Christo & sanctificatum, non adeo degenerare, vt ipsi opus sit denuo iustificari & sanctificari, opus tamen illi esse vt progressum faciat in sanctificatione perpetuum, vt qui iter faciat perpetuo per coenum ac lutum huius mundi, ac proinde opus habeat perpetuo saltem pedum lotione, & Christo illo qui solus abluit sordes nostras sibi praesente. Qui iustus est, iustificetur adhuc: Qui sanctus est, sanctificetur adhuc. Sed est purus totus. Ratio propositionis a puritate. Purum totum vocat, non quod nihil sordium ac peccati in ipso reliquum sit. Nou, inquit Paulus iam regenitus, in me (hoc est in carne mea) bonum non habitare. Sed a potiori parte, nempe spiritu, homine nonnisi ex parte regenitum, appellare solet. Sic spirituales dicimur, sic perfecti. Nam licet non sit perfectio graduum (vt loquuntur) tamen partium est perfectio. Tum assumit & applicat id quod in genere dixit, At vos estis puri, & loti. Applicat Dominus ideo, vt Apostolorum quisque applicaret ipse sibi puritatem istam: Nam applicante Domino, applicat conscientia: Absoluente eo absoluit conscientia necessario: condemnante eo condemnat conscientia necessario. Neque minus nunc efficaciter applicat nobis gratiam in Euangelio oblatam per Spiritum sanctum, quantum olim discipulis puritatem illam. Vt non fit quod Papistae discrimen in haec nostri & Apostolorum faciant, & priuent nos consolatione scripturarum. Sed non omnes. Excipit vnum aliquem ex discipulis, sed suppresso nomine, vt & alij discipuli non male sibi conscij, seipsos tamen excuterent esse debet.
units.tr: By the name of feet are understood here the remnants of indwelling sin. From these words it can be gathered that one who is already justified and sanctified in Christ does not so degenerate as to need again to be justified and sanctified; yet he needs to make continual progress in sanctification, as one who travels continually through the mire and mud of this world, and therefore has continual need at least of the washing of his feet, and of that Christ who alone washes away our filth being present to him. Let him who is righteous be justified still; let him who is holy be sanctified still. But is wholly clean. This is the reason for the statement, drawn from its purity. He calls him wholly clean not because no filth or sin is left in him. Paul, already regenerate, says, In me (that is, in my flesh) dwells no good thing. But he is accustomed to name a man by the better part, namely the spirit, though he is regenerate only in part. Thus we are called spiritual, thus perfect; for although there is no perfection of degrees (as they say), there is perfection of parts. Then he takes up and applies what he had said in general: But you are clean and washed. The Lord applies it so that each of the Apostles might apply that purity to himself: for when the Lord applies, the conscience necessarily applies; when he absolves, the conscience necessarily absolves; when he condemns, the conscience necessarily condemns. Nor does he now apply to us less effectively the grace offered in the Gospel through the Holy Spirit than he once applied that purity to the disciples. So the Papists have no ground for making this distinction between ours and the Apostles' and depriving us of the comfort of the Scriptures. But not all. He excepts one of the disciples, but suppresses the name, so that the other disciples, not conscious of any fault, should nevertheless examine themselves.

units.la: Iustificatorum officium.
units.tr: The office of those who are justified.

units.la: Purus quis.
units.tr: Who is pure?

units.la: Consolatio piorum in applicatione consistit.
units.tr: The comfort of the godly consists in application.

units.la: Explorationem conscientiae seria esse debet. (non enim fit particularis ista applicatio & fiducia sine magna & seria examinatione, & exploratione, cordis nostri) & Iudam sibi male conscium ad resipiscentiam inuitaret. Ita enim temperat Deus iustitiam suam, in reprobandis hominibus cum misericordia, ut nonnisi inuitatos prius ad resipiscetiam abiiciat. Multa lenitate perfert vasa ire coagmentata ad interitum. Nouerat enim. Ratio exceptionis a notitia facti ac proditionis Iudę. Nota igitur, Quis est qui excipit impuros ac discernit hypocritas? Non nisi is qui novit & intima cordis, & quae faciunt hypocritae in occulto. Hinc discimus non temere iudicandum de aliis, sed sistendos nosipsos Deo probatos: Nouit Dominus qui sint sui, & discedat ab iniustitia omnis qui nominat nomen Christi. Quo significat Apostolus Deo relinquendum iudicium aliorum, & iudicandum potius de nobis ipsis, & nosipsos explorandos, ut vita respondeat professioni, id quod certum est electionis nostrae argumentum.
units.tr: The examination of conscience must be serious. For this particular application and faith does not come about without a great and serious examination and testing of our heart. And it would have roused Judas, who was conscious of his own guilt, to repentance. For God so tempers his justice with mercy in rejecting men that he casts off only those who have first been invited to repentance. He bears with great gentleness the vessels of wrath fitted for destruction. For he knew it. The reason for the exception is the knowledge of the deed and the betrayal by Judas. Note, then: who is it who singles out the impure and distinguishes the hypocrites? Only he who knows both the inmost heart and what hypocrites do in secret. From this we learn not to judge others rashly, but to submit ourselves to God's approval: The Lord knows those who are his, and let everyone who names the name of Christ depart from iniquity. By this the Apostle signifies that judgment of others is to be left to God, and that we should rather judge ourselves and examine ourselves, so that our life corresponds to our profession, which is a certain proof of our election.

units.la: 12 Postquam ergo lauisset pedes eorum, & pallium suum recepisset, rursum discubuit & dixit eis, Noftisne quid fecerim vobis?
units.tr: 12 After he had therefore washed their feet and taken his garment, he sat down again and said to them, Do you know what I have done to you?

units.la: 13 Vos me vocantes, dicitis, Praeceptor ac Domine, & recte dicitis: sum enim.
units.tr: 13 You call me Teacher and Lord, and you say rightly, for so I am.

units.la: 14 Itaque si ego lauipedes vestros, Dominus & Praeceptor, vos quoque debetis aliorum pedes lauare.
units.tr: 14 If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.

units.la: 15 Exemplum enim praebui vobis, ut quemadmodum ego feci vobis, ita & vos faciatis.
units.tr: 15 For I have given you an example, that as I have done to you, so you also should do.

units.la: 16 Amen, amen dico vobis, Seruus non est maior domino suo, neque legatus maior eo a quo missus est.
units.tr: 16 Verily, verily, I say to you, the servant is not greater than his lord, nor the one sent greater than he who sent him.

units.la: 17 Si haec nouerit is, beati eritis si ea feceritis.
units.tr: 17 If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.

units.la: Expositurus rationem facti sui non stat exutus pallio suo, verum assumpto pallio accubuit, nempe ut maiori cum gratia & authoritate suos doceret. Haec enim externa aliquid momenti habent, & gratiam afferunt verbo prædicto, cuiusmodi sunt, locus è quo quis doc-turus sit, habitus corporis honestus ac decorus. Hæc enim ad decorem pertinent & neglectis aut contemptis his verbum sæpe dedecoratur. Intelligitur quid. Exordium ad attentionem animos præparans. Admonent autem hæc verba, sæpenumero ignaros esse nos eorum quæ Deus facit nobis quo tempore nos exercet, vsque dum ipse nobis causam aperiat. Interea autem nos sæpe reluctamur per impatientiam, & vt de Petro vidimus supra, ægrè ferimus. At Deus suo tempore causam aperit, & opus suum ita probat, vt iam videatur ipsis nihil iis potuisse magis gratum aut commodum accidisse. Vos me vocatis. Fundamentum futuræ conclusionis subsistit, accipitque ex ipsorum confessione, Ego Magister ac Dominus vester sum. Magistri nomen respicit discipulos: Domini vero nomen respicit seruos. Christus enim noster & Rex est siue Dominus, & Propheta. Posito hoc fundamento argumentatur. Propositio comparata est hoc versu: q.d. Si ego qui dignior vobis sum laui pedes vestros, &c. Quanto magis debetis vos qui æquales inter vos estis hoc facere? Neque enim Petrum excipit, sed æqualem aliis statuit. Quod si principem Apostolorum eum voluisset esse, profectò sermone direxisset ad eum nominatim, Tu Petre quem statui aliorum principem, tu tamen aliis inseruito. Sed nihil tale ne cogitauit quidem Dominus. Ex fundamento isto deducta inde argumentatione discere, quid faciendum nobis sit ad hoc vt humilietur animus: Nempe ponendus est perpetuo Christus ante oculos, & primum in gloria sua inspiciendus est, vt Rex gloriosus, Dominus & magister: deinde in humilitate sua, vt humiliatus in carne nostra ad mortem vsque crucis. Hoc vbi factum est, sic deinde cogitandum argumentandumque est; Christus gloriosus seipsum mea causa ita humiliauit, Annon igitur debeo ego æqualibus meis, & aliis quibuscunque me humiliare, etiam si rex sim? Nam gloria & maiestas regis non consistit in superbia, & gloriosum quemque humilitas ac modestia commendat. Paulus piis commendans modestiam ad Christum continuò nos dedu-cit, Sic, inquit, is affectus in vobis qui in Christo fuit. Tum cnim gloriosum videndum præbet: Qui, inquit, cum in forma Dei esset, &c. Postremò humilem describit, Sed, inquit, exinanivit se sumpta serui forma, &c.
units.tr: In explaining the reason for what he did, he does not stand stripped of his garment, but having taken up his garment he reclined, namely so that he might teach his own with greater grace and authority. For external things carry some weight and lend grace to the word preached, such as the place from which one is to teach and an honourable and becoming bearing of the body. For these belong to propriety, and when they are neglected or despised the word is often dishonoured. Understand what. This is an introduction preparing the minds for attention. These words also remind us that we are often ignorant of what God does to us at the time he exercises us, until he himself reveals the cause to us. Meanwhile we often struggle against it through impatience and, as we saw above concerning Peter, bear it with difficulty. But God reveals the cause in his own time and so proves his work that it then seems to them that nothing more pleasing or advantageous could have happened to them. You call me. The foundation of the conclusion to come stands here and is drawn from their own confession: I am your Teacher and Lord. The name of Teacher looks to the disciples; the name of Lord looks to the servants. For Christ our Lord is both King and Prophet. On this foundation he argues. The proposition is set out in this verse, as if to say: If I, who am worthier than you, have washed your feet, etc., how much more ought you, who are equals among yourselves, to do this? For he does not except Peter but places him as equal to the others. If he had wished him to be the chief of the Apostles, he would certainly have addressed him by name: You, Peter, whom I have appointed chief of the others, yet serve the others. But the Lord did not even think of anything like this. From this foundation the argument drawn shows what we must do so that the mind is humbled: namely, Christ must always be set before our eyes, and first he must be viewed in his glory, as the glorious King, Lord and Teacher; then in his humility, as one humbled in our flesh even to the death of the cross. When this has been done, we should then think and argue thus: Christ, being glorious, humbled himself for my sake; should I not then humble myself before my equals and before whomever else, even if I am a king? For the glory and majesty of a king does not consist in pride, and humility and modesty commend every man who is glorious. Paul, commending modesty to the pious, leads us at once to Christ: Let this mind be in you, he says, which was also in Christ. Then he presents him as glorious: who, he says, being in the form of God, etc. Lastly he describes him as humble: but he says, emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, etc.

units.la: Exemplum enim. Sequitur propositionis duæ rationes: prior est à fine facti sui. Est autem vt sit exemplum illis, vt illi quoque idem faciant. Discere igitur finem factorum nostrorum non esse nos ipsos solos, sed aliorum oportere respectum habere, vt simus bono aliis exemplo, & alij moueantur nostro exemplo ad bene agendum. Sic enim cogitare debemus, nos alios perpetuo in hac vita quasi interire, & aliorum omnium oculos in nobis defixos esse, aliósque nostris vestigiis insistere. Hoc dum cogitamus, debemus, vt loquar cum Apostolo, accurate & circumspecte incedere, vel aliorum causa. Væ enim illis per quos scandalum. Hoc ad omnes spectat, non ad solos ministros Dei in Ecclesia. Omnes enim vita sua aliios tenentur instituere, & in actionibus sermonem vitæ prætedere. Philip. 2. 1. Pet. 3. Vxores, inquit, subiectæ sint viris suis, vt etiam si qui non obediunt sermoni, per vxorum conuersationem absque sermone lucrifiant. Vnde lucrefiunt homines vel sola vita, sine verbo prædicare: magna vis est in exemplis in vtranque partem. Amen, Amen. Secunda ratio per grauem assuerationem. Est autem ab inferiori conditione serui & legati sumpta, si is comparetur cum domino suo. Diximus supra ad militatem requiri vt oculus figatur in Christum. Nunc discimus figendum simul oculum in nos ipsos, & considerandum nos non esse nisi seruos & legatos; ea quæ optima nostra in hac vita conditio. Nunquam profecto satis conditionem nostram eleuare possumus. Paulus se minimum Apostolorum dixit, imò sanctorum minimum, imò nihil esse se dixit, imò nihilo deteriorem significavit, persequutorem, blasphemum, iniurium. Ita nos nunquam satis submisse ac modeste de nobis ipsis sentire vel loqui possumus. Iam vbi vidimus nos non nisi seruos esse, autem etiam seruis natura deteriores, sic argumentandum est: Quòd si Dominus noster, noster cau sa, sic se humiliauit, quanto magis humiliari debemus nos serui alij aliis inuicem? Si hæc nouerit is. Hæc est conclusio; inferri autem debuit, Ergo debetis alij aliorum pedes.
units.tr: For I have given an example. The two reasons for the proposition follow. The first is drawn from the purpose of his action. It is so that there may be an example for them, that they likewise may do the same. We learn, therefore, that the purpose of our actions is not only ourselves but that we ought to have regard for others, so that we may be a good example to others, and others may be moved by our example to act well. For we ought to think in this way: that we are, as I may speak with the Apostle, perpetually perishing in this life, and that the eyes of all others are fixed upon us, and that others tread in our footsteps. While we think this, we ought, as I may speak with the Apostle, to walk carefully and circumspectly, even for the sake of others. For woe to those through whom scandal comes. This applies to all, not only to the ministers of God in the Church. For all are bound by their whole life to instruct others and to set forth the word of life in their actions. Philippians 2; 1 Peter 3. Wives, he says, let them be subject to their own husbands, so that even if some do not obey the word, they may be won without a word by the conduct of their wives. Thus men are won even by life alone, preaching without a word: examples have great power for good and for evil. Verily, verily. The second reason is by a solemn asseveration. It is taken from the lower condition of a servant and a messenger, when this is compared with his lord. We said above that for the sake of humility the eye must be fixed on Christ. Now we learn that the eye must also be fixed on ourselves, and that we must consider that we are nothing but servants and messengers, which is our best condition in this life. Certainly we can never sufficiently lower our condition. Paul said he was the least of the Apostles; indeed, the least of the saints; indeed, he said he was nothing; indeed, he showed himself to be no better than a persecutor, a blasphemer and an insolent man. Thus we can never think or speak of ourselves with sufficient lowliness and modesty. Now when we have seen that we are nothing but servants, and indeed worse by nature than servants, the argument must be this: If our Lord, for our sake, humbled himself thus, how much more ought we servants humble ourselves before one another? If you know these things. This is the conclusion; but it ought to have been inferred: Therefore you ought to wash one another's feet.

units.la: Ephes. 5. 15. pedes lauare. Verùm conclusionem vertit in beatitatis promissionem. Debitum proprie est, quod rependere debemus ob beneficium prius acceptum: Quod vbi factum est,& debitum iam persoluimus, non tenetur cui persolutum est debitum, nos nouo aliquo officio prosequi. At Deus postquam persoluimus illi debitum, & vix millesimam debiti partem, cumulat nos nouis beneficiis, imò ipsa felicitate. Atque hic elucet gratia illa Dei in Christo, quòd debitoribus promittat & det mercedem, non secus ac si non debitum quidem esset quod damus, sed meritum potius. Hic, inquam, vel maximè apparet, gratia Dei, quam Papistæ meritis suis conantur eleuare: nequeenim tam conspicua est gratia, cùm datur beneficium merenti, quàm cùm datur multa debenti & seruo inutili. Nota hic rursus beatitatem inchoari à notitia officij nostri, perfici verò opere.
units.tr: Ephesians 5:15. To wash feet. But he turns the conclusion into a promise of blessedness. A debt, properly speaking, is what we must repay for a benefit previously received. When this has been done and we have already paid the debt, the one to whom the debt has been paid is not bound to bind us by any new obligation. But God, after we have paid him the debt, and scarcely the thousandth part of it, heaps new benefits upon us, indeed happiness itself. And here that grace of God in Christ shines forth, that he promises and gives a reward to debtors, just as if what we give were not a debt at all but rather a merit. Here, I say, the grace of God, which the Papists try to exalt by their merits, appears most of all: for grace is not so conspicuous when a benefit is given to one who deserves it as when it is given to one who owes much and is an unprofitable servant. Note here again that blessedness begins from the knowledge of our duty and is perfected in the doing of it.

units.la: 18 Non de omnibus loquor: ego scio quos elegerim, sed oportet vt impleatur scriptura. Qui edit mecum panem, sustulit aduersum me calcem suum.
units.tr: 18 I do not speak of all of you: I know whom I have chosen, but the Scripture must be fulfilled: He who eats bread with me has lifted up his heel against me.

units.la: 19 Iam nunc dico vobis, priusquam fiat, vt cum factum fuerit credatis me eum esse.
units.tr: 19 From now on I tell you, before it happens, so that when it has happened you may believe that I am he.

units.la: 20 Amen, amen dico vobis, Quando aliquem misero, quisquis eum recipit, me recipit: qui vero me recipit, recipit eum qui misit me.
units.tr: 20 Truly, truly I say to you, whoever receives anyone whom I send receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me.

units.la: RVrsus excipit Iudam, ad quem non vult pertinere promissionē hanc beatitatis. Ex quo discere promissiones istas, quæ in genere dicuntur omnibus, exceptionem tamen pati,& ad aliquos non pertinere. Qui autem exceptionem faciat, is est Deus. Tantùm nos illud scientes, in eo laborare debemus, ne nos ipsi excipiamur, & discedat ab iniustitia, quicunque nominat nomen Christi. Ego scio: q.d. Nõ de omnibus loquor, sed de electis quos ipse ego probè noui. Vide igitur hic fundamētū beatita tis nostræ primū esse in electione: Solidū, inquit, stat funda mentū. Deinde in notitia Dei, vt enim quos præsciuit, præ destinauit vel elegit: ita quos semel elegit, eos perpetuò cognoscit, neque ab oculis vnquam discedere eos patitur. Atque nos virtute huius notitiæ Dei, seruamur ad vitā illam, quam dicit Petrus nobis in cælis seruatam. Sed Veritatis oportet. q.d. Verum quoad Iudam oportet, &c. Hoc testimonium depromptum est ex Psalm. 41. 10. vbi Dauid, tanquam Christi typus, queritur de Achitophele familiari suo quondam & consiliario, tanquam Iudæi typo, cui etiam in eo similis fuit, quòd tandem se ipse suspenderit. Discimus autem hoc loco non minus reprobationem Iudæ & reproborum pendere ex necessitate quàm beatitate piorum: vel enim sola ista necessitas est, quod scriptura ita prædixerit. Neque tamen hac necessitate excusantur reprobi. Nam Dominus postquam dixit, Necesse est vt eueniant offendicula, Verumtamen, inquit, vae homini illi per quem offendiculum euenit: Et de Iudæ facto, filius quidem hominis abit sicut scriptum est de eo, Vae autem homini illi per quem filius hominis proditur: Bonum erat homini illi si natus non fuisset. Hæc optimè cohærent. Iam nunc dico. Hic finem ostendit cur de Iuda prædixerit, nempe ne vbi euenerunt ista, ipsa offendantur. Christus ac Euangelium ipsius comitem habent crucem, Esto particeps, inquit Paulus, afflictionum Euangelij. Orta persecutione statim offenduntur homines Euangelio, qui prius in luce exultare: Non me pudet, inquit, Euangelij Christi. Et Timotheum alloquens, Ne pudeat te(stimonij) Domini, neque te pudeat mei, &c. Quibus significatur, orta semel persecutione, tum pudere hominem Euangelij. Hinc sequitur opus esse vt assiduè aduersus scandalum Euangelij præparemur. Sic Christus cum videret instare horam mortis suæ, assiduè admonuit discipulos crucis propediem futuræ, ne cùm eueniret ipsi offenderentur. Ex eo, inquit, tempore cœpit Iesus indicare discipulis suis se abire, &c. Neque vero satis vnquam præparari possumus aduersus crucis offendiculum: Nam, etiam præparati, sæpe offendimur. Sic Christus discipulis quos tam diligenter præparauit, omnes offendemini in me hac nocte, inquit, & offensi quidem sunt reipsa. Quare nisi potentia Dei sustineantur homines, vt ait Paulus, offendetur, etsi quidem millies præparentur. Nota deinde quòd dicit vt credatis eum esse, nempe Messiam. Non dicit vt non offendamini, quo significat præparatos iam tatum ab eo debere abesse, vt offendantur Euangelio tempore perpersecutionis,vt è contrà tum temporis credere tenean- tur:quemadmodum ex Pauli testimonio ad Timotheŭ repetito liquidò constat.
units.tr: Again he excludes Judas, to whom he does not wish this promise of blessedness to apply. From this we learn that such promises, which are stated in general terms to all, nevertheless admit an exception and do not apply to some. But the one who makes the exception is God. We, knowing this only, ought to labour so that we ourselves are not excluded, and that everyone who names the name of Christ departs from iniquity. I know: that is, I do not speak of all, but of the elect, whom I myself know well. See therefore here that the first foundation of our blessedness lies in election: the firm foundation, he says, stands. Then it lies in the knowledge of God: for as those whom he foreknew he predestined or chose, so those whom he has once chosen he knows for ever, and never allows them to vanish from his eyes. And by virtue of this knowledge of God we are kept for that life which Peter says is reserved for us in heaven. But the Scripture must: that is, it is true with regard to Judas that it must be fulfilled, and so on. This testimony is taken from Psalm 41.10, where David, as a type of Christ, complains of Ahithophel, his former familiar friend and counsellor, as a type of Judas, to whom he was also similar in this, that he at last hanged himself. We learn in this place that the reprobation of Judas and of the reprobate depends no less on necessity than the blessedness of the godly; for this necessity is perhaps only that Scripture so foretold it. Yet the reprobate are not excused by this necessity. For the Lord, after saying, It is necessary that offences come, but woe to that man through whom the offence comes, and concerning the deed of Judas, the Son of Man indeed goes, as it is written of him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed; it would have been good for that man if he had not been born, these agree very well. From now on I tell you: here he shows the reason why he foretold it concerning Judas, namely so that when these things have come to pass they themselves may not be offended. Christ and his gospel have the cross as their companion: Be a partaker, says Paul, of the afflictions of the gospel. As soon as persecution arises, men who previously rejoiced in the light are at once offended by the gospel. I am not ashamed, he says, of the gospel of Christ. And addressing Timothy, Be not ashamed of the testimony of the Lord, nor of me, and so on. By these words it is signified that once persecution has arisen, a man is then ashamed of the gospel. Hence it follows that we must constantly prepare ourselves against the scandal of the gospel. So Christ, when he saw the hour of his death approaching, repeatedly warned the disciples of the cross soon to come, so that they would not be offended when it came upon him. From that time, he says, Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go away, and so on. Nor indeed can we ever prepare ourselves enough against the stumbling-block of the cross: for even when prepared, we are often offended. So Christ said to his disciples, whom he had prepared so diligently, You will all be offended in me this night, and indeed they were offended in fact. Wherefore unless men are sustained by the power of God, as Paul says, they will be offended, even though they have been prepared a thousand times. Note next that he says, that you may believe that I am he, namely the Messiah. He does not say, that you may not be offended, by which he signifies that those already prepared must not be entirely absent from him, so that they are offended by the gospel in the time of severe persecution, whereas conversely at that time they are bound to believe; as is clear from the testimony of Paul to Timothy, cited above.

units.la: Quando aliquem.Nunc consolatur discipulos,propediè discessurus ab iis: Tres sunt hic qui recipiuntur ,seruus, Dominus Iesus,Pater cælestis: Qui ex his vnum recipit, omnes simul recipit:Qui minimum recipit, maximum recipit. Quod fecistis,dicit Dominus in extremo illo iudi- cio,vni ex minimis istis,mihi fecistis. Imò verò hic in recipiendo,ordo est:vt seruus primùm omnium recipiatur. Non enim ait, Qui me recipit, recipit eum quem ego mitto,sed contrà, Qui eum recipit quem ego mitto,me recipit. Contra his vera sunt, Qui recusat ex his vnum , recusat pariter omnes,Qui recusat minimum,recusat maximum,Amen, inquiet Dominus in extremo illo iudicio,dico vobis, quod non fecistis vni ex minimis istis, non fecistis mihi. Inanis est hic prætextus quorundam qui dicunt, quòd si Dominum ipsum haberemus præsentem , omnia in eius gratiam faceremus. Mentiuntur: Qui enim non recipiunt seruum , ne dominum quidem ipsum reciperent.Qui seruum interficerent, dominum interficerent pariter si possent. Nam odium domini est causa odij in seruum , & Domini causa persequuntur seruum. Nouissimus illam parabolam vineæ.Operarij illi qui fer- uos Domini male affecerunt & trucidarunt , intereme-runt quoque ipsius Domini filium vnigenitum, ac hæredem omnium. Quid sibi vult hoc? Quem Prophetarum, inquit Stephanus,non sunt persequuti patres vestri? trucidarút eos qui prænuntiauerunt aduentum iusti illius, cuius nunc vos proditores & occisores fuistis.Notandus autem est hic recipiendi modus, quando, inquit,aliquem misi: quo significat recipiendum seruum qua ratione missus est à Domino:Sic Christus,Qui recipit Prophetam nomine Prophetæ, accipiet mercedem Prophetæ,&c. Ergo in recipiendis hominibus ratio perpetuò haberi debet Domini , vt recipiatur propter Dominum, vt diligatur in Domino.
units.tr: Whoever receives anyone. Now he comforts the disciples, about to depart from them soon. There are three here who are received: the servant, the Lord Jesus, the heavenly Father. Whoever receives one of these receives all together; whoever receives the least receives the greatest. What you have done, says the Lord at that last judgement, to one of the least of these, you have done to me. Indeed the order in receiving is here that the servant is received first of all. For he does not say, He who receives me receives him whom I send, but on the contrary, He who receives him whom I send receives me. Conversely these things are true: whoever rejects one of these rejects them all alike; whoever rejects the least rejects the greatest. Truly, the Lord will say at that last judgement, I tell you, inasmuch as you did not do it to one of the least of these, you did not do it to me. Vain is the pretext of some who say that if they had the Lord himself present, they would do everything for his favour. They lie: for those who do not receive the servant would not receive the Lord himself. Those who would kill the servant would kill the Lord as well, if they could. For hatred of the lord is the cause of hatred of the servant, and they persecute the servant for the lord's sake. Consider the parable of the vineyard. Those labourers who ill-treated and slew the servants of the lord also killed the lord's only-begotten son and heir of all things. What does this mean? says Stephen, Which of the prophets did not your fathers persecute? They slew those who foretold the coming of that Just One, whose betrayers and murderers you have now become. Moreover the manner of receiving is to be noted here: when, he says, I have sent someone, by which he signifies that the servant is to be received for the reason that he was sent by the Lord. So Christ says, He who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet's reward, and so on. Therefore in receiving men, regard ought always to be had to the Lord, so that a man is received on account of the Lord, and loved in the Lord.

units.la: Quum hæc dixisset Iesus , turbatus est Spiritu , & testatus est , dixitque, Amen, amen dico vobis,vnus ex vobis prodet me.
units.tr: When Jesus had said these things, he was troubled in spirit, and testified, and said, Truly, truly I say to you, one of you will betray me.

units.la: 22 Discipuli ergo aspiciebant alij ad alios, dubitantes de quo diceret.
units.tr: 22 The disciples therefore looked at one another, doubting of whom he spoke.

units.la: 23 Erat autem quidam ex discipulis Iesu recumbens in sinu ipsius, nimirum is quem diligebat Iesus.
units.tr: 23 Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved.

units.la: 24 Innuit ergo huic Simon Petrus, vt percontaretur quisnam esset de quo diceret.
units.tr: 24 Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, that he should ask who it was of whom he spoke.

units.la: 25 Ille vero cum incubuisset pectori Iesu, dixit ei, Domine quis est?
units.tr: 25 He then, leaning back on Jesus' breast, said to him, Lord, who is it?

units.la: 26 Respondit Iesus, ille est cui ego intinctam offulam dedero. Et cum intinxisset offulam, dedit Iudæ filio Simonis Iscariotæ.
units.tr: 26 Jesus answered, He it is to whom I shall give a sop when I have dipped it. And when he had dipped the sop, he gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot.

units.la: 27 Et post sumptam offulam, tunc ingressus est in illum Satanas. Dicit igitur ei Iesus, Quod facis, mox facito.
units.tr: 27 And after the sop, Satan entered into him. Jesus therefore said to him, What you do, do quickly.

units.la: 28 Hoc autem nemo accumbentium intelligebat, quorsum ei dixisset.
units.tr: 28 Now no one at the table knew for what purpose he said this to him.

units.la: 29 Quidam enim putabant, quia marsupium habebat Iudas, Iesum ei dixisse, Eme quibus opus est nobis ad festum, aut egenis vt aliquid daret.
units.tr: 29 For some thought, because Judas had the money-bag, that Jesus had said to him, Buy what we need for the feast, or that he should give something to the poor.

units.la: 30 Ille igitur accepta offula, statim exiuit, erat autem nox.
units.tr: 30 He then, having received the sop, went out at once; and it was night.

units.la: Turbatus est Spiritu, id est anima, vt supra 11.27. Turbata est anima mea. Hic interrumpi videtur oratio inchoata sensu iræ paternæ aliquo aduersus peccata nostra. Nam appropinquante illa hora mortis, & extremæ passionis, subinde commotus est ac turbatus animo Dominus, ira Patris sui in peccata hominum, quæ omnia simul ac semel ipse in se recepit. Sic supra 12.27 Turbata est anima mea. Ita nunc de eo dicitur, quòd turbatus fuerit Spiritu, eodem sensu vt videtur. Turbatio hæc, vel perturbatio, non tantum fuit ex metu mortis & passionis mox sequuturæ: verum ex præsenti aliquo sensu iræ. Supra 12.27. Perturbatus animo Dominus, conuertit se ad Patrem suum, Pater, inquit, conserua me ab hac hora: Nunc vero convertit se ad Iudam proditorem: Quo sig-nificatur, quæcunque demum sunt Dei partes in afflictionibus suorum non carere sua culpa instrumenta analia: imo ab eorum manu requirenda singula suspiria, singulas commotiones ac perturbationes animorum, quibus afficiuntur pij. Deus dicitur in vtre suo suorum lachrymas reseruatas habere: nempe vt requirat eas e manu persequutorum, & vt totidem testimonia sint ad-uersus eos, ad iustam ipsorum condemnationem. Notandum etiam hic, quod nunc Iudam proditorem apertius designet, quam supra, vbi eum semel atque iterum excepit, primum quod non esset purus, deinde quod beatas ad eum non pertineret. Nunc vero proditorem designat, & suppresso adhuc nomine. Unde discimus Deum hypocritas paulatim in lucem educere, neque prius designare eos suo nomine aut digito demonstrare, quam opus illud, quod per eos faciendum est, siue proditio sit, siue quid aliud, absoluerit ad gloriam nominis sui: Glorificatur enim Deus etiam proditione Iudæ & aliorum proditorum.
units.tr: Troubled in spirit, that is, in soul, as above 11.27: My soul is troubled. Here the discourse which was begun seems to be interrupted by a sense of the Father's wrath against our sins. For as that hour of death and extreme suffering drew near, the Lord was from time to time moved and troubled in mind by his Father's wrath against the sins of men, which he took into himself all at once and together. So above at 12.27: My soul is troubled. So now it is said of him that he was troubled in spirit, in the same sense as it seems. This troubling, or perturbation, arose not only from fear of death and of the suffering soon to follow, but from some present sense of wrath. Above at 12.27, the Lord, troubled in mind, turned himself to his Father: Father, he said, save me from this hour. Now, however, he turns himself to Judas the traitor. By this is signified that whatever the parts of God may be in the afflictions of his own, the instruments of them are not free from their guilt; indeed each sigh and each agitation and perturbation of mind, by which the godly are affected, is to be required at their hand. God is said to keep the tears of his own in his bottle: that is, to require them from the hand of the persecutors, and that they be so many testimonies against them, for their just condemnation. It is also to be noted here that he now designates Judas the traitor more openly than above, where he had already excluded him once and again, first because he was not clean, and then because blessedness did not pertain to him. But now he designates him as a traitor, while still suppressing his name. Whence we learn that God brings hypocrites into the light gradually, and does not designate them by their name or point them out with a finger until the work which is to be done through them, whether it be betrayal or something else, has been completed to the glory of his name. For God is glorified even by the betrayal of Judas and of the other traitors.

units.la: Discipuli ergo aspiciebant. Discipuli commoti verbis Domini sui, inquisitionem quandam faciunt: primum omnium singuli proculdubio in se descendunt, & se excutiunt: Tum vbi vident se non conscios obiectæ prodi-tionis, conuertunt se alij ad alios. Ita nos omnes cum audimus obiectum aliquod malum, vel denuntiatum iudicium, statim ad inquisitionem & examinationem veniendum. Ac primum omnium, singulos se oportet explorare apud conscientias suas: quo facto deinde ad alios coduerendi sunt oculi. Erat autem quidam ex discipulis. Petrus bene sibi conscius non desistit, sed vrget revelatione proditoris. Ita fieri solet, cum enim conscientia absoluit, tum requirimus iudicium Domini, & appellamus ad eius tribunal. Ita Dauid saepenumero bene sibi conscius, petiit a Domino, vt ipse iudicaret causam suam. Vbi vero conscientia damnat, tum nulla est apparitio coram tribunali Dei. Nam si cor nostrum nos condemnat, potentior est Dominus corde nostro. Vrget autem Petrus per Iohannem, quasi interrogasset. In præsatione præmittuntur causæ, cur per eum id faciat. Prima est ab accubitu eius & situ: recumbebat in sinu eius. Sic enim accubuit Iohannes, vt caput haberet in suo lectulo versus caput Iesu: ideóque facilè attingere potuit sinum Iesu : Nam antiquitus prono pectore accumbere soliti sunt. Subinnui autem videtur amor quo Iohannes ad Christum propius accedebat. Nam reclinatio hæc in sinu significat appropinquationem in corde. Is quem diligebat. Hæc est altera causa ab eo amore quo prosecutus est Dominus Iohannem. Nota igitur hic amorem mutuum. Ille ex amore recumbebat in sinu Christi: Christus eum vicissim dilexit. Nota rursus in amore gradus esse, significatur enim hoc loco specialis quidam amor quo Iohannem prosequutus est Dominus præ cæteris. Neque enim in eo peccamus quòd alios præaliis amplectamur amore, exemplo hoc Christi, si modò omnis amor noster in Christo sit & propter eum. Innuit ergo. Obserua reuerentiam qua prosequuti sunt discipuli Dominum suum simul mensæ accumbentem. Nota etiam hoc, quòd intercessore Iohanne nunc vtatur Petrus: vt non sit quòd Papistæ ex istiusmodi prærogatiuis primatum Petri colligant. Neque enim vsquam legimus de illa Petri prærogatiua tanta, quantam legimus fuisse Iohannis, tum hoc loco, tum aliis, vt capite huius Euangelij 19.20.21. Specialiter enim insignitur Iohannes hac nota, quòd imprimis charus fuerit Domino: & Petrus nunc eo vsus est intercessore, vtpote familiarissimo, sed nugæ sunt istæ Papistarum, quas ideo obtrudunt, vt stabiliant Antichristum suum in cathedra Petri. Incumbens pectori. Iohanni soli videtur designatus Iudas proditor. Nam cum eo videtur secreto Dominus hunc sermonem habuisse, vt videas quid sit Dominum dilini soli desi gnatus. gere, & à Domino diligi, eóque vti familiariter. Deinde vides Petrum, qui vrgebat proditoris demonstrationem, non tamen id consequuti: quo significat Dominus nō retegēdos hypocritas cōtinuò pro arbitratu nostro. Nobis autem cōquiescendū in bona conscientia, donec visum fuerit Domino eos in lucem hanc extrahere. Et post sumptam. Hoc dictum est, non quòd non prius possederit eum Satanas, occupauerítque eius animum: (nam {a}nam supra hoc cap. verf.2. hæc verba legimus, cùm diabolus iam immisisset in cor Iudæ.) Sed significatur his verbis tentationem diaboli inualuisse, & incrementum cœpisse. Occasio fuit ex permissione Domini, cuius hoc fuit signum, Traditio offulæ, & eius sumptio. Sësus enim est, quasi dicatur, permisit eum Dominus sibi ac diabolo, cuius rei signum fuit offulæ traditio, & acceptio. Procul dubio exacerbatus est eius animus in Dominü, quòd videret se proditorem designari, & malitia eius ideo auꝯta est. Discite igitur ex hoc loco non simul & semel absolui tentationem diaboli, sed paulatim ac pedetentim progredi ac augeri prout sese occasiones offerunt. Sic paulatim occupatus est Saul à spiritu illo malo Domini. Quare resistendum est principiis, & si progressus iam aliquis factus est, adhuc desistendum: ne nos tandem totos occuper Satan, & in certam perniciem agat. Quod facis fac. Verba hæc significant plenam traditionem in manus Satanæ, qua permisit, ut sine mora, & quàm celerrimè absoluteret flagitium illud, quod machinatus est. Cùm igitur videmus præcipites ferri ad malum homines, celeriter agere: & (ut loquitur Apostolus) patrare iniquitatem ἐν πνεύματι & certatim, id argumento est, dixisse uis Dominum, Facite citò quod facitis, & dedisse eos quasi præcipites in exitium. Quamobrem non est quòd glorientur impij in eo, quòd sine impedimento, citò & celeriter absoluant quod impiè decreuerunt: id enim argumento est, quòd Dominus sinat ipsos abire in vias suas. Præstat enim multò à malo retrahi, ne id perficiatur, quàm in malo promoueri. Hæc autem nemo. Excepto Iohanne, cui tum in aurem insusurrauit Dominus, omnes ignorabant quid diceretur, vel fieret àDomino. Putabat autè discipuli aliud quid imperari à Domino, & aliud quid Iudam facere, cùm tamen ille iret proditum Dominum suum. Ita fere solet vsu venire: cùm per hypocritas etiam Dominus operatur in gloriam nominis sui, vult eos occultè adeo facere quæ faciunt mala, vt nemo resciat: imò vt putent sæpe homines eos bene agere, vt pauperibus ministrare, vt alia officia honestatis exercere, cùm illi interea eunt proditum Dominum, Euangelium eius, Ecclesiam eius: & agant in-
units.tr: Then the disciples looked at one another. The disciples, moved by the words of their Lord, make a kind of inquiry. First of all, each one doubtless looks into himself and examines his own heart. Then, when they see that they are not conscious of the betrayal charged against them, they turn to one another. So too we, when we hear of some evil charge or threatened judgment, must at once enter upon inquiry and examination. Above all, each of us ought first to test himself before his own conscience, and only after that should our eyes be turned to others. Now there was one of the disciples. Peter, being conscious of his own innocence, does not give up but presses for the revelation of the traitor. This is usually how it goes: when conscience acquits us, we seek the judgment of the Lord and appeal to his tribunal. So David, often conscious of his own integrity, asked the Lord to judge his cause. But when conscience condemns us, there is no appearing before the tribunal of God. For if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart. Peter presses through John, as if he had asked a question. In the preface, the reasons why he does it through him are set out. The first is from John's place at table and his position: he was leaning on Jesus' breast. For John reclined in such a way that his head lay on his couch toward the head of Jesus, and so he could easily reach the breast of Jesus; for in ancient times they were accustomed to recline with the chest forward. Moreover, the love by which John drew nearer to Christ seems to be hinted at, for this leaning on the breast signifies closeness of heart. The one whom he loved. This is the second reason, drawn from the love with which the Lord pursued John. Note, then, a mutual love: John, out of love, leaned on the breast of Christ, and Christ in turn loved him. Note again that there are degrees in love, for this place signifies a special love with which the Lord favoured John above the others. For we do not sin in embracing some with greater love than others, following this example of Christ, provided that all our love is in Christ and for him. He therefore signalled. Observe the reverence with which the disciples regarded their Lord reclining together with them at table. Note also that Peter here uses John as an intermediary, so that the Papists may not gather from such prerogatives a primacy for Peter. For nowhere do we read of any such great prerogative of Peter as we read of John's, both in this place and in others, as in chapters 19, 20 and 21 of this Gospel. For John is especially marked with this note, that he was above all dear to the Lord; and Peter now uses him as intermediary, as one most intimate, but those are trifles of the Papists, which they press upon us so that they may establish their Antichrist in the chair of Peter. Leaning on the breast. Judas the traitor seems to have been pointed out to John alone. For the Lord seems to have spoken this word to him in secret, so that you may see what it is to be singled out by the Lord, to be loved by the Lord, and to enjoy his familiar favour. Then you see Peter, who pressed for the identification of the traitor, yet did not achieve it; by this the Lord signifies that hypocrites are not to be exposed continually at our pleasure. For us, rather, it is enough to rest in a good conscience, until it pleases the Lord to bring them out into the light. And after the morsel. This was said not because Satan had not previously possessed him and occupied his mind (for above, in verse 2 of this chapter, we read these words: when the devil had already put it into the heart of Judas). Rather, these words signify that the temptation of the devil had grown strong and had begun to increase. The occasion came by the permission of the Lord, of which the sign was the giving and receiving of the morsel. The sense is, as if it were said: the Lord permitted him to himself and to the devil, and the sign of this was the giving and receiving of the morsel. Without doubt his mind was inflamed against the Lord, because he saw himself being pointed out as the traitor, and his malice was therefore increased. Learn therefore from this passage that the temptation of the devil is not completed all at once, but advances and grows little by little and step by step, as occasions present themselves. So Saul was gradually seized by that evil spirit of the Lord. Therefore one must resist beginnings, and if some progress has already been made, one must still stop, lest Satan at last take us wholly and drive us to certain destruction. What you do, do quickly. These words signify a complete handing over into the hands of Satan, by which he permitted him to carry out without delay, and as quickly as possible, the crime he had plotted. When therefore we see men rushing headlong into evil and acting swiftly, and (as the Apostle says) committing iniquity in the Spirit [ἐν πνεύματι] and eagerly, this is a sign that the Lord has said, Do quickly what you are doing, and has given them over, as it were headlong, to destruction. Wherefore the wicked have no reason to boast that they carry out quickly and speedily, without hindrance, what they have wickedly decreed; for this is a sign that the Lord allows them to go on their way. For it is far better to be drawn back from evil, so that it is not carried out, than to be advanced in evil. But no one. Except John, into whose ear the Lord then whispered, all were ignorant of what was said or done by the Lord. They thought that the disciples were being commanded something else by the Lord, and that Judas was doing something else, though in fact he was going to betray his Lord. This usually happens in this way: when the Lord also works through hypocrites for the glory of his name, he wills them to do secretly those things which are evil, so that no one knows, indeed so that men often think they act well, such as ministering to the poor and performing other duties of honesty, while meanwhile they go to betray their Lord, his Gospel and his Church; and they carry on meanwhile, under some pretext of what is honest and lawful, something perverse.

units.la: Ephes.4.10. terea sub praetextu aliquo honesti & liciti aliquid peruersi. Accepta offula statim. Non modò celeriter & cito perficit quod decreuit, sed impudenter & in ipso conspectu Domini, quem habebat conscium sceleris sui: voluit tamen in eius oculis & eo inspiciente ire perpetratū scelus suscepturn. Ita enim fit, vt cùm semel permiserit Dominus hominem sibi, nihil ipse tum metuat, non erubescat scelera sua quaecunque perpetrare, hominem occidere, adulterium committere, etiam inspiciēte Deo, etiam in conspectu totius mundi, elata quasi manu; cū, inquam, permiserit eum sibi Dominus & animum eius semel induraverit, vt non immeritò illud semper precemur, Et ne nos inducas in tentationem.
units.tr: Ephes.4.10. Having received the morsel at once. He not only carries out what he has decided quickly and speedily, but shamelessly and in the very sight of the Lord, whom he knew to be witness of his crime; he nevertheless willed to undertake the committing of the crime in his eyes and while he looked on. For thus it happens that, once the Lord has allowed a man to himself, he himself then fears nothing, does not blush to commit whatever crimes, to kill a man, to commit adultery, even with God looking on, even in the sight of the whole world, with his hand lifted high; when, I say, the Lord has allowed him to himself and has once hardened his mind, we may well always pray that prayer: And lead us not into temptation.

units.la: 31 Cum ergo exiuisset, dicit Iesus, Nunc glorificatus est filius hominis, & Deus glorificatus est in eo.
units.tr: 31 When therefore he had gone out, Jesus said: Now the Son of man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.

units.la: 32 Quod si Deus glorificatus est in eo, Deus quoque glorificabit eum in se, & statim glorificabit eum.
units.tr: 32 If God is glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself, and will glorify him straightway.

units.la: 33 Filioli, adhuc paulisper vobiscum sum, quaeretis me: sed sicut dixi Iudaeis, Quò ego vado, vos non potestis venire: ita & vobis nunc dico.
units.tr: 33 Little children, yet a little while I am with you. You will seek me; and as I said to the Jews, Where I go you cannot come, so now I say to you.

units.la: Egressō iam Iuda, incipit Dominus familiariter agere cum discipulis suis, quos satis sciuit innocentes esse, & concionari apud eos de gloria sua propediem futura. Paulò ante Dominus tristis fuit, iam verò & per mediam illam nubem mortis, atque itaque paternae, videt gloriam illam quae mortem insequuntur fuit, eaque apud discipulos suos praedicat. Ita omnes qui sunt Christi, postquam deiecti sunt aspectu & sensu mortis & rerum tristium, statim erigi solet, perque mediam mortem, per tristia omnia videre gloriam illam eiusque aliquo sensu affici. Hic enim ordo est percipiedae gloriae. Necesse est prius percipiamus miseriam quam sentiamus laetitiā in Domino: necesse est, vt cū Paulo loquar, sentiamus prius mortificationē Domini in corpore, quā sentiamus eius vitā. Et Deus glorificatus est. Hoc fundamentum est prioris. Quia
units.tr: With Judas now gone out, the Lord begins to deal familiarly with his disciples, whom he knew well to be innocent, and to preach to them about his glory, which is soon to come. A little before, the Lord was sad; but now, through the middle of that cloud of death and of his approaching departure, he sees that glory which follows death, and he proclaims it to his disciples. So all who belong to Christ, after they have been cast down by the sight and feeling of death and of sad things, are usually raised up at once, and through the middle of death, through all sorrows, they see that glory and are moved by some sense of it. For this is the order of perceiving glory: we must first perceive misery before we feel joy in the Lord; we must, to use Paul's words, feel first the mortification of the Lord in the body before we feel his life. And God is glorified. This is the foundation of what goes before. For

units.la: 2. Cor. 4.10 Quia ille glorificauit Patrem, ideo Pater glorificauit ipsum. Glorificauit Patrem in terris agens, vt videbimus postea cap. 17. postquam absoluit illud opus, quod ipsi a Patre impositum fuit: ita enim ipse argumentatur illo capite: Glorificaui te, & absolui illud opus mihi impositum: Ergo glorifica Filium tuum. Glorificatur etiam Pater in gloria Filij, vt apparet ex principio illius capitis, vt Filius, inquit, te glorificet, sicut dedisti ei authoritatem in omnem carnem, ecce in gloria illa & authoritate Filij glorificatur Pater. Sed hic sermo est de glorificatione ea qua Patrem in terris agens glorificauit. Vide igitur, Dominus honorat se honorantes. Aspirant homines ad honorem & gloriam sine Domino. At re vera non honorantur, nisi qui honorant Dominum & necessitate quadam honorantur, vt ex versu sequenti apparet. Necessaria enim connexio est ista: Si Deus glorificatus est in eo, Deus eum glorificabit. Neque enim fieri potest, vt sit sine gloria, saltem in altero sæculo, qui Deum in vita sua honorat. Et necesse est Christus sit illi lucrum in vita & morte, in cuius vita & morte magnificatur Christus; Glorificabit eum in sese. Hoc est ea gloria quam habuit cum ipso ante iacta mundi fundamenta. Nam gloria Filij est in Patre, eadem nimirum quæ est ipsius Patris: Iohann. 17. 5. Filioli, adhuc. Quæ prædicauit Christus de gloria sua, ea importunia discedendum & migrationem aliquam: ideo nunc per occupationem significat se migraturum, blandè copellans discipulos: non secus ac parens aliquis peregrè abiturus, eam rem cum liberis suis blandè communicaret. Blanda hæc appellatio filiorum arguit absentem Dominum corpore, animo tamen complexum discipulos, vt filiolos. Dum supra cap. 7. Iudæos admonet de discessu suo breui tempore futuro, non ita blandè compellauit, sed discessum suum quasi iudicium interminatus est. Quo significatur Dominum aliter suos de discessu suo admonere, aliter persequutores: Recordari eū suorum vt filiorum, recordari persequutorum vt aduersariorum, ac proinde in ira sua. Quare multum refert quemadmodum Dominus admoneat nos de discessu suo, & de substractione Euangelij sui: in quo habemus eius quasi visibilem praesentiam, blandè ne nos admoneat qui vellemus eum praesentem, an interminetur. Malè enim erit iis à quibus Dominus iratus discedet. Sed sicut dixit Iudaeis. Dici potuit à discipulis, Quò es abiturus? Respòdet, Quò ego abiturus sum, vos non poteritis venire, eodem nimirum modo, quo suprà Iudaeis persequutoribus cap.7. Sed discrimen tamen esse, verba Domini ad Petrum postea, significant. Nam sequentur eum postea suo tempore, persequutores nunquam sequentur. Discrimen etiam est in hac vita: nam sui fruentur per fidem, & spem, & desiderium aliquo modo, eo etiam absente: aduersarij nullo modo.
units.tr: 2. Cor. 4.10 Because he glorified the Father, therefore the Father glorified him. He glorified the Father on earth by his work, as we shall see later in chapter 17, after he had finished the work that the Father had laid upon him. For he argues in that chapter in this way: I have glorified you and finished the work given to me; therefore glorify your Son. The Father is also glorified in the glory of the Son, as appears from the beginning of that chapter, where he says: That your Son may glorify you, as you have given him authority over all flesh. Here, in that glory and authority of the Son, the Father is glorified. But this passage is about the glorifying by which he glorified the Father on earth. See, then, the Lord honours those who honour him. Men aspire to honour and glory without the Lord, but in truth they are not honoured unless they honour the Lord and are honoured by a certain necessity, as appears from the following verse. For this connection is necessary: if God has been glorified in him, God will glorify him. Nor can it be that one who honours God in his life should be without glory, at least in the other age. And it must be that Christ is gain to the one in whose life and death Christ is magnified. He will glorify him in himself. This is the glory that he had with him before the foundation of the world. For the glory of the Son is in the Father, certainly the same as that of the Father himself: John 17.5. Little children, yet a little while. When Christ spoke of his glory, he was speaking of a departure and a kind of migration that was to take place soon. So now, by the diminutive, he signals that he is about to depart, addressing the disciples kindly, just as a parent about to go abroad would share the matter kindly with his children. This tender address of "children" shows the Lord absent in body but still embracing the disciples in spirit, as little children. When in chapter 7 he warned the Jews of his departure, which was to come in a short time, he did not address them so kindly, but threatened them with his departure as a judgment. By this it is signified that the Lord warns his own of his departure in one way, and his persecutors in another: he remembers his own as children, and his persecutors as adversaries, and therefore in his anger. Hence it matters greatly how the Lord warns us of his departure and of the withdrawal of his Gospel, in which we have his presence as it were visibly: whether he warns us kindly, we who would wish him present, or threatens us. For it will go ill with those from whom the Lord departs in wrath. But as I said to the Jews. The disciples could have said: Where are you going? He answers: Where I am going you cannot come, in exactly the same way in which he had said above to the Jewish persecutors in chapter 7. But that there is a difference, the words of the Lord to Peter afterwards show. For they will follow him later, in their own time; the persecutors never will. There is also a difference in this life: for his own enjoy him through faith, hope and desire in some measure, even when he is absent; his adversaries in no way.

units.la: 34 Mandatum novum do vobis, Vt alij alios diligatis: sicut, inquâ, dilexi vos, vt vos etiam diligatis alij alios.
units.tr: 34 A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another.

units.la: 35 Ex hoc omnes cognoscent vos esse discipulos meos, si charitatem habueritis alij in alios.
units.tr: 35 By this all will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.

units.la: 36 Dixit ei Simon Petrus, Domine, quo abis? Respondit ei Iesus, Quò abeo non potes nunc me sequi, postea verò sequeris me.
units.tr: 36 Simon Peter said to him, Lord, where are you going? Jesus answered him, Where I am going you cannot follow me now, but you shall follow me afterwards.

units.la: 37 Dicit ei Petrus, Domine, quare non possum te sequi? animam meam pro te deponam.
units.tr: 37 Peter said to him, Lord, why can I not follow you? I will lay down my life for you.

units.la: 38 Respondit ei Iesus, Animam tuam pro me deponès? Amen, amen dico tibi, non emittet vocem gallus, donec ter me abnegaueris.
units.tr: 38 Jesus answered him, Will you lay down your life for me? Amen, amen I say to you, the cock shall not crow until you have denied me three times.

units.la: Discessurus breui Dominus, instituit suos in charitate, quam, vt videtur Dominus cùm reflaretur in terra in ore perpetuò habuisse, vnde suum mandatum vocat illud charitatis mandatum. & Paulus legem Christi vocat Gal.6.2. imò adeo suum aestimauit, vt ante se non extitisse ipsum significaret, dum nouum dicit, acsi ante ipsum, non fit auditum. Non autem hinc colligendum est, quòd ante Christum non fuerit mandatū charitatis. Quid enim aliud lex sonuit? Sed quod aliud sit ac nouum istud Christi mandatum charitatis in proponedi modo, non in ipsa substantia. Nam lex mandauit quidem charitatem, sed non dedit vires eius implendi. Inscribit
units.tr: The Lord, about to depart soon, instructed his own in love, which, as it seems, he had always kept on his lips while he was still on earth; hence he calls it his commandment, the commandment of love. Paul also calls it the law of Christ (Gal. 6.2). Indeed he so esteemed it as his own that by calling it new he signified that it had not existed before him, as if it had not been heard before him. But it should not be concluded from this that there was no commandment of love before Christ. For what else did the law proclaim? Rather, this new commandment of love of Christ differs in the manner of proposing it, not in its substance. For the law indeed commanded love, but did not give the power to fulfil it. He inscribes

units.la: Dilectio fraterna quo sensu nouū mandatū Christi. Scribit enim charitatem in tabulis cordis carneis: Vnde vetus doctrina dicitur à Iohanne, nempe quoad substantiam ipsam. Noua autem ibidem, quoad formam & modum tractandi, quia tenebræ prætereunt ac lux vera iam lucet, illuminans nimirum corda ac reformans animū, ad hoc vt charitatis doctrina efficax sit. Notandum autem non temere factum quòd habuerit perpetuò in ore charitatem Dominus. Nam vt dici solet, ex abundantia cordis os loquitur. Domini enim cor impletū fuit charitate, dilectione hominum & φιλαδελφια: Hinc charitas illa erupit ac effusa est in admonitionem aliorum. Qui enim ipsi diligunt, diligenter alios admonent. Qui vero à dilectione alieni sunt, nihil iis gratum est nisi odia atque dissentiones: & authores existunt turbarum omnium. Sicut, inquam, ailexi. Exemplum suum proponit, quo admonemur non satis esse, si præcipiamus charitatem aliis, nisi aliis exemplo nostro præeamus, & non tam verbis, quam vita persuadeamus charitatem. Quanta autem charitate nobis præiuerit Dominus, re ipsa cognitum est. Nam maior dilectio esse non potest ea, qua pro amico suo quis moritur: & commendat nobis charitatem, in eo quod pro inimicis suis mortuus est. Cæterum vt moveat nos exemplum charitatis Domini, necesse est ut sentiamus corde penitus quantopere nos dilexerit: Hoc est, vt cum Apostolo loquar, sentiamus effundi in cordibus nostris dilectionem Dei per Spiritum sanctum, qui datus est nobis. Secus, profecto exemplum nudum tantæ charitatis nos non movebit. Nam sensus eius charitatis resoluit ineffabili quadam cum suavitate corda nostra in dilectionem, primum eius qui tantopere dilexit nos: deinde in dilectionem proximi propter eum. Ex hoc omnes. Secundum est argumentum, ex eo quod dilectio sit nota quædam qua cognoscitur nos discipulos esse Christi in eius schola educatos. Nam Christus suos maximè instituit in charitate, eámque quasi cordibus insculpsit, inscripta nimirum lege in cordibus, vt cum Propheta loquar: Ita fit vt indicium & nota discipulorum Christi sit charitas, &, qui velint se ostendere mundo educatos esse in schola Christi, amet alij alios quamplurimum.
