Tam difficile est spem porrigere extra hanc vitam, tum praesertim cùm datur tranquillè & pacatè agere in praesenti ista vita. Ideo solet Deus suos rebus aduersis exercere, ne beatitatem suam in praesentibus collocent, & vt aspiciant spectare non ea quae cernuntur, sed ea quae non cernuntur. Ter enim miseri sumus, si vltra hanc vitam & omnia bona vel corporalia vel etiam spiritualia quae obtingunt nobis in hac vita, spem nostram non porrigamus. Vnde Paulus, Omnium miserrimi sumus, inquit, si in hac solùm vita speramus in Christum. Sed ego veritatem. Hactenus reprehendit eos, verùm magna cum lenitate. Nunc vicissim consolatur, ac serio admonet expedire iis vt abeat. Ideo dicit, Veritatem vobis loquor. Hac praefatione vtitur, vt significet se ex animo loqui, & vt res habet. Hic nota Spiritum dari nobis virtute resurrectionis & glorificationis Christi, vnde supra, Nondum erat spiritus sanctus, quia Iesus nondum erat glorificatus. Christi enim plenitudine illa capimus omnes. Venus autem tu est Christus, cùm glorificatus est. Ergo ex Christo glorificato capimus omnia. Vnde dictum est, Ascendit in sublime, & dedit dona hominibus. Nota hic, cùm duplex sit Christi praesentia, vna corporalis, altera spiritualis, spiritualem hanc meliorem, hoc est, ea quae fit per Spiritum sanctum, repraesentantem Christum cordibus nostris: dico istam praestantiorem ea quae Christi fuit in terris humiliati. Nam de altera illa gloriosa Christi praesentia vt dicam, illa quidem omni exceptione maior est, & virtute illius praesentiae, quae tamen tam longè à nobis dissita est, Spiritum sanctum & omnem Spiritus sancti gratiam accipimus. Tanta quidem gloria ne coelis quidem contineri potest, neque etiam ipso Christo homine, qui caput est membrorum: Quin in terras istas & membra ipsius, quae in terris agunt defluat necesse est. Quod argumento est quòd cum Christum coram videbimus in illo die, tum implendi sumus gloria, & conformanda sunt vilia haec corpora nostra corpori ipsius glorioso.
units.tr: This is a rebuke, as if he said: "Should you not rather rejoice at my departure than grieve over it? Or do you grieve immoderately and beyond measure? Rather, he says, you ought to have asked where I am going, so that knowing where I am going, namely to the Father, you would rejoice for my good and your own. But because I said that I was going away, your heart is filled with sorrow, as if it were all over for me and for you." The disciples of Christ rested so much in his bodily presence that they desired nothing beyond it, nor did they seriously think about any other happiness, either his or their own. So whenever they heard anything about his departure from them, they grieved as if no happiness were to be hoped for from then on. Undoubtedly this grief in others came from a certain carnal sense. We are all so made that if some rest is granted us in this life, if we have enough riches, enough glory, enough pleasure, enough friends and family, we suffer with the greatest difficulty either to be torn away from these very things or to have them torn from us; and we neither think nor hear of any separation without pain. It is so hard to stretch our hope beyond this life, especially when we are allowed to live quietly and peacefully in the present life. Therefore God is accustomed to exercise his people with adversities, so that they do not place their blessedness in present things, and so that they look not at what is seen but at what is not seen. For we are wretched indeed if we do not extend our hope beyond this life and all the goods, whether bodily or even spiritual, which come to us in this life. Hence Paul says: "We are of all men most miserable, if in this life only we have hope in Christ." But I tell you the truth. Hitherto he has rebuked them, but with great gentleness. Now in turn he comforts them and seriously assures them that it is expedient for them that he go away. So he says, I tell you the truth. He uses this preface to signify that he speaks from the heart, and as the matter really is. Here note that the Spirit is given to us by the power of the resurrection and glorification of Christ; hence above: The Holy Spirit was not yet, because Jesus was not yet glorified. For we all receive from that fullness of Christ. Then indeed Christ is truly the one who is glorified. Therefore we receive all things from the glorified Christ. Hence it is said: He ascended on high, and gave gifts to men. Note here that since there is a twofold presence of Christ, one bodily and the other spiritual, I say that this spiritual presence, that is, the one which is effected through the Holy Spirit, representing Christ to our hearts, is better than the presence which Christ had on earth in his humiliation. For as to that other glorious presence of Christ, it is indeed greater than every exception, and by the power of that presence, which is nevertheless so far removed from us, we receive the Holy Spirit and all the grace of the Holy Spirit. Such glory cannot be contained even in the heavens, nor even in Christ as man, who is the head of the members. Indeed it must flow down into these lands and into his members who labour on earth. This is evidence that when we see Christ face to face in that day, we shall be filled with glory, and these vile bodies of ours shall be made conformable to his glorious body.

units.la: Cui sit omnis gloria, Amen.
units.tr: To whom be all glory, Amen.

units.la: 8 Et cùm venerit ille, arguet mundum de peccato, & de iustitia & de iudicio.
units.tr: 8 And when he has come, he will convict the world concerning sin, and concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment.

units.la: 9 De peccato quidem, eo quòd non crediunt in me:
units.tr: 9 Concerning sin, indeed, because they do not believe in me;

units.la: 10 De iustitia verò, eo quòd ad Patrem abeam, & amplius non conspicietis me:
units.tr: 10 but concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father, and you will see me no more;

units.la: 11 De iudicio autem, eo quòd princeps huius mundi condemnatus sit.
units.tr: 11 but concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been condemned.

units.la: Docet his verbis effectum quoddam Spiritus sancti venturi, quod futurum est respectu mundi, hoc est obstinatorum Iudæorum: Qui, cùm Christum habuerunt præsentem, noluerunt credere. Arguet, inquit, mundum. Idem ille Spiritus qui futurus erat consolator Christi discipulis & credentibus quibusque. Mundum, id est obstinatos & incredulos erat reprehensurus, idque ore & ministerio discipulorum. Nota igitur venturi post Christi discessum Spiritus duo effecta, siue officia. Primum respectu credentium, quos consolatur, secundum respectu infidelium, quos arguit ac reprehendit continuò, idque etiam ministerio & ore fidelium illorum, quos consolatur. Per hos enim interius confirmatos mundum & obstinatos illos arguit. Quare omnes iste reprehensiones ex ore fidelium ministrorum, non tam ipsis quàm Spiritui sancto tribuendæ sunt, & qui ministros & eorum reprehensiones ludibrio habent, non tam ipsos homines quàm Spiritum per eos arguentem habent ludibrio: & quid mirum est, conuicti etiam conscientia, per eundem Spiritum, id tamen faciunt, ac sæpe tident, non quidem tam corde, quàm ore. Sed videamus in Spiritu ea quæ reprehensurus est Spiritus. Arguet, inquit, mundum de peccato. Ex his tribus primum quidem pertinet ad ipsum mundum, & obstinatos qui peccatores erant: duo verò ad Christum qui iustus est & iudex gloriosus. Sed sigillatim singula expendamus. Arguet, inquit, mundum. Tum causam reddens, eo, inquit, quod non credunt in me. Peccatum igitur designat incredulitatis nomine, quam ἁμαρτίαν ita insignit, licet non sit vnicum istud incredulitatis peccatum. Sunt enim alia peccata varij generis, verùm peccatum omnium grauissimum est incredulitas, quæ secum vnà trahit reatum maximum & condemnationem grauissimam simul & velocissimam. Ideo dictum est supra, Qui non credit in Filium, iam condemnatus est. Contrà vero fides iustitia potissima est, adeóque sola. Nam ea aufert reatum omnium peccatorum & liberat à condemnatione. Nulla est condemnatio iis qui sunt in Christo Iesu. Atque hinc vsurpata est præclara illa sententia: Nullum peccatum nisi infidelitas, nulla iustitia nisi fides. Non quòd sola infidelitas sit peccatum, sed quòd infidelitate, vt ait Augustinus, manente, maneat peccatum omne, & ea rursus decedente aboleatur; quod reatum, peccatũ aliud quodcunque. Et certè peccantibus in tam clara luce Euangelij quouis modo, siue per adulterium, siue homicidium, siue per furtum, &c. adscribendum est maximè infidelitati, & obstinationi cordis, qua tantæ luci resistitur. Quòd si quis exemplum huius rei requirat, legat illum locum, qui 1. Corinth. 14. 24. de infideli siue idiota ingredienti in Ecclesiam & cœtum fidelium, dum quis prophetat, arguitur, inquit, diiudicatur, & manifesta fiunt occulta corde ipsius. Id etiam omnes nos quotidie in nobisipsis experimur, dum intersumus verbo Dei prædicato. Certè conuincimur peccati si non conuertimur à Spiritu Dei sancto. Secundum est id de quo arguet mundum: Arguet, inquit, de iustitia. Nempe Christi, quòd sanctus ille sit & iustus, vt vocatus est Act. 7. 52. Iudæorum enim increduli inter iniustos & fures eum numerarunt: At Spiritus sanctus conuicit eos, post discessum ipsius, quòd iustissimus fuerit. Constitit autem eum iustum fuisse, ex eo quod ex mortuis resurgens, abiit ad Patrem. Nisi enim immunis fuisset ab omni labe peccati, non fuisset ei ad patrem aditus, neque ingressus illi patuisset in sanctuarium illud cœleste. Nihil enim immundum ingreditur cœlos. Ergo ex eo quòd receptus sit in cœlos arguit Spiritus Sanctus Christum iustum ac innocentem. Huius rei exemplum habemus Act. 2. 23. Vbi paulò post ascensionem Christi in cœlos, Petrus vel potius Spiritus sanctus per Petrum, obiicit Iudæis, quòd quem illi sceleratis manibus trucidárunt, Dominus excitarit ex mortuis, & in cœlis glorificárit. Sic eos tum convicit, & conscientiam eorum sic compunxit Spiritus sanctus, vt responderent Petro ac Apostolis aliis, Quid faciemus, viri fratres? nempe vt liberemur ab innocenti illo sanguine, ibid. Tertium autem de quo arguet eos Spiritus sanctus est de iudicio. Nempe quòd non tantùm iustus sit Christus, sed etiam mundi ille Iudex sit gloriosus. Omne iudicium dedit filio, suprà. Id autem ex eo arguet atque convincet quòd Christi morte iudicatus ac condemnatus sit princeps mundi, hoc est, is qui in mundo potest plurimum. Christus enim insidens cruci suæ tanquam currui triumphali imperia ac potestates omnes aduersarias spoliauit ac palàm in triumpho traduxit. Nam etsi, vt dicitur alibi, diabolus efficax sit etiam adhuc in filiis incredulitatis, tamen iam supèratus est à Christo ac reseruatur catenis caliginis ad condemnationem futuram. Atque victum eum in sese sentiunt & experiuntur fideles, in quibus mortificatum est peccatum. Nam hæc coniuncta sunt, regnum diaboli & regnum peccati. Infideles etiam quos excæcat princeps huius sæculi, ne irradiet eos lumen Euangelii, vt loquitur Apostolus: Infideles etiam ipsi, inquam, convincuntur eius quod diabolus iam sit superatus, ac conscientiæ ipsorum convictæ luce ista Euangelij testantur se inseruire nisi mancipio misero, hoc est diabolo: ita tamen indurati sunt, vt nialint seruì detineri sub peccato & diabolo, quàm liberi sub Christo. Ex his quę dicta sunt, hoc in summa obseruamus: Spiritum sanctum continuò Christo absente in reditum ipsius ex duobus alterutrũ facere, vel conuertere vel convincere: Nam quos non conuertit & per ministerium verbi captiuos ducit ad obedientiam Christo, vt loquitur Apostolus, eos profecto convincit: & contumaciam eorum vindicat, vt ibidem loquitur vers.6. & convictos demum sistet coram iudice suo Christo in postremo illo die.
units.tr: He teaches, in these words, a particular effect of the Holy Spirit that is to come, which will be directed towards the world, that is, the stubborn Jews: although they had Christ present with them, they refused to believe. He will convict, he says, the world. That same Spirit, who was to be the Comforter of Christ's disciples and of all believers, was also to rebuke the world, that is, the obstinate and unbelieving, and to do so through the mouth and ministry of the disciples. Note, then, that the Spirit who was to come after Christ's departure has two effects, or offices. The first concerns the believers whom he comforts; the second concerns the unbelievers whom he convicts and rebukes continually, and this too through the mouth of those same believers whom he comforts. For it is by means of these men, inwardly strengthened, that he convicts the world and those obstinate people. Therefore all these rebukes coming from the mouths of faithful ministers are to be ascribed not so much to the men themselves as to the Holy Spirit, and those who make a mockery of the ministers and their rebukes are mocking not so much the men as the Spirit who convicts through them. And it is no wonder that, even when they are convicted in conscience by the same Spirit, they nevertheless do this, and often gnash their teeth, not so much in heart as in mouth. But let us see what the Spirit is going to rebuke. He will convict, he says, the world of sin. Of these three, the first indeed pertains to the world itself and to the obstinate, who were sinners; the other two pertain to Christ, who is righteous and the glorious judge. But let us weigh each one separately. He will convict, he says, the world. Then he gives the reason: because, he says, they do not believe in me. So by the name of unbelief he designates sin, which he marks with the word ἁμαρτία, although this unbelief is not the only sin. For there are other sins of various kinds, but the most grievous sin of all is unbelief, which carries with it the greatest guilt and at the same time the most grievous and most swift condemnation. That is why it was said above, He who does not believe in the Son is already condemned. On the contrary, faith is the chief righteousness, and indeed the only one. For it takes away the guilt of all sins and frees from condemnation. There is no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. Hence that famous saying has been current: no sin except unbelief, no righteousness except faith. Not that unbelief alone is sin, but that, as Augustine says, while unbelief remains, all sin remains, and when it departs, all sin is abolished; the guilt of which, any other sin whatever... And certainly those who sin in such a clear light of the Gospel, whether by adultery, murder, theft, or whatever, must be ascribed above all to unbelief and to the obstinacy of heart by which such great light is resisted. If anyone wants an example of this, let him read that passage in 1 Corinthians 14:24 about the unbeliever or layman who comes into the Church and the assembly of the faithful, while someone is prophesying: he is convicted, it says, he is judged, and the secrets of his heart are made manifest. All of us also experience this daily in ourselves, whenever we are present at the preaching of the Word of God. Certainly we are convicted of sin if we are not converted by the Holy Spirit. The second thing about which the Spirit will convict the world is this: he will convict, he says, concerning righteousness. Namely, the righteousness of Christ, that he is holy and just, as he was called in Acts 7:52. For the unbelieving Jews numbered him among the unrighteous and thieves; but the Holy Spirit convicts them, after his departure, that he was most righteous. It has been established that he was righteous from the fact that, rising from the dead, he went away to the Father. For unless he had been free from every stain of sin, he would not have had access to the Father, nor would an entrance have been opened to him into that heavenly sanctuary. For nothing unclean enters the heavens. Therefore, from the fact that he was received into the heavens, the Holy Spirit proves Christ to be just and innocent. We have an example of this in Acts 2:23, where shortly after Christ's ascent into the heavens, Peter, or rather the Holy Spirit through Peter, objects to the Jews that the Lord has raised up him whom they slew with wicked hands, and has glorified him in the heavens. So the Holy Spirit then convicted them and pricked their conscience, so that they answered Peter and the other Apostles, What shall we do, men and brothers? Namely, how we may be freed from that innocent blood, ibid. The third thing about which the Spirit will convict them is judgment. Namely, that Christ is not only righteous but is also the glorious judge of the world. He has given all judgment to the Son, above. He will convict and prove this from the fact that by Christ's death the prince of this world was judged and condemned, that is, he who has the greatest power in the world. For Christ, mounted on his cross as on a triumphal chariot, stripped all hostile powers and authorities and openly led them in triumph. For although, as is said elsewhere, the devil is still active even now in the sons of unbelief, nevertheless he has already been overcome by Christ and is kept in the chains of darkness until the future condemnation. And believers, in whom sin has been mortified, feel and experience him as conquered in themselves. For these things are joined together: the kingdom of the devil and the kingdom of sin. Even unbelievers, whom the prince of this age blinds so that the light of the Gospel does not shine on them, as the Apostle says, even unbelievers, I say, are convicted that the devil has already been overcome, and their consciences, convicted by this light of the Gospel, testify that they serve no master but a wretched slave, that is, the devil. Yet they are so hardened that they would rather be held as slaves under sin and the devil than be free under Christ. From what has been said, we observe this in summary: that the Holy Spirit, while Christ is absent until his return, makes one of two things happen: either he converts or he convicts. For those whom he does not convert, and whom through the ministry of the Word he leads captive to obedience to Christ, as the Apostle says, these he certainly convicts, and he avenges their obstinacy, as the same Apostle says in verse 6, and at last he will bring them, convicted, before their judge Christ on that last day.

units.la: 12 Adhuc multa habeo, quæ vobis dicam, sed nunc non potestis portare.
units.tr: 12 I still have many things to tell you, but you cannot bear them now.

units.la: 13 Quùm autem venerit ille, id est Spiritus illè
units.tr: 13 But when that one comes, that is, the Spirit of

units.la: 2. Cor. 4. 4. veritatis, introducet vos in omnem veritatem: non enim loquetur a semetipso, sed quaecunque audierit loquetur, & quae ventura sunt renuntiabit vobis.
units.tr: 2 Cor. 4. 4. of truth, he will guide you into all truth; for he will not speak of himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will declare to you the things that are to come.

units.la: 14 Ille me glorificabit, quia de meo accipiet, & renuntiabit vobis.
units.tr: 14 He will glorify me, because he will receive of mine and declare it to you.

units.la: 15 Omnia quae habet Pater sunt mea: propterea dixi illum de meo accepturum, & renuntiaturum vobis.
units.tr: 15 All that the Father has is mine; therefore I said that he will receive of mine and declare it to you.

units.la: HIc inceptum illum sermonem de officio Spiritus venturi interpellat ac rescindit. Causam subiungit, Quia nunc, inquit, non potestis portare. Est enim causa ab impotentia ipsorum & infirmitate. Sunt & aliae causae, hoc nominatim quod hora mortis instaret, ut videre est supra 14. 30. Ad hanc accedebat quod omnia quae audiuit a Patre, iam nota fecerit iis. Ergo haec non ita dicta sunt iis nunc, quasi non omnia illis iam expoluerit: sed quod ipsi visum fuerit non nunc exponere aut repetere ea, sed remittere eos potius ad illum Spiritum, quem propediem erant accepturi, adeo ut non tam ad hanc locus traditionibus Papisticis. Notandum hoc loco Christum rationem quidem habere infirmitatis & ruditatis discipulorum suorum, admonere tamen esse multa praeterea altiora & profundiora: ut nimirum excitet in iis desiderium proficiendi continuo ac pergendi ad maiora. Idem profecto desiderium debet esse in omnibus nobis, neque contenti esse debemus primis illis rudimentis ac elementis religionis, sed perpetuo ad altiora aspirare. Neque etiam contenti esse debemus quacunque etiam perfectissima cognitione, quae contingit in hac vita (Nunc enim cognoscimus tantum ex parte, & videmus quasi in speculo) sed perpetuo aspirare debemus ad plenam perfectamque illam cognitionem, quae futura est in altera demum vita, cum Dominum coram videbimus, & cognoscemus sicut et edocti eximus. Profana enim est ista vox quorundam hominum, qui dicunt satis se habere, quod Credo illud suum & Pater noster, ut loquuntur, intelligunt, neque supra haec sapere se velle dicunt. Ignorant enim quod qui non feruntur ad perfectionem,
units.tr: Here he interrupts and cuts short this discourse he had begun about the office of the Spirit who is to come. He adds the reason: because now, he says, you cannot bear it. The reason lies in their incapacity and weakness. There are also other reasons, namely that the hour of death was at hand, as can be seen above in 14:30. To this was added that he had already made known to them all that he had heard from the Father. Therefore these things were not said to them now as if he had not already explained everything to them, but because it seemed good to him not to set out or repeat those things now, and to refer them rather to that Spirit whom they were soon to receive; so that this passage is not to be taken as support for Papistical traditions. It should be noted here that Christ indeed took account of the weakness and rawness of his disciples, yet reminded them that there are many other things higher and deeper, so that he might stir up in them a desire to advance continually and to press on to greater things. Certainly the same desire ought to be in all of us, and we should not be content with those first rudiments and elements of religion, but should always aspire to higher things. Nor should we be content with any knowledge, however perfect, that is attainable in this life (for now we know only in part, and we see as in a mirror), but we should always aspire to that full and perfect knowledge which will be in the other life, when we shall see the Lord face to face and shall know as we also are known. Profane indeed is the saying of certain men who say that it is enough for them to understand their so-called Creed and Lord's Prayer, and say that they do not wish to be wise beyond these things. For they do not realise that those who are not carried on to perfection must necessarily slip back. How great the danger attached to this is, let them read Hebrews 6:4. Therefore our joy ought to lie in this, that we learn something new every day. And certainly those who have seriously tasted once those heavenly things...

units.la: Infirmitati suorum consulit Christus. sectionem, necesse est ipsi relabantur. Quanto autem cū periculo illud cōiunctū sit legant Apost. Heb. 6. 4. Quare gaudiū nostrum oportet sit in eo, vt quotidie aliquid addiscamus. Et certè qui serio degustarunt semel illa cœlestia, accenduntur perpetuo maiori desiderio proficiendi in iis. Expetite, inquit Petrus, sincerum illud lac sermonis, si modò gustastis quàm benignus sit Dominus. Quum autem venerit. Occupatio: Ne enim putarent neminem doctorum, occurrit, admonetque Spiritum sanctum cùm venerit doctorum: quo significat Spiritū sanctum potiorem futurum doctorem post decessum ipsius, quàm sit ipse in præsentia sine Spiritus efficacia. Dominus enim efficax est, non quidem tam per præsentiam corporalem, aut per viuam ipsius vocem, quàm per Spiritum suum. Postquam cor eorum conuersum fuerit ad Dominum, tolletur velamen: Nam Dominus Spiritus ille est, vbi autem Spiritus ille Domini, illic libertas. Vbi cum viua voce nō concurrit Spiritus tanquam internus quidam doctor, nihil prodest viua vox. Imò vox hominunc​ionis cuiusuis, cum Spiritus Domini efficacia illa, melior est voce ipsius Domini, si cum ea non est visum Spiritum suum coniungere. Quamobrem non tam ad voces hominum nobis attendendum est, quàm ad Spiritum sanctum. Neque tā ad externum doctorem, quàm ad internum illū, ad hoc, vt simus
units.tr: Christ provides for the weakness of his people. [...] they must necessarily fall back. How great the danger attached to this, let them read the Apostle, Heb. 6. 4. Therefore our joy must lie in this, that we learn something new every day. Certainly those who have seriously tasted those heavenly things are kindled with a constant and greater desire to make progress in them. "Desire," says Peter, "the sincere milk of the word, if indeed you have tasted how gracious the Lord is" (1 Pet. 2. 2). When he comes. Occupatio: lest they should think that none of the teachers is present, he anticipates the objection and reminds them of the Holy Spirit, when he comes. By this he signifies that the Holy Spirit will be a greater teacher after his departure than he himself is in person without the efficacy of the Spirit. For the Lord is effective not so much through his bodily presence, or through his living voice, as through his Spirit. When their heart shall have turned to the Lord, the veil shall be taken away. For the Lord is that Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty. Where the Spirit does not come together with the living voice as an inward teacher, the living voice profits nothing. Indeed, the voice of any man whatever, when the efficacy of the Spirit of the Lord is present, is better than the voice of the Lord himself, if his Spirit is not joined with it. Therefore we must attend not so much to the voices of men as to the Holy Spirit; and not so much to the external teacher as to that inward one, so that we may be...

units.la: Id est, Spiritus. In hac appellatione inest obscurè argumentū, quo arguit Spiritum sanctum doctorū veritate. Neq; enim fieri potest quin Spiritus ille verax doceat veritatem. Vult igitur eum quicunque tandem institui se cupiat à Spiritu sancto, hoc tanquam præiudicium animo suo habere, quòd Spiritus is, qui loquitur in verbo, verax sit. Vix enim fidem habemus homini, nisi ei quę persuaderemus nobis veracem esse. Si igitur primum sit veritatis amor, deinde præiudicium de Spiritu illo in verbo loquente, quòd is verax sit: tum profectò doctrinam Spiritus & veritatem auidè & suauiter imbibimus. Neque certè est aliud fundamentum cognitionis & fidei melius aut firmius, quàm sit hoc, nempe quòd Spiritus loquens in verbo hoc scripto verax sit in omnibus, quódque hæc sola sit veritas. Deducet vos in omnem veritatem. Neque enim Spiritus ille veritatis aliquam tantum particulam veritatis docuit Apostolos: sed totam & integram: Ergo Apostolica doctrina, plena perfectaque fuit. Ergo etiam scripta Apostolica suis numeris absoluta sunt. Nihil enim docuerunt quod non re ipsa sit scriptum. Etsi enim hodierno die viuerent Apostoli, nihil traderent nisi quod in his scriptis quae habemus vel expresse ponitur; vel ex necessario consequenti sequitur. Neque etiam Spiritus sanctus docet quenquam intus & in corde, nisi quod in verbo scripto continetur. Neque denique vera fides percipit aliam doctrinam quam eam quae in verbo hoc scripto continetur. Nunquam enim ego veram illam fidem existimaui, quae sine delectu abripi se patitur quouis doctrinae vento. Neque verum illum Spiritum esse, qui non potest discernere scriptam hanc veritatem a fictis illis traditionibus, sed omnia iuxta recipit docetque interius hominem. Non enim loquetur. Ratio ab authore veritatis, quam docebit Spiritus: Author est non tantum Spiritus, sed filius: Ergo is commendat doctrinam Spiritus, tanquam suam. Quicquid docuit filius, illud totum accepit a Patre, vt passim restatur in hoc Euangelio. Quicquid docet Spiritus, illud totum accipit a filio. Ergo doctrina ista Euangelii non procedit ab vna tantum Trinitatis persona, sed est decretum quasi totius Trinitatis, & vox vna eademque ab omnibus procedens. Verum certo quodam ordine: primum enim loquitur Pater, deinde filius, tertio Spiritus sanctus. Quare oportet magnam authoritatem esse huius doctrinae Euangelicae. Decreta illa quae in regum Conciliis constituta sunt, magnam habent authoritatem, & maiorem quidem quam verbum solius principis seorsim a Concilio suo positi. Quo igitur loco esse oportet decretum gloriosae illius Trinitatis? Christus passim admonet se nihil loqui, nisi quod a Patre accepit, hoc est, nisi quod in Concilio illo Trinitatis prius conclusum est: vt significet oportere magnam fidem haberi verbo illi quod sit tantae authoritatis. Ex ore etiam comminatur graue iudicium non credenti, quod sermo ipsius acceptus sit a Patre: hoc est, quod decretum sit commune totius Trinitatis. Nam profecto cum tanta sit authoritas verbi huius Euangelici: alterum horum sequetur neces-
units.tr: That is, the Spirit. In this appellation there is hidden an argument, by which he proves the Holy Spirit by the truth of the teachers. For it cannot be that the Spirit of truth should teach anything but the truth. He wishes, therefore, that whoever at last desires to be instructed by the Holy Spirit should hold this as a presupposition in his mind: that the Spirit who speaks in the Word is true. For we scarcely trust a man unless we are persuaded that he is truthful. If, therefore, the love of truth comes first, and then the presupposition about that Spirit speaking in the Word, that he is true, then certainly we drink in the Spirit's teaching and the truth eagerly and sweetly. Nor is there surely any other foundation of knowledge and faith better or firmer than this: namely, that the Spirit speaking in this written Word is true in all things, and that this alone is the truth. He will lead you into all truth. For that Spirit of truth did not teach the Apostles only some small part of the truth, but the whole and entire truth. Therefore the Apostolic doctrine was full and perfect. Therefore also the Apostolic writings are complete in their parts. For they taught nothing that is not in fact written. For even if the Apostles were living today, they would teach nothing except what is either expressly set down in these writings which we have, or follows from them by necessary consequence. Nor does the Holy Spirit teach anyone inwardly and in the heart anything except what is contained in the written Word. Finally, true faith receives no doctrine other than that which is contained in this written Word. For I have never regarded as true that faith which allows itself to be swept away without discernment by any wind of doctrine; nor is that the true Spirit which cannot distinguish this written truth from those invented traditions, but receives all things indiscriminately and teaches the inner man accordingly. For he will not speak on his own. The reason is drawn from the author of the truth whom the Spirit will teach: the author is not only the Spirit but the Son. Therefore he commends the Spirit's doctrine as his own. Whatever the Son taught, he received all of it from the Father, as is repeatedly stated in this Gospel. Whatever the Spirit teaches, he receives all of it from the Son. Therefore this doctrine of the Gospel does not proceed from one person of the Trinity only, but is, as it were, the decree of the whole Trinity, and one and the same voice proceeding from all. Yet it proceeds in a certain order: for the Father speaks first, then the Son, and third the Holy Spirit. Hence this Gospel doctrine must have great authority. The decrees that are established in the councils of kings have great authority, and indeed greater than the word of a prince alone, set forth apart from his council. In what place, then, should the decree of that glorious Trinity be? Christ repeatedly reminds us that he says nothing except what he received from the Father, that is, nothing except what was previously concluded in that council of the Trinity; so that he signifies that great faith must be given to that word, since it has such authority. He also threatens with a grave judgment the one who does not believe that his speech was received from the Father, that is, that it is a decree common to the whole Trinity. For surely, since the authority of this Gospel word is so great, one of two things must follow:

units.la: Iohan. 11. 44. &c. necessario, vel fides ei adhibenda est, vel non credentem manet grauissimum iudicium.
units.tr: Iohan. 11. 44. &c. necessarily, either faith must be given to it, or a most grievous judgment remains for the one who does not believe.

units.la: Quae fit dicturus Spiritus ostendit: In summa, Quae ventura sunt, inquit, renuntiabit, nempe quae ventura sunt post decessum ipsius. Intelligitilla beneficia, quae post Christi ascensionem & glorificationem tam copiose in terras effusa sunt, acquisita nimirum morte eius, & applicata resurrectione ex mortuis, cuiusmodi sunt remissio peccatorum, Iustificatio, vita aeterna, vt nihil de donis illis extraordinariis loquamur quae in Apostolos & primitiuam illam Ecclesiam sunt effusa. Haec sunt renuntiata per Spiritum sanctum, hoc est, per Spiritum sancti applicata interius per illuminationem mentis, & omnino Spiritus sancti internam operationem. Nisi enim Spiritus sanctus nos doceat, frustra offertur remissio peccatorum, frustra vita, frustra omnia. Ille me glorificabit. Rursus summa doctrinae Spiritus sancti apertius & speciatius proponit: huc enim redibunt omnia, quae renuntiabit, quod Christum in omnibus, & omni doctrinae suae parte glorificabit. Causa autem addita est: Quia de meo accipiet quod renuntiabit, q.d. legationem suam a me habebit.
units.tr: He shows what the Spirit is about to say: In sum, he says, he will declare the things that are to come, namely, the things that are to come after his departure. Understand those benefits which, after Christ's ascension and glorification, were poured out upon the earth so abundantly, obtained certainly by his death and applied by his resurrection from the dead, such as the remission of sins, justification, and eternal life; not to speak of those extraordinary gifts which were poured out upon the Apostles and the primitive Church. These are declared by the Holy Spirit, that is, they are applied inwardly by the Spirit through the illumination of the mind, and in short by the inward operation of the Holy Spirit. For unless the Holy Spirit teaches us, the remission of sins is offered in vain, life in vain, everything in vain. He will glorify me. Again he sets forth the sum of the Holy Spirit's doctrine more clearly and specifically: for everything that he will declare comes back to this, that he will glorify Christ in all things and in every part of his teaching. The reason is added: because he will take of what is mine and declare it, as if to say, he will have his commission from me.

units.la: Qui autem legatur ab aliquo, is omnia loquitur ad gloriam & utilitatem eius, a quo legatur. Filius legatus est, & missus a Patre, ideo Patrem glorificauit in terris, vt ipse loquitur capite sequenti, verf. 7. Spiritus sanctus legatur a filio, ideo omnia ad gloriam filij loquitur. Sed quomodo glorificat filium? Non enim audimus vocem eius: Glorificat filium ministerio verbi huius & opera hominum infirmorum. Quare quisquis non in omni parte doctrinae suae glorificat Christum, Spiritus sanctus per eum non loquitur. Qui merita hominum, sanctorum invocationem, & alia id genus docet, Spiritus sanctus per eum non loquitur, & per hoc discernuntur Spiritus: Quod qui Christum tantum docet, Spiritus Christi sit. Qui praeter Christum docet quicquam, Spiritus antichristi sit. Vide 1. Iohan. 4. 2. 3. Atque hic est ille doctor qui auditur in papatu hodierno die. Omnia quae habet. Occupatio: Annon renuntiabit quae accepit a Patre? Respondet, Omnia quae habet Pater mea sunt, & mihi tradita sunt, ergo a me immediate accipiet quae renuntiabit omnia. Nota igitur, Spiritus sanctus immediate mittit
units.tr: For whoever is sent by someone speaks everything for the glory and benefit of the one by whom he is sent. The Son is sent and dispatched by the Father; therefore he glorified the Father on earth, as he himself says in the following chapter, verse 7. The Holy Spirit is sent by the Son; therefore he speaks everything for the glory of the Son. But how does he glorify the Son? For we do not hear his voice: he glorifies the Son through the ministry of this Word and the work of weak men. Therefore whoever does not glorify Christ in every part of his teaching, the Holy Spirit does not speak through him. Whoever teaches the merits of men, the invocation of saints, and things of that kind, the Holy Spirit does not speak through him; and by this the spirits are discerned. Whoever teaches Christ only, is of the Spirit of Christ; whoever teaches anything besides Christ, is of the spirit of antichrist. See 1 John 4. 2, 3. And this is that teacher who is heard in the Papacy today. All things that he has. Occupatio: will he not declare what he has received from the Father? He answers: All things that the Father has are mine, and have been delivered to me; therefore he will receive from me immediately all the things he will declare. Note, therefore, that the Holy Spirit is sent immediately...

units.la: Quae fit dicturus Spiritus S. tur à filio, mittitur quidem à Patre, sed mediatè per filiū. Vnde suprà, Quem Pater mittet in nomine meo, & quem ego mittam a Patre. Idem iudicium est de ministris verbi omnibus in Ecclesia. A Christo immediatè non autem à Patre mittuntur. Vnde de Christo dicitur quòd post ascensionem dederit alios Apostolos, alios Prophetas, alios Euangelistas, &c. Et Paulus de se sic loquitur, Quòd sit Apostolus Christi, verum per voluntatē Dei, nempe Patris. Significat enim se immediatè à Christo missum esse, mediatè verò à Patre. Fundamentum autē huius rei est, quòd omnia quæ Pater habet, filij sint, & data sit illi omnis potestas in cælo & in terra. Hinc est quod Spiritus sanctus immediatè sit ab illo: Apostoli & ministri omnes in Ecclesia immediatè sunt ab illo: omnia denique dona immediatè sunt ab illo. Non quidem id volo Patrem omnibus sese exuisse, ac spoliasse. Nam sequenti cap.verf. 10. filius dicit, Mea omnia tua sunt, & tua mea sunt. Ergo Patris sunt etiam ea, quæ data sunt filio, & filius est quasi thesaurus quidam Patris, & nos omnia accipimus à Patre, sed per manum filij. Ideo Patrem glorificamus, tanquam fontem omnium beneficiorum, filium verò tanquam mediatorem, Spiritum sanctum denique tanquam sanctificatorem glorificamus, & parem omnibus gloriam tribuimus, quia ipsi pares sunt gloria ac maiestate.
units.tr: He is about to speak, the Holy Spirit... is sent indeed by the Father, but mediately through the Son. Hence above: "Whom the Father will send in my name," and "whom I will send from the Father." The same judgment holds concerning all the ministers of the Word in the Church: they are sent immediately by Christ, not by the Father. Hence it is said of Christ that after his ascension he gave some apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, and so on. And Paul speaks of himself thus, that he is an Apostle of Christ, but by the will of God, namely the Father. For he signifies that he was sent immediately by Christ, but mediately by the Father. The foundation of this matter is that all things that the Father has are the Son's, and all power in heaven and on earth has been given to him. Hence it is that the Holy Spirit is immediately from him; the Apostles and all the ministers in the Church are immediately from him; in short, all gifts are immediately from him. I do not wish, indeed, to say that the Father has stripped and despoiled himself of all things for all. For in the following chapter, verse 10, the Son says, "All mine are yours, and yours are mine." Therefore those things which have been given to the Son are also the Father's, and the Son is as it were a treasury of the Father, and we receive all things from the Father, but through the hand of the Son. Therefore we glorify the Father as the fountain of all benefits, the Son as the mediator, and finally the Holy Spirit as the sanctifier, and we give equal glory to all, because they are equal in glory and majesty.

units.la: 16 Paulisper, & non conspicietis me, & rursum Paulisper, & videbitis me: quia ego vado ad Patre.
units.tr: "A little while, and you will not see me; and again a little while, and you will see me, because I go to the Father."

units.la: 17 Dixerunt ergo quidam ex discipulis eius ad alios, Quid est hoc quod dicit nobis, Paulisper & non conspicietis me, & rursus, Paulisper & videbitis me: & Quia ego vado ad Patrem?
units.tr: Then some of his disciples said to one another, "What is this that he says to us, 'A little while, and you will not see me, and again, a little while, and you will see me,' and, 'Because I go to the Father'?"

units.la: 18 Dicebant ergo, Quid illud est quod dicit, Paulisper? nescimus quid loquatur.
units.tr: So they said, "What is this that he says, 'A little while'? We do not know what he is talking about."

units.la: Rursus admonet de decessu suo, & ne graue iis videatur, simul consolatur eos, promittens se breui reditur um ad eos, nempe per Spiritum suum: ideòque subiungit, Quia ego vado ad Patrem, & propterea glorificandus dus sum, vt fiatis participes gloriæ meæ. Nam Christus etsi morte sua promeritus sit nobis beneficia omnia, tamen non proueniunt ea ad nos, nisi virtute resurrectionis, ascensionis & glorificationis ipsius. Nam vt sacerdos humiliatus in terris promeritus est nobis omnia: at vero vt Rex glorificatus communicat nobis ea ipsa bona quæ morte sua promeritus est. Quemadmodum igitur Dominus ante mortem & ascensionem suam ad Patrem spem discipulis suis fecit, quòd recepturi essent Spiritum sanctum, idque ex eo quòd ipse ascensurus esset ad Patrem: ita nos quoties audimus de Christi ascensione iam præteritâ, toties explorare nos ipsos oportet an Spiritum sanctum receperimus, & an in nobis habitet. Hic enim fructus est ascensionis & glorificationis Christi.
units.tr: Again he speaks about his departure, and so that it may not seem grievous to them, he at the same time comforts them, promising that he will return to them soon, namely through his Spirit. Therefore he adds, "Because I go to the Father," and for this reason I must be glorified, so that you may become partakers of my glory. For Christ, although by his death he merited for us all benefits, nevertheless these do not reach us except by the power of his resurrection, ascension and glorification. For as priest, humbled on earth, he merited all things for us; but as king, glorified, he communicates to us those very goods which he merited by his death. Just as, therefore, before his death and ascension the Lord gave his disciples hope that they would receive the Holy Spirit, and this from the fact that he himself was about to ascend to the Father, so whenever we hear of Christ's ascension, now past, we ought to examine ourselves: whether we have received the Holy Spirit, and whether he dwells in us. For this is the fruit of Christ's ascension and glorification.

units.la: Porrò hic admonemur Dominum nunquam plane deserere suos aut Ecclesiam suam. Si non det corporalem præsentiam, certè dat spiritualem. Nam non possunt pij vitam in terris agere citra aliquam saltem Domini præsentiam: neque etiam citra eam potest Ecclesia consistere, quæ ipsa beneficio præsentiæ Domini cœpit esse primùm. Nam quid est Ecclesia aliud nisi cœtus hominum segregatus à reliquo mundo per præsentiam illam Spiritus sancti, qua ipsi significantur? Dixerunt ergo quidam. Produnt quidem discipuli crassam quandam ignorantiam, cùm toties de hoc iam antea admoniti fuerint. Mirum enim est quàm surdi & quàm stupidi maneant homines ante receptum Spiritum illū sanctum, ad omnem doctrinam & verbi prædicationem, atque etiam ad voces eas quæ penetrare posse videantur lapides ipsos & truncos, vt illud plane videas <bl>ψυχικὸν</bl> hominem non capacem esse eorum quæ sunt Spiritus Dei. Post verò receptum Spiritum sanctum magis profecerunt in veritatis cognitione, vel vno die, quam sine Spiritu sancto tota vita sua. Discipuli Christi plus profecerunt vno die post decessum Domini, & missum ipsius Spiritum, quàm profecerunt toto illius temporis spacio quo sine efficacia Spiritus sancti Dominum habuerunt præsentem. Quare ne contenti simus vocibus hominum, & externa prædicatione, nisi simus <bl>θεοδιδάκτοι</bl> & internum illum doctorem in animis nostris penitus do-
units.tr: Here we are further reminded that the Lord never utterly forsakes his people or his Church. If he does not give bodily presence, he certainly gives spiritual presence. For the godly cannot live their life on earth without at least some presence of the Lord; nor can the Church, which at first began by the benefit of the Lord's presence, subsist without it. For what is the Church but an assembly of men set apart from the rest of the world by that presence of the Holy Spirit by which they are marked out? "Then some said..." The disciples indeed betray a gross ignorance, although they have been warned about this so often before. For it is remarkable how deaf and how dull men remain, before they receive that Holy Spirit, toward all teaching and the preaching of the Word, and even toward those voices which seem able to penetrate stones and logs, so that you may plainly see that the natural [ψυχικὸν] man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God. But after they received the Holy Spirit, they advanced more in knowledge of the truth in a single day than in their whole life without the Holy Spirit. The disciples of Christ advanced more in one day after the Lord's departure and the sending of his Spirit than they had advanced in the whole span of time in which they had the Lord present without the efficacy of the Holy Spirit. Therefore let us not be content with the voices of men and external preaching, unless we are taught by God [θεοδιδάκτοι] and feel that inner teacher deeply in our souls.

units.la: Discipuli Christi stupor, ante Spiritus S. receptionem. centem sentiamus.
units.tr: The stupor of Christ's disciples before the reception of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 19 Cognouit autem Iesus eos velle ipsum interrogare, & dixit eis, De hoc quaeritis inter vos, quod dixi, Paulisper & non conspicietis me, & iterum, paulisper & videbitis me.
units.tr: And Jesus, knowing that they wished to ask him, said to them, "Do you inquire among yourselves about this, that I said, 'A little while, and you will not see me, and again, a little while, and you will see me'?"

units.la: 20 Amen, amen dico vobis, flebitis vos & lamentabimini, mundus autem gaudebit: vos vero tristes eritis, sed tristitia vestra vertet in gaudium.
units.tr: Amen, amen I say to you, you will weep and lament, but the world will rejoice; you indeed will be sorrowful, but your sorrow will be turned into joy.

units.la: 21 Mulier cum parit, dolorem habet, quoniam venit hora eius: postquam autem peperit puerulum, iam non meminit afflictionis, propter gaudium quod homo sit natus in mundum.
units.tr: A woman, when she is in labour, has pain, because her hour has come; but when she has borne the child, she no longer remembers the anguish, for joy that a man has been born into the world.

units.la: 22 Et vos igitur nunc quidem tristitiam tenemini: sed rursum videbo vos, & gaudebit cor vestrum, & gaudium vestrum nemo tollet a vobis.
units.tr: And so you now indeed have sorrow; but again I will see you, and your heart will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.

units.la: Parcit Dominus eorum rudibus, neque tacrasa ignorantia statim iratus reiicit, sed cum lenitate docet eos, suo exemplo admonet pastores, ut semper spargant semen illud verbi, & semper inculcent auribus hominum doctrinam veritatis, etiamsi non statim fructificare verbum illud videat. Fieri enim non potest, ut verbum ad tempus delitescens, ut semel quasi mortuum reuiuiscat suo tempore & pullulet. Nam inter cetera, hoc officium est Spiritus sancti suggerere ea quae videntur obliuioni tradita & plane deperdita: unde supra 14.16. Omnia quae dixi vobis suggeret vobis. Amen, amen. Hactenus praefatus est Dominus: Nunc docet eos apertius quod dixit de decessu suo, & reditu breui futuro. Docet autem ex effectis iis quae ipsi in se perceperunt sunt. Effectus autem decessus duo sunt, videlicet, Lamentabimini, & flebitis, mundus autem gaudebit. Effectum vero reditus eius unum est: Tristitia vestra vertet in gaudium. Quod ad doctrinae formam, illud non praetermittendum, quod efficax non tantum ad cognitionem, sed etiam ad motum animorum: & doctrina sit quae est ex effectis sensui ipsi obuiis: ut si ostendat quis migraturum Christum a nobis ex istiusmodi effectis, fletu piorum, & gaudio impiorum: Item, si quis doceat Christum venturum illo die, ex pleno illo gaudio quod tum demum percipiemus. Sed ad rem ipsam: Discimus hic primò, absentiam Domini dolori esse piis, qui semel gustarunt quàm benignus sit Dominus. His quidem sine Domino omnes huiusmodi mundi voluptates ingratæ sunt. Cū Domino verò omnes calamitates mundi huius gratæ sunt ac suaues. Contrà verò, discimus præsentiam Dei impiis ingratam esse, qui nunquàm gustarunt quàm benignus sit Dominus. His quidem omnia cum Christo ingrata sunt, sine Christo autem omnia grata. Non enim percipiunt plenam voluptatem, si Christus præsens sit. Affulget enim ipse tanquam lux quædam non modò externis operibus, sed etiā internis cogitationibus, & arguit omnia. Discimus etiā tristitiā piorū euadere in gaudiū: atqz illud quidē, fateor, in hac vita nō parū, sed perminxtū perpetuo aliquo dolore: verùm tamen tantū abest ab eo dolor, vt impediat gaudiū, vt è contrà gaudiū excitet: Excitatum autem gaudium tādem omnē dolorem absorbet, & lachrymæ abstergunțur ab oculis nostris.
units.tr: The Lord spares his rude disciples, and does not immediately reject them in anger for their crass ignorance, but teaches them with gentleness, and by his own example admonishes the ministers always to scatter that seed of the Word, and always to inculcate the doctrine of truth in men's ears, even if they do not at once see the word bear fruit. For it cannot be that the word, lying hidden for a time, should not in its season come back to life, as if once dead, and sprout again. For among other things, this is the office of the Holy Spirit: to bring to mind those things which seem to have been consigned to oblivion and utterly lost; whence above, 14:16: "He will bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you. Amen, amen." Hitherto the Lord has spoken; now he teaches them more openly what he said about his departure and his return soon to come. He teaches, moreover, from the effects which they themselves perceive. The effects of his departure are two: "You will lament and weep, but the world will rejoice." The effect of his return is one: "Your sorrow will be turned into joy." As to the form of the teaching, this must not be passed over: it is effective not only for knowledge but also for moving the minds; and the teaching is drawn from effects that are obvious to the senses, as when someone shows that Christ will depart from us by such effects: by the weeping of the godly and the joy of the impious. Likewise, if someone teaches that Christ will come on that day, from the full joy which we shall then at last perceive. But to the matter itself: here we learn first that the absence of the Lord is a grief to the godly, who have once tasted how kind the Lord is. Indeed, without the Lord all such pleasures of the world are unpleasant to them; with the Lord, all the calamities of this world are welcome and sweet. On the contrary, we learn that the presence of God is unpleasant to the impious, who have never tasted how kind the Lord is. To them indeed everything is unpleasant with Christ, but everything pleasant without Christ. For they do not perceive full pleasure if Christ is present. For he shines forth like a light, not only in external works but also in internal thoughts, and convicts all things. We learn also that the sorrow of the godly turns into joy: and this, I admit, in this life is not slight, but mixed with some perpetual grief; yet that grief is so far from hindering the joy that, on the contrary, it stirs up joy. And the joy once stirred up at length swallows up all grief, and tears are wiped from our eyes.

units.la: Mulier cùm parit. Declarat similitudine, quod dixit de dolore & gaudio piorū: Ex hac autem similitudine notabimus primùm, quæ sit natura doloris, deinde gaudij illius piorum. Dolor parturientis gravis est admodum, sed vtilis: tendit enim ad partum, ideóque mulier quæ parturit spem quandam concipit, non tantùm quòd finiendus sit dolor, sed etiam quòd perceptura sit doloris sui fructum. Spes autem coniunctum habet perpetuò aliquod gaudium. Quare mulier in dolore partus posita etiam gaudet aliquo modo: huiusmodi est dolor piorū, qui quodammodò in hac vita parturiunt, id quod Apostolus applicat etiam rebus creatis quæ suspirant, & vnà parturiunt ad tempus vsque reuelationis filiorū Dei. Vnde dolor ille rendit ad partū quasi futuræ gloriæ atqz gaudij: ideóque sub spe gloriantur in mediis oppressionibus & doloribus. Quare dolor eorum permixtus est aliquo certè gaudio. At verò dolor impiorum, in infernis præsertim, post hanc vitam sine spe omni futuræ liberationis, nedū fructus alicuius futurus est. Bene enim esset iis si expectare possent finem aliquem doloris sui tandem fore, etsi non simul sperare possent fructum aliquem gaudij futurū, & doloribus illis tantis atque miferiis. Quare cùm sine spe futurus sit eorum dolor, erit quoque sine gaudio, & lætitiæ vlla quasi mixtura. Rursus quod sit futurum gaudium piorum, in altera vita, videmus ex eadem ista similitudine. Mulier postpuam peperit non amplius reminiscitur oppressionis præteritæ, nempe quia homo natus est in mundo: Ita postquam semel fuerimus in possessione gaudij illius & gloriæ futuræ missi, sic absorbebit gaudiū illud præteritam omne quæ in hac vita fuerat tristitiam, vt non amplius eius recordaturi simus. Ac tum quidem reuera videbitur nobis oppressio quæcunq; in hac vita præterita fuerat momentanea esse & leuis, cùm percipiemus æternum illud pondus excellenter excellentis gloriæ. Tum, inquam, illud quod apud Paulum legimus reipsa experiemur. Et vos igitur nunc quidem. His verbis est similitudinis accommodatio, de qua quia iam dictum est, hoc tantum nunc admonebimus, nempe hic Iesum transfire ad enumerationem partium felicitatis illius, quam tum percipient, cùm ipse in Spiritu suo reuersus fuerit ad eos. Sic enim concludit sermonem illum cum discipulis suis habitu. Quem exorsus inde à capite 13. & consolationem illam in qua ministranda præcipuè laborauit in toto hoc suo sermone. Felicitatis illius hæc prima pars est, quod cùm videbunt eum rursus, gaudebunt gaudium sempiternum. Non est existimandum promissum esse hoc gaudium Apostolis duntaxat, sed & toti Ecclesiæ: neque decessisse illud vnà cum Apostolis, sed etiamnum permanere in Ecclesia, & permansurū ad finem vsque. Sicuti enim Christi Spiritus, qui vicarius est Christi in terris manus rus est in reditum vsque Christi; ita permansurum est gaudium: Nam Spiritus ille gaudij est ac pacis: Et quotquot verè pij sunt, illi quidem percipiunt penitus corde suo Spirituale istud gaudium. Spiritu nimirum sancto habitante in ipsis. Quod si verò quis sit qui ipsum non percipiat, is non habet Spiritum, & qui non habet Spiritum, is non est Christi. Paulus dicit non vno in loco gaudendū esse semper: quo significat materiā esse satis magnam perpetui gaudij in Spiritu sancto, & verbo hoc Euangelij, quod nuncium est salutis per Christum, lætū illud oc optatum: materiam, inquam, gaudij nullis in vita
units.tr: A woman when she is in labour. He declares by a likeness what he said about the sorrow and joy of the godly. From this likeness we shall note first what the nature of that sorrow of the godly is, and then the joy of those same godly. The pain of a woman in labour is very grievous, but useful: it tends toward the birth, and therefore the woman who is in labour conceives a certain hope, not only that her pain will end, but also that she will receive the fruit of her pain. Hope, however, always has some joy joined with it. Therefore the woman, placed in the pain of childbirth, also rejoices in some way: such is the pain of the godly, who in some measure travail in this life, which the Apostle applies even to created things that groan and travail together until the revealing of the sons of God. Whence that pain tends toward birth, as it were of future glory and joy; therefore they glory in hope amid the oppressions and sorrows. Hence their sorrow is mixed with some certain joy. But the sorrow of the impious, especially in hell, after this life, without any hope of future deliverance, will not even have any fruit. For it would be well with them if they could at least expect that some end of their sorrow would come at last, even though they could not at the same time hope for any fruit of future joy amid those great sorrows and miseries. Hence, since their sorrow will be without hope, it will also be without joy, and without any mixture of gladness. Again, that the joy of the godly will come in the other life, we see from this same likeness. The woman, after she has given birth, no longer remembers the past oppression, namely because a man is born into the world. So, once we have been sent into possession of that joy and future glory, that joy will swallow up all the sorrow that was in this life, so that we shall no longer be mindful of it. And then indeed the oppression, whatever it was in this life, will truly seem to us momentary and light, when we receive that eternal weight of glory, exceedingly excellent. Then, I say, we shall actually experience what we read in Paul. "But you, now indeed..." In these words is the application of the likeness, about which, since it has already been said, we will only now remind you of this: here Jesus passes over to the enumeration of the parts of that happiness which they will then perceive, when he himself, in his Spirit, shall have returned to them. For thus he concludes the discourse which he had with his disciples, begun from chapter 13, and that consolation in which he laboured especially in ministering throughout this whole discourse. The first part of that happiness is this: when they see him again, they will rejoice with an everlasting joy. It is not to be thought that this joy was promised to the Apostles only, but also to the whole Church; nor has it departed with the Apostles, but still remains in the Church, and will remain to the end. For just as the Spirit of Christ, who is the vicar of Christ on earth, remains until Christ's return, so the joy will remain. For that Spirit is the Spirit of joy and peace; and all who are truly godly both perceive that spiritual joy deep in their heart, the Holy Spirit dwelling in them. But if anyone does not perceive it, he does not have the Spirit, and he who does not have the Spirit is not Christ's. Paul says in more than one place that we must always rejoice; by which he signifies that there is matter enough for perpetual joy in the Holy Spirit, and in this word of the Gospel, which is the message of salvation through Christ, that joyful and desired news: matter, I say, of joy which no evils and miseries of this life can interrupt

units.la: Rom. 8, 9. vita hac malis ac miseriis interrumpendi, siquidem sic oblectatio in Spiritu & in verbo. Verùm non percipimus eum quem debemus fructum, vel ex Spiritu sancto, vel ex verbo hoc Euangelij, cuius comes est Spiritus sanctus. Non enim petimus Spiritum sanctum, non attentè audimus Euangelium.
units.tr: Rom. 8, 9. This life, interrupted by evils and miseries, since in this way there is delight in the Spirit and in the word. But we do not receive the fruit we ought to, either from the Holy Spirit or from this word of the Gospel, of which the Holy Spirit is the companion. For we do not ask for the Holy Spirit, and we do not listen attentively to the Gospel.

units.la: 23 Et illo die me non interrogabitis quicquam. Amen, amen dico vobis, quæcunque petieritis à Patre in nomine meo, dabit vobis.
units.tr: And in that day you will ask me nothing. Amen, amen, I say to you, whatever you ask of the Father in my name, he will give it to you.

units.la: 24 Vsque adhuc non petiistis quicquam in nomine meo: petite & accipietis, ut gaudium vestrum sit plenum.
units.tr: Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and you will receive, that your joy may be full.

units.la: 25 Hæc loquutus sum vobis per similitudines, venit tempus cùm non amplius per similitudines loquar vobis, sed aperte de Patre meo renuntiabo vobis.
units.tr: I have spoken these things to you in figures. The time is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures, but will tell you plainly of my Father.

units.la: HÆc secunda pars est felicitatis quam promittit discipulis futuram in reditu suo per Spiritum sanctum. Non tum quidem intelligebant, ac proinde dubitabunt, ut nunc paulo ante dixit Dominus; Paulisper & non conspicietis me. Illi inter se anxiè de sensu illorum verborum quærebant. Promittit igitur Dominus futurum illud cognitionis lumen: quo quidem omnis dubitatio tollenda sit. Spiritus enim ille quem missurus est, deducet eos in omnem veritatem, & docebit omnia. Et nos quoque qui in Ecclesia Christi nunc sumus ad finem usque σωτηρίας sumus, ut promissum fuit per Prophetas supra 6. 45. manet enim in Ecclesia ad finem usque idem ille spiritus, qui ut spiritus quidem est gaudij; ita Spiritus est cognitionis, & mentes hominum interius illuminat inferendo in eas lucem istam verbi prædicati, id quod etiam pij sentiunt in se re ipsa, qui fouent in animis suis Spiritum hunc sanctum, & voluptatem capiunt ex verbo hoc prædicato. Sentiunt enim reipsa non modo illustrari sibi mentem, sed aperiri etiam sibi cor, ut de Lydia purpuraria proditum est, ad Euangelij huius prædicationem. Quod quisquis non sentit, profecto is arguit se non tanti facere, vel Spiritum, vel verbum. Miretur enim quiuis in tanta Euangelii luce, tantam passim grassari ignorantiam. Hoc profecto imputandum est contemptui Euangelij qui passim regnat. Fieri non potest, quin si homines voluptatem aliquam caperent ex Euangelio, Spiritus sanctus magis efficax esset in cordibus eorum ad ipsorum illuminationem & reformationem.
units.tr: THIS is the second part of the happiness which he promises the disciples will come at his return through the Holy Spirit. At that time they did not understand, and so they were in doubt, as the Lord had just said a little before: A little while, and you will not see me. They therefore asked one another anxiously about the meaning of those words. The Lord therefore promises that the light of knowledge will come, by which every doubt will be removed. For that Spirit whom he is to send will lead them into all truth, and will teach them all things. And we also, who are now in the Church of Christ, remain until the end of salvation [σωτηρίας], as was promised through the prophets (see above, 6:45). For that same Spirit remains in the Church until the end. He is indeed the Spirit of joy, and he is also the Spirit of knowledge, and he illuminates the minds of men inwardly by bringing into them the light of the preached word. The godly also feel this in themselves in actual experience, for they cherish this Holy Spirit in their hearts and take delight in this preached word. For they really feel that not only is their mind enlightened, but their heart is also opened to them, as is recorded of Lydia the seller of purple, at the preaching of this Gospel. Whoever does not feel this, certainly shows that he does not value either the Spirit or the word. For anyone would be amazed that in such a great light of the Gospel such great ignorance rages everywhere. This must certainly be blamed on the contempt for the Gospel which reigns everywhere. It cannot be that, if men took any delight in the Gospel, the Holy Spirit would not be more effective in their hearts for their enlightenment and reformation.

units.la: Amen, amen dico. Tertium beneficium, siue tertia felicitatis pars, in qua omnis gratia promittitur petentibus eam; petentibus, inquam, & non procurantibus aut promerentibus. Solus enim Christus promeritus est omnem gratiam ac misericordiam: A nobis autem nihil postulatur, nisi hoc, vt peramus in ipsius nomine, qui promeritus est nobis omnem gratiam. Quod dixi mus de gaudio, de cognitione, idem dicimus de gratia Christi vniuersa. Ea perpetuò offertur petentibus eam in Ecclesia Dei, in qua habitat Spiritus omnis gratiæ: Et sentiunt quidem sese pij participes fieri ipsa omnis gratiæ quoties eam petunt in nomine Christi. Quod si qui querantur non fieri se participes gratiæ, hoc sibi imputent, & negligentiæ suæ quod non dignentur eam petere. Id autem petere non detur, nisi filiis, non etiam seruis in domo Dei, sed filiis, & iis in quorum cordibus testatur Spiritus sanctus quod filij Dei sint. His, inquam, os aperitur ad clamandum Abba Pater. Vsque adhuc non petiistis. Quum sciret Dominus, & quanta necessitas esset in precibus, & quàm segnes essent isti ad precandum, instigat eos ad preces. Ne autem ab iis obiiceretur, Nos quidem petimus, at non impetramus? Respondet, vsque adhuc, Nihil petiuistis in nomine meo. Petiuerunt quidem & precati sunt Apostoli ante Christi manifestationem, & pij quique viri precati sunt in nomine Christi. Neque enim Spiritus sanctus alias dictat preces, praeter eas quae in ipsius nomine concipiuntur. Verum precati sunt pij quique in eius nomine non nisi obscure, vt obscura tum fuit Christi notitia: At vero postquam Christus iam manifestatus est & cōsummatum est illud opus redemptionis humanæ, iam Christum non obscure, sed clarè videmus: Ita in eius nomine non obscure, sed
units.tr: Amen, amen, I say to you. The third benefit, or third part of the happiness, in which all grace is promised to those who ask for it: to those who ask, I say, and not to those who procure it or merit it. For Christ alone has merited all grace and mercy, and nothing is required of us except that we pray in the name of him who has merited for us all grace. What we have said about joy and about knowledge, we say the same about the whole grace of Christ. It is continually offered to those who ask for it in the Church of God, in which the Spirit of all grace dwells. And the godly indeed feel that they become partakers of all grace whenever they ask for it in the name of Christ. But if some complain that they do not become partakers of grace, let them impute this to themselves, and to their own negligence, that they do not deign to ask for it. Moreover, to ask for it is granted only to sons, not also to servants in the house of God, but to sons, and to those in whose hearts the Holy Spirit testifies that they are children of God. To these, I say, the mouth is opened to cry out, Abba, Father. Until now you have not asked. Since the Lord knew both how great the need was in prayers and how slack these men were in praying, he urges them to pray. But lest they should object, "Indeed we do ask, yet we do not obtain," he answers, until now, you have asked nothing in my name. The apostles indeed asked and prayed before the manifestation of Christ, and all the godly men prayed in the name of Christ. For the Holy Spirit does not dictate prayers at any other time, except those that are conceived in his name. But the godly, praying in his name, did so only obscurely, since the knowledge of Christ was then obscure. But now that Christ has already been manifested, and that work of human redemption has been completed, we now see Christ not obscurely but clearly. So in his name we ask not obscurely but openly,

units.la: {y} In nomine Christi. sed aperte petimus, precantes Deum per Iesum Christũ Dominum nostrum. Notandum autem & quàm neces- sariæ sint preces, sine quibus nihil à Deo obtinemus, & quàm segnes simus ad preces, vt non precemur nisi excitati primùm à Deo, deinde excitati precemur frigidè adeo ac segniter. Notandum denique quæ cura & solicitudo sit Domini in nobis excitandis ad preces. Nunc enim precibus nos excitat, nunc minis, nunc afflictionibus, quibus sensum aliquem efficit in nobis indigentiæ nostræ, vt & ex sensu indigentiæ petamus, & ex sensu gratię impetratę gratias ei agamus. In hoc enim duplici sensu materia est perpetuarũ precũ. Vel enim sensus est indigentiæ, & tum quidem occasio se offert petendi gratiam: vel sensus est gratiæ, ac tũ occasio est agendi Deo gratias. Vnde Paulus, Omni prece & supplicatione, precantes omni tempore per Spiritum. Vt enim omni tempore confligendum nobis est cum aduersariis, & colluctandum cũ tentationibus: ita nullum tempus esse debet à precibus vacuum. Vt gaudium vestrum. Finis omnis gratiæ est gaudium, quantóque maior est gratia quam consequimur, tanto maius est gaudium: perfectam gratiam sequitur perfectum ac plenum gaudium.
units.tr: In the name of Christ. openly, praying to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. It should also be noted how necessary prayers are, without which we obtain nothing from God, and how slack we are to pray, so that we do not pray unless first stirred up by God, and then, once stirred up, we pray so coldly and so sluggishly. Lastly, it should be noted what care and concern the Lord shows in stirring us up to prayer. For he now stirs us up by prayers, now by threats, now by afflictions, by which he produces in us some sense of our need, so that from the sense of our need we may ask, and from the sense of grace obtained we may give thanks to him. For in this twofold sense lies the matter of continual prayers. For either there is a sense of need, and then the occasion of asking for grace presents itself; or there is a sense of grace, and then the occasion is giving thanks to God. Hence Paul says, With all prayer and supplication, praying at all times in the Spirit. For just as we must fight with our adversaries at all times, and wrestle with temptations, so no time ought to be free from prayers. That your joy may be. The end of all grace is joy, and the greater the grace we obtain, the greater the joy; perfect grace is followed by perfect and full joy.

units.la: Hæc loquutus sum. Hæc est quarta pars consolationis, siue beatitatis eorum, quam percipient tum cùm in Spiritu suo reuersus fuerit ad eos; nempe Euidentia in sermone. Nam Christus cùm commoratus est in terris, seré tum per parabolas loquutus est, neque id quidè turbæ tantùm & vulgo hominum, quibus vt habes Matth. 13. 13. omnia per parabolas loquutus est, & sine parabolis nihil: sed etiam discipulis suis, vt conspicitur ex hoc loco. Nam nondum absoluto illo redemptionis opere, neque misso adhuc Spiritu sancto, necesse fuit non tam apertum sermonem esse, de redemptione humana. At perfecto iam opere illo redemptionis & misso iam Spiritu sancto, clarius per os discipulorum suorum loquutus est, quàm præsens per suum ipsius os. Atque hodierno etiam die non destituimur hac felicitatis parte ac consolatione. Nam præterquam quod habeamus Apostolos quodammodo loquentes in scriptis suis multa cũ παῤῥησίᾳ & euidentia, Deus etiam quotidie nobis excitat eos qui super fundamento illud Apostolorum ædificâ, non stramen aut stipulam, aut ligna, sed argentum, aurū, pretiosos lapillos, & quod dixit Paulus, in quorum cordibus adeo splendet, vt ipsi splendeant aliis, & tantam Euangelij lucem ministrent, vt si tectum sit hoc Euangelium quod prædicamus, tectum sit iis qui pereunt.
units.tr: I have spoken these things. This is the fourth part of the consolation, or blessedness, of those which they will receive when he has returned to them in his Spirit; namely, clearness in speech. For while Christ dwelt on earth he spoke for the most part in parables, and this not only to the crowd and common people, to whom, as you have in Matthew 13:13, he spoke everything in parables, and nothing without parables, but also to his disciples, as appears from this passage. For before that work of redemption was finished, and before the Holy Spirit had been sent, it was necessary that his speech about human redemption should not be so open. But now that the work of redemption is completed and the Holy Spirit has been sent, he has spoken more clearly through the mouth of his disciples than he did present in his own person. And even today we are not deprived of this part of happiness and consolation. For, besides the fact that we have the apostles speaking in their writings, in a sense, with much boldness [παῤῥησίᾳ] and clarity, God also daily raises up for us those who build upon that foundation of the apostles, not with straw or stubble or wood, but with silver, gold, and precious stones; and, as Paul said, they shine in such a way in the hearts of others that they themselves shine on others and minister such a great light of the Gospel that, if the Gospel we preach is veiled, it is veiled to those who perish.

units.la: 26 Illo die in nomine meo petetis: & non dico vobis, me rogaturum Patrem pro vobis.
units.tr: 26 In that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father for you.

units.la: 27 Ipse enim Pater amat vos, quia vos me amastis, & credidistis me à Deo prodiisse.
units.tr: 27 For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came forth from God.

units.la: 28 Prodij à Patre, & veni in mundum: iterum relinquo mundum, & proficiscor ad Patrem.
units.tr: 28 I came forth from the Father and came into the world; again I leave the world and go to the Father.

units.la: HÆc est quinta consolatio, quam percepturi sunt in reditu ipsius per Spiritum suum; facilitas quidam ac promptitudo Dei, ad audiendum preces eorum: quam quidem significat dum ait se non rogaturum pro ipsis, quasi dicat, Prompte adeo ac facilè concedet quæ petetis, vt nihil opus sit futurum meis precibus. Vtrum Christus precibus intercedat apud Patrem in cœlis iam glorificatus hic non disputo: tantum de hoc admoneo, supplicationes & abiectionem ad pedes Patris, partem fuisse aliquam humiliationis ipsius quæ in terris fuit. At Christus iā in cœlis glorificatus est. Intercedit autē pro nobis odore vnici illius sacrificij perpetuo. Intercedit autē illis precibus quas aliquādo cū in terris ageret nostra causa conceperat. Nam cùm in terris nobiscum commoraretur, proculdubiò, vt materiam precum perpetuam habuit; cùm quot homines videret tot miseros ac perditos videret, & quòd pro miseris & perditis nullo non tempore precatus est. Neque verò pius quisquam est, qui ex inspectis hominum miseriis non habeat perpetuam precum materiam. Nam in quot incidit homines, in tot miseros & perditos incidit. Ipse enim Pater amat. Hæc causa est facilitatis & promptitudinis Patris ad audiendum preces eorum. Causa autem subiecta est, Quia vos me amastis. Hoc quidem dicit, non quòd ipsi priores dilexerint Iesum, sed cùm amor incipiat à Deo, & ipse prior amet, desinit etiam in Deū, & ipse posterior amat, & non & nostrum hunc erga ipsum amorem non nisi finitum & modicum, infinito & immodico suo illo amore, vndequaque cõpleƈtitur. Nota igitur fidem in Christum, causam esse hoc loco praecipuam ac fundamentum, cur tam facilis sit Deus ac promptus ad nos audiendos: Est & isto fundamentum quoddam altius: nempe amor Patris in filium ineffabilis; hinc fit vt amet eos qui amat filium suum, & odio prosequitur eos, qui odio prosequuntur filium. Si quis non amat Dominum Iesum Christum, sit Anathema Maranatta. Exiui à Patre. Id quod obscurè dixit supra,& per parabolam versu 16. nunc per occasionem verborum proximorum aperte profert. Obseruandum autem quod non statim aperte dixerit discipulis, se decessurum: verum medio loco multiplicem consolationis materiam subministrarit, eo nimirum fine, vt æquiori animo ferrent apertum sermonem de decessu suo, quem aliqui egerrimè tulerunt. Ex quo discimus quàm parcat suis Dominus, & quòd nolit eos tristitia afficere, non modò facto, sed neverbo quidem: Ideo instruit ac praeparat eorum animos antequam grauiora in medium afferat, ad hoc vt æquiori animo ferant ea: vt sit nobis exemplo in perpetuum, ne statim ac temerè tristitia afficiamus quenquam, & vt semper cum lenitate aliqua, & misericordia cum quibusuis agamus. Id quod video à Paulo factum, qui non tantum monuit alios, vt reprehenderent cum doctrina & lenitate, sed & aliis praeiuit suo exemplo, & semper in omnibus ministerij sui partibus lenitate est vsus; id quod indicant omnes eius reprehensiones ad Galatas, ad Corinthios, quas mitigari perpetuò & suauitate quadam quasi conditi cernimus. Ait se idcirco nondum venille ad eos, nõ alia quidem de causa, quàm hac vt ipsis parceret, & post-eâ ne ipsos tristitia afficeret. Quo significat non nisi inuitum se descendisse ad reprehensiones; abstinuisse autè se ab occasionibus quibuscunque reprehendendi. Notanda est etiam forma, qua proponit nuncium hoc grate, & ingratum decessus sui. In proponendo enim gratì ac tristi nuncio, ea vtitur forma, qua etiam per significationem discessus sui eos consolatur. Ait enim se relinquere mundum, & proficisci ad Patrem, vt nimirum ad eius dextram sedeat gloriosus. E quo loco futurum sit, vt magis eos consoletur quàm vnquam antea in terris consolatus est eos, dum vna cum iis versaretur. Sic planè nobis faciendum. Tristia & grauia ea forma proponenda quæ grauiora aliquo modo leuiora reddat. Vt si nunc quis(id quod graue admodum est ac triste)dicat decessurum ac migraturum Christum è nostra ista gente, sed bene fore interea iis, qui seriò dolent de decessu ipsius.
units.tr: This is the fifth consolation which they were to receive at his return, through his Spirit: a certain readiness and promptness of God in hearing their prayers. He indicates this when he says that he is not going to ask the Father on their behalf, as if he were saying: the Father will grant what you ask so promptly and easily that my prayers will be unnecessary. I do not here dispute whether Christ, now glorified in heaven, intercedes with the Father by prayer. I only remark that the supplications and the prostration at the Father's feet were a part of that humiliation which he underwent on earth. But Christ is now glorified in heaven, and he intercedes for us by the perpetual fragrance of that one sacrifice. He also intercedes by those prayers which, when he was on earth, he had offered on our behalf. For while he lived with us on earth, he surely had a constant matter for prayer, since he saw as many miserable and lost people as he saw men, and he prayed for the miserable and the lost at all times. Nor is there any godly person who, having looked at the miseries of men, does not have a constant matter for prayer. For whatever men he encountered, he encountered miserable and lost ones. For the Father himself loves you. This is the cause of the Father's easiness and readiness to hear their prayers. The cause is then added: because you have loved me. He does not say this because they had loved Jesus first; but since love begins with God, and he loves first, it also ends in God, who loves last, and our love for him, which is finite and small, is wholly embraced by his infinite and immeasurable love. Note, therefore, that faith in Christ is here the chief cause and foundation of God's being so easy and ready to hear us. There is also a deeper foundation for this: namely, the Father's ineffable love for the Son. Hence it comes about that he loves those who love his Son, and pursues with hatred those who pursue his Son with hatred. If anyone does not love the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be anathema, Maranatha.
