Qui enim sunt, qui ignominia afficiunt corpora sanctorum demortua? non Pilatus, non Ethnici, non Turci ipsi, sed Caiaphas, hoc est, is qui emettitur nomen Pontificis, Sacerdotis, Pharisæi, vno verbo Papistæ, & adultera illa Ecclesia: qui corpora sanctorum vel non sepeliri patiuntur omnino, vel certè sepulchris eruta probris & ignominiæ exponunt. Vasa scilicet ignominiæ plerùque in hac vita afficiunt ignominia vasa illa gloriæ, quæ ipsa tandem, cùm vasa gloriæ gloriam suam obtinebunt, æterna afficientur ignominia.
units.tr: And the matter being known. Thus far was Joseph's request; now Pilate grants what he asked. But note that he does not hand Christ over to Joseph, or permit the burial, until he has fully ascertained that Christ is dead. This was done according to Roman law: a man condemned to death is not to be taken from the judge's hand until it is established that he is already dead. If they did this to the green tree, what will be done to the dry? If they acted with the utmost strictness against the innocent, what will become of the guilty and the accused on that day of God's last judgement? Now certain that Jesus had expired, he gave Joseph the body of the dead man. This was an act of humanity, as is credible from Pilate's awareness of Christ's innocence, which he never wholly lost. Whatever the case, this deed was one of humanity. But if Joseph had resisted Caiaphas the high priest, the other priests, the scribes and the Pharisees, surely he would not have obtained it so easily; for they would have allowed the Lord nothing but the burial of an ass, as they say. For who are those who treat with ignominy the dead bodies of the saints? Not Pilate, not the heathen, not the Turks themselves, but Caiaphas, that is, he who arrogates to himself the name of pontiff, priest, Pharisee: in one word, the Papists, and that adulterous Church. They either suffer the bodies of the saints not to be buried at all, or, dug out of their tombs, certainly expose them to reproach and ignominy. Plainly, the vessels of dishonour for the most part treat with dishonour in this life those vessels of glory, who, when at last the vessels of glory obtain their glory, will themselves be subjected to eternal dishonour.

units.la: Is autem emit sindonem. Hactenus veniam sepeliendi corpus Domini impetrauit Iosephus: sequitur nunc sepultura ipsa. In sepultura primùm sunt partes Iosephi seorsum, deinde sunt partes Nicodemi seorsim. Tertiò sunt partes vtriusque coniunctim. Iosephus itaque primùm mercatus est sindonem, & inuoluit deinde corpus Domini sindone illa pura. Spiritus sanctus sindonem in qua inuolutum est corpus Domini ex puritate & munditie sua, vt vel ex sindone, in qua inuolutum est eius corpus, accedat ad sepulturam Domini aliqua pars gloriæ. Sepultura enim Domini omni ex parte honorabilis fuit: deinde notada in Iosepho perseuerreturn cœpto illo opere. Non enim satis habuit semel impetrasse veniæ sepeliendi corporis Domini, vt deinde sepulturam ipsam aliis relinqueret curandam, vt fratribus Domini, & co-
units.tr: But he bought a linen cloth. Thus far Joseph obtained leave to bury the body of the Lord; now follows the burial itself. In the burial, first are Joseph's parts, taken separately, then Nicodemus's parts, taken separately; thirdly, the parts of both together. Joseph therefore first bought a linen cloth, and then wrapped the body of the Lord in that pure linen. The Holy Spirit, through the purity and cleanness of the linen in which the body of the Lord was wrapped, so that some part of glory might attach to the burial of the Lord, even from the linen in which his body was enfolded. For the burial of the Lord was honourable in every respect. Next, to be noted in Joseph is his perseverance in that undertaking. For he did not think it enough to have obtained once the pardon for burying the Lord's body, so as then to leave the burial itself to others to be carried out, as to the brothers of the Lord and co-

units.la: Impiorum dura sors.
units.tr: The hard lot of the wicked.

units.la: Pilati moderatio.
units.tr: Pilate's moderation.

units.la: Ecclesiæ militantis conditio.
units.tr: The condition of the militant Church.

units.la: 4. Sepulturæ Christi apparatus.
units.tr: 4. The preparation of Christ's burial.

units.la: Sindone pura corpus inuoluitur.
units.tr: The body is wrapped in a pure linen cloth.

units.la: gnatis aliis. Quin imò incœptum opus persequitur ad finem usque. Non enim satis est bene incepisse nisi ad finem usque perseueremus. Et in stadio hoc Christiano nunquam retrospiciendum ad illud quod iam confectum est itineris, vt cum Apostolo loquamur: sed perpetuò conuitendum ad metam. Nam cùm omnia fecerimus quæcunque potuimus, inutiles tamen serui sumus: & qui non perseuerauerit ad finem, non coronabitur. Sed videndum diligentius quanam re adductus sit Iosephus ad perseuerandum in opere illo sepulturæ Domini. Ad inchoandum opus primum allectus est suauí illo odore corporis Domini, odore nimirū amoris illius ineffabilis. Nā is odor est quē spirat mors Domini, nempe amoris: mortuus est enim Dominus pro nobis ex dilectione illa qua nos est prosequu tus etiam inimicos. Mors igitur Domini spirat amorē. Ergo allectus primum est suauí illo odore corporis Domini. Quo propiùs ad corpus illud Domini accedebat, eo magis magisque odorem inde quasi proficiscentem, sensit. Quo magis sensit, eo magis magisque perpetuò inuitatus est ad ipsum, adeo vt non acquieuerit donec corpus illud Domini vlnis suis excepisset. Nā verisimile est eum manibus suis ipsius Iosephum inuoluisse sindone corpus illud Domini, adeo ipsi pretiosum. Qui semel hausit illam odoris fragrantiā, quæ est à morte Domini, non acquiescit tantisper dum ad Dominum perueniat. Vt ad eum eat habitatum, cū Paulo probat migrare è corpore: vt sit cū Domino, cū eodem illo paulo cupit dissolui: nihili enim facit mortem istam primam. O si semel daretur gustare quàm benignus sit Dominus.
units.tr: Having been granted this, he did not leave the rest of the burial to others to care for. On the contrary, he pursues the work he had begun right to the end. For it is not enough to have made a good start unless we persevere to the end. And in this Christian race we must never look back at the distance already covered, to use the Apostle's words, but must always press on towards the goal. For although we have done everything we could, we are still unprofitable servants, and whoever does not persevere to the end will not be crowned. But we must consider more carefully what moved Joseph to persevere in that work of burying the Lord. He was first drawn to begin the work by that sweet fragrance of the Lord's body, namely the fragrance of that ineffable love. For this is the fragrance breathed out by the death of the Lord, that is, of love: the Lord died for us out of that affection with which he also embraced his enemies. Therefore the death of the Lord breathes out love. So Joseph was first drawn by that sweet fragrance of the Lord's body. The closer he came to that body, the more and more he sensed the odour, as it were, coming forth from it. The more he sensed it, the more and more he was constantly drawn to it, so that he would not rest until he had received that body of the Lord into his arms. For it is likely that he himself wrapped that body of the Lord in the linen with his own hands, a body so precious to him. Whoever has once drawn in that fragrance which comes from the death of the Lord does not rest until he reaches the Lord. As Paul proves, to be away from the body is to be at home with him; with that same Paul he desires to be dissolved and to be with the Lord, for he counts this first death as nothing. O, if only it were granted to taste how kind the Lord is!

units.la: Hactenus fuerunt partes Iosephi, sequuntur partes Nicodemi seorsim. Dū hæc ageret Iosephus, accedit Nicodemus cū dono suo ad Christum in sepultura sua honorandum. Ipsa hominis persona honorat sepulturam Domini: nam vt Iosephus princeps quidā fuit inter Iudeos, ita Nicodemus vt dives fuit, ita quoque Nicodemus, vt Christi discipulus fuit, sed occultus propter metum Iudæorum: ita Nicodemus, vt vir bonus & iustus. Verùm Christus Iohan. 3. 10. vocat Nicodemū doctorē in Israele, qualis non fuit Iosephus. Ergo accedente Nicodemo, accedit aliquid quod in persona Iosephi non fuit, ad honorem. porem sepulturæ Domini.Nam honoratus est Dominus in morte & sepultura sua per has personas vel maximè. Cū in personis duorum istorum virorū, pedibus Christi etiam demortui subiecta sunt simul & semel diuitiæ,honores,sapientia huius mundi, vt facilè videas infirmitatem,pauperatem,ignominiam ,stultitiam crucis Christi,plus virium ac potestatis habere quàm diuitias,honores & sapientiam mundi. Imò verò crucem Christi cum infirmitate sua,hæc omnia pude facere.Sic igitur Paulus gloriatur ex Prophetæ verbis aduersus ista omnia, Vbi est sapiens?vbi scriba? vbi conquisitor sæculi huius? Nóne insipiens Deus sapientiam mundi huius? Et idem ille Paulus priusquam Christum cognosceret,putauit hęc lucere: postquam autem Christum cognouit, omnia damna esse duxit, imò stercora, vt Christum lucrifaceret.Hæc de Nicodemi persona, sequitur ipsius donum.
units.tr: So far were the parts of Joseph; now follow the parts of Nicodemus, taken separately. While Joseph was doing these things, Nicodemus came with his gift to honour Christ in his burial. The very person of the man honours the Lord's burial. For just as Joseph was a certain prince among the Jews, so Nicodemus was rich; and just as Joseph was a disciple of Christ, but secret for fear of the Jews, so Nicodemus was a good and just man. Yet Christ, in John 3.10, calls Nicodemus a teacher in Israel, which Joseph was not. Therefore with Nicodemus's arrival there comes something to the honour of the Lord's burial that was not present in the person of Joseph. For the Lord was honoured in his death and burial above all through these persons. In the persons of these two men, riches, honours and the wisdom of this world are at once laid at the feet of Christ even in death, so that you may easily see that the weakness, poverty, shame and foolishness of the cross of Christ have more strength and power than the riches, honours and wisdom of the world. Indeed, the cross of Christ with its weakness makes all these things ashamed. Thus Paul also glories, in the words of the prophet, against all these things: "Where is the wise? Where is the scribe? Where is the disputer of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?" And that same Paul, before he knew Christ, thought these things shone; but after he knew Christ, he counted all things loss, indeed dung, that he might gain Christ. So much for the person of Nicodemus; now follows his gift.

units.la: Estimatem mistura myrrhæ & aloes, eaque magni ponderis, nimirum centum librarum. Proculdubiò non tantum pretij impendisset in emendo tanto pondere odorum pretio sorum, nisi pretiosum duxisset corpus illud Domini mortuum: neque rursus hoc genus munis suaueolentis mercatus fuisset aut obtulisset, nisi ad id enim impulisset suaueolentia illa & fragrantia corporis Domini.Quales enim sunt quibus offerimus munera, talia solent esse munera quibus ipsos honoramus. Auari ga Christū isti & sacrilegi (tantum absunt à muneribus offerendis) isti,inquam, nunquâ senserunt quàm suaueolens & pretiosum sit corpus Domini; non dicam iam crucifixum, sed glorificatum in cælis.
units.tr: A mixture of myrrh and aloes, and that of great weight, namely a hundred pounds. Certainly he would not have spent so much money in buying such a weight of spices, unless he had considered the dead body of the Lord precious; nor would he have bought or offered this kind of sweet-smelling gift, unless the sweetness and fragrance of the Lord's body had moved him to it. For the gifts we offer are usually such as those with which we honour the persons themselves. But those greedy and sacrilegious men who are so far from offering gifts never perceived how sweet-smelling and precious the Lord's body is; I say nothing now of it crucified, but of it glorified in heaven.

units.la: Acceperunt ergo. Hactenus fuerunt primùm partes Iosephi,deinde Nicodemi seorsim,sequuntur nunc eorum partes coniunctim. Quum accedit Nicodemus cum suo munere,vt videtur,maioris pretij,quàm fuit munus illud Iosephi,Iosephus tum neq; subducit sea sepultura, neq; inuidet Nicodemo munus illud suum, sed collatis manibus & coniuncta opera linteis & aromatibus illis Domini corpus inuoluunt: docentes nos suo exemplo,nunquam subtrahendam esse manum nostram à Domino, quin semper aliquid faciendum in ipsius gratiam,quantumcunque illud sit: vt neque inuidendum esse aliis,
units.tr: They therefore took it. So far were first the parts of Joseph, then of Nicodemus, taken separately; now follow their parts together. When Nicodemus comes with his gift, which seems of greater value than the gift of Joseph, Joseph neither withdraws from the burial nor begrudges Nicodemus his gift; rather, with hands joined and work combined, they wrap the Lord's body in the linen and those spices. By their example they teach us never to withdraw our hand from the Lord, but always to do something for his grace, however small it may be; and not to envy others,

units.la: Dicitur: non sine dicamus ergo. qui ad honorandum Dominum cum maiori aliquo dono accedunt, sed perpetuò cū quibusuis, siue illi maioribus donis instructi accedant, siue minoribus, manus essse conferendas. Illud enim oportet in nobis esse studium Domini ipsiúsque gloriæ, vt obliti nostri ipsorum, tantū de ipso ipsiúsque gloria cogitemus. Sicut est mos Iudæorum. Hoc ex consuetudine & ritu Iudæorum factum esse docet. Cæremonia ista & ritus hic, vt aliæ omnes cæremoniæ, Christum ipsiúsque aduentum aliquo modo adumbrabat hauddubiè. Nominatim autem respexit venturi Christi ex mortuis resurrectionem: quod est pignus nostræ resurrectionis. Quamobrem in aduentu & resurrectione Christi ista cæremonia, vt & aliæ omnes huiusmodi cessarunt, nisi dicamus Christum nondum venisse, & resurrexisse. Odores etiam isti in sepulturis adhibeti non debent, nisi malumus odorem illum resurrectionis ipsius extinguere. Non ista dico eo animo quòd velim nullam sepulturę habeti rationem, quam quidem dictat & natura ipsa, quæ immortalitatem illam hominum aliquo modo sentit, ideoque suadet sepulturæ hominum rationem non mediocrem habeti, & recepta consuetudo primùm quidem patrū, inde à condito mundo, qui non tam à natura quam à Deo edocti honore habuerunt sepulturę. Hinc illę ablutiones Act 9.37. hinc condimenta adhibitis odoribus, vt hic legimus: hęc, inquā, & alia ipsę gloriæ resurrectionis sepultorū obsignarunt: deinde idé docet consuetudo sepeliendi vsurpata etiā ab Ethnicis & prophanis gentibus, idque ad imitationem Patrū: quāuis id ab iis factū fit, sine ipse resurrectionis, quia sine vero Dei vixerunt, sine quo omnes ceremoniæ mortuæ sunt & animæ suæ inanes. Anima enim quasi quæ viuificat cęremonias, est verbū & promissio Dei: quanquā in re sepulturæ, vt & in aliis officiis omnibus, traditi sunt Ethnici in mente reprobā. Nā ex iis aliqui corpora hominum, vt cadauera bellúarum insepulta abiecerunt, alij flammis comburenda commiserunt: quorum vtrunque inhumanum est & barbarum. Qui autē ex iis inhumandi consuetudine retinuerunt, degenerarunt in sumptus immodicos & pŏpas ad inanem gloriam comparatas. Quæ consuetudo Christianis hominibus etiam in sepultura
units.tr: Let us say, then, not without reason. who come to honour the Lord with some greater gift, but always to join hands with whoever else comes, whether they are furnished with greater gifts or lesser. For there ought to be in us this zeal for the Lord and his glory, so that, forgetting ourselves, we think only of him and of his glory. As is the custom of the Jews. He teaches that this was done in accordance with the custom and rite of the Jews. This ceremony and rite, like all other ceremonies, undoubtedly foreshadowed Christ and his coming in some way. But it especially looked forward to the resurrection of the coming Christ from the dead, which is the pledge of our resurrection. Therefore at the coming and resurrection of Christ this ceremony, like all others of this kind, has ceased, unless we say that Christ has not yet come and risen. Odours too used in burials ought not to be used, unless we would rather extinguish that odour of his resurrection itself. I do not say this with the intention that I want no regard to be had for burial, which indeed nature itself dictates, which in some way perceives the immortality of men, and therefore urges that men's burial be given no small regard, and the custom accepted first by the fathers, from the beginning of the world, who were taught to honour burial not so much by nature as by God. Hence those washings of Acts 9.37; hence the spices applied with the odours, as we read here. These and other things, I say, sealed the glory of the resurrection of the buried; and then the same custom of burying, adopted even by the heathen and profane nations, and that in imitation of the fathers, though it was done by them without the true resurrection, since they lived without the true God, without whom all ceremonies are dead and their souls empty. For the promise and word of God is the soul which, as it were, gives life to the ceremonies. Yet in the matter of burial, as in all other duties, the heathen were given over to a reprobate mind. For some of them cast out the bodies of men, like the carcasses of beasts, unburied; others committed them to the flames to be burnt. Both are inhuman and barbarous. But those who retained the custom of burial fell away into immoderate expenses and pomp, arranged for empty glory. This custom must be avoided by Christians also in burial, as in the burial of kings.

units.la: { } Regum est vitanda: quos etiam ne patres quidem ipsos, & veterem illam Ecclesiam imitari in sepulturis suis oportet, ne vmbris ipsum corpus, & odorem resurrectionis Christi, illis odoribus exquisitis excludere videantur. Modum autem in sepultura tenebimus, si duo haec extrema defugerimus: primum contemptum sepulturae: deinde superstitiosam, quae sapit vel ambitionem, vel superstitionem. Est autem mediocritas ipsa, simplex illa & Christiana honestas, habita interim ratione temporum, locorum & personarum. Haec de sepultura hactenus quam potuimus paucis.
units.tr: Nor should they imitate even the fathers themselves and the ancient Church in their burials, lest they seem to shut out the body itself and the odour of Christ's resurrection with those exquisite perfumes, as if with shadows. We shall keep to moderation in burial if we avoid these two extremes: first, contempt of burial; then, a superstitious burial, which savours of either ambition or superstition. Moderation itself, that simple and Christian decency, is to be observed, with regard meanwhile to times, places and persons. So much on burial, as briefly as we could.

units.la: In eo autem loco ubi crucifixus. Duę sunt sepulturae Christi partes; prior involutio ipsius in sindone cū applicatis aromatibus: de hac iā egimus: posterior est inhumatio, de qua iam dicemus. Primum, occurrit locus in quo inhumatus est & sepultus, & locus primū in genere, nēpe hortus, qui à situ suo descriptus est. Erat in eo loco vbi crucifixus est Christus. Hunc locū delegerunt Iosephus & Nicodemus, quia is propinquior erat. Propinquiorē autem locum delegerunt, quia appropinquabat tempus celebrandi Paschatis, quod erat vespertinum: non autem iam longe aberat vespere: sed aliud fuit consilium Dei in loco illo eligendo, vtpote celebri & conspicuo, qui non procul aberat ab vrbe, vt ex notitia loci resurrectio Christi eruderet notior & illustrior: deinde occurrit locus particularis, nempe monumentū in quo positus est. Hic locus particulariter descriptus est a petra vnde est excīsum hoc monumentū: non erat effossum ex humo, sed excisum e petra. Tertiò descriptus est hic sepulturae locus particularis ab eo cui fuit destinatus, nēpe Iosepho ipsi: sibi enim excidit monumentum hoc ipsum ac sibi apparauit. Sibi autem destinatum & apparatum Domino iam mortuo lubens concessit. In particulari hoc sepulturae loco qui ipse insignis fuit ac conspicuus, videmus Patris prouidentiam, qui vel ex illo loco voluit filij sui resurrectionem innotescere. Loci quoque ac monumenti species, nempe nouum erat, excisum erat e lapide, destinatum erat viro nobili ac honorabili, addit aliquid honoris sepulturae Domini. Nouitate denique ipsa sepulchri, Dei prouidentia obuiam itum est calumniae aduerfariorum, qui, si fortasse monumentum vetus fuisset, obiecissent alium aliquem non Dominum ex monumento resurrexisse, omnibus modis voluit Pater innotescere resurrectionem filij sui, sine qua nulla peccatorum remissio. Nam resurrexit ad iustificationem nostri De loco hactenus, sequitur inhumatio. Ioseph us et Nicodemus arreptum posuerunt in hoc monumento, et lapidem magnum aduoluerunt ostio monumenti. Hoc ab iis factum procul dubio consilio honorandi Dominum in sepultura sua: nam nihil est ab iis praetermissum quod vel utilitati, vel ornamento posset esse Domino in sepultura sua. Quanquam Pater Christi etiam in aduoluto hoc grandi lapide voluit obuiam ire calumniae aduersariorum, ne illi post resurrectionem fortasse dicerent Dominum furto sublatum esse e sepulchro. Voluit itaque conspici Domini non furto sublatum esse, sed sua ipsius vi resurrexisse, neque modo remouisse grandem illum lapidem, sed rupisse vincula mortis et sepulchri. Nam in Christi resurrectione efficacitas illa fortis roboris Dei vel maxime sese exeruit. Atque haec sepultura Domini quam omnibus modis honorabilem esse vidimus, sive eius curatores respicias Ioseph um et Nicodemum, vitos honorabiles et illustres, sive partes eius, inuolutionem in pura sindone, inhumatione, honorabilia denique omnia: ut facile videas Dominum in sepultura sua, quae alioqui ignominiosa fuit, et postrema pars humiliationis gloriam suam aufspicatu esse. Sic et quicunque in Domino sepeliuntur per sepulturam alioqui in se igno miniosam, ad gloriam illam aeternam transeunt, eamque a sepultura aliquo etiam modo inchoant.
units.tr: In that place where he was crucified. Christ's burial has two parts: first, his wrapping in the linen cloth with the spices applied, which we have already discussed; second, his interment, which we will now discuss. First, there is the place where he was buried and entombed, and the place in general, namely a garden, described by its situation. It was in the place where Christ was crucified. Joseph and Nicodemus chose this place because it was nearer. They chose a nearby place because the time for celebrating the Passover was approaching, and that day was the evening of the Passover, and evening was not far off. But God had another purpose in choosing that place, since it was well known and conspicuous and not far from the city, so that the resurrection of Christ might become better known and more illustrious from the familiarity of the place. Next there is the particular place, namely the tomb in which he was laid. This place is described particularly by the rock from which the tomb was cut: it was not dug out of the ground but hewn out of the rock. Third, this particular place of burial is described by the man for whom it was destined, namely Joseph himself, for he had hewn this tomb for himself and prepared it for himself. Yet he gladly gave to the Lord, now dead, what had been destined and prepared for himself. In this particular burial place, which was itself remarkable and conspicuous, we see the providence of the Father, who wished the resurrection of his Son to be made known even from that place. The character of the place and the tomb also added some honour to the burial of the Lord: it was new, it was hewn from stone, and it was destined for a noble and honourable man. Finally, by the very newness of the sepulchre, God's providence met the slander of the adversaries, who, had the tomb been old, might have alleged that some other man, not the Lord, had risen from it. The Father wished in every way to make known the resurrection of his Son, without which there is no forgiveness of sins, for he rose for our justification. So much for the place; there follows the entombment. Joseph and Nicodemus took the body and laid it in this tomb, and they rolled a great stone to the door of the tomb. Without doubt they did this with the intention of honouring the Lord in his burial, for they omitted nothing that could be of use or ornament to the Lord in his burial. Yet the Father of Christ also wished, by this great stone rolled across, to meet the slander of the adversaries, lest they should later say that the Lord had been stolen from the sepulchre. He wished it to be seen that the Lord was not taken away by theft, but rose by his own power, not merely removing that great stone but breaking the bonds of death and the grave. For in Christ's resurrection that effective strength of God's mighty power chiefly showed itself. And this burial of the Lord, which we have seen to be honourable in every way, whether you look at those who cared for it, Joseph and Nicodemus, honourable and illustrious men, or at its parts, the wrapping in pure linen and the entombment, in short, at all its honourable features: so that you may easily see that the Lord, in his burial, which was otherwise ignominious, and in the last part of his humiliation, began his glory. So too whoever is buried in the Lord, through a burial otherwise ignominious in itself, passes over into that eternal glory, and in some measure begins it from the burial.

units.la: 8. Mulieres Christum vsque ad monumentum sequuntur.
units.tr: 8. The women follow Christ as far as the tomb.

units.la: Maria Magdalene vero. Obiter inserta est historia de Maria Magdalene, et Maria Iosis matre. De his primum dictum est quod sedebant contra sepulchrum, haec Christum sequutae ad crucem, ad monumentum vsque eum persequuntur. Indicium, quidem amoris ipsarum erga Dominum: sed potius argumentum efficaciae et amoris Domini. Spirabat enim corpus illud de mortuo amorem admirabilem. Mortuum enim fuit pro peccatis mundi, et sic dilexit Christus mundum hunc, ut pro eo traderet mortem semetipsum. Quod si enim Deus diligat nos priorprofectò fieri non potest, quin ipsum diligamus: & nemo potestvenire ad Christum, nisi Pater eum traxerit. Sequuntúque Dominum ad monumentum vsque factæ sunt testes quoque sepulturæ Domini, vt prius sequuntur eum ad crucem, factæ sunt testes crucis. Crucis & sepulturæ totidem præcones euaserunt, & hæc docuerunt etiam Apostolos ipsos Domini. Nunquâ enim sine fructu aliquo sequemur Dominum ad monumentum vsque. Sedent é regione, sedentes spectabant monumentum, vbi ponebatur: spectabant quidem cum dolore, sed cũ gaudio etiam fidei & spei: secus enim spectare sepulchrum illud non sustinuissent. Spectabant etiam non animo curioso & otioso, sed animo solicito & anxio, de modo illo quo ponerētur ipsius corpus in sepulchro: atque ita vel intuitu hoc suo ministrant Domino in sepultura. Qui enim opus Domini cũ animo ipsius studioso, ac de ipso solicito intuetur, etsi manum ad opus non admoucat, tamen vel beneuolo suo animo & propensa voluntate dicitur ministrare Domino, & in swuepɣeis numeratur. Tanti facit Dominus vel nutum solū, & animi soiam assensionem. Sed non contentæ mulieres inseruire sepulturæ Domini sola animi solicitudine & studio; reuersa domum parauerunt aromata & vnguenta, quæ non statim afferunt ad vngendum corpus Domini: nam sabbatho quieuerunt propter mandatum: non contentæ igitur solo studio & propensa voluntate, conferre volūt aliquid in commune & re ipsa beneuolum animū ostendere. Quod si ipsæ priūs non fuissent perfusæ maiori odore sepulchri Domini, profectò his odoribus perfundere sepulchrū Domini non curassent: nisi enim alle&ti priūs beneficiis ipsius in ipsum non sumus benefici. Nã quod reddimus ipsi, ab ipso iam priùs accepimus. Qui autem acceperunt à Domino gratiam aliquâ, præsertim spiritualem, ij cogitant de compensanda gratia, vt accepta illa gratia redeat ad authorem suum & datorē: ipsam etiam vitam suam, nedum bona ista temporaria Domino & authori vitæ & omnium bonorū authori & datori reddunt. Qui autem nihil reddere volunt, ne bonorum quidem istorum temporariorum & externorum, næ illi quidem hoc ipso arguunt, se non accepisse spiritualem gratiam, acceperunt quidem externa ista, regna, dominia, diuitias, honores, sed internam gratiam Christi non acceperunt, cuius si comparatio bonorum fit, vel sola vnica praeponderat.
units.tr: But Mary Magdalene. The story of Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses is inserted in passing. Of these women it was said first that they sat opposite the sepulchre; these women, who had followed Christ to the cross, now follow him right to the tomb. This is a sign of their love for the Lord, but it is rather a proof of the efficacy and the love of the Lord. For that body, though dead, breathed out a wonderful love. He died for the sins of the world, and so Christ loved this world that he gave himself to death for it. For if God first loves us, it cannot but be that we love him in return, and no one can come to Christ unless the Father draws him. And as they followed the Lord as far as the tomb, they became witnesses also of the Lord's burial, just as they had followed him to the cross and become witnesses of the cross. They became heralds of the cross and of the burial, and they taught these things even to the Lord's own apostles. For we shall never follow the Lord as far as the tomb without some fruit. They sat opposite, and sitting they watched the tomb where he was laid. They watched indeed with grief, but also with the joy of faith and hope; otherwise they could not have endured to look at that sepulchre. Nor did they watch with an idle and curious mind, but with an anxious and solicitous mind, concerned as to the manner in which his body was laid in the sepulchre; and so by this very watching they minister to the Lord in his burial. For whoever watches the work of the Lord with a mind eager for it and anxious about it, even if he does not put his hand to the work, yet is said to minister to the Lord by his kindly mind and willing disposition, and is counted among the fellow-workers [συνεργοί]. So much does the Lord value even a mere nod and the assent of the mind. But the women, not content to serve the Lord's burial only with anxious concern and zeal, went home and prepared spices and ointments, which they did not at once bring to anoint the Lord's body, for they rested on the sabbath because of the commandment. Not content, then, with zeal and a willing disposition alone, they wished to contribute something to the common cause and in deed to show a kindly mind. But if they had not first been filled with the greater fragrance of the Lord's sepulchre, they would surely not have cared to pour these perfumes over the Lord's tomb. For unless we are first drawn by his benefits, we do not become beneficial to him. What we give back to him we have already received from him. Those who have received from the Lord some grace, especially a spiritual one, consider how to repay that grace, so that the grace received may return to its author and giver. They give back to the Lord, the author of life and of all good things and its giver, even their own life, not to speak of these temporal goods. But those who wish to give back nothing, not even these temporal and external goods, by that very fact show that they have not received spiritual grace. They have indeed received these external things, kingdoms, dominions, riches, honours, but they have not received the inner grace of Christ, which, if it is compared with the other goods, alone outweighs them all.

units.la: Matthæi 27.
units.tr: Matthew 27.

units.la: 62 Postero autem die quæ est post parasceuen, couenerunt primary Sacerdotes & Pharisæi ad Pilatum,
units.tr: 62 On the next day, which is the day after the Preparation, the chief priests and Pharisees gathered together before Pilate,

units.la: 63 Dicentes, Domine, meminimus planum illum dixisse, quòd adhuc viueret, Tertio post die suscitabor.
units.tr: 63 Saying, Sir, we remember that this deceiver said, while he was still alive, After three days I will rise again.

units.la: 64 Iube ergo muniri sepulchrum vsque in diem tertium, ne quando veniant discipuli eius nocte, & furentur eum, dicantque populo, Suscitatus est a mortuis: & erit vltimus error peior priore.
units.tr: 64 Therefore order the tomb to be guarded until the third day, lest his disciples come by night and steal him and say to the people, He has risen from the dead; and the last error will be worse than the first.

units.la: 65 Dixit eis Pilatus, Habetis custodiam, abite, munite sicut scitis.
units.tr: 65 Pilate said to them, You have a guard; go, make it as secure as you know how.

units.la: 66 Ipsi autem profecti munierunt sepulchrum obsignato lapide cum custodia.
units.tr: 66 So they went and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone and setting the guard.

units.la: Equitur iam sepulto Christo sepulchri ipsius custodia obtinetur per petitionem. Petitionis tempus notatur, Postero, inquit, die, qui nimirum erat post parasceuen. Is dies erat sabbathi, cuius initium fuit vesperaqua celebrarunt Iudæi pascha suum. Nam Iudæi diem naturalem inchoarunt à nocte. Petitio dirigitur ad Pilatum iudicem. In hoc Christi negotio nihil sine iudice terrestri factum; eo fine vt nos plane liberaremur à Iudice illo caelesti. Qui petitionem faciunt sunt principes Sacerdotum & Pharisæi congregati in vnum. Plures quidem in tota ista actione, repetitas petitiones, & multos petitores; ex his aliquot malos, aliquot bonos, multos malos, paucos bonos. Mille clamant, Crucifige, crucifige: multi petunt vt confringeretur crura Domini: multi petunt vt munitur eius sepulchrum custodia, & consequenter eius rectio ignoraretur. Vnicus Iosephus petit, vt sublatus periretur. Hoc ipsum visu venit, quoties pij propter nomen Christi trahuntur ad tribunalia principum terrestrium, tum multos inuenias qui crucem, qui ignes, qui tormenta deposcant: vix vnum autem qui vitam innocentum hominum,
units.tr: Now that Christ is buried, the guarding of his tomb is secured by a petition. The time of the petition is noted: "On the next day," it says, which was of course the day after the Preparation. That day was the Sabbath, whose beginning was the evening on which the Jews celebrated their Passover, for the Jews began the natural day from night. The petition is addressed to Pilate, the judge. In this business of Christ nothing was done without an earthly judge, so that we might be wholly freed from that heavenly Judge. Those who make the petition are the chief priests and Pharisees gathered together. In the whole of this affair there were many petitions, repeated, and many petitioners: of these some were bad, some good, many bad, few good. A thousand cry, Crucify, crucify; many ask that the legs of the Lord be broken; many ask that his tomb be guarded, and so that his rising be unknown. Only Joseph asks that he be taken down and buried. This very thing happens whenever the godly are dragged before the tribunals of earthly princes: then you will find many who demand the cross, the fires, the torments, and scarcely one who asks for the lives of innocent men,

units.la: Iudæis id postulantibus, à iudice Pilato concessa.
units.tr: granted by the judge Pilate to the Jews who asked for it.

units.la: Mundi furor aduersus Christum & Christi membra. minum, qui sepulturam. Qua quidem re profecto non minus adeoque etiam maius periculû creatur ipsis viris principibus, quibus res est cû Christo, magis quàm cum hominibus, ne ipsi implicentur reatu illo & damnatione perversae multitudinis. Implicatus quidem est Pilatus; neque vero id eum excusabit quod corpus Domini iam crucifixum & mortuum condonarit Iosepho sepelien- dum. Quantulum enim est illud sepulturae beneficium, cum iam in crucem egeris hominem innocentem? Parva ista concessa in gratiam bonorum non excusant, si magna concesserint viri principes in gratiam malorum & perfequutorum. Sed nunc videamus petitionem, Domine, inquiunt, memores quod ille, &c. dixerit dum adhuc in vivis esset. Post tres dies resurgam, iube ergo muniri sepulchrum usque in tertium diem: ad hoc ne innotescat illa gloriosa ipsius quam praedixit resurrectio. Concedo quidem petitionem hanc ab ipsis ideo factam, ut obscuraretur gloria resurrectionis ipsius, &, ut, si fieri possit, vi detineretur in sepulchro. Verùm Dominus qui è tenebris lucem educit, vertit hanc ipsam eorum petitionem in manifestationem gloriosae resurrectionis Christi. Neque enim magis inservire potuisset manifestationi resurrectionis illius Christi, si ad eam rem mercede fuissent conducti. Ita enim solet Dominus consilia & prava facinora impiorum convertere in suam gloriam & ignominiam ipsorum. Dicam id quod fortasse mirum alicui videatur, perversa quaeque consilia, & facta impiorum magis in Dei gloriam cedere solent, quàm bona consilia & facta piorum. Maius enim est lucem è tenebris educere, quàm lucem è luce. Is quidem artifex est longè peritissimus & potentissimus, qui lucem è tenebris, vitam ex morte educit, & vocat ea quae non sunt, quasi sint. Non tamen istos excusat hoc Dei tantum, támque admirabile artificium. Nam post tantam divinae gloriae in illis, de quibus diximus, miraculis manifestationem: tamen in Christum vt impostorem (sic enim vocant eum) sic inuehi, est non tantùm Deum oppugnare, sed in ipsius Dei faciem conspuere. Verùm ad extremam istam malitiam non statim est deuentum, sed eius minora & magistrnuia erant initia cum Christus primum se manifesta-ret: deinde in peius processerunt continuò cum Christus apud eos ageret. Cum vero ad crucem, mortem & sepulturam ipsius ventum esset,iam consummata est desperata illa eorum malitia; vt tristissimo eorum exemplo discas quanto cum periculo coniunctum sit illud, si semel resistas Spiritui sancto & oblatam illam Christi lucem respuas. Ad maiorem, inquit Paulus, procedent impietatem. Quamobrem, quando & quoties se profert lux illa Dei, auide eam arripiamus, nisi malimus tandem extremam duritiem cordis contrahere, & in horribilem excæcationem incidere. Porro quoties legimus apud Euangelistas, tot blasphemas voces, vt & nominatim hoc loco, toties succurrat nobis eas esse proditas à Spiritu sancto de industria, vt intelligamus nimirum quæ Christus pro nobis passus est, non tantum in vita, sed in morte, denique post mortem. Ipse enim impostor agnominatus est, vt nos ab impostura liberaret. Conuitia eorum qui conuitiantur tibi, inciderunt in me. Tantum enim ab eo abesse debemus, vt offendamus, & in eum impingamus ob hanc causam, vt è contra vel hac ipsa de causa in eum magis credamus, præsertim cum videamus blasphemias eiusmodi & totam istam ignominiam cedere tandem in Christi gloriam. Nam vt de presenti hac contumelia dicam, hoc ipso quod in eum inuecti sunt isti vt impostorem, eum ab impostura nota vindicarunt, ac tanquam veracem iustificarunt: eò enim Dei prouidentia res tandem rediit. Dixit eis Pilatus. Hactenus fuit istorum petitio, sequitur Pilati responsio. Facile concedit quod petunt: omnia facile impetrantur à Pilato, bona, mala: vt videas miserum tunc inseruisse libidini hominum, quæ ipsa seruitus est miserrima. Et reipsa quidem viri principes, qui Deum & æquitatem non habent ante oculos, verum seipsos, commodum suum, gloriam suam, illi serui sunt seruorum. Nam necesse est eos dum non Deum, sed se respiciunt in vita sua, necesse, inquam, est sua ipsorum causa multa inique facere, ex arbitratu multorum, & fas & nefas, æquum & iniquum iuxta æstimare. Vbi enim meta ad quam aliquid dirigitur tur non est iusta, oportet cursum ad metam flexuosum esse & iniustum, non ex voluntate Dei, sed hominum. Ipsi autem profecti. Impetrarunt quod voluerunt, impetratum nunc exequuntur. Munierunt sepulchrum custodia, obsignant lapidem annulo, nimirum signatorio. Atque ita omnes arcet vel ab eius attactu. Nam sigillum hoc violare capitale fuit. Quo magis laborant in detinendo quasi Domino in sepulchro, eo illustriorem reddunt resurrectionem ipsius: quae ipsa non potuit impediri, vel custodia, vel signaculo isto: quin potius hoc suo sigillo obsignatum & obturarunt os suum, ne exuscitato iam Christo et mortuis, haberent quod aduersus ipsius resurrectionem reluctante conscientia, strenuè oppugnarent.
units.tr: The rage of the world against Christ and Christ's members. ...men, who ask for burial. Indeed this creates no less, and even greater, danger for the princes themselves, who have to deal with Christ rather than with men, lest they become entangled in that guilt and condemnation of the perverse multitude. Pilate is indeed entangled, nor will it excuse him that he handed over the body of the Lord, already crucified and dead, to Joseph to be buried. For how small is that favour of burial, when you have already crucified an innocent man? Small things granted to please good men do not excuse, if princes have granted great things to please evil men and persecutors. But now let us look at the petition: "Sir," they say, "we remember that he, etc., said while he was still alive, After three days I will rise. Therefore order the tomb to be guarded until the third day," namely so that his glorious resurrection, which he foretold, may not become known. I grant that this petition was made by them so that the glory of his resurrection might be obscured and, if it were possible, so that he might be held by force in the tomb. But the Lord, who brings light out of darkness, turned this very petition of theirs into the manifestation of Christ's glorious resurrection. Indeed, it could not have served the manifestation of that resurrection any better had they been hired for that purpose. For the Lord is accustomed to turn the counsels and wicked deeds of the impious to his own glory and their shame. I will say what may perhaps seem strange to someone: the perverse counsels and deeds of the impious tend more to the glory of God than the good counsels and deeds of the pious. For it is greater to bring light out of darkness than light out of light. He is by far the most skilful and powerful craftsman who brings light out of darkness and life out of death, and calls those things that are not as though they were. Yet this so admirable work of God does not excuse these men. For after so great a manifestation of divine glory in those miracles of which we have spoken, to rail against Christ as an impostor (for so they call him) is not only to attack God but to spit in the very face of God. But they did not come to that extreme wickedness at once; its beginnings were smaller and milder when Christ first revealed himself, and then it grew continually worse as Christ dealt with them. But when it came to his cross, death and burial, their desperate malice was at last complete, so that from their most sorrowful example you may learn how great a danger is joined to resisting the Holy Spirit and rejecting the light of Christ once it is offered to you. "They will proceed to greater impiety," says Paul. Therefore, when and as often as that light of God shows itself, let us seize it eagerly, unless we prefer at last to contract extreme hardness of heart and fall into a dreadful blindness. Moreover, as often as we read in the Evangelists of so many blasphemous words, here even by name, so often let it come to mind that these were recorded by the Holy Spirit deliberately, so that we may understand what Christ suffered for us, not only in life but in death and, finally, after death. For he was himself called an impostor, so that he might free us from imposture. "The reproaches of those who reproach you have fallen upon me." We ought to be so far from being offended by him and stumbling over him for this reason, that on the contrary, for this very reason, we should believe in him all the more, especially since we see blasphemies of this kind, and all this shame, turning at last to the glory of Christ. For, to speak of this present insult: by the very fact that they railed against him as an impostor, they freed him from the stain of imposture and justified him as truthful; for by God's providence the matter came in the end to exactly that. "Pilate said to them." So far was their petition; now follows Pilate's answer. He easily grants what they ask. Everything is easily obtained from Pilate, good and bad alike, so that you may see the wretched man served the desire of men, which is the most wretched slavery. And indeed princes who do not keep God and equity before their eyes, but themselves, their own advantage and their own glory, are slaves of slaves. For necessarily, while in their life they look not to God but to themselves, they must, I say, do many unjust things for their own sake, and judge right and wrong, lawful and unlawful, by the will of many. For where the goal to which something is directed is not just, the course towards the goal must be crooked and unjust, not according to the will of God but of men. "But they went." They obtained what they wanted and now carry out what was obtained: they guard the tomb with a guard, and seal the stone with a ring, namely the signet. And so they keep everyone away, even from touching it, for to break this seal was a capital offence. The harder they labour to hold the Lord, as it were, in the tomb, the more illustrious they make his resurrection, which could not be prevented either by the guard or by that seal. Rather, by sealing it with their own seal they have closed their own mouths, so that once Christ had risen from the dead they would have nothing with which to fight vigorously against his resurrection, their conscience struggling against it.

units.la: Matthæi 28.
units.tr: Matthew 28.

units.la: 1 Exiremo autem Sabbatho, quum lucesceret in primum diem hebdomadis, venit Maria Magdalene, & altera illa Maria, ut spectarent sepulchrum.
units.tr: 1 But late on the Sabbath, as it began to dawn toward the first day of the week, came Mary Magdalene and the other Mary, to see the sepulchre.

units.la: 2 Et ecce terræmotus factus est magnus. Angelus enim Domini quum descendisset è cælo, accessit & advolvit saxum ab ostio, sedebatque super illud.
units.tr: 2 And behold, there was a great earthquake. For the angel of the Lord, descending from heaven, came and rolled back the stone from the door, and sat upon it.

units.la: 3 Erat autem visus eius ut fulgur, & vestimentum eius album sicut nix.
units.tr: 3 His appearance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow.

units.la: 4 Custodes autem perculsi sunt præ ipsius timore, & facti sunt sicut mortui.
units.tr: 4 The guards were struck with fear of him, and became as dead men.

units.la: Marci 16.
units.tr: Mark 16.

units.la: 1 Et exacto intercedente Sabbatho, Maria Magdalene, & Maria Iacobi mater & Salome emerant aromata, ut venientes ungerent eum.
units.tr: 1 And when the Sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome had bought spices, that they might come and anoint him.

units.la: Lucæ 24.
units.tr: Luke 24.

units.la: 1 Primo autem die hebdomadis, profundo diluculo venerunt ad monumentum, ferentes quæ paraverant aromata, & nonnulla cum ipsis.
units.tr: 1 But on the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared, and some others with them.

units.la: ATque hæc hactenus de Christi sepultura: sequitur nunc ipsius gloriosa resurrectio, de qua nobis discendum erit, ex quatuor Euangelistis inter sese collatis. Tempus resurrectionis Christi non est hic præcise notatum, hora nimirum noctis illa in qua resurrexerit: de modo resurrectionis ipsius nulla facta est mentio, nullos legitimus eius fuisse testes, qui ipsum resurgentem viderint: sic nimirum disponente Deo secus quam sapientia carnis poscceret. At certum est ex Euangelio eum resurrexisse tertio die: hoc est initio diei Dominicæ, quam vocamus, vtpote nocte ea quæ insecuta est Sabbathum. Resurrectionem etiam ipsius testatam legimus lucalenter & abundè paulò post quam resurrexisset ex mortuis. Primùm enim de ea testata est mulieribus, sepulchri vacuitas, deinde testatus est mulieribus angelus Dei: tertiò etiam mulieribus testatus est ipse Dominus, viuum se ipsis ingerens: postea mulieres de ea testatæ sunt, Apostoli Christi, etiam ipse Christus testatus est Apostolis de resurrectione sua. Et cùm exactum esset Sabbathum. Primùm est occasio in his verbis Marci, qua fictum est vt mulieres resurrectionis Domini testes erant: est autem ea; Mulieres hæ, nominatim Maria Magdalene & Maria Iacobi mater, & Salome emerunt aromata, vt venientes vngerent eum. Posteaquam Dominus humo commissus est à Iosepho & Nicodemo, hæ mulieres reuersæ sunt domum, vt pararent aromata & vnguenta: verùm quieuerunt die Sabbathi: neque statim quidem in reditu, vt mihi videtur, emerunt aromata: Verba enim Lucæ hoc non important, quæ ego sic expono: Reuersæ vero, inquit Lucas, parauerunt aromata & vnguenta, & Sabbatho quieuerunt: hoc est, quia Sabbathum instabat, quo celebrandum fuit Pascha, & parasceue tum fuit, ideo rem distulerunt in diem sequentem. Videntur mihi aromata empta & parata nocte ea quæ Sabbathum est sequuta. Hoc est quod dicit Marcus, Cùm transisset Sabbathum. Sed vt hæc missa faciamus, studium istud mulierum, & perseuerantia in instituto suo, præterea unda nō est. Non modò non deleuit memoriam eius quod iam istę instituerunt faciendum interueniens Sabbathum, sed ne remissiores quidem eas reddidit: ideòque die sequenti
units.tr: And so much for Christ's burial. Now follows his glorious resurrection, which we must learn about from the four Evangelists compared with one another. The time of Christ's resurrection is not stated precisely here, namely the hour of the night at which he rose; nor is anything said about the manner of his resurrection, and there were no lawful witnesses who saw him rising. God so arranged it, otherwise than the wisdom of the flesh would have demanded. But it is certain from the Gospel that he rose on the third day, that is, at the beginning of the day of the Lord, which we call Sunday, since it was the night that followed the Sabbath. We also read that his resurrection was attested fully and abundantly shortly after he had risen from the dead. For first the emptiness of the tomb bore witness to it to the women; then an angel of God bore witness to the women; thirdly the Lord himself bore witness to the women, presenting himself to them alive; afterwards the women bore witness to it to the apostles of Christ, and Christ himself bore witness to the apostles about his resurrection. And when the Sabbath was past. The first occasion is in these words of Mark, by which it came about that the women were witnesses of the Lord's resurrection. It is this: these women, namely Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome, bought spices, that coming they might anoint him. After the Lord had been committed to the ground by Joseph and Nicodemus, these women returned home to prepare spices and ointments; but they rested on the Sabbath day. Nor, as it seems to me, did they buy the spices at once on their return; for the words of Luke do not imply this, and I explain them thus: But they returned, says Luke, and prepared spices and ointments, and rested on the Sabbath; that is, because the Sabbath was at hand, on which the Passover was to be kept, and it was then the Preparation, therefore they deferred the matter to the following day. It seems to me that the spices were bought and prepared on the night that followed the Sabbath. This is what Mark means, When the Sabbath was past. But, setting these things aside, the zeal of these women and their perseverance in their purpose is not to be passed over. Not only did the intervening Sabbath not blot out the memory of what they had resolved to do, it did not even make them more lax. Therefore on the following day

units.la: {y} quenti recordatæ instituti illius sui, sedulò rem sunt aggressa. Hæsit enim Dominus in memoria ipsarum, etiā cum in Paschate & die Sabbathi celebrando occupata essent. Nos verò vix incepimus cogitare de opere Domini, tum statim eam cogitationem deponimus. Nox interveniens vel plane oblivionem inducit, vel certè remissionem reddit. Studium & zelus Dei non agit radices penitus in cordibus nostris. Sed explorandum est factum hoc mulierum: illud est extra controversiam, zelum istarum laudabilem esse ac studium illud erga Dominum, non satis commendari posse: sed factum ipsum culpandum esse ostendit vel unica hæc prædictio Domini, quod ipse tertio demum die resurrecturus esset. At istæ tertio die vivum inter mortuos quærebant. Dominus tamen ratione habita non tam facti quàm studij istarum, quàm dilectionis, quàm fidei, qua personæ istarum ipsi placuerunt, non modò non condonauit factū, sed & ipsum convertit in bonum ac salutem earum; quumque ipse instituerent & proponerent sibi vnctionem corporis demortui, fecit ut testes essent vivi. Diligentibus enim se Dominus omnia conferre facit ad bonum: & lucem è tenebris educit; hoc est, non tantùm gloriam nominis sui, sed etiam bonū & salutem suorū, quorum vel peccata ipsa cedere facit in ipsorum bonū.
units.tr: mindful of their resolve, they set about the task diligently. For the Lord stuck in their memory, even while they were occupied with keeping the Passover and the Sabbath day. But we, scarcely have we begun to think about the work of the Lord, when at once we put that thought aside. The intervening night either brings complete forgetfulness or at least makes us slack. The zeal and passion for God do not strike deep roots in our hearts. But this deed of the women must be examined: it is beyond dispute that their zeal is praiseworthy and their devotion to the Lord cannot be commended enough. Yet the deed itself is shown to be blameworthy even by this one prediction of the Lord, that he was to rise only on the third day. But these women were seeking the living among the dead on the third day. Nevertheless the Lord, taking into account not so much the deed as the zeal of these women, their love and their faith, by which their persons pleased him, not only did not pardon the deed but turned it to their good and salvation. For when they intended and proposed to themselves the anointing of a dead body, he made them witnesses of the living. For the Lord makes all things work together for good for those who love him, and he brings light out of darkness; that is, he brings about not only the glory of his name but also the good and salvation of his own, whose very sins he makes turn out to their good.

units.la: Extremo autem Sabbatho. Hactenus occasio fuit, nunc veniunt vnā ad sepulchrum Maria Magdalene, Maria Iacobi mater, & Salome cum aliis nonnullis, vt addit Lucas. Tempus quo veniunt præcisè est notatum ab omnibus Euangelistis. Matthæus dicit eas venisse vespera Sabbathi, hoc est septimanæ: quæ cùm septe constaret diebus, Sabbathi et dicta. Vespera septimanæ est finis. septimanæ vltimus, quę nimirū inclinat in principiū septimanæ sequentis. Sed ipse Matthæus verbis sequentibus exponit sc, quę subaudi vespera illucescit in primâ Sabbathi, hoc est septimanæ sequentis. Prima Sabbathi est dies Dominica, sc dicta ad recordationē resurrectionis Dni. Marcus vocat, valde mane primo Sabbathi: Lucas verò, prima Sabbathi diluculo profundo. Sed de tempore satis. Venerunt istæ ad monumentū, animo quidem vngendi Domini corpus, sed Deus aliò vertit earum aduentū, nempe
units.tr: But late on the Sabbath. So far the occasion; now Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome, with some others as Luke adds, come together to the sepulchre. The time at which they come is stated precisely by all the Evangelists. Matthew says they came late on the Sabbath, that is, of the week; and since the week consisted of seven days, it is called the Sabbath. The evening of the week is its last end, which indeed inclines toward the beginning of the following week. But Matthew himself explains this in the words that follow, namely that, understand, the evening dawned toward the first of the Sabbath, that is, of the following week. The first of the Sabbath is the Lord's day, so called in remembrance of the Lord's resurrection. Mark calls it very early on the first of the Sabbath; but Luke, at the first of the Sabbath, at very early dawn. But enough about the time. These women came to the tomb, indeed with the intention of anointing the body of the Lord; but God turned their coming to another end, namely

units.la: 2. Mulieres accedunt ad sepulchrum. ad hoc vt testes fierent resurrectionis Domini, & totidem praecones ipsius, qua quidem re honoratae sunt ipsae, etiam non sine Apostolorum aliquo dedecore, qui toto hoc tempore prae timore delituerunt. Earum autem exemplum verum esse illud Apostoli ostendit, Elegit Deus stulta, infirma, ignobilia quae sunt in mundo, ut pudefaciat sapientia, potentia, nobilia quaeque. Et illud quoque ostendit earum exemplum, quod in eadem epistola sequitur cap. 3.18. Si quis videtur sapiens in hoc saeculo, stultus fiat, ut fiat sapiens. Nam ipsi Apostoli, qui videbantur sapere, in scholam quasi istarum mulierum iam redacti, & ab iis informati, stulti quodammodo facti sunt, ut sapientes demum euaderent. Ita nos quoque hodierno die habemus istas resurrectionis Christi testes, adeo ut demirari nos oporteat ad testimonium resurrectionis Domini ex earum ore accipiendum: secus profecto nunquam futurum est, ut resurrectionis illius participes efficiamur, spreto nimirum hoc quod a Deo ordinatum est mulierum istarum testimonio. Ecce terrae motus factus. Narrantur quae inciderunt interea temporis, dum veniunt unā mulieres istae ad sepulchrum. Terrae motus magnus fit: causa addita est, quia Angelus descendit e coelo. Unā iter instituunt ad sepulchrum Domini, mulieres quidem Hierosolymis, Angelus vero e coelis veniēs. Missus est hic a Deo, mulierum in gratiam: missus autem est Angelus non homo aliquis a Deo, ad glorificandam nimirum resurrectionem illam Christi. Resurrectio enim Christi in se gloriosa fuit. Oportuit itaque nuntium resurrectionis primum gloriosum esse, qui glorificaret tam gloriosam legationem. Quāquam, ut fatear, quod verum est, magis a legatione illa glorificatus est legatus, quam a legato ipsa legatio. Res enim gloriosissima est resurrectio illa Iesu Christi, qua victor evasit mortis & sepulchri: cuius praedicatio vel Angelos ipsos honorat; ne dū homines, & inter homines summos etiam reges. Vt autem nuncius fuit gloriosus, & magis gloriosum nuntium: ita & legatum, vel legatione potius decorauit Deus terremotu isto ingeti. Oportuit enim tāti Regis, tantum ligatū, cum legatione tanta, cū honore & gloria in terrā descendere. Sed ratione habuit Deus etiam mulierum in hoc terraemotu, ut scilicet etiā ipsę praeparentur ad recipiendam tantam legationem cum fide & reuerētia. Ad prædicationem enim Euangelij opus est vt descen- damus cum animo cum fide & reuerentia præparato. Opusculum est abiectissimis quibusque siue viris, siue fœminis, Dei potentia, qua humilietur cordis ista innata altitudo & elatio, ad hoc vt legatum Dei cum legatione sua recipiat. Vt ne sit qui obiiciat nobis mulierculas istas quasi indignas tanta gloria siue legati, siue terræmotus, qui legati aduentum illum gloriosum reddidit: nam terræmotus, signum quoddam fuit sensibile præsentiæ diuinæ.
units.tr: 2. The women approach the sepulchre to become witnesses of the Lord's resurrection and, as it were, heralds of it. By this deed they were honoured, not without some dishonour to the apostles, who during all this time hid themselves for fear. Moreover, that their example is true is shown by that saying of the Apostle, God has chosen the foolish, the weak, the base things of the world, that he may shame the wise, the mighty, and the noble. Their example also shows what follows in the same epistle, ch. 3.18: If anyone among you seems to be wise in this age, let him become foolish, that he may become wise. For the apostles themselves, who seemed to be wise, were, as it were, brought into the school of these women and instructed by them, and became in a sense foolish, so that at last they might turn out wise. So we too today have these women as witnesses of Christ's resurrection, so that we ought to marvel that the testimony of the resurrection of the Lord is received from their mouth. Otherwise, certainly, it will never come about that we become partakers of that resurrection, if we despise this testimony of the women, which God has ordained. Behold, there was a great earthquake. There is narrated what happened meanwhile, while these women were coming together to the sepulchre. A great earthquake occurs; the cause is added, because an angel descended from heaven. The women set out together on the way to the Lord's sepulchre, indeed from Jerusalem, while the angel came from heaven. He was sent here by God, for the sake of the women; and the angel was sent, not some man from God, namely to glorify that resurrection of Christ. For the resurrection of Christ was glorious in itself. It was therefore fitting that the first message of the resurrection should be glorious, to glorify so glorious an embassy. Although, to confess what is true, the envoy was glorified by that embassy more than the embassy by the envoy. For that resurrection of Jesus Christ is a most glorious thing, by which he came forth victor over death and the grave; and the proclamation of it honours even the angels themselves, not to mention men, and among men even the highest kings. But as the messenger was glorious, and the message more glorious still, so God adorned the envoy, or rather the embassy, with this great earthquake. For it was fitting that so great a King, so great a message, should come down to earth with such an embassy, with honour and glory. But God also took account of the women in this earthquake, so that they too might be prepared to receive so great an embassy with faith and reverence. For to the preaching of the Gospel it is necessary that we descend with a mind prepared in faith and reverence. It is a small thing for the power of God to humble the innate height and pride of the heart of the most abject, whether men or women, so that they may receive the envoy of God with his embassy. Lest anyone object to us that these little women were unworthy of so great a glory, whether of the envoy or of the earthquake, which made the envoy's coming so glorious; for the earthquake was a certain sensible sign of the divine presence.

units.la: De uoluit lapidem. In Christo sepeliendo homines, vt- pote Ioseph & Nicodemus, aduoluerunt lapidem. At in resurrectione Christi vtitur Dominus non hominū, sed Angelorum ministerio: vt vel hinc videas quàm fuerit gloriosa Christi resurrectio, in qua iā Deitas illa inhabitāt in ipso, quæ in morte & sepultura eius ad tempus delitescebat, se exeruit ac gloriam suam manifestauit. Hinc omnia gloriosa in resurrectione Domini; etiam gloriosum ministerium fuit. Sepulturæ honor fuit quasi terrestris, administratus per homines: Resurrectionis gloria cœlestis fuit, administrata per Angelos. In sepultura ostendit se Dominum hominum, etiam honorabilium & illustrium quorumcunque: in resurrectione ostendit se Dominum Angelorum cœlestium, qui ipsi in resurrectione ministrarunt. Verum in hoc Angeli ministerio, & in lapide deuoluto rationem habuit mulierum, quæ aduentabant, imbecillitatisque eorum consuluit, quæ ipsæ suis viribus tantum lapidem ne loco quidem mouere potuerunt. Hinc videbimus postea eas, antequam nimirum deuolutum lapidem viderent, animadvertebant re inter se quærere. Mulieres quærebant Dominum, Dominus suppleт illud viribus Angeli quod deerat ipsis, misitque ante ipsas Angelum illum suum, qui paraeret id quo ipsis fuit opus. Sic agit cū suis Deus quotidie: Infirmitatem eorum supplet Angelorū viribus, & missis ante ipsos Angelis, cum aliquo prosi- cisc̄untur, præparat quibus ipsis est opus: adeo vt Dei illam providentia cogatur in admiratione habere. Sedebatque super. Deuoluto iam lapide non statim decedit Angelus, sed sedit super lapidem illum quem deuoluit, sturus. expectans scilicet mulieres iamiam affuturas, vt nimi- rum iis testaretur de Christi resurrectione. Primum enim testem resurrectionis oportuit Angelum esse, id enim resurrectionis gloria postulabat. Passio Christi primum testem habuit hominem: Sepultura primum testem habuit hominem: at resurrectio primum testem habuit Angelum: sic postulante gloria resurrectionis, in qua oportuit omnia gloriosa esse. Et in hoc quoque ratio mulierum aduentantium est habita: His enim satis fuit videre sepulchrum vacuum & inane, ad hoc vt certò intelligerent resurrexisse Christum, praesertim cum hoc iam praedictū acceperint ex ipsiusmet Christi ore, Dominum tertio die resurrecturum. Sed quae fuit infirmitas earum, oblitae iam sunt praedictionis illius Domini: ideoq; Dominus, vt deuoluto lapide per Angelum, consuluit infirmitati corporis earum, ita testimonio illo Angeli accedente ad inspectam ab iis sepulchri vacuitatem, consuluit infirmitati fidei earum. Deus omnibus modis infirmitati suorum consulit: quod si vnum aliquod de Christo testimonium non sufficiat, alterum adiicit secundo, deinde tertium, tertio denique quartum, donec tandem credant. Erat autem visus eius. Hactenus de aduentu Angeli, deq; lapide deuoluto ac sessione ipsius super lapidem. Iam sedens super lapidem describitur Angelus. 1. ab aspectu, erat sicut fulgur. 2. à vestimento: erat album sicut nix. 3. ab effectis praesentiae ipsius gloriosae ac terribilis: prae timore ipsius concussi sunt custodes, &c. Vt terrae motus ille magnus signum fuit praesentiae Dei comitantis Angelum: ita quoque eiusdem praesentiae signa fuerunt aspectus & fulgur, & vestimentum candidum vt nix: pertinebantque ad honorandam legationem tantam, & glorificandam resurrectionem illam Domini gloriosam: respiciebant quoque mulieres, easque praeparabant ad recipiendum cum fide & reverentia tantum nuncium cum tanto Euangelio & nuncio resurrectionis Domini. Vt autem de signis istis praesentiae Domini, nonnihil dicam: Non opus habuit Dominus vt mutuaretur vel fulgur à fulmine, vel candorem à nive, quasi vero hae species mutuatitiae aliquid decoris afferre possent ipsius praesentiae & gloriae incom
units.tr: He rolled away the stone. In burying Christ, men such as Joseph and Nicodemus rolled a stone against the tomb. But in Christ's resurrection the Lord uses the ministry not of men but of angels, so that you may see from this alone how glorious Christ's resurrection was. In it, that Deity which lay hidden for a time in his death and burial now dwells in him, and it showed itself and manifested its glory. Hence everything in the Lord's resurrection was glorious, even the ministry. The honour of the burial was, as it were, earthly, administered through men; the glory of the resurrection was heavenly, administered through angels. In the burial he showed himself Lord of men, even of the most honourable and illustrious of them; in the resurrection he showed himself Lord of the heavenly angels, who themselves ministered in the resurrection. But in this ministry of the angel, and in the stone rolled away, he took account of the women who were approaching and provided for their weakness, since by their own strength they could not even move the stone from its place. Hence we shall see later that before they saw the stone rolled away, they were wondering among themselves who would roll it back for them. The women sought the Lord, and the Lord supplied by the strength of an angel what was lacking to them, and sent before them his angel, who would prepare what they needed. So God deals with his people every day: he supplies their weakness with the strength of angels, and by sending angels ahead of them, he prepares what they need when they set out on some task, so that we are compelled to admire God's providence. And sat upon it. The angel did not leave at once after rolling away the stone, but sat upon the stone which he had rolled away, as a witness, plainly waiting for the women who were about to arrive, so that he might testify to them about Christ's resurrection. For the first witness of the resurrection had to be an angel; the glory of the resurrection demanded it. The passion of Christ had a man as its first witness; the burial had a man as its first witness; but the resurrection had an angel as its first witness, since the glory of the resurrection demanded this, for in it all things had to be glorious. In this too the approaching women were taken into account. For it was enough for them to see the sepulchre empty and bare, so that they might be certain that Christ had risen, especially since they had already heard this foretold from Christ's own mouth, that the Lord would rise on the third day. But their weakness had caused them to forget that prediction of the Lord; therefore the Lord, as by the rolling away of the stone through the angel he provided for the weakness of their body, so by the angel's testimony added to their inspection of the empty sepulchre, he provided for the weakness of their faith. God in every way provides for the weakness of his people; if one testimony about Christ is not enough, he adds a second, then a third, and finally a fourth, until at last they believe. And his appearance was. So far we have spoken of the coming of the angel, of the stone rolled away, and of his sitting upon the stone. Now the angel is described sitting upon the stone: (1) from his appearance, his countenance was like lightning; (2) from his clothing, his raiment was white as snow; (3) from the effects of his glorious and terrible presence, for fear of him the guards shook, etc. As that great earthquake was a sign of the presence of God accompanying the angel, so also the appearance and the lightning, and the raiment as white as snow, were signs of that same presence. They served to honour so great an embassy and to glorify that glorious resurrection of the Lord, and they also had regard for the women and prepared them to receive with faith and reverence so great a message, with so great a gospel and the announcement of the Lord's resurrection. But to say something about these signs of the Lord's presence: the Lord had no need to borrow lightning from the thunderbolt or whiteness from snow, as if these borrowed forms could add any beauty to his presence and glory. But it was so ordained, that by taking on these forms of his creatures he should lower himself to our capacity, and make visible what was otherwise invisible glory, and present it to our senses. Not indeed to the end that we should cling to those forms and external signs of his glory, but that by the eyes of the mind and of faith, through those external symbols, we should penetrate to that inner light, represented by the external symbols, but otherwise inaccessible, in which our God dwells and that incomprehensible majesty. And God himself, who wishes to be seen by his people, at the same time that they behold those external signs of his glory, kindles in their hearts that inner light and glory, represented by them. As the Apostle says, he who said that light should shine out of darkness is the one who shines in the hearts of his people. For fear of him. This is the effect of the presence of the angel upon the guards. They, accustomed before to tumults and to all the terrible spectacles of war, who had doubtless only a little before threatened even heaven itself, were, I say, so dismayed at the sight of this slight shadow, as it were, of God's glory, that they lost all sense and fell down for a time as dead. You may see those profane and atheistic men, who make a mockery of God and heaven, horribly shaken at the presence of God, however small, not only in the lightning in the sky but in the lightning itself. The cause lies not only in the presence of that majesty, but also in their own sin and evil conscience, which is stirred up and tormented together with the sight of that presence. For those who are well conscious of themselves are not wont to be so struck with terror at the sight of their God. Those women were indeed afraid, but they were not made as if dead, for a little after they gathered themselves together. Yet this presence and this glory of God which they beheld was the very glory which shines in the face of Christ, for it was the glory of Christ's resurrection, from which those guards ought to have drawn comfort. For that majesty of God, in itself terrible, yet while it shines in Christ is sweet and pleasant and effective for consolation. But it is sweet and pleasant only to those who are in Christ Jesus; to others, and to those who are outside Christ, such as those guards, being profane men and persecutors of Christ, it is terrible. I grant that even for those who are in Christ, as long as the remnants of sin remain in them, that majesty of God and his glorious presence are a terror. The women here are an example, who, on seeing the angel, were afraid. But when that indwelling sin has been wholly cast off, then indeed we shall be able to behold the glory of our Lord, which the reprobate will by no means be able to bear on that day; indeed, they will call on the mountains themselves to hide them from the sight of that Lamb. For if the mere shadow of that glory of Christ which shone out in the angel was so great a terror to these men, how great will be the horrors when the reprobate see not only one glorious angel but thousands of angels, and even more glorious than that angel was then? And they will behold not only glorious angels, but the Lord himself as Judge, with all his majesty?

units.la: Angeli aspectus, quid effecerit. comparabili: sed ita visum est, assumptis his speciebus creaturarum suarum sese demittere ad captum nostrum, & inuisibilem alioqui illam gloriam, visibilem facere & sensibus nostris obuiam: non quidem co fine vt nos hæreamus in speciebus illis & externis signis gloriæ ipsius, sed vt oculis animi & fidei, per externa illa symbola, penetremus in lucem illam internam, externis symbolis repræsentatam, alioqui inaccessam, quam habitat Deus noster & maiestas illa incomprehensibilis. Atque ipse Deus qui vult à suis conspici, simul cum inspectis externis illis signis gloriæ suæ, lucis illa & gloria interna ac repræsentata, cordibus suorum afflget, &, vt ait Apostolus, qui dixit vt è tenebris lux splendescere, is est qui splendet in cordibus suorum. Præ ipsius timore. Hoc est effectu præsentiæ Angeli in custodibus. Isti prius assuefacti tumultibus, & horribilibus quibusque in bello spectaculis, qui etiam paulo ante haud dubie in cælos ipsos sunt comminati: Isti, inquam, ad inspectam hanc tenuem quasi vmbellam gloriæ Dei, sic consternati sunt, vt omnem sensum amitterent, & vt mortui, ad tempus corruerent. Videas prophanos istos & atheos, qui Deum & cœlos ludibrio habent, ad Dei tamen præsentiam quantulamcunque, non tantum in cœlo fulgurante, sed in ipsomet fulgure, horribiliter concuti. Causa quidem est, non tantum in præsentia aliqua illius maiestatis, sed etiam in peccato & mala conscientia ipsorum, quæ simul cum aspectu illius præsentiæ excitatur atque cingilat. Qui enim bene sibi conscij sunt, non solent sic horrore concuti ad aspectum Dei sui. Mulierculæ istæ expauerunt quidem, sed non sunt factæ veluti mortuæ, paulo enim post sese collegerunt. Fuit quidem hæc præsentia & gloria ista Dei quam inspexerunt, ea ipsa gloria, quæ splendet in facie Christi: erat enim gloria resurrectionis Christi, ex qua oportuit custodes istos consolationem capere. Majestas enim illa Dei, alioqui in se terribilis, tamen in Christo dum splendet suauis ac iucunda, & ad consolationem efficax est: verum suauis est ac iucunda iis duntaxat qui sunt in Christo Iesu: alijs vero & iis qui sunt extra Christum, cuiusmodi fuerunt custodes isti, vtpote prophani homines & Christi persecutores, terribilis est. Fateor iis etiam qui sunt in Christo quandiu manent in ipsis reliquiae istae peccati; Maiestatem istam Dei ac praesentiam gloriosam esse terrori. Exemplo sunt mulieres istae, quae inspecto Angelo expauerunt: verum cum exutum iam penitus fuerit peccatum istud inhaerens, tum quidem sustinebimus illam Domini nostri gloriam intueri, quod reprobi in illo die ferre nequaquam poterunt: quin inclamaturi sunt montes ipsos, vt iis abscondantur a conspectu illo agni. Quod si enim istis hominibus vel vmbra istius gloriae Christi, qui in Angelo emicuit, tanto terrori fuit, quanti tum futuri sunt horrores cum reprobi videbunt, non tantum Angelum aliquem gloriosum, sed millionesAngelorum, eosque etiam magis gloriosos quam tum fuit iste Angelus: neque vero gloriosos tantum Angelos inspecturi sunt, sed ipsum Dominum iudicem cum vniuersa sua illa gloria & Maiestate?
units.tr: The effect of the angel's appearance. For fear of him. This is the effect of the presence of the angel upon the guards. They, accustomed before to tumults and to all the terrible spectacles of war, who had doubtless only a little before threatened even heaven itself, were, I say, so dismayed at the sight of this slight shadow, as it were, of God's glory, that they lost all sense and fell down for a time as dead. You may see those profane and atheistic men, who make a mockery of God and heaven, horribly shaken at the presence of God, however small, not only in the lightning in the sky but in the lightning itself. The cause lies not only in the presence of that majesty, but also in their own sin and evil conscience, which is stirred up and tormented together with the sight of that presence. For those who are well conscious of themselves are not wont to be so struck with terror at the sight of their God. Those women were indeed afraid, but they were not made as if dead, for a little after they gathered themselves together. Yet this presence and this glory of God which they beheld was the very glory which shines in the face of Christ, for it was the glory of Christ's resurrection, from which those guards ought to have drawn comfort. For that majesty of God, in itself terrible, yet while it shines in Christ is sweet and pleasant and effective for consolation. But it is sweet and pleasant only to those who are in Christ Jesus; to others, and to those who are outside Christ, such as those guards, being profane men and persecutors of Christ, it is terrible. I grant that even for those who are in Christ, as long as the remnants of sin remain in them, that majesty of God and his glorious presence are a terror. The women here are an example, who, on seeing the angel, were afraid. But when that indwelling sin has been wholly cast off, then indeed we shall be able to behold the glory of our Lord, which the reprobate will by no means be able to bear on that day; indeed, they will call on the mountains themselves to hide them from the sight of that Lamb. For if the mere shadow of that glory of Christ which shone out in the angel was so great a terror to these men, how great will be the horrors when the reprobate see not only one glorious angel but thousands of angels, and even more glorious than that angel was then? And they will behold not only glorious angels, but the Lord himself as Judge, with all his Majesty?

units.la: ARGVMENTVM.
units.tr: ARGUMENT.

units.la: Postremis duobus Euangelij Iohannis capitibus, narratur quo pacto Christus post resurrectionem suam ex mortuis se virum discipulis suis ostenderit.
units.tr: In the last two chapters of John's Gospel it is related how Christ, after his resurrection from the dead, showed himself to his disciples.

units.la: CAP. XX.
units.tr: CHAPTER 20.

units.la: 1 PRimo vero die hebdomadis, Maria Magdalene venit mane, quum adhuc tenebrae essent, ad monumentum, videtq; lapidem sublatum a monumento.
