units.tr: 1 Now on the first day of the week Mary Magdalene came early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and saw the stone taken away from the tomb.

units.la: 2 Currit ergo & venit ad Simonem Petrum, & ad alterum illum discipulum quem amabat Iesus, & dicit eis, Sustulerunt Dominum è monumento, & nescimus ubi posuerunt eum.
units.tr: 2 So she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and said to them, "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid him."

units.la: Resurrectio Christi sine teste fuit: Narratur autem ab Euangelistis, quomodo quæ sine teste fuit, testata tamen euaserit ac innotuerit. Innotuit autem in hunc modum: Primùm mulieres quæ sepultura intererant, & reuersæ sunt domum ad id vt venerent ac pararent aromata, quibus vngerent corpus Domini iam sepultum: Mulieres, inquam, illæ postquam iam transisset sabbathum, emerunt ac paraverunt aromata, vt venientes vngerent eum. Venerunt itaque primo diluculo consilio & animo vngendi Domini. Hæc prima occasio, cur innotuerit & in lucem venerit resurrectio illa Christi, quæ fuerat sine teste. Altera autem occasio est in Angelo illo qui descendit de cœlo, idque animo testandi de Christi resurrectione. Atque hæ fuerunt occasiones, & quasi præparationes ad futuram testificationem & manifestationem resurrectionis Domini: Nam mulieribus de improuiso incidentibus in Angelum, Angelus primùm testatus est iis de Christi resurrectione. Hanc testificationem ipse Christus cum mulieribus appareret, deinde confirmauit. Mulieres deinde testatæ sunt de resurrectione Christi Apostolis. Hanc testificationem mulierum ipse Christus apparuit discipulis suis, deinde confirmauit: Hinc fama resurrectionis Christi diuulgata est. De occasionibus iam ante audiuimus, nunc ipsam testificationem & manifestationem resurrectionis Domini agredimur. Quo autem facilius intelligantur quæ dicenda sunt, notandum duas fuisse quasi classes mulierum, quæ alio atque alio tempore egressæ sunt ad sepulchrum Domini, vna citius, altera tardius. In prima classe nominantur duæ speciales Maria Magdalene & Maria Iacobi mater, non exclusis interim aliis, sed hæ nominatæ sunt, quia fortasse maximè celebres fuerunt inter Apostolos. Marcus tres nominat, Mariam Magdalenam, Mariam Iacobi matrem, Salomen, non exclusis aliis, sed quod fortasse hæ primæ nominis fuerunt inter Apostolos: Lucas nullam expresse nominat: sed in genere vocat mulieres, quæ eum sequutæ sunt è Galilæa. Quibus cap. 24. 1. addit nonnullas alias; Iohannes vnicam tantum ex hoc cœtu nominat, nempe Mariam Magdalenam, non exclusis interim aliis, sed fortasse quod hæc omnibus aliis celebrior fuerit. De profectione huius primi ordinis mulierum diximus supra: de tempore quo egressæ sunt ex urbe sepulchrum versus etiam diximus. Cum egrederentur ex urbe simul descendit Angelus e cælo cum terræmotu magno, quo hauddubie perterritæ sunt mulieres: attamen impellente eas Dei spiritu progressæ sunt: inter progrediendum autem cœperunt inter se disputare de devoluendo lapide illo magno qui aduolutus fuit ostio sepulchri: Nunc serius de eo lapide cogitantes, qui non iam prius iis venit in mentem, tanto enim in egressu suo ferebantur studio, atque adeo properabant. Videas enim præ ferio quodam alicuius rei studio festinantes, non cogitare eos statim de impedimentis, quorum, progressi iam paululum, recordantur non sine magna molestia: ut melius fuerit de his primo quoque tempore cogitare. Neque tamen oportet nimium sapere in opere Domini aggrediendo, sed multa impedimenta, quæ habituruum est opus Domini, ipsi Domino committenda. Verum ad mulieres redibo. Progressæ sepulchro appropinquabant. Appropinquantes vident lapidem devolutum. Hic Maria Magdalene temere coniectans sublatum esse e sepulchro corpus Domini, statim ac festinanter regressa est ad rei tantam indignitatem communicandam cum Petro & Iohanne. Hanc historiam Mariæ solus Iohannes pertexuit cap. 20. Quamobrem de ea ex Iohanne dicendum erit nonnihil. Apud Iohannem primum habemus de aduentu Mariæ. Venit mane, inquit: venit quidem vna cum aliis mulieribus, quæ fuerunt in primo illo mulierum ordine, de quo dictum est: de tempore quo cum aliis semel est egressa vidimus quoque. Hoc nunc tantum addimus ad ea quæ de his mulieribus (sic quidem à Deo honoratis præ viris & Apo-
units.tr: The resurrection of Christ was without a witness at first, yet the Evangelists tell how it, though without a witness, nevertheless came to be attested and made known. It was made known in this way. First, the women who had been present at the burial went home and came back so that they might come and prepare spices with which to anoint the body of the Lord already buried. Those women, I say, after the Sabbath had passed, bought and prepared spices, so that they might come and anoint him. So they came very early in the morning, with the purpose and intention of anointing the Lord. This was the first occasion for that resurrection of Christ, which had been without a witness, to become known and come into the light. The second occasion was the angel who came down from heaven, with the purpose of bearing witness to Christ's resurrection. These were the occasions, and, as it were, the preparations for the future testimony and manifestation of the Lord's resurrection. For when the women unexpectedly met the angel, the angel first bore witness to them about Christ's resurrection. Christ himself then confirmed this testimony when he appeared to the women. Afterwards the women bore witness to the Apostles about Christ's resurrection. Christ himself then appeared to his disciples and confirmed this testimony of the women. Hence the report of Christ's resurrection was spread abroad. We have already heard about the occasions; now we come to the testimony and manifestation of the Lord's resurrection itself. So that what must be said may be more easily understood, it should be noted that there were, as it were, two groups of women who set out for the Lord's tomb at different times, one earlier and the other later. In the first group two are named in particular, Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James, without excluding others; but these are named because perhaps they were the most famous among the Apostles. Mark names three: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome, without excluding others, but perhaps because these were the first in renown among the Apostles. Luke names none expressly, but speaks in general of the women who had followed him from Galilee. To these, in chapter 24, verse 1, he adds some others. John names only one from this company, namely Mary Magdalene, without excluding others, but perhaps because she was more celebrated than all the rest. We have spoken above about the departure of this first order of women, and we have also spoken about the time at which they went out from the city towards the sepulchre. As they were leaving the city, an angel came down from heaven together with a great earthquake, by which the women were no doubt terrified; yet, impelled by the Spirit of God, they went on. But as they went, they began to discuss among themselves how the great stone that had been rolled against the door of the sepulchre could be rolled away. They thought about that stone only belatedly, for it had not come into their minds before; so carried away were they by zeal in their going out, and indeed they hurried. For you may see that people hastening in the heat of some eagerness do not at once think of the obstacles, which, once they have gone on a little, they recall not without great distress; so it would have been better to think of these things at the very first. Yet one must not be too wise in undertaking the work of the Lord, but should commit the many obstacles that the work of the Lord will meet to the Lord himself. But I shall return to the women. Having gone forth, they drew near the sepulchre. Drawing near, they see the stone rolled away. Here Mary Magdalene, rashly supposing that the body of the Lord had been taken out of the sepulchre, at once hurried back to share so great an outrage with Peter and John. Only John has related this story of Mary, in chapter 20; therefore something must be said about her from John. In John we first have the arrival of Mary. "She came early in the morning," he says. She came, indeed, together with the other women who were in that first order of women of which we have spoken; we have also seen the time at which she once went out with the others. We add only this to what has been said about these women (so honoured by God above men and the Apostles themselves, that they became the first witnesses of the Lord's resurrection after the angel): that they were authentic witnesses, beyond all exception, and this alone is enough, that the Lord wished them to bear witness of his resurrection immediately after the angels, so that there is no need to seek further for the reasons for this pre-eminence. Now let us proceed to other matters.

units.la: Quid in illarum accessu ad sepulchrum acciderit. & Apostolis ipsis, vt nimirum primæ post Angelum testes euaserint resurrectionis Domini) eas fuisse authenticas testes & omni exceptione maiores, vel hoc vno nomine, quod voluerat Dominus eas testari proximè post angelos de resurrectione sua, vt nō sit opus de causis prærogatiuæ huius iam amplius quærere. Nunc pergamus ad alia. Postquam venit ad sepulchrum vna cum aliis, vidit lapidem deuolutum, hoc est quod ipsam cum aliis paulo ante anxiam & solicitam habuit. Quod si, cũ Magdalene & aliarum mulierum institutū hoc vngendi corpus Domini tertio post sepulturam die parū laudabile fuit: tamen Dominus impedimentum illud remoueratquod ipsis negotium facessebat: quanto magis, qui bonum opus aliquod & cum verbo Dei consentiens instituunt, huiusmodi Dei prudentiam in remouendis impedimentis sunt experturi: vt videas non oportere nimis super in Dei opere aggrediendo, sed vbi semel constituit illud ex Dei voluntate fieri, ipsum primo quoque tempore aggrediendum, & cætera Deo, qui facile potest omnia impedimenta remouere, committenda est. Sic enim honoratur Deus, & ei datur gloria illa debita, cum sub spe contra spem credimus eum abiturum. At, inquies, etsi deuolutum lapidem inuenerit Magdalene, tamen non inuenit corpus Domini quod quærebat vngendū & aromatibus condiendum. At inquam, si non Dominum inter mortuos inuenit, quod longe melius fuit, eum inuenit tamen inter vivos: nunquam enim futurum est, vt pij qui Dominum quærunt, omnibus plane modis frustrētur: quod si quod quærunt non inueniant, occurrit iis sæpe quod superat expectationem. Nunc de præpropero Magdalene reditu videndum. Zelo quidem, fateor, & studio Domini abrepta fuit, sed peccauit tamen: oportuit enim cum aliis paulisper subsistere, & videre quonam pacto res sese haberet, sepulchrum ingredi cum aliis, vbi veritatem rei ex angelo liceret discere. Sed videas etiam optimos alioqui & Domini studiosissimos, sic nonnunquam præcipitari, nō quidem quod vllum fit in zelo Dei vitium, sed peccatū ascribendum est cæcitati & ignorantiæ. Nam zelum nostrum oportet cognitionis luce quasi face quadā præeūte
units.tr: What happened at their approach to the sepulchre. After she came to the sepulchre with the others, she saw the stone rolled away; this is what had a little before troubled and disquieted her along with the others. But if the plan of Magdalene and the other women to anoint the body of the Lord on the third day after the burial was scarcely commendable, yet the Lord removed the obstacle that caused them trouble. How much more, then, will those who undertake some good work in agreement with the Word of God experience this prudence of God in removing obstacles! So you may see that one must not be too anxious in undertaking the work of God; but once it has been determined that it is to be done according to the will of God, it must be undertaken at the very first opportunity, and the rest committed to God, who can easily remove all obstacles. For in this way God is honoured and given the glory due to him, when we believe, in hope against hope, that he will go on. But you will say: though Magdalene found the stone rolled away, yet she did not find the body of the Lord that she was seeking to anoint and embalm with spices. I answer: if she did not find him among the dead, which was far better, yet she found him among the living; for it will never happen that the godly, who seek the Lord, are altogether disappointed in every way; and if they do not find what they seek, something often meets them that exceeds their expectation. Now let us consider Magdalene's hasty return. Carried away by zeal and eagerness for the Lord, I confess, she nevertheless erred; for she ought to have stayed a little with the others and seen how matters stood, and entered the sepulchre with them, where she might have learned the truth of the matter from the angel. But you may see that even those otherwise excellent and most zealous for the Lord are sometimes thus rushed headlong; not that there is any fault in the zeal of God, but the error must be ascribed to blindness and ignorance. For our zeal ought to go before, as it were with a torch, by the light of knowledge

units.la: dirigi. Quamobrem quoties ex zelo faciendum est aliquid, subsistamus paulisper dum penitus rem habeamus exploratam. Cum de re iam constitit præeunte iam cognitionis luce, zelus deinde sequatur cognitionis illam lucem. Sed video plures esse qui in eo peccant, quòd zelum Dei non habeant omnino, quàm quòd cognitionis luce destituantur. Atque ego præstantius esse duco ignaros ex zelo ferri & abrupi ad aliquid faciendum, vt ipsis videtur, ad Dei gloriam, quàm omni etiã luce cognitionis collustratos, nihil tamen ex zelo Dei facere. Postquam conuenit Petrum & Iohannem, triste satis nuntium proponit: Sustulerunt, inquit, Dominum. Querela est de sublato è monumento Domini corpore, à quo ne ipsi quidem morte separati se passa est: quia nimirum in morte Christus efficax fuit & & sui participationem. Quantò magis in gloria iam debet esse in nobis efficax? Sed expendenda verba: Non quidem tum mentita est Magdalene: nam sermo oris simul & mentis cogitatio inter se consentiebant. Peccauit tamen ex ignorantia, quia veritatè alioqui discere ac cognoscere potuit. Ignorantia, magnum quidem malum est, & ex peccato in peccatum præcipitat etiam bonos & pios nonnunquam. Peccauit ex ignorantia Magdalene in facto, peccauit etiam in verbo. Sed Deus peccata suorum, dilectione illa sua in ChristoIesu, operit: Id enim quod dicitur 1.Pet.4.8. Dilectio operit multitudinem peccatorum. De Dei in Christo dilectione illa longè verissimum est. Præterea ex his ipsis Magdalenæ tenebris ipse lucem eduxit: Nam hoc ipso nuntio excitati sunt Petrus & Iohannes, vt exirent ad Christi sepulchrum & veritatem de Christi resurrectione penitus discerent. Verùm non propterea faciendum est malum vt bonum eueniat. Non est hic præterenndũ, quantum difficultate perueniat Maria Magdalene ad cognitionem gloriosæ illius resurrectionis Christi. Anxia ad sepulchrum profecta est: Re non cognita anxia reuersa est domum à sepulchro, & apud Petrum & Iohannem de ea re questa est graviter. Non est tam leue ac facile peruenire ad Christi cognitionem, & ad inspectionem gloriæ ipsius: quin oporteat ad eam videndam præparari nos multis doloribus, curis, laboribus, quæ omnia absorbentur momento ab illa ipsa gloria, vbi semel datum fuerit præsentem eam intueri.
units.tr: and be directed by it. Therefore, whenever something must be done from zeal, let us pause a little until we have the matter thoroughly examined. When the matter has been established, with the light of knowledge going before, let zeal then follow that light of knowledge. But I see that there are more who sin in this, that they have no zeal for God at all, than that they lack the light of knowledge. And I consider it better to be carried by zeal, though ignorant, and rushed into doing something which seems to them to be for the glory of God, than to be enlightened with all the light of knowledge and yet do nothing from zeal for God. After she met Peter and John, she gave a sad enough report: "They have taken away," she said, "the Lord." It is a complaint about the body of the Lord taken from the sepulchre, from which not even death itself had separated her; for surely in death Christ was effective, and [in the communion of himself]. How much more ought he to be effective in us now in glory? But the words must be weighed. Magdalene did not then speak falsely, for the utterance of her mouth and the thought of her mind agreed with each other. Yet she erred through ignorance, because she could otherwise have learned and known the truth. Ignorance is indeed a great evil, and it sometimes casts even good and godly people from one sin into another. Magdalene erred through ignorance in the deed; she erred also in the word. But God covers the sins of his own by that love of his in Christ Jesus; for what is said in 1 Peter 4:8 is true: love covers a multitude of sins. Concerning this love of God in Christ it is most truly the case. Moreover, out of this very darkness of Magdalene, he himself brought forth light; for by this very message Peter and John were roused to go out to the sepulchre of Christ and to learn fully the truth about Christ's resurrection. Yet evil must not be done so that good may come of it. Here it must not be passed over how great a difficulty Mary Magdalene had in coming to the knowledge of that glorious resurrection of Christ. She set out to the sepulchre anxious; not having learned the matter, she returned home from the sepulchre anxious, and complained bitterly of it to Peter and John. It is not so light and easy to come to the knowledge of Christ and to the sight of his glory; rather, we must be prepared for it by many sorrows, cares and labours, all of which are swallowed up in a moment by that very glory, once it has been granted to behold it in its presence.

units.la: Matthæi 28.
units.tr: Matthew 28.

units.la: 5 Respondens autem Angelus dixit mulieribus, Vos vero ne timete, scio enim vos Iesum crucifixum quaerere.
units.tr: 5 And the angel answered and said to the women, Do not you be afraid; for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified.

units.la: 6 Non est hic: resurrexit enim prout dixit, Adeste, videte locum vbi iacebat Dominus.
units.tr: 6 He is not here, for he is risen, as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.

units.la: 7 Et cito profecta dicite discipulis eius eum resurrexisse a mortuis, & ecce praecedit vobis in Galilaeam: illic eum videbitis, ecce dixi vobis.
units.tr: 7 And go quickly and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead; and behold, he goes before you into Galilee: there you shall see him. Behold, I have told you.

units.la: 8 Tunc egressi cito a monumento cum timore & gaudio magno, currebat vt renunciarent discipulis eius.
units.tr: 8 Then they went out quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, and ran to bring word to his disciples.

units.la: Marci 16.
units.tr: Mark 16.

units.la: 2 Et valde mane primo die hebdomadis, veniunt ad monumentum exorto sole.
units.tr: 2 And very early on the first day of the week they come to the tomb when the sun had risen.

units.la: 3 Dicebant que inter se, Quis auoluet nobis saxum ab ostio monumenti?
units.tr: 3 And they said to one another, Who will roll away the stone for us from the door of the tomb?

units.la: 4 Inuneta vero conspiciunt saxum esse auolutum: nam erat magnum valde.
units.tr: 4 But looking up, they see that the stone has been rolled away, for it was very large.

units.la: 5 Ingressi igitur in monumentum, viderunt iuuenem sedentem ad dexteram, amictum stola candida, & expauerunt.
units.tr: 5 So entering the tomb, they saw a young man sitting on the right, clothed in a white robe, and they were amazed.

units.la: 6 Ipse vero dixit eis, Ne expauescite: Iesum quaeritis Nazarenum illum, qui fuit crucifixus: suscitatus est, non est hic: ecce locus vbi posuerant eum.
units.tr: 6 But he said to them, Do not be amazed. You seek Jesus the Nazarene, who was crucified: he is risen, he is not here. Behold the place where they laid him.

units.la: 7 Sed abite, dicite discipulis eius & Petro, ipsum praecedet vobis in Galilaeam: illic eum videbitis, sicut dixit vobis.
units.tr: 7 But go, tell his disciples and Peter that he goes before you into Galilee; there you will see him, as he told you.

units.la: 8 Tum digressae cito fugerunt a monumento: tenebat enim eas tremor & stupor,neque cuiquam quicquam dicebant,timebant enim.
units.tr: 8 Then the women went out quickly and fled from the tomb, for trembling and astonishment seized them, and they said nothing to anyone, for they were afraid.

units.la: HAðtenus de Magdalene ex historia & Euangelio Iohannis. Nunc sequuntur partes cæterarum, quæ vnà cum Magdalene ad sepulchrũ venerunt. Non sunt eæ quidè cum Magdalene statim regressæ,sed restitæ ingressæ sunt sepulchrum. Atq; hac quidem re Magdalene fuerūt superiores. Etsi alioqui quod ad zelum Domini Magdalene inferiores videantur fuisse: Id enim euenire solet nonnunquà vt inferiores gratia & donis certis aliquibus,euadat tamen superiores aliqua in re alia,etiā iis ipsis quibus alioqui inferiores sunt: Deonimirū deserēte nonnunquā superiores,assistente autē inferioribus præsentia & gratia sua in eum nempe finem, vt cognoscant omnes omnem gratia à Deo esse. Et qui gloriatur,siue maiora habeat dona,siue minora,in Domino gloriētur. Quis te disternit? Quid habes quod non acceperis? si acceperis, quid gloriaris, vt qui non acceperis? Ingressæ vident quasi inuenē longa albaque stola indutum. Hic mihi videtur, idem ille Angelus, qui iam prius reuoluto lapide ipsi insidebat: Insidebat lapidi primùm,vt absterreret custodes,ne ij molestiæ essent mulieribus venturis ad sepulchrum Domini. Absterritis iam ac fugatis iis, recepit se deinde in sepulchrum:primùm ne si foris sedens, venientes mulieres absterreret ac in fugam verteret,priusquam copia daretur inuisendi sepulchrum: deinde vt cõmodum locum haberet in quo doceret mulieres resurrectionem Christi. In sepulchro enim vnà cum mulieribus confidens, digito quasi demonstrauit resurrectionem Domini,vt postea videbimus. Ecce,inquit, non est hic. Idem Angelus qui minister est iudicii & terroris impiis, idem minister est misericordiæ & consolationis iis: & terret impios, ne impij sint terrori bonis. Iudicia enim in improbos non tantum inseruiunt gloriæ Dei,sed etiā saluti piorum & Ecclesiæ Dei. Sed non est silentio prætereundum,quam particularem rationem habeat omnium circunstantiarum Deus,in promulgando Euangelio resurrectionis Christi. Ratione habuit personæ quæ effet ea promulgatura, ad eámq; re non homine aliquo, sed Angelo gloriosum adhibuit. At noluit ea ab Angelo promulgari custodibus & prophanis illis militibus, qui sepulchrum Domini muniebat; sed mulieribus illis sanctis & Domini studiosis. Deniq; ratione habuit loci, in quo Angelus mulieres docturus esset, elegitq; sepulchrū ipsum Domini, tanquā commodissimum ad eam rem demonstrandā locū. Hodierno etiam die habet rationem Dominus omniū circumstantiarū in promulgando Euangelio sui, personarū, locorum, temporum, &c. vt scia-mas quidam quam fit Domino & gloria Filij sui, salúsq; no stra. Sequitur effectū inspecti in sepulchro Angeli. Mulieres aspectum ipsius expauerunt: Non quidē facte sunt vt mortuę, vt de custodibus audiuimus, tamen expauerunt. Nam ne pij quidem possunt ferre aspectū illius maiestatis in hac vita dū sunt. Et quod mirum videtur, illi qui cum mulieribus istis Christum quærunt, tamen non possunt ferre gloriosum illius maiestatis effectum, si sese videndum oculis istis corporeis aliquo modo offerret: vt tum se videndum in imagine Maiestatis aliqua obtulit hisce mulieribus. Nā gloria illa Angelii imago quædam fuit & vmbra gloriæ Christi, in gloria sua resurrectione. In causa huius rei nō tantū est maiestas illa Dei, ad cuius quidem aspectū æquū est vt omnis caro obstupeat: sed etiā reliquę istę peccati quę etiam optimis quibusq; remanēt, quas comitatur necessario aliquo certe modo mala cōscientia. At cum impij nihil in se habeat quod ipsos erigat, cum deiiciuntur sensu peccati sui: Pij vt deiiciuntur ex sensu peccati, & mala aliqua conscientia: ita eriguntur sensu remissionis peccati & bonæ conscientiæ per Christum Iesum. Atq; inde est quod mulieres istę, etsi ob sensū peccati expauerint, tamen cū custodibus nō sunt factę velut mortuę.
units.tr: Thus far concerning Mary Magdalene, from the history and the Gospel of John. Now follow the parts of the other women who came to the sepulchre with Mary Magdalene. Indeed they did not return at once with Mary Magdalene, but remained and entered the sepulchre. In this respect, then, they were superior to Mary Magdalene. Yet in other respects they seem to have been inferior to Mary Magdalene in zeal for the Lord. For it often happens that those who are inferior in certain gifts and graces excel in some other matter, even in those things in which they are otherwise inferior to others; for God sometimes leaves the superior, and his presence and grace attend the inferior, namely to this end, that all may know that all grace is from God. "And let him who glories, whether he has greater or lesser gifts, glory in the Lord. Who makes you to differ? What do you have that you did not receive? If you received it, why do you glory, as if you had not received it?" [1 Cor. 4:7]. The women, having entered, see a young man clothed in a long white robe. It seems to me that this is the same angel who before had sat upon the stone after it was rolled away. He sat first upon the stone so as to frighten away the guards, lest they be a hindrance to the women coming to the sepulchre of the Lord. Having now frightened and driven them off, he then withdrew into the sepulchre: first, lest, if he sat outside and frightened the women coming and turned them to flight before they had the opportunity of viewing the sepulchre; and then, that he might have a convenient place in which to teach the women about the resurrection of Christ. For sitting inside the sepulchre with the women, he pointed out with his finger, as it were, the resurrection of the Lord, as we shall see afterwards. "Behold," he says, "he is not here." The same angel who is a minister of judgment and terror to the wicked is also a minister of mercy and comfort to the good; he terrifies the wicked, so that the wicked may not be a terror to the good. For judgments upon the wicked serve not only the glory of God but also the salvation of the pious and of the Church of God. But it must not be passed over in silence what particular account God takes of all the circumstances in publishing the Gospel of Christ's resurrection. He took account of the person who was to publish it, and for this purpose he employed not a man but a glorious angel. Yet he did not will that it be published by the angel to the guards and those profane soldiers who were keeping watch over the Lord's sepulchre, but to those holy women who were devoted to the Lord. Finally, he took account of the place in which the angel was to teach the women, and chose the Lord's own sepulchre, as the most fitting place for demonstrating that matter. Even today the Lord takes account of all the circumstances in publishing his Gospel: of persons, places, times, and so on, so that some may learn how much it matters to the Lord and to the glory of his Son, and to our salvation. There follows the effect of the sight of the angel in the sepulchre. The women were terrified at his appearance; not indeed were they made as dead, as we heard of the guards, yet they were terrified. For not even the pious can bear the sight of that majesty while they are in this life. And what seems strange: those who seek Christ along with these women cannot bear the glorious effect of his majesty, if it presented itself to their bodily eyes in any way; just as it then presented itself to these women in some image of majesty. For that glory of the angel was a certain image and shadow of the glory of Christ, in his glorious resurrection. The cause of this is not only that majesty of God, before whose sight it is right that all flesh should be astonished, but also those remnants of sin which remain even in the best of men, which are necessarily accompanied by some evil conscience. But since the wicked have nothing in themselves that lifts them up, when they are cast down by the sense of their sin, the pious, when cast down by the sense of sin and some evil conscience, are thus lifted up by the sense of the forgiveness of sins and a good conscience through Jesus Christ. And hence it is that these women, although they were terrified on account of the sense of sin, nevertheless were not made as dead, as the guards were.

units.la: Sequitur nūc oratio Angeli ad mulieres, in qua primū erigit deiectas. 2. restatur de resurrectione Domini. 3. præcipit vt ipse vicissim restetur Apostolis de eadē illa resurrectione. Ne timete. His verbis Angelus deiectas erigit. Non quidem audiuimus sic loquutū Angelum militibus. Vnde aliud discrimen cernimus inter pios & impios pariter deiectos: vt enim impij nihil intra se habeat,
units.tr: There now follows the angel's speech to the women, in which first he raises up the dejected; second, he bears witness concerning the resurrection of the Lord; third, he orders that they in turn bear witness to the Apostles about that same resurrection. "Do not be afraid." By these words the angel raises up the dejected. Indeed we have not heard that the angel spoke thus to the soldiers. Hence we see another difference between the pious and the impious, who are equally cast down: for just as the wicked have nothing within themselves,

units.la: Sapientia Dei in Euangelica doctrina dispensatione.
units.tr: The wisdom of God in the dispensing of the evangelical doctrine.

units.la: Pauor mulierum ad aspectum Angeli.
units.tr: The women's fear at the sight of the angel.

units.la: Vnde pauor iste.
units.tr: Whence this fear.

units.la: Remedium.
units.tr: The remedy.

units.la: 6. Angeli sancti pastes.
units.tr: 6. The holy angel's words.

units.la: 1. Mulieres deiectas erigitur. quo erigantur, nullum sensum remissionis peccatorum nullam bonam conscientiam: ita quoque extra se nihil habent, Dominus non dignatur deiectos eos vel vna vocula: at vero pij, vt habent intus, quo erigantur iam deiecti, ita foris habent verbum Dei, & alias rationes ac adiumenta quibus subleuentur. Eriguntur ab iis etiam a quibus sunt deiecti: deiectæ sunt mulieres istæ ab angelo, ab eodem angelo sunt erectæ: neque tantum deiectæ eriguntur, sed etiam loco timoris ac doloris quo sunt quasi vulneratæ, infunditur cordibus eorum quasi oleū quoddam lætitiæ. Angelus enim non tantum remouet tristitiā, sed etiam loco tristitiæ materiā lætitiæ offert in prædicatione gloriosæ resurrectionis Domini nostri. Ex mulierū deiectione ex aspectu illo Angeli, & erectione per vocē Angeli, discimus quomodo oporteat præparari nos ad audiendū Euangelium Christi: opus est primū vt deiiciamur sensu peccati & miseriæ nostræ, etiā concutiamur horroribus certo modo inferorū: deinde ante auditū Euangelium opus est vt erigamur audita hac vel huiusmodi aliqua voce. Ne expauescite. Sic enim præparamur ad nuntium illud gaudii, quod Euangelium vocamus, recipiendum. Scio vos Iesum. Sic præparatis iam illis accedit ad secundam partem orationis suæ, ad testificandum nimirum de resurrectione Domini. Primum autē conciliare videtur personæ suæ authoritatem apud mulieres, dum non ignarum se mentis ac propositi ipsarum, idque ex revelatione quadam Dei facta significat, ac proinde a Deo missum, diuino quodā testimonio ornatum se venire, ad testificandū de resurrectione Christi. Conciliat autem authoritatem personæ, quo mulieres testimonio ipsius maiorem haberent fidem. Obseruandū igitur Deum, perinde atque tum hunc Angelū misit, sic instructum notitia propositi illius mulierū iSTarum: ita perpetuo eos quos mittit ad testificandū de se, solere nō inanes gratiæ mittere: verum instructos luce revelationis & cognitionis aliqua, & potentia qua penitus in hominum corda & secretas cogitationes penetrent, vt sciat homines a Deo missos esse eos, & testimonio ipsorū habeant fidem. Paulus dum commendat prophetiæ donū, dicit, Quod si Prophēta aliquis prophetet, atque tum idiota {ι}diota quis ingrediatur audiatque prophetantem cum efficacia & authoritate, idiotam sic statim commotum iri retectis secretis cordis ipsius, & in lucem productis, vt procidens in faciem adoraturus sit Deum, & de Propheta ipso sic renunciaturus, quod Deus sit in ipso. Quibus verbis significat, prophetam cum qui a Deo mittitur cum gratia & potentia mitti. Sed notandi sunt hoc loco hi tituli, quos tribuit Iesu: Non filium Dei, non Dominum gloriae nominat, sed Nazarenum ex vrbe Nazareth vili & abiecta, ac crucifixum ex mortis illo genere execrabili & ignominioso designat: quia, vt videtur, ex his omnibus, mulieribus potius fuit cognitus, quam ex illis. Significat etiam Angelus non pudere se infirmitatis & crucis Christi: re vera autem, teste Petro, desiderant Angeli introspicere in haec ipsa quibus lu-daei offendebantur. Vident enim in Christi infirmitate, infinitam illam Dei potentiam, vident in stulta cruce, Dei multiplicem illam sapientiam; vident in morte filii infinitam illam Patris iustitiam, simulque misericordiam erga humanum genus ineffabilem. Vsurpata sunt etiam haec Christi epitheta ab Angelo, ad amplificandam resurrectionis gloriam, qua verbis sequentibus annuntiaturus erat. Nam quo abiectior Christus ante resurrectionem fuit, eo in resurrectione gloriosior euadit. Et Angeli quidem ipsi mirati sunt hominem paulo ante ad inferos usque detrusum tam cito euectum in summa illam sublimitatem. Non est hic. Hactenus conciliauit authoritatem personae, sequitur testimonium & annuntiatio resurrectionis Christi. Prima illa verba paulo mulieribus tristiora fuisse videntur. Suspicatae enim sunt fortasse cum Maria Magdalene sublatum Dominum e sepulchro fuisse; verba autem quae sequuntur tristes consolantur, dum Angelus statim ideo non esse eum in sepulchro dicit, quia surrexit: no quidem sublatus est furtim, sed ipse sua vi resurrexit. In hac formula annunciationis resurrectionis Christi, tanquam in imagine aliqua discere licet formam ordinemque proponendi illius nuntij, quod in Euangelio haberur. Primum in Euangelio annunciantur tristiora, deinde laetiora. Primum annuntiatur Christum passum, crucifixum, mortuum, sepultum. Hęc omnia tristiora. Tum annuntiatur Christum resurrexisse ex mortuis, ascendisse ad cælos, sedere ad dextram Patris, &c. hæc latiora. Sed quæ nos propius attingunt, sequuntur, cum annuntiantur illa beneficia remissionis peccatorum, resurrectionis carnis, vitæ denique æternæ, quæ ad nos ex Christi illa passione & resurrectione promanant. Deinde quæ de fidelibus & Christi Ecclesia annuntiantur, prima facie sunt tristia: ut est illud, oportere omnes qui pie volunt viuere in Christo Iesu, afflictione pati: sed lætiora sunt quæ sequuntur, Quod qui cum Christo patiuntur, cū Christo glorificabuntur. Verum formula ista & docendi ordo conspici potest in ipsis Euangelij verbis. Dicitur & annuntiatur à Domino, quod oporteat filium hominis ascendere Hierosolyma, ibique multa pati à senioribus & principibus Sacerdotum, & Scribis, & occidi: hæc tristia sunt: quod autem sequitur lætum est: Oportet, inquit, tertio die eum suscitari. Alibi Euangelium annuntiat primum in hæc verba, Ecce veniet tempus, & iam venit, cum dispergemini unusquisque ad suos, meque solum relinquetis. Hoc triste est nuncium: at quod sequitur lætum est: Sed non sum solus, Pater enim meum est. Item, sic alloquitur primum discipulos suos: Eritis exosi omnibus propter nomen meum: hoc triste nuncium: sed quid sequitur? Qui fuerit ad finem usque, is seruabitur. Lætum est hoc nuncium. Et alibi, In mundo, ait discipulis, oppressionem habebitis: hoc triste: Sed confidite, ego vici mundum: hoc lætū est. Prout est verbum Euangelij, quod annuntiatur, sic se habet vere Christianus quisque, qui verbum illud audit: primum tristis est, deinde lætus: primum deiicitur, deinde erigitur. Et quantisper audit verbum Euangelij in hac vita, necesse est eum sic affici, cū vero audito mutata erit in aspectum, tum quidem nihil sentiet nisi purum, impermixtumque gaudium. Prout dixit.
units.tr: 1. The women are raised up after being cast down. Whatever raises them up is not a sense of the forgiveness of sins or a good conscience; they have nothing of that kind outside themselves, and the Lord does not deign to speak even one little word to those who are cast down. But the godly, as they have within them what raises them up when they have been cast down, so outside they have the word of God and other reasons and helps by which they are sustained. They are raised up also by those who cast them down: these women were cast down by the angel, and by the same angel they are raised up. And not only are the cast-down raised up, but in place of the fear and grief by which they were, as it were, wounded, a certain oil of joy is poured into their hearts. For the angel not only removes sadness but, in place of sadness, offers the matter of joy in the proclamation of the glorious resurrection of our Lord. From the women's dejection, from that sight of the angel, and from their being raised up by the angel's voice, we learn how we ought to be prepared to hear the Gospel of Christ. First, we must be cast down by a sense of sin and of our misery, and also be shaken by the horrors of, as it were, a certain hell; then, before the Gospel is heard, we must be raised up by hearing this or some such voice: Do not be afraid. For thus we are prepared to receive that message of joy which we call the Gospel. I know that you seek Jesus. Now that they are so prepared, he comes to the second part of his speech, namely, to bear witness to the resurrection of the Lord. He first seems to win the authority of his person with the women, when he indicates that he is not unaware of their mind and purpose, and that this is through some revelation made by God; and so he comes as one sent by God, adorned with a divine testimony, to bear witness to the resurrection of Christ. He wins authority for his person so that the women may have greater faith in his testimony. We should observe, therefore, that God, just as he sent this angel instructed with knowledge of the purpose of these women, so he is accustomed always to send those whom he sends to bear witness concerning him not empty of grace, but furnished with the light of some revelation and knowledge, and with a power by which they penetrate into the hearts of men and their secret thoughts, so that people may know that they have been sent by God and may have faith in their testimony. Paul, when he commends the gift of prophecy, says: "If any prophet prophesies, and then an idiot [ἰδιώτης] comes in and hears the prophet speaking with efficacy and authority, the idiot will at once be so moved, his secrets of heart being laid bare and brought into the light, that falling on his face he will worship God, and will report of the prophet himself that God is in him." By these words he signifies that a prophet who is sent by God is sent with grace and power. But at this point we should note the titles which he gives to Jesus: he does not name him the Son of God or the Lord of glory, but he designates him as the Nazarene from the lowly and despised city of Nazareth, and as crucified, by that detestable and ignominious kind of death; because, as it seems, he was known to the women rather from these things than from the others. The angel also signifies that he is not ashamed of the weakness and the cross of Christ; indeed, as Peter bears witness, the angels desire to look into these very things by which the Jews were offended. For they see in the weakness of Christ that infinite power of God, they see in the foolish cross the manifold wisdom of God; they see in the death of the Son that infinite justice of the Father, and at the same time his mercy towards the human race, which is unspeakable. These titles of Christ were also used by the angel in order to magnify the glory of the resurrection, which he was about to announce in the words that follow. For the more lowly Christ was before the resurrection, the more glorious he becomes in the resurrection. And indeed the angels themselves marvelled that a man who a little before had been thrust down even to the depths of hell was so quickly carried up to such great height. He is not here. So far he has won the authority of the person; there follows the testimony and announcement of the resurrection of Christ. Those first words seem to have been somewhat sadder for the women. For they perhaps suspected, with Mary Magdalene, that the Lord had been taken from the tomb; but the words that follow comfort the sorrowful, since the angel at once says that he is not in the tomb because he has risen: he was not taken away secretly, but rose by his own power. In this formula of the announcement of Christ's resurrection, we may learn, as it were from a certain image, the form and order of setting forth that message which is contained in the Gospel. First, in the Gospel, sadder things are announced, and then happier things. First it is announced that Christ suffered, was crucified, died and was buried: all these are sadder things. Then it is announced that Christ rose from the dead, ascended into heaven, sits at the right hand of the Father, and so on: these are more cheerful things. But those things which touch us more closely follow, when those benefits are announced: the forgiveness of sins, the resurrection of the flesh, and finally eternal life, which flow to us from that passion and resurrection of Christ. Then the things that are announced concerning the faithful and the Church of Christ are at first sight sad, as is that saying: "all who wish to live godly in Christ Jesus must suffer affliction"; but what follows is happier: "that those who suffer with Christ will be glorified with Christ." Indeed this formula and order of teaching may be seen in the very words of the Gospel. It is said and announced by the Lord that the Son of man must go up to Jerusalem, and there suffer many things from the elders and the chief priests and the scribes, and be killed: these things are sad; but what follows is joyful: "It is necessary," he says, "that he be raised up on the third day." Elsewhere the Gospel announces first in these words: Behold, the time will come, and now has come, when you will be scattered each to his own, and you will leave me alone. This is a sad message; but what follows is joyful: But I am not alone, for the Father is with me. Likewise he first addresses his disciples thus: You will be hated by all men for my name's sake: this is a sad message; but what follows? He who endures to the end, he will be saved. This message is joyful. And elsewhere: In the world, he says to the disciples, you will have tribulation: this is sad; But be of good cheer, I have overcome the world: this is joyful. As the word of the Gospel that is proclaimed is, so truly is every Christian who hears that word: first he is sad, then he is glad; first he is cast down, then he is raised up. And as long as he hears the word of the Gospel in this life, he must be affected in this way; but when, after hearing, it is changed into sight, then indeed he will feel nothing but pure and unmixed joy. As he said.

units.la: Duobus deinde argumentis confirmat Angelus testificationem illam suam de Christi resurrectione. Primum est à Christi ipsius prædictione, Matthæi 16. & alibi. Nota omnium prædictionum & prophetiarum de Christo, hunc esse vsum, vt confirment nobis verbum Euangelij de Christi manifestatione in carne, passione & glorificatione. Etsi enim ista oculis nostris non vidimus, tamen hoc plurimù facit ad fidem Euangelij, dum audimus nihil nobis narrari factum esse in Euangelio, quod non idem sit prædictum iam olim & denunciatum futurum esse, & euenturu suo tempore. Mulieres istæ prædictionis huius iam oblitæ fuerant, cuius tamen vidimus meminerisse Principes Sacerdotum, cū petierunt custodiam à Pilato ad muniendū Christi sepulchrum. Nonnunquam ipsi pij sequius audiunt verbum Christi, quàm impij, qui tamen ipsum audiunt ad perniciem suam. Sed nota hoc in exemplo mulierum Deum consulere infirmitati suorum, neque pati vt verbum suum in ipsis perpetua oblivione seruetur. Vsus autem est tunc temporis opera Angeli ad hanc prædictionem mulieribus hisce in memoriam reuocandam. At nunc vtitur opera fidelium ministrorum, quorum officium est hoc inter alia testibus Apostolis, reducere in memoriam ea quæ iam prius sunt audita & percepta. Præcipuè id muneris ad Spiritum sanctum consolatorem pertinet, cuius est suggerere ea quæ iam sunt audita, & per infirmitatem obliuioni tradita. Matth. 14. 26 tam, inquit Christus, consolatorem qui suggeret vobis omnia quæ dixi vobis. Renocat autem Deus in memoriam nostram prædictionem, vel antequam sunt impleta, vel postquam impleta sunt, vt hoc loco per Angelum renocata est in memoriam mulieribus prædictio resurrectionis Christi, posteaquam iam impleta est. Tū autem iucunda est recordatio postquam prædictio est impleta. Atque in summa maxime illa rerum omnium iucundissima suauissimaque futura est recordatio omnium, quæ nunc quotidie audimus ex Euangelio isto Christi. Nūc quidem gloriatio est sub spe, tunc gloriatio erit sub aspectu: nunc quidem glorificatio Dei in veritate verbi sui ex parte est: at tunc glorificatio erit perfecta, postquam omnia quæ prædicta ac promissa sunt iam plane pleneque sunt impleta. Veni-te, videte. Alterum est argumentum confirmationis ab oculari quadam facti ipsius demonstratione. Eas propius ad se vocat Angelus, vt plane videant rem ita se habere. Dominus non contentus nudo verbo suo, offert etiā oculis videndum, quod in verbo iam auribus obtulit audiendum: vt in Sacramentis verbo annexis videre est. Præterea ipsum Dei verbum præterquam quod audibile sit, etiam
units.tr: Next the angel confirms his testimony concerning the resurrection of Christ by two arguments. The first is from Christ's own prediction, Matthew 16 and elsewhere. Note that the use of all the predictions and prophecies concerning Christ is this: that they confirm for us the word of the Gospel concerning the manifestation of Christ in the flesh, his passion and his glorification. For although we have not seen these things with our eyes, yet this greatly contributes to faith in the Gospel, when we hear that nothing has been related to us in the Gospel as having happened which was not foretold and announced long before as going to happen, and coming to pass in its time. These women had forgotten this prediction, though we see that the chief priests remembered it, when they asked Pilate for a guard to secure Christ's tomb. Sometimes the godly hear the word of Christ less well than the ungodly, who nevertheless hear it to their own destruction. But note in this example of the women that God takes account of the weakness of his own people, and does not allow his word to be kept in them by perpetual forgetfulness. He used the work of an angel at that time to bring this prediction back to the memory of these women. But now he uses the work of faithful ministers, whose office, among other things, is, as witnesses to the Apostles, to bring back to memory those things which have already been heard and received before. This task belongs especially to the Holy Spirit the Comforter, whose function is to suggest those things which have already been heard and through weakness have been given over to forgetfulness. Matth. 14. 26 tam, says Christ, the Comforter who will suggest to you all things that I have said to you. Moreover God brings back to our memory his prediction, either before it is fulfilled or after it has been fulfilled; as here, through the angel, the prediction of Christ's resurrection, now fulfilled, is brought back to the memory of the women. And the recollection is pleasant after the prediction has been fulfilled. And in sum, the recollection of all those things which we now hear daily from this Gospel of Christ will be most pleasant and sweetest of all things. Now indeed our glorying is in hope, then our glorying will be in sight; now indeed the glorifying of God in the truth of his word is in part, but then the glorifying will be perfect, after all things that have been foretold and promised have been plainly and fully fulfilled. Come, see. The second argument of confirmation is from a demonstration of the fact itself by sight. The angel calls them nearer to himself, so that they may see plainly that the thing is so. The Lord, not content with his bare word, offers also to the eyes what he has already offered to the ears to be heard in the word, as may be seen in the sacraments joined to the word. Moreover, the word of God itself, besides being audible, also...

units.la: Ispridem salutis my steria Ecclesiæ prædicta sunt, antequam implerentur.
units.tr: Long ago, the mysteries of the Church's salvation were foretold, before they were fulfilled.

units.la: Iucundissima recordatio.
units.tr: A most delightful recollection.

units.la: Alterum argumentum confirmationis testimonii Angeli. visibile est, & in oculos incurrit. Sermo enim crucis, ait Paulus, est cum demonstratione spiritualis potentiae. Et idem Paulus dicit se in verbo Euangelij crucifixisse Christum ante oculos ipsorum. Et cito profecta, dicite. Hactenus fuit secunda pars sermonis Angeli, sequitur tertia, quae mandatum quoddam est. Praecipit autem duo. 1. Primum ut ipsae eant cito, & vicissim discipulis, nominatim autem Petro annuntient resurrectionem Christi ex mortuis. 2. Ut dicant Christum praecessurum ipsos in Galilaeam: ibi ipsum coram sunt visuri. Sed primam mandati partem videamus: Iubet ut cito eant; celeritate enim postulabat Christi resurrectio, ne si testificatio eius & promulgatio differretur, obscurior iam euaderet. Et certe Euangelium Christi oportet primo quoque tempore promulgetur. Periculum enim est in mora.
units.tr: The second proof of the angel's testimony is visible and falls under the eyes. For Paul says, "the word of the cross is with a demonstration of spiritual power." And the same Paul says that in the word of the Gospel he had set Christ crucified before their eyes. "And go quickly, and tell." Up to this point is the second part of the angel's speech; the third part follows, which is a command. He enjoins two things. (1) First, that the women go quickly and in turn announce to the disciples, and especially to Peter by name, the resurrection of Christ from the dead. (2) Second, that they say Christ will go before them into Galilee, where they will see him in person. But let us look at the first part of the command. He bids them go quickly. The resurrection of Christ demanded speed, for if its testimony and proclamation were delayed, it would soon become less clear. And certainly the Gospel of Christ ought to be proclaimed at the earliest opportunity, for there is danger in delay.

units.la: Predica sermonem, insta tempestiue, intempestiue. Deinde notandum quod nominatim iubeat Petro hoc annuntiari. Non hinc quidem inferendus est Petri primatus aliquis: sed e contra, si causa recte aducertatur, Petri subiectio. Arguit enim hoc illius defectionem & constantem abnegationem, cuius conscientia indigebat imprimis hac consolatione inexpectata. Nam Petrus non fuisset ausus, post tam turpem abnegationem Domini sui, tantum beneficium, tantamque misericordiam Domini sui sibi in posterum polliceri. Sic Dominus suos iam deiectos & prostratos solet praevenire gratia sua inexpectata. Sed de mulieribus his & ipsarum testimonio, ut dicam: Iam videmus testificationem ipsarum, ut & fidem eorum qui credunt per ipsarum testimonium, niti fundamento satis firmo: nempe Dei ipsius per Angelum suum vocationis. Quae profecto vocatio Dei adeo necessaria est, ut sine ea non posset vlla esse de Christo testificatio. Quomodo praedicabunt nisi missi fuerint? Nam quod ad testificationem praeconum eorum, qui non a Deo missi, sponte sua currunt, testificationem illam eorum non dixerim authenticam esse: sed Deus est Iudex. Hoc scimus interea neminem posse dicere Iesum Dominum, nisi per Spiritum sanctum. Rursus admonemur hoc loco testimonium Christi non esse abscondendum, sed nobis iam traditum tradendum aliis, ut per ora omnium nium quàm latissimè propagetur. Sic Paulus discipulo suo, Quæ audiuisti (inquit) à me inter multos testes, committe fidelibus hominibus, qui sint idonei ad alios docendos. Præit vobis in Galilæam. Hæc secunda est mandati pars, vti modò diximus. Hinc autem docemur Euangelium, quod est historia rei gestæ, licet à nobis non conspectæ, esse tamen cum promissione aspectus eiusdem reiuturi. Verbi gratia, Euangelium passionis Christi est cum promissione aspectus alicuius eiusdem illius passionis, resurrectionis, est cum promissione aspectus alicuiusdem resurrectionis. Hoc autem fit, vt incedamus per fidem Euangelij. Quòd si non credederimus Euangelio rei illius, quàm hisce oculis nostris non spectamus, profectò futurum non est vt rem ipsam post baptismum oculis nostris cernamus. Prout dixit vobis. Prædictio hæc habetur Marci 14.28. & alibi, tantùm hoc seruamus, nihil ab Angelo hic dici, quod non ipsam confirmer ipsius Christi voce & prædictione. Solum Christi & Dei verbum fundamentum est fidei nostræ, & quicunque, siue Angelus sit, siue homo, annuntiat aliud, quàm quod iam prius ab ipso Christo est, Anathema esto. Ecce dixi. Hæc sermonis huius Angeli extrema pars est & conclusio qua obsignat quàm annuntiauit mulieribus. Idem fieri debet à Ministris omnibus Euangelij Christi. Quod quidem vt ab iis opus est, vt quæ de Christo testantur, primùm obsignentur in ipsorum cordibus, hoc est eorum ipsi habeant πληροφορίαν & fiduciam, quæ rursus non minuetur, nisi etiam viuentes in mundo migret quodammodo è mundo & municipes fiant regni cœlorum. Hoc autem rursus consequentur, si in lectione Scripturarum in meditatione, in precibus assiduis fuerint. Non enim abs re commendauit Paulus Timotheo suo Scripturas sacras.
units.tr: "Preach the word; be urgent in season, out of season." Next, it should be noted that he bids this be announced to Peter by name. From this we must not infer any primacy of Peter; on the contrary, if the reason is rightly considered, it shows Peter's subjection. For this names his defection and his steadfast denial, and his conscience above all needed this unexpected consolation. Peter would not have dared, after so shameful a denial of his Lord, to promise himself so great a benefit and so great a mercy from his Lord in the future. Thus the Lord is wont to anticipate those who have been cast down and prostrated with his unexpected grace. But as to these women and their testimony, I will say this: we already see that their testimony, and the faith of those who believe through their testimony, rests on a foundation firm enough, namely the calling of God himself through his angel. Indeed this calling of God is so necessary that without it there could be no testimony about Christ. "How shall they preach unless they are sent?" As for the testimony of those heralds who are not sent by God but run of their own accord, I would not call that testimony authentic; but God is the Judge. Meanwhile we know that no one can say "Jesus is Lord" except by the Holy Spirit. Again, we are reminded here that the testimony of Christ is not to be hidden, but, once handed down to us, is to be handed on to others, so that it may spread as widely as possible through the mouths of all. So Paul to his disciple: "What you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit to faithful men, who will be fit to teach others." "He goes before you into Galilee." This is the second part of the command, as we have just said. From this we are taught that the Gospel, which is the history of things done, though not seen by us, nevertheless comes with the promise that we shall see the same things hereafter. For example, the Gospel of Christ's passion comes with the promise of seeing that very passion, and the Gospel of the resurrection comes with the promise of seeing that very resurrection. This happens so that we may walk by faith in the Gospel. But if we do not believe the Gospel about a thing which we do not see with these eyes, certainly it will not happen that we see the thing itself with our eyes after baptism, as he told you. This prediction is found in Mark 14:28 and elsewhere. We only observe this: nothing is said here by the angel which is not confirmed by the very voice and prediction of Christ himself. The word of Christ and of God alone is the foundation of our faith, and whoever, whether angel or man, announces anything other than what has already been announced by Christ himself, let him be anathema. There, I have said it. This is the last part and conclusion of this angel's speech, by which he seals what he announced to the women. The same ought to be done by all the ministers of the Gospel of Christ. For it is necessary for them that what they testify about Christ be first sealed in their own hearts, that is, that they themselves have full assurance [πληροφορίαν] and confidence, which again will not diminish unless, while still living in the world, they in a way depart from the world and become fellow citizens of the kingdom of heaven. They will attain this again if they are constant in reading the Scriptures, in meditation and in unceasing prayer. Indeed Paul did not without reason commend the holy Scriptures to his Timothy.

units.la: Tunc citò. Hactenus sermo fuit Angeli & mandatum eius ad mulieres, sequitur ipsarum obedientia. Et quidem citò redeunt à monumento cum timore & gaudio magno: ergo in iis tria obseruamus. 1. Timorem expræsentia Angeli. 2. Gaudium ex annuntiatione resurrectionis Christi. 3. Obedientiam expedi-
units.tr: "And quickly." Up to now has been the speech of the angel and his command to the women; now follows their obedience. And indeed they return quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy. So in them we observe three things: (1) fear, at the presence of the angel; (2) joy, at the announcement of Christ's resurrection; (3) obedience, most prompt.

units.la: Mandati Angelici pars posterior. tissimam. Quæ omnia commendationem merentur,& imitationem postulât. Nos enim his modis affici oportet aliquo pacto cùm recedimus à verbi diuini prædicatione: timore quidem ex præsentia Dei,quam promisit fore in Ecclesia sua;gaudio deinde ex Euangelij prædicatione,obedientia denique ex præceptionibus & mandatis illis quæ coniuncta sunt perpetuò cum Euangelij annuntiatione: hoc præsertim mandato, vt quod audiuimus cum aliis communicemus. Etsi autem nihil expresse præcipiatur in Euangelio prædicando, tamen nuda Christi & gratiæ prædicatio postulat sanctitatem vitæ & obedientiam. Interdiu enim composite ambulandum est. Vel lux ista diurna & solaris exigit, vt composite ac decenter incedamus: quanto igitur magis sol ille iustitiæ & lux Euangelij id requirit? Etsi impudentes sunt ij, qui in sole & luce ista diurna, fœda quæque & abominanda perpetrant, quanto magis impudentes sunt, qui in luce Euangelij & in facie Christi,qui opera lucis flagitat, tamen non nisi opera tenebrarum producunt?
units.tr: The latter part of the angelic command. All these things deserve commendation and call for imitation. For we ought in some way to be affected in these ways whenever we depart from the preaching of the divine Word: with fear, indeed, at the presence of God, whom he has promised to be in his Church; then with joy at the preaching of the Gospel; and finally with obedience to those precepts and commands which are always joined with the announcement of the Gospel, especially this command, that we share with others what we have heard. Although nothing is expressly commanded in preaching the Gospel, yet the bare preaching of Christ and of grace demands holiness of life and obedience. For we must walk becomingly in the daytime. Even this daylight and sunlight requires us to walk in a composed and decent manner; how much more, then, does that sun of righteousness and the light of the Gospel require it? Shameless are those who, in this daylight and sunshine, commit every foul and abominable deed; how much more shameless are those who, in the light of the Gospel and before the face of Christ, who demands the works of light, nevertheless produce only the works of darkness?

units.la: Lucæ 24.
units.tr: Luke 24.

units.la: 2 Inuenerunt autem saxum amolutum à monumento:
units.tr: 2 And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre.

units.la: 3 Et ingressa non inuenerunt corpus Domini Iesu.
units.tr: 3 And when they had entered in, they did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.

units.la: 4 Et factum est dum in ea re hæsitarent, tum ecce duo viri superuenerunt eis induti vestibus fulgurantibus:
units.tr: 4 And it came to pass, as they were perplexed about this, that behold, two men stood by them in shining garments.

units.la: 5 Quum autem expauefacta inclinarent faciem in terram, dixerunt eis, Quid inter mortuos quæritis eum qui viuit?
units.tr: 5 And as they were afraid and bowed their faces to the earth, they said unto them, Why seek ye the living among the dead?

units.la: 6 Non est hic, sed suscitatus est. Mememinte vt loquutus sit vobis quum adhuc in Galilæa esset,
units.tr: 6 He is not here, but is risen. Remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee,

units.la: 7 Dicens, Oportet filium hominis tradi in manum hominum peccatorum, & crucifigi, & die tertio tertio resurgere.
units.tr: 7 Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.

units.la: 8 Recordata sunt igitur verborum illius.
units.tr: 8 And they remembered his words.

units.la: 9 Etreuersa a monumento annunciauerunt hac omnia illis vndecim & reliquis omnibus.
units.tr: 9 And they returned from the sepulchre and told all these things to the eleven and to all the rest.

units.la: HÆc hactenus dicta sunt de mulieribus primo egressis: nunc ex Lucæ Euangelio dicendum de mulieribus secundo egressis. Nam Lucas videtur texere historiam de his mulieribus, quæ posterius sunt egressæ: cùm Matthæus & Marcus narrationem instituerint de mulieribus iis quæ prius sunt egressæ ad sepulchrum. Namalij fuisse ac diuersum à superiore illo hunc mulierum numerum, apparet ex diuersis apparitionibus. Ab illo tantùm conspectus est vnus Angelus, ab hoc duo. Sic enim fuit Deo testium suorum cœlestium numerum angere ad maiorem fidem faciendam resurrectioni. Historia autem ea quæ apud Lucam reperitur, non longè diuersa est ab illa quæ apud Matthæum & Marcum legitur. Itaque non immorabimur in hac Lucæ historia. Primùm de mulieribus istis hoc obseruamus, quod quo plures ex iis egrediuntur ad sepulchrum Domini, eo maius sit dedecus Apostolorum, quos oportuit omnium primos egredi: & sexus & vocatio id postulabat. Præreptus autem est iis locus à mulieribus: non vlla quidem virtute quæ in sexu ipso fuit, sed sola Dei gratia, quæ voluit Christi resurrectionem & vitam tum primùm magis efficacem esse in vasis illis infirmioribus quàm in viris, adeóque etiam Apostolis ipsis. Nam illud extra controuersiam pono, in his mulieribus, quæ tanto Christi studio ducebantur, quæ tanto mane egressæ sunt intepidè ad sepulchrum Domini, in his, inquâ efficacem fuisse Christi vitam in resurrectione sua, & vitâ illam Christi causam extitisse cur sic hæ extra-ordinem fecerint. Nam vita nostra spiritualis, tota est à Christi vita, & virtute resurrectionis ipsius, sine qua nihil possumus facere. Tum videmus mulieres istas multis obnoxias fuisse affectionibus. Primùm egressæ sunt cum anxietate animi & dolore: deinde, cùm non invenerunt corpus Domini quod quærebant, iam planè cō{a}fternatæ sunt. Tum cùm viderent angelos fulgurantes expauefactæ sunt: postremò audito læto illo resurrectionis Christi nuncio gauisæ sunt, & cum gaudio domum reuersæ. Quotquot quærunt Dominum in hac vita, variis animi perturbationibus sunt obnoxij, &ferè impij magis tranquillo & securo sunt animo quàm pij(si modo carnalis ista securitas hoc nomine sit dicenda) ijenim sunt qui dicunt, Pax & tuta omnia. Sed cùm dicent, Pax & tuta omnia, tum repentinum imminet exitium. At perturbationum piorum semper finis est gaudium & pax illa Dei, quæ superat omnem intellectum: & recordatio ipsa perturbationum præteritarum & afflictionũ, gaudium adauget: quum impiis recordatio pacis illius falsæ & voluptatis omnis in qua aliquando vixerunt augeat dolorem.
units.tr: These things have been said so far about the women who went out first. Now, from the Gospel of Luke, we must speak of the women who went out afterwards. For Luke seems to weave the story of those women who went out later, whereas Matthew and Mark began their narrative with the women who had gone out earlier to the sepulchre. That this number of women was different from that earlier group, and not the same, appears from the different appearances: to the earlier women only one angel was seen, to these two. For so God willed to multiply the number of his heavenly witnesses, to make the resurrection more firmly believed. The account found in Luke, however, is not far different from the one read in Matthew and Mark, and so we will not linger over this story of Luke. First, we observe concerning these women that the more of them go out to the sepulchre of the Lord, the greater is the shame of the Apostles, who ought to have gone out first of all; both their sex and their calling demanded it. But the place was taken from them by women, not by any virtue that was in the sex itself, but by the sole grace of God, who willed that the resurrection and life of Christ should then prove more effective in those weaker vessels than in men, and even in the Apostles themselves. For I lay this down beyond controversy: in these women, who were led by such zeal for Christ, who went out so early in the morning and yet came too sluggishly to the sepulchre of the Lord, in these, I say, the life of Christ in his resurrection was effective, and that life of Christ was the cause why they acted so beyond the ordinary course. For our spiritual life is wholly from the life of Christ and the power of his resurrection, without which we can do nothing. Next we see that these women were subject to many emotions. First they went out with anxiety and sorrow of mind; then, when they did not find the body of the Lord that they sought, they were utterly dismayed; then, when they saw the shining angels, they were terrified; lastly, having heard the joyful news of Christ's resurrection, they rejoiced and returned home with joy. Whoever seeks the Lord in this life is subject to various disturbances of mind, and the wicked are almost more calm and secure in mind than the godly (if indeed that carnal security may be called by this name). For they are the ones who say, "Peace and safety," but when they say, "Peace and safety," then sudden destruction hangs over them. But the disturbances of the godly always end in joy and that peace of God which surpasses all understanding; and the very recollection of past disturbances and afflictions increases their joy, whereas for the wicked the recollection of that false peace and of all the pleasure in which they once lived increases their grief.

units.la: Nunc de Angelis dicamus, qui hac vice duo conspiciuntur, cùm prius vnus tantum conspectus sitâ priori illo mulierum cœtu, orationem suam ordiuntur à reprehensione. Quid, inquiunt, quæritis viuentem inter mortuos? Reprehensio ista indicat aliquid reprehensione dignũ fuisse in istis mulieribus. Id autem, vt verba sequentia docet, est obliuio, quòd nimirum oblitæ sint prædictionis Domini. Ex quo discimus hanc esse Dei voluntatem, vt firma memoria retineamus quæ ab ipso dicuntur omnia. Quod si ea obliuioni tradita à nobis fuerint, tum profectò non carebimus iusta aliqua reprehensione, & iram Dei nostri in nos aliquam prouocabimus. At reprehendendo pariter annunciant Christum viuere, docéntque mulieres istas, id quod argumento est, cum ira illa aliqua coniunctam esse misericordiam Dei paternam ac lenitatem. Tum quæ sequuntur in oratione Angelorum absque omni iræ significatione annunciata, arguunt iram illam Dei erga suos semel conceptam fratim euanescere, misericordiam autem durare. Ira Dei perpetuò coniuncta est cum misericordia paterna erga suos. Ira deinde abit & dicto citius euanescit. Misericordia verò manet quantisper viuimus vitam istam præsentem, est ira Dei aliqua etiam erga suos, quoniam multæ sunt defectiones etiam sanctorum. At postquam peccare iam desiuimus in altera vita, tum quidem sola Dei cles
units.tr: Now let us speak of the angels, who on this occasion are seen as two, whereas before only one had been seen with the earlier company of women. They begin their address with a rebuke: "Why," they say, "do you seek the living among the dead?" That rebuke indicates that there was something in those women worthy of reproof. This, as the words that follow show, was forgetfulness, namely that they had forgotten the Lord's prediction. From this we learn that it is God's will that we retain firmly in memory all the things that are spoken by him. If these are committed to oblivion by us, then assuredly we shall not be free from some just reproof, and we shall provoke some anger of our God against us. Yet by rebuking they equally announce that Christ lives, and they teach these women, which is a proof that the paternal mercy and gentleness of God is joined with some anger. Then the things that follow in the angels' speech, announced without any sign of anger, show that the anger of God once conceived towards his own quickly vanishes, but his mercy endures. The anger of God is always joined with his paternal mercy towards his own. Then the anger departs and vanishes faster than the word is spoken. But mercy remains as long as we live this present life, and there is also some anger of God even against his own, since there are many failings even in the saints. But after we have ceased to sin in the other life, then indeed the sole mercy of God

units.la: Quærentium Christum varie tentationes in hac vita. 1 Thess. 5.3.
units.tr: The varied temptations of those who seek Christ in this life. 1 Thess. 5.3.

units.la: 9. Duo Angeli, testes resurrectionis.
units.tr: 9. The two angels, witnesses of the resurrection.

units.la: Obliuionis nostræ censura.
units.tr: The censure of our forgetfulness.

units.la: Charitas Dei erga suos. {a}Clementia, sola benignitas in æternum futura est. Pueri enim hic sumus, qui indigemus assiduis castigationibus: ut infantes loquimur, ut infantes sentimus, ut infantes agimus: at in altera vita viri erimus & perfecti, ut vivientiemus, loquemur, agemus deniq; omnia. Tū eo quod dicit Angelus, Mementote ut loquutus sit, Innuit Deum non oblitum fuisse verborum suorum: tanti enim sunt ponderis verba Dei apud Deum ipsum, ut nihil loquatur unquam temere, & si loquatur, nullo unquam tempore obliuiscatur se locutum esse. Quia vero non sunt eius nos ponderis verba Dei, ideo nos statim ea obliuiscimur tradimus. Vt autem ipse Deus verborum suorum recordatur perpetuò, neque finit quæ loquutus est unquam sibi excidere: ita non patitur ut nos eorum in æternum obliuiscamur: verùm suo demum tempore in memoriam nobis ea reducit, quæ ipsa recordatio bonis quidem suavis est ac iucunda, malis verò ingrata & iniucunda. Nam in hoc etiam colloco aliquam partem infernorum, quod reprobis in memoriam reducenda sunt Dei verba illa quæ loquuntur est aliquando ipsis. Conscientia enim verborum illorum Dei in æternam accusatura est & vexatura miseros, quæ ipsi dum viverent, contemnerunt, & quasi nulla digna memoria obliuioni dederunt. Nunc redimus ad mulieres: de his dictum est quod recordatæ sunt illorum verborum Domini ac receperunt a sepulchro, denique omnia ista annuncia-runt vnde cum discipulis ac reliquis quibuscunque. Gaudiū illud quod ipsæ conceperunt ex annuntiatione illa Angeli, liberaliter cum aliis communicant. Neque tamē propter aliquid quam ex eo est imminutum. Expeto, inquit Paulus, videre vos, ut aliquod donum spirituale vobis impertiar. Quid tum? hoc est, inquit, ut consolationem percipiam apud vos communem per mutuam fidem vestram simul & meam. Ecce, communicare spirituale donum, Paulo fuit consolationem percipere, loquendo aliis, ut & audiendo alios ædificamur. Sed quibus demum annunciarunt illa, non quibusuis, sed iis quos existimarunt simul secum gauisuros gaudium. Natura enim omnes hac συμπαθείας, &, ut sic dicam, compassionem requirimus, ut alij gaudeant nobiscum gaudentibus, doleant nobiscum dolentibus. Secus profecto non lubenter cum aliis communicamus, vel gaudium vel dolorem nostrum.
units.tr: The love of God towards his own. Clemency, the sole kindness, will endure for eternity. For here we are children, who need constant chastisements; we speak as infants, we feel as infants, we act as infants; but in the other life we shall be men and perfect, so that we shall live, speak, and finally act in all things as adults. Then, in that the angel says, "Remember how he spoke," he hints that God has not forgotten his own words; for the words of God are of such weight with God himself that he never speaks rashly, and if he speaks, he never at any time forgets that he has spoken. But because our words are not of that weight, we straightway forget and let go of them. And just as God himself perpetually remembers his words and never allows what he has said to slip from himself, so he does not permit us to forget them forever; rather, in his own time he brings them back to our memory, and this recollection is indeed sweet and pleasant to the good, but unwelcome and unpleasant to the wicked. For I also count it as part of hell that the words of God which were once spoken to the reprobate must be brought back to their memory. For the conscience of those words of God will accuse and torment the wretched forever, which they despised while they lived and, as if worthy of no remembrance, gave over to oblivion. Now we return to the women: of them it has been said that they remembered the words of the Lord and returned from the sepulchre, and finally that they announced all these things to the disciples and the rest. The joy which they themselves conceived from the angel's announcement they share generously with others, and it is not diminished in any way by this. "I long," says Paul, "to see you, that I may impart to you some spiritual gift." What then? "That is," he says, "that I may receive comfort among you, through our mutual faith, both yours and mine." Behold: for Paul to communicate a spiritual gift was to receive comfort by speaking to others, just as we are built up by hearing others. But they announced those things not to just anyone, but to those whom they thought would rejoice with them in their joy. For by nature we all require this sympathy (συμπάθεια), and, as I may say, fellow-feeling, that others should rejoice with us when we rejoice and grieve with us when we grieve. Otherwise we surely do not gladly share with others either our joy or our sorrow.

units.la: Lucæ 24.
units.tr: Luke 24.

units.la: 10 Erant autem ℳaria Magdalene, & Iohanna, & Maria Iacobi mater, & reliqua cum ipsis, quæ hæc dicebant Apostolis.
units.tr: 10 Now it was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and the others with them, who told these things to the apostles.

units.la: 11 Sed visa sunt apud eos quasi deliramentum verba ipsarum, neque crediderunt ijs.
units.tr: 11 But their words seemed to them like nonsense, and they did not believe them.

units.la: NARRAT Lucas interea dum mulieres hæ, quæ posterius sunt egressæ ad sepulchrum Domini, redierunt, interfuisse eas Apostolorum cœtui, quæ iam prius sunt egressæ ad sepulchrum, in quibus præcipuæ fuerunt Maria Magdalene, Iohanna, Maria Iacobi mater: interfuisse, inquam, eas & eadem quæ posteriores istæ Apostolis annunciasse. Mulieres istæ, quæ aliæ post alias superveniunt discipulis, atque eadem annuntiant, ut arguunt summam in Apostolorum corpore, summam stupiditatem, ut quibus opus fuit totiens: ita arguunt summam in Deo misericordiam, qui non passus est eos sic segnescere, & in securitate illa carnali perpetuo conquiescere. Eadem Dei misericordia semper manet erga suos: qui & ipsi nisi subinde excitarentur modis omnibus, nunc testibus aliis post alios continuo missis, nunc afflictionibus, profecto in securitate illa sua perire eos oporteret. Hinc sunt testes hi ac ministri verbi sui, quos quotidie mittit ad nos scilicet expergefaciendos ex tam profundo isto sopore. Dum autem testantur mulieres, & annunciant resurrectionem Christi, idque blandè ac leniter: eadem opera exprobrant Apostolis summam segnitiem & cessationem. Eos enim oportuit ex officio mulieribus ista omnia annuntiare. Sed Deus in mulieribus his extraordinariis voluit docere regnum Christi positum esse in extraordinaria virtute, & penes se esse pro absoluta illa sua potestate extra ordinem mittere testes, quos ipsi est visum, & extra ordinem seruare etiam absque testibus & verbi sui ministris, quos ipsi est visum. Ut non sit quod Pontificij tatopere vrgeant perpetua petuò ordinariam vocationem pastorum & doctorum in Ecclesia. Sed visa sunt apud eos quasi deliramenta. Ex mi- sericordia Dei fuit, quod mulieres aliæ post alias, Apostolis illis vndecim superuenerint: nunc videmus quàm male compensent ij tantam Dei misericordiam: recusant discere veritatem istam resurrectionis Domini ex mulieribus hisce: & Euangelium resurrectionis ipsis est quasi stultitia & deliramentum. Vnde apparet eos adhuc animales fuisse magis quàm Spirituales homines.
units.tr: Luke relates that, while these women, who had gone out to the Lord's tomb later, were returning, the women who had gone out to the tomb earlier, chief among them Mary Magdalene, Joanna and Mary the mother of James, were present at the gathering of the apostles. I say they were present and had told the apostles the same things that these later women did. These women came to the disciples one after another and announced the same news, which shows, on the one hand, the great dullness of the apostles' company, since they needed so many witnesses, and on the other hand the great mercy of God, who did not allow them to grow so sluggish and rest forever in that carnal security. God's mercy toward his own always remains. Unless they were roused in every way, sometimes by witness after witness sent without pause and sometimes by afflictions, they would surely have perished in that security of theirs. Hence these witnesses and ministers of his Word, whom he sends to us every day, to wake us from such a deep sleep. And while the women bear witness and announce the resurrection of Christ, they do so gently and mildly, yet at the same time they reproach the apostles for their great sloth and inactivity. For the apostles ought by their office to have announced all these things to the women. But God wished in these extraordinary women to teach that the kingdom of Christ rests on extraordinary power, and that it lies within his own absolute power to send witnesses outside the ordinary order, as he sees fit, and to preserve his people outside the ordinary order even without witnesses and ministers of his Word, as he sees fit. So there is no reason for the Papists to press so insistently the perpetual and ordinary calling of ministers and teachers in the Church. But their words seemed to them like nonsense. It was by the mercy of God that one woman after another came to those eleven apostles.
