Now we see how badly they repay so great a mercy of God: they refuse to learn this truth of the Lord's resurrection from these women, and the gospel of the resurrection seems to them foolishness and nonsense. From this it appears that they were still more natural than spiritual men.

units.la: Animalis enim homo non est capax eorum quæ sunt Spiritus Dei: sunt enim illi stultitia, nec potest ea cognoscere: quòd si Apostolis, ex parte quidem regenitis, sed nūc ad tempus obstupefactis, tam parum profuit annuntiatio Euangelij & resurrectionis Christi, quàm parum proderit annuntiatio Euangelij non regenitis, si initium ab ea sumpseris in eis docendis, & ex summa illa qua consopiti sunt securitate expergefaciendis? quin potius si cum iis res sit, exordium sumendum est à legis comminationibus, idque exemplo Pauli, qui dum concionatur peccatoribus sic exorsus est, Palam est ira Dei e cælo, adversus omnem impietatem & iniustitiam hominum. Postea verò vbi iam ex lege comminatus est, aggreditur doctrinam Euangelij. Nunc autem, inquit, iustitia Dei absque lege manifestata est, &c. Discimus præterea exemplo Apostolorum, quod etsi sermone de Christo sit Dei potentia & sapientia vocatis, tamen manente adhuc in animis nostris aliqua parte sapientiæ mundi huius, aliquid stultitia & deliramenti videri nobis ei subesse, quia nimirum sapientia humana & carnis ista Deo inimica est, & spiritualia ducit pro stultitia: quum autem videbimus omnium complementum in vltimo illo die, tum quidem dicemus cum Sara, quæ post aquam promissum illi Isaac peperit: Risum, inquit, fecit mihi Deus: quisquis audiet arridebit mihi. q.d. Risi quidem antea & irrisi promissionem de filio factam, nunc verò serio & præ animi gaudio rideo. Sic & nos quod nunc ex parte irridemus, quia nimirum non toti regeniti sumus, id ipsum erit nobis materia risus & solidi gaudij in æternum. In hac Apostolorum incredulitate non est prætermittenda Dei providentia in gubernandis iis sic, vt noluerit eos cre-
units.tr: For the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God; they are foolishness to him, and he cannot know them. But if the announcement of the gospel and of Christ's resurrection did so little good to the apostles, who were indeed regenerate in part but for the moment stunned, how much good would the announcement of the gospel do to those who are not regenerate, if you began with it in teaching them and in waking them from that deep security into which they have sunk? Indeed, if the matter stands thus with them, the beginning must be taken from the threats of the law, following the example of Paul, who, when he preached to sinners, began thus: For the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of men. Afterwards, when he had already threatened by the law, he turns to the teaching of the gospel: But now, he says, the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from the law, etc. We learn further from the example of the apostles that, although the power and wisdom of God are preached to those who are called through the message about Christ, nevertheless, while some part of the wisdom of this world still remains in our minds, something of it seems to us to be foolishness and nonsense, because human wisdom and the flesh are hostile to God, and they count spiritual things as foolishness. But when we see the fulfilment of all things on that last day, then we shall say with Sarah, who bore Isaac, the son promised her after the water: God has made laughter for me; everyone who hears will laugh with me. That is, I laughed before and mocked the promise of a son, but now I laugh in earnest and for joy of spirit. So too, what we now in part laugh at, because we are not yet wholly regenerate, will be to us a cause of laughter and of solid joy for ever. In this unbelief of the apostles we must not overlook the providence of God in governing them in such a way that he would not let them believe except once the matter was thoroughly known and Christ himself had been seen, after he had risen from the dead.

units.la: XXX dere nisi re penitus cognita, & inspecto tandem ipso Christo, postquam ex mortuis resurrexisset. Voluit enim Apostolos exire in mundum, & de se testari. Oportet autem eos, qui aliis praedicant Christum, habere in se ϑεοπνευστια eorum quae aliis enuntiant, & ideo loqui quia crediderunt. Sic enim loquentur cum demonstratione spiritualis potentiae, & ut Paulus ipse de se dixit, eiusmodi habentes spem multa in loquendo euidentia vtentur.
units.tr: For he wished the apostles to go out into the world and bear witness concerning him. Those, however, who preach Christ to others ought to have in themselves the divine inspiration [θεοπνευστία] of what they announce to others, and therefore speak because they believe. For so they will speak with a demonstration of spiritual power, and, as Paul himself said of himself, having such hope, they will use great plainness in speaking.

units.la: Lucae 24.
units.tr: Luke 24.

units.la: 12 Petrus autem surgens cucurrit ad monumentum, & cum introspexisset, videt lintea sola illic iacentia, abiitque, apud semetipsum mirans factum.
units.tr: 12 But Peter rose and ran to the tomb. Stooping to look in, he saw the linen cloths lying there alone, and he went away wondering to himself at what had happened.

units.la: Iohannis 20.
units.tr: John 20.

units.la: 3 Exiuit ergo Petrus, & alter ille discipulus, & venerunt ad monumentum.
units.tr: 3 So Peter and the other disciple went out and came to the tomb.

units.la: 4 Currebant autem duo simul, sed alter ille discipulus praecucurrit citius Petro, venitque prior ad monumentum.
units.tr: 4 The two ran together, but the other disciple outran Peter and came to the tomb first.

units.la: 5 Et cum se incurvasset vidit postea lintea, non tamen introiuit.
units.tr: 5 And stooping down, he saw the linen cloths lying there, but he did not go in.

units.la: 6 Venit ergo Simon Petrus sequens eum, & introiuit in monumentum, & conspexit lintea ibi posita:
units.tr: 6 Then Simon Peter came after him, went into the tomb, and saw the linen cloths lying there,

units.la: 7 Et sudarium quod fuerat super caput eius, non cum linteis positum, sed seorsum inuolutum in vnum locum.
units.tr: 7 and the napkin that had been over his head, not lying with the linen cloths but folded up in a place by itself.

units.la: 8 Tunc ergo introiuit etiam alter ille discipulus, qui venerat prior ad monumentum, viditque & credidit.
units.tr: 8 Then the other disciple, who had come to the tomb first, went in too; he saw and believed.

units.la: 9 Nondum enim noverant scripturam, videlicet quod oporteret eum a mortuis resurgere.
units.tr: 9 For as yet they did not know the Scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.

units.la: 10 Redierunt ergo illi discipuli ad suos.
units.tr: 10 So the disciples went back to their own homes.

units.la: 11 Maria vero flens stabat ad monumentum foris: dum ergo sederet incurvauit se in monumentum,
units.tr: 11 But Mary stood outside the tomb weeping. As she wept, she stooped down and looked into the tomb,

units.la: 12 Et conspexit duos Angelos albatos, sedentes, unum ad caput & alterum ad pedes, illic vbi iacuerat corpus Iesu.
units.tr: 12 and she saw two angels in white, sitting, one at the head and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain.

units.la: 13 Qui dixerunt, Mulier, quid fles? Dicit eis, Sustulerunt Dominum meum, nec scio vbi posuerunt eum.
units.tr: 13 They said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping?" She said to them, "They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him."

units.la: Non crediderunt quidem testimonio mulierum: tamen excitati sunt ad indagandam rei veritatem: id quod arguit semen illud fidei eorum semel exceptum non prorsus extinctum toto illo tempore quo segregati ac latitabant. Nam verum illud semen quamuis est, si semel excipiatur, nunquam plane extingui potest, ut ad tempus ipsum suffocetur, ne is quidem, qui illud in se habeat, intelligat se id habere. Nam spatium quoddam temporis est, quo Christus formatur in cordibus, ut loquitur Apostolus, quoque idem temporis spatio fere non sentitur: at tandem verbo incipit se movere in spirituali quasi vtero, & in nobis viuere. Neque vero statim erumpit in lucem, sed prius edit aliquem in nobis fructum, & per nos, donec mandat in lucem prodeat & in apertum. Exemplum est Iudaeorum eorum qui Berrheae agebant: hi quidem iacebant sine Christo. At aliquid boni etiam tum in iis restantur verba illa quibus dictum est eos generosiores fuisse iis qui tum erant Thessalonicae. Audito iam paulo, coepit semen illud quod latebat & iacebat quasi mortuum, vires suas colligere, ac vitam aliquam quamque recipere: verum non prima facie crediderunt verbis Apostoli, sed scrutati sunt scripturas, nunquid ita se haberet, tandem vero ex iis crediderunt non pauci. Quamobrem temere iudicandum non est de secutis, sed periculum faciendum primum de semine, an lateat in iis aliquod necne. Periculum autem fiet, si de Christo ipsiusque verbo iis loquaris. Quo fit necessario ut tandem aliquando, si modo sit aliquod semen in iis verae pietatis, in lucem prodeat. Excitati igitur duo discipuli currunt, non ambulant: quod indicium erat motus alicuius & affectionis in animis eorum concitatae. Cucurrit Maria Magdalene, cum revertisset domum, sed ex dolore hoc fecit: currunt discipuli duo nunc, sed non ex dolore, verum ex gaudio aliquo. Gaudium autem illud excitatum est ex mulierum illo sermone & testimonio de Christi resurrectione: nam etsi ipsi non tum primum crediderunt, tamen cum vnicè voluerunt rem ita se habere, vt annuntiarunt mulieres, gaudium conceperunt ex earum sermone, id quod vel quotidiana experientia docet in aliis rebus. Difficilius quidem fidem habemus iis quae maximè fieri optamus, laetamur tamen sermonibus iis, quos audimus de eorum aduentu atque successu. Quanquam eò adducor vt putem non extitisse gaudium istud sine aliqua cordis eorum inclinatione ad ea ipsa quae annunciabantur à mulieribus, quòd nimirum vera essent. Gaudium enim istud spirituale est ex aliqua certè fide & cordis inclinatione. Vbi verò nulla est cordis inclinatio, ibi nulla sinceri gaudii perceptio, verum dolor potius ex verbo Christi audito. Currebat autem. In cursu hoc contentio fuit inter discipulos duos, certabant enim vterad sepulchrum Domini prior perueniret. Certare in bonis bonū, sed certare in malis malum. Vis, inquit Christus, affertur regno caelorū, & violenti rapiunt illud: quibus verbis significat sanctā contentionem. Similiter, Contendite, inquit, intrare per angustam portam. Paulus qui alios omnes ad cursum prouocabat, ipse quoque cū aliis certabat, vt vnā particeps fieret Euangelij sui: & ne quo modo, cum aliis praedicarit ipse reprobus fieret. Quanta cum contentione animi ipse cucurrerit ad metam propositā ipse retis est. Vnum, inquit, ago, ea quidem quae à tergo sunt obliuiscens, ad ea verò quae à fronte sunt contendens scopum versus ferre ad palmā supernè vocationis Dei in Christo Iesu. Ex iis qui currunt in stadio hoc terrestri, alij aliis inuidêt propositam coronam: quia, ait Paulus, Omnes quidem currunt, sed vnus accipit praemium: nimirum quia vna tantum propositā est currentibus corona. At qui vnā currunt in stadio illo coelesti, tantum abest vt alij aliis inuideant coronam, vt è contrà ad cursum cohortentur & coronam accipiendam: nimirum quia non est vna tantum cora proposita, sed infinitæ sunt. Ideo Paulus, postquam dixit sibi repositam esse coronam iustitiæ confecto iam cursu suo, subiungit cōtinuō, Non mihi soli̇ṁ sed & omnibus qui expetierint illustrem illum aduentum Domini. Imò vero quo plures ex aliis promouemus in stadio illo, eo gloriosior corona nobis est expectanda. Quæ est spes nostra, quod gaudium, quæ corona, de qua glorieris, annon & vos in conspectu Domini nostri Iesu Christi in aduentu ipsius? Itaque vos estis gaudium meum & corona mea. Inter currendum Iohannes Petrum anteuertit & prior ad sepulchrum, vel quia agilior fuit, vtpote iunior: vel quia maiori lætitia ferebatur. Cum ad sepulchrum venit, non statim ingressus est, sed intuitus tàm est in ipsum, viditque lintea ibi posita. Petrus autem posterior venit, statim ingressus est consperxitq; lintea posita vna in parte: sudarium autem, quo inuolutum erat caput Domini, alia in parte: quo significabatur nō furtim sublatū esse corpus Domini, sed resurrexisse Christum. Nam si furtim sublatus fuisset, vna linteū quoque cū sudario sublatū fuisset, vt verisimile est. Ex hoc obiter apparet nō vno & cōtinuo linteo opertum fuisse totū corpus Domini, sed seorsum caput inuolutū fuisse mappa: qui mos fuit sepeliendi apud Iudeos. Postea verò Iohānes ingressus est & vidit & credidit. Inæquabile valde videmus hic cursū, quæ corripimus ad cœlos: nūc enim celerius, nūc segnius currimus: vt illud cōspiciatur verū esse quod dicitur, Nō est currétis aut volétis, sed miseréetis Dei. Adinoue-te enim manu sua Deo, celerius currit aliquis, subducere rursus manu sua, segnius. At qui perseuerat ad finem, siue celerius, siue segnius currat, coronabitur. Petrus credidit, vel certè raptus est in admirationē, vt loquitur Lucas: Petrus, inquā, qui prior ingressus est sepulchrum. Iohānes quoq; credidit, qui posterior ingressus est. Non enim scriptū est: Qui currit celeriter coronabitur; sed omnino, Qui perseuerat coronabitur. Perseuerem̃ igitur & celeriter curramus si vires adsint: sin minus curramus certè & ad metam pro viribus cōnitamur. Nondum enim resurrexerant. Occupatio est; In scripturis prædictum fuit non semel Christum resurrecturum: cur igitur non credidit Iohannes prius quā vidit? Respondet ignaros fuisse infirmitas. discipulos scripturæ illius,quæ extabat deChrifti refur-rectione:quo quidem loco significat Iohannes peccasse se pariter cum aliis, quod non priùs crediderit quàm oculis viderit. Bonum quidem est credere cùm oculis conspicimus. At malum est non credere, cùm auribus audimus.Verùm suspendere fidem nostram ad præsentem rei cuius mentio fit aspectum,malum est: imò cum magno periculo hoc coiunctum est, non credere verbo Dei,priusquam videamus eius complementum. Periculum enim est ne vnquam futurum sit, vt oculis complementum videamus. Credamus igitur quàm primùm verbo Dei, vt illa ipsa re de qua loquitur verbum, & aspectu eius tandē suo tempore fruamur. Beati sunt, inquit,qui non viderunt & crediderunt. Non est hic prætereundus candor hic qui in Iohanne Euangelista nostro conspicitur:nam ne sibi quidem pepercit, sed scriptor commisit etiam suum errorem, & ignorantiam illam suam qua scripturam sacram non nouerat; nobisq; imitandum eius exemplum, in nobis ipsis quidem,non autem Scripturis Dei damnandis,quoties vel ignari, vel incredúli deprehendimur. Non enim citra blasphemiâ obiicitur Scripturis,quod eæ obscuræ,ambiguæ, mutilæ, mancæ sunt. Blasphemi autem isti quantumvis nunc ad rauim vsque vociferantur, tamen in illo die non habebunt vel vnam voculam quam obiiciant aduersus sacras Dei scripturas.
units.tr: They did not indeed believe the women's testimony; yet they were stirred to inquire into the truth of the matter. This shows that the seed of faith in them, once received, was not utterly extinguished during all that time when they were cut off and hiding. For that true seed, once it has been received, can never be quite extinguished; it may be smothered for a time, so that even the one who has it does not perceive that he has it. There is a certain span of time in which Christ is formed in hearts, as the Apostle says, and during that span it is almost unfelt. At last, however, by the Word, it begins to stir in a spiritual womb, as it were, and to live in us. Nor does it break out into the light at once; first it brings forth some fruit in us and through us, until at last it comes forth into the light and into the open. The Jews of Berea are an example. They lay without Christ, yet something good was still in them, as the words say that they were more noble than those at Thessalonica. When they had heard a little, that seed which had lain hidden and as though dead began to gather its strength and to receive some kind of life. Yet they did not believe the Apostle's words at first sight, but searched the Scriptures to see whether these things were so; and at last not a few of them believed. Therefore we must not rashly judge those who follow, but first make trial of the seed, whether there is any seed in them or not. The trial will be made if you speak to them of Christ and of his Word. Thus it comes about necessarily that at last, if there is any seed of true godliness in them, it will come forth into the light. So the two disciples are roused and run, they do not walk; and this was a sign of some movement and affection stirred in their minds. Mary Magdalene ran when she had returned home, but she did so out of grief. These two disciples run now, but not out of grief; rather out of some joy. That joy was stirred by the women's speech and testimony about Christ's resurrection. For although they themselves did not believe it at first, yet, since they very much wished the thing to be as the women announced, they conceived joy from their words. Everyday experience teaches this in other matters too. It is harder to put faith in what we most desire to happen, yet we rejoice in the reports that we hear of their coming and their success. Still, I am inclined to think that this joy did not arise without some inclination of their hearts towards the very things announced by the women, namely that they were true. For that joy is spiritual; it arises from some faith and inclination of the heart. Where there is no inclination of the heart, there is no perception of true joy, but rather grief from the word of Christ heard. Yet they were running. In this running there was a contest between the two disciples, for each strove to reach the tomb of the Lord first. To strive in good things is good, but to strive in evil things is evil. "The kingdom of heaven," says Christ, "suffers violence, and the violent take it by force"; by these words he signifies a holy eagerness. Similarly, "Strive," he says, "to enter by the narrow gate." Paul, who urged all others to run, himself also strove with others, so that he might be made a partaker together with them of his Gospel, and lest in any way, after preaching to others, he himself should become a castaway. How eagerly he ran to the goal set before him is clear from his own words. "One thing I do," he says, "forgetting the things which are behind, and reaching forward to those which are before, I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus." Among those who run in this earthly stadium, some envy others the crown set before them; but, says Paul, "all indeed run, yet one receives the prize": clearly because only one crown is set before the runners. But those who run together in that heavenly stadium are so far from envying one another the crown that, on the contrary, they urge one another on to the race and to receive the crown; clearly because the crown set before them is not one only, but countless. Therefore Paul, after saying that the crown of righteousness was laid up for him, now that his course was finished, adds at once, "Not for me only, but for all who have loved the appearing of our Lord." Indeed, the more of others we bring forward in that stadium, the more glorious the crown we may expect for ourselves. "What is our hope, our joy, the crown in which you glory? Are not you, in the presence of our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming? For you are my joy and my crown." While running, John outran Peter and came first to the tomb, either because he was swifter, being the younger, or because he was carried along with greater gladness. When he came to the tomb, he did not go in at once, but looked into it and saw the linen cloths lying there. Peter came later; he went in at once and saw the linen cloths lying in one place, and the napkin, with which the head of the Lord had been wrapped, in another place. This signified that the body of the Lord had not been stolen away secretly, but that Christ had risen. For if he had been stolen away, the linen cloth would likely have been taken with the napkin. From this it appears in passing that the whole body of the Lord was not wrapped in one continuous linen cloth, but that the head was wrapped separately in a cloth, which was the custom of burial among the Jews. Afterwards John went in, and saw, and believed. Here we see a very uneven course in the race we run towards heaven: for now we run more swiftly, now more slowly, so that it may be seen that what is said is true: "It is not of him who runs, nor of him who wills, but of God who shows mercy." For when someone stretches his hand out to God, he runs more swiftly; when he draws his hand back again, he runs more slowly. But whoever perseveres to the end, whether he runs more swiftly or more slowly, will be crowned. Peter believed, or at least was caught up in wonder, as Luke says; Peter, I say, who entered the tomb first. John also believed, who entered after him. For it is not written, "He who runs swiftly will be crowned," but simply, "He who perseveres will be crowned." So let us persevere, and run swiftly if our strength allows; if not, let us at least run and strive to the goal as far as our strength allows. For as yet they had not risen. It is an objection: the Christ was foretold in the Scriptures more than once as going to rise again; why then did John not believe before he saw? He answers that the disciples were weak in not understanding that Scripture, which stood concerning Christ's resurrection. In this place John signifies that he sinned together with the others, in not believing until he had seen with his eyes. It is good to believe when we see with our eyes; but it is bad not to believe when we hear with our ears. Yet to suspend our faith until we see the thing spoken of present is bad; indeed, it is joined with great danger not to believe the Word of God before we see its fulfilment. For there is a danger that it may never happen that we see its fulfilment with our eyes. Let us therefore believe the Word of God as soon as possible, so that at its proper time we may enjoy the very thing of which the Word speaks, and also see it. "Blessed are they," he says, "who have not seen and yet have believed." Here we must not pass over the frankness that is seen in our Evangelist John. For he did not spare himself, but the writer committed to record even his own error and that ignorance of his by which he had not known the holy Scripture. Let his example be imitated by us, in condemning ourselves, not the Scriptures of God, whenever we are caught either ignorant or unbelieving. For it is not without blasphemy that one objects to the Scriptures that they are obscure, ambiguous, mutilated, and defective. Yet those blasphemers, however loudly they now shout until they are hoarse, will not on that day have even one little word to bring against the holy Scriptures of God.

units.la: Verùm vbinam prædicta inuenitur in sacris scripturis Christi resurrectio? Act.13. Paulus resurrectionem Christi confirmat duobus testimoniis: prior ex Esaia 55. 3. 34. &c. Dabit vobis firmas illas Dauidis beneficentias: Ergo Christus resurrexit ex mortuis: In quo omnes promissiones Dei sunt etiam & amen. Nam ex ipsius vita profluit omnis vita & promissa quæcunque gratia. Posteriore ex Psalm. 16. 10. Non sines sanctum tuum sentire corruptionem. Ergo Christus resurrexit. Quod si enim non resurrexisset,corruptionem sentisset. Testimonium hoc ad asserendum resurrectionem Christi allegat quoque Petrus Act.2. 31. Sunt & alia in hunc sensum Scripturæ loca, imprimis verò illud Esaiæ 53. 8. vbi postquam prædicta est mors & passio ipsius futura, additum est continuò : At generationem ipsius ipsius quis enarraturus esset? Significat enim post resurrectionē in sempiternū eum superuicturū. Nam Christus, excitatus ex mortuis nō amplius moritur. Redierunt ergo discipuli. Id est, postquā iā crediderūt, reuersi sunt ad suos & Apostolorū & sanctorū coetum illum, ex quo nimirū sunt egressi. Nā fides in Christum tanquā caput, coniungit nos per vinculū charitatis cū corpore ipsius & membris corporis, non autē cū quibusuis promiscuē, non cū mundo illo, aut cum prophanis hominibus huius mundi.
units.tr: But where in Holy Scripture is the aforesaid resurrection of Christ to be found? Acts 13. Paul confirms the resurrection of Christ by two testimonies. The first is from Isaiah 55:3, etc.: I will give you the sure mercies of David. Therefore Christ rose from the dead, in whom all the promises of God are yea and amen. For all life, and every promised grace, flows from his life. The second is from Psalm 16:10: You will not allow your Holy One to see corruption. Therefore Christ rose. For if he had not risen, he would have seen corruption. Peter also cites this testimony to prove the resurrection of Christ, Acts 2:31. There are other passages of Scripture to the same effect, above all Isaiah 53:8, where, after his death and passion are foretold, it is immediately added: But who will declare his generation? For it signifies that after the resurrection he would live on for ever. Christ, raised from the dead, no longer dies. The disciples therefore returned. That is, now that they had come to believe, they went back to their own people, to that company of the Apostles and saints from which they had indeed gone out. For faith in Christ as the head joins us through the bond of love to his body and to the members of his body, but not indiscriminately to just anyone, not to that world, or to profane men of this world.

units.la: Maria autem. Maria videtur subsequuta Apostolos duos, Petrum & Iohannem, quibus digressis, venit ipsa ad monumentū vbi substitit lugēs ac flens: suspicabatur enim dām sublatū esse Dominum. Fletus hic ex amore quodāmodo vulgari est profectus, sed tamen non caret vitio, quia nimius, tum quia superstitiosus est. Origo peccati est ignorantia & obliuio prædictionis Domini: prædixit enim tertio die se resurrecturum ex mortuis. Pij etiam dum bene agere volunt, præcipites ferunt in difficultates & anxietates multas. Dū Christum agere volunt, peccant in Christum. Magna autem peccausa solet esse in ignorantia & obliuione verbi & promissionum Dei. Nam hauddubiè in verbo Dei, si quis ipsum habeat cognitum & in memoria fixum, medium est aduersus omnia quæ incidunt in nos mala. Verùm cur stetit flens? Cur non simul atque venit ad sepulchrum, quæsiuit an ita se res haberet, vt suspicaretur? Peccauit quidem antea, quia hanc de corpore Domini furto sublato opinionem nimis temere concepit. Peccat verò nunc, quia in illa opinione & sententia nimis est pertinax. Cauendum est ne temerè & leuiter re non prius examinata & expensa, opinionem de Deo, de Christo, de religione aliquam conpiamus, concepta enim adeo altè imprimi solet animo, vt vix inde euelli possit. Incuruauit se. Hactenus permisit Deus eam progredi in peccato suo & errore: nunc incipit eam reuocare. Nam, quæ fuit mulieris in dolore pertinacia, nisi Deus prius flexisset ipsi animum, profectō ipsa corpus suum non incuruasset vt videret num Christus in sepulchro adhuc iaceret necne. Tandem suos reuocat Dominus, vbi plus æquo iam indulserunt. affectibus suis. Prima autem gratia est, non quidem tei ipsius quam quaerunt donatio, sed commotio & inflexio animi ad eam expetendam: nam absque Dei gratia, ne volumus quidem bonum, neque expetimus bonum: Deus enim is est qui dat velle & perficere. Et conspexit duos Angelos. Postquam se incuruauit & quaesiuit, videt & invenit. Sed quid? An corpus Domini mortuum? hoc quidem quaesiuit: imo videt quod longe melius fuit, Angelos resurrectionis Domini testes. Qui accepit primam illam gratiam quaerendi, accipiet quoque secundam inveniendi, & invenit quidem saepenumero quiddam expectatione sua maius. Dei enim gratia facile vincit omnem expectationem nostram. Sed quid vidit? non tantum linteum & sudarium, quae viderunt paulo ante eam Apostoli duo, quaeque satis testari poterant non furto ablatum corpus Domini. Quod si enim furto fuisset ablatum, profecto non fuisset exutum linteo & sudario.
units.tr: But Mary. Mary seems to have followed the two Apostles, Peter and John, and after they had departed she came to the tomb, where she stood weeping and wailing, for she supposed that the Lord had been taken away. This weeping springs in a way from ordinary love, yet it is not free from fault, because it is excessive and also superstitious. The source of the sin is ignorance and forgetfulness of the Lord's prediction, for he had foretold that on the third day he would rise from the dead. Even the godly, when they wish to do well, are often carried headlong into many difficulties and anxieties. In trying to act for Christ, they sin against Christ. Great sin commonly arises from ignorance and forgetfulness of the word and promises of God. For undoubtedly, if anyone knows the word of God and keeps it fixed in memory, it is a remedy against all the evils that befall us. But why did she stand weeping? Why did she not, as soon as she came to the sepulchre, inquire whether things were as she supposed? She had sinned earlier, in conceiving too rashly the opinion that the body of the Lord had been stolen. Now she sins again, in being too obstinate in that opinion and judgment. We must take care not to form any opinion, rashly and lightly, about God, about Christ, or about religion, without first examining and weighing the matter. For an opinion once conceived is usually so deeply impressed on the mind that it can scarcely be rooted out. She stooped down. Hitherto God has allowed her to go on in her sin and error; now he begins to call her back. For the obstinacy of the woman in her grief, unless God had first bent her mind, would certainly not have made her stoop to see whether Christ still lay in the tomb or not. At last the Lord recalls his own, when they have indulged their emotions more than is right. The first grace, however, is not the granting of that which they seek, but the stirring and bending of the mind to desire it. For without the grace of God we neither will nor desire what is good; for God is he who gives both to will and to do. And she saw two angels. After she stooped down and sought, she sees and finds. But what? The dead body of the Lord? That indeed was what she sought; but she sees something far better, angels as witnesses of the Lord's resurrection. He who received the first grace of seeking will receive the second grace of finding, and often he finds something greater than he expected. For the grace of God easily surpasses all our expectation. But what did she see? Not only the linen cloth and the napkin, which the two Apostles had seen a little before, and which could sufficiently testify that the body of the Lord had not been stolen. For if it had been stolen, certainly it would not have been stripped of the linen cloth and the napkin.

units.la: Nota igitur, Maria praelata est Apostolis Petro & Iohanni: imo vero omnes mulieres quotquot ad sepulchrum egressae sunt, eo ipso nomine praelatae sunt omnibus Apostolis: omnes enim viderunt Angelos & audiverunt testificantes eos de resurrectione Christi. Dum paulo diligentius considero hanc historiam, video duas mulierum istarum praerogativas. Primam, quod revelatio resurrectionis ipsis primum omnium facta fit. Secundam quod revelatio haec data sit per Angelorum ministerium. Utraque hac re inferiores fuerunt Apostoli, quibus neque primum revelatio facta est, neque per Angelos facta est, sed per mulieres tanquam testes secundarias.
units.tr: Note, then, that Mary was preferred to the Apostles Peter and John; indeed all the women who went out to the sepulchre were, by that very fact, preferred to all the Apostles. For they all saw the angels and heard them bearing witness to the resurrection of Christ. As I consider this history a little more carefully, I see two privileges of these women. The first is that the revelation of the resurrection was made to them first of all. The second is that this revelation was given through the ministry of angels. In both respects the Apostles were inferior, for the revelation was not made to them first, nor was it made through angels, but through women, as secondary witnesses.

units.la: Postremo non est hoc praetereundum, quod narratur de sessione duorum angelorum: alter sedet ibi, ubi caput Domini positum fuit, alter vero ubi pedes: hac ipsa sessione sua docuerunt ac demonstrarunt locum in quo caput positum fuit, & locum in quo pedes erant positi pariter vacuum fuisse, ac proinde a mortuis iam resurrexisse Dominum. Deus quos mittit testes ad suos instruendos sic disponit, ut omnibus modis inserviant docendis atque edificandis suis, non tantum sermone, sed etiam habitu ipso corporis & gestu. Nihil enim in hoc negotio toto temere accidit. Qui etiam dixerunt. Non tantum vidit Angelos, sed etiam quoque loquentes audiit: Atque hoc est incrementum gratiæ, Custodes viderunt& perterriti sunt, sed nihil plane audiuerunt. Omnibus modis suis consulit Deus, & per omnes sensus eorum fecit ac consolatur per aspectum, per auditum, pertinet, totos denique implet gratia sua. Sed quid auditurus? Vocem quidem corripientium & castigationum moderatum illum fletum suum, sed vocem tamen miserentium. Nam nō sine συμπαθεία quadam accipiet vox hæc angelorum. Συμπαθὴς autem, & vt sic compassio fuit, quia etsi peccauit Maria in dolore nimio ac immoderato: tamen dolor ex amore extitit ineffabili. Miseretur autem Dominus, etiam cum ex amore dolent supra modum, nunquam etiam absque iusta doloris causa. Sed audiuit mulier? non vocem illam quam mulieres primò ingressæ sunt monumentum audiuerunt tegelo hac, nempe, Ne metuite: Maria enim dolore stupefacta videtur vt obduruerit aduersus omnē metum & terribilem quemcunque aspectum, fuit tum Angelorum, qui in candidis vestibus fulgurantibus inducti in sepulchro consideruunt: non quinquam, vocē audiuit, verum hanc, Quid fles? Flebat vehementer. Qui autem dolent ac plorant supra modum, illi opus habent vt sistatur fletus eorum ac ploransistit autem Deus fletum suorum, qui ipsum diligunt cum in fletu suo peccant. Beati qui luget, quoniam consolationem accipient. Luctus autem noster in hac vita est plane expers omnis peccati, vel enim in excessu vel in defectu. Attamen beati prædicantur qui agent. Denique quid audiuit Maria? Non quidem vocem quam secundus ille ordo mulierum audiuit, Quid quæritis viuentem inter mortuos? hac enim paulò acerbior castigatio fuit. Commeritum autem Maria est castigationem eandem istam, vel certè huic similem aliquam. Peccauit in obliuione prædictionis Domini, vt & ille peccauit in dolore & inconsto & nimio. Attamen non audiuit eam vocem quam illæ superiores, sed hanc, Quid ploras? Dominus enim non tam quid merita sit respexit, quàm quia re opus haberet. In summo autem dolore opus
units.tr: Lastly, we must not pass over what is related about the sitting of the two angels: one sits where the head of the Lord had been laid, the other where the feet had been. By this very posture they taught and showed that the place where the head had lain and the place where the feet had lain were equally empty, and that therefore the Lord had already risen from the dead. God, in sending witnesses to instruct his people, so arranges them that they serve in every way to teach and edify his people, not only by speech but also by their very bearing and gesture. For nothing in this whole business happens by chance. They also said. She not only saw the angels but also heard them speaking. And this is an increase of grace: the guards saw and were terrified, but they heard nothing at all. God provides for his people in every way, and through all their senses he comforts them: by sight, by hearing, and so on; in short, he fills them wholly with his grace. But what was she to hear? Indeed a voice of rebuke and correction, yet tempered, and a voice of pity for her weeping. For this voice of the angels is received not without a certain sympatheia [συμπαθεία]. And it was a compassion of this kind, sympathēs [συμπαθής], because although Mary sinned in her excessive and immoderate grief, nevertheless the grief sprang from an ineffable love. The Lord, moreover, shows pity even when people grieve beyond measure out of love, yet never without a just cause for grief. But did the woman hear? Not that voice which the women who first entered the tomb had heard, namely Do not fear. For Mary, stunned by grief, seems to have grown hardened against all fear and every frightening sight, namely of the angels clothed in white garments, shining, who sat in the tomb. Not indeed that voice, but this one: Why are you weeping? She was weeping bitterly. Those who grieve and lament beyond measure need that their weeping be checked, and God does check the weeping of his people, who love him, when they sin in their weeping. Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall receive comfort. Our mourning in this life, however, is never entirely free of sin, for it is either in excess or in defect. Yet those who mourn are pronounced blessed. Finally, what did Mary hear? Not indeed the voice which the second group of women heard, Why do you seek the living among the dead? For that was a somewhat sharper rebuke. Mary deserved the same rebuke, or certainly something similar to it. She sinned by forgetting the Lord's prediction, as well as by grieving unsteadily and excessively. Yet she did not hear that voice which the others heard, but this one: Why are you weeping? For the Lord looked not so much at what she deserved as at what she needed. And in her supreme grief she needed comfort.

units.la: Ad Mariæ affectum vox Angeli componitur. habebat consolatione. Dominus itaque qui arundinem quassatam non frangit, neque linum fumigans extinguit, eam est cõsolatus. Meritum autem peccati tectum eit per eam, nempe Christum quem tantopere dilexit, & cuius causa tam vehementer doluit. Sustulerunt Domi-num. Vt prius nihil territa est visis illis Angelis, ita nihil nunc est cömota auditis iis: ita enim oppletus est animus dolore, vt nullus potuerit in eo esse locus pauori. vt oculi fuerunt lachrymis obfuscati, ita aures ei fuerunt dolore praepeditae. Sed quaerat quis cur tantopere expetiuerit sibi mortuum illud Domini corpus? Quidnam eo fieri voluit? Profecto ipsa postea indicat cum dicit, Ego eum tollam. A mortuo Domini corpore non est passa se diuelli: quàm igitur aegre diuulsa est à viuo? Hoc arguit amorem Domini ineffabilem, neque naturalem aliquem, vt loquimur, duntaxat affectum, sed supernaturalem, excitatum ex sensu quodam amoris Domini ipsius, qui prior eum dilexit. Vtcunque autem alias peccauit, profecto amorem hunc nō possum vertere illi vitio, quem Dominus ipse, vt video, acceptauit, & propter quem, vel potius propter Christum, quem dilexit, non venit in rationem peccati illud ipsius in dolore & nimio & iniusto. Dū de hac muliere diligentius cogito, video in ea vehementia omnia, vehementè amore, vehementè dolorem, vehemes desiderium, adeo vt cogar in violetis illis eam numerare, qui vim afferunt regno caelorum, ac rapiunt ipsum: de quibus Matthaei 11. Et re ipsa quidem vi Christum rapuisse videtur eumq; praeripuisse quodam modo omnibus aliis, non modo mulieribus, sed Apostolis etiam ipsis, nam Mariae primum omnium se videndum obtulit Dominus.
units.tr: The angel's voice was suited to Mary's feeling; she had it for consolation. So the Lord, who does not break a bruised reed or quench a smoking flax, comforted her. Yet the guilt of her sin was covered by her love for Christ, whom she loved so greatly and for whose sake she grieved so intensely. They have taken away the Lord. Just as she was not frightened at the sight of those angels, so now she was not moved by hearing them. Her mind was so filled with grief that there was no room in it for fear. As her eyes were clouded with tears, so her ears were blocked by sorrow. But someone may ask why she so earnestly desired the dead body of the Lord. What did she want to do with it? Surely she herself later shows this when she says, I will take him away. She did not allow herself to be parted from the dead body of the Lord; how reluctantly, then, was she parted from the living one! This shows her love for the Lord to be beyond words. It was not merely a natural feeling, as we say, but a supernatural one, kindled by a sense of the Lord's own love, which had loved her first. However she sinned in other respects, I cannot count this love as a fault, since the Lord himself, as I see, accepted it, and on account of it, or rather on account of Christ whom she loved, her excessive and unjust grief was not reckoned as sin. As I think more carefully about this woman, I see in her everything in its intensity: intense love, intense sorrow, intense longing. So I am compelled to number her among the violent who take the kingdom of heaven by force, of whom we read in Matthew 11. And indeed she seems to have seized Christ by force and to have snatched him, in a sense, from all others, not only women but even the Apostles themselves; for the Lord first presented himself to Mary to be seen before anyone else.

units.la: Vehementia omnia in Maria Magdalene. Violenti rapiunt Christum & regnum caelorum.
units.tr: The intensity of everything in Mary Magdalene. The violent seize Christ and the kingdom of heaven.

units.la: Marci 16.
units.tr: Mark 16.

units.la: 9 Quum autem resurrexisset Iesus, mane primo die hebdomadis, apparuit primum Mariae Magdalenae, ex qua eiecerat septem daemonia.
units.tr: 9 Now when Jesus was risen early on the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.

units.la: 10 Illa profecta annunciauit iis qui cum ipso fuerant, lugentibus ac flentibus.
units.tr: 10 She went and told them that had been with him, as they mourned and wept.

units.la: 11 Illi vero quum audiissent eum viuere, & conspectum fuisse ab ea, non crediderunt.
units.tr: 11 And they, when they had heard that he was alive and had been seen of her, believed not.

units.la: Iohannis 20.
units.tr: John 20.

units.la: 14 Et cum haec dixisset, convertit se retrorsum, conspexitque Iesum stantem: nec sciebat Iesum esse.
units.tr: 14 And when she had thus said, she turned herself back and saw Jesus standing, and knew not that it was Jesus.

units.la: 15 Dicit ei Iesus, Maria quid fles? quem quaeris? Illa putans olitorem esse, dicit ei, Domine, si tu eum abstulisti, dicito mihi ubi posueris eum, & ego eum tollam.
units.tr: 15 Jesus saith unto her, Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.

units.la: 16 Dicit ei Iesus, Maria. Illa se convertens dicit ei, Rabboni, quod dicitur praeceptor.
units.tr: 16 Jesus saith unto her, Mary. She turned herself and saith unto him, Rabboni; which is to say, Master.

units.la: 17 Dicit ei Iesus, Noli me tangere: nondum enim ascendi ad Patrem meum: sed proficiscere ad fratres meos, et dic eis: ascendo enim ad Patrem meum & Patrem vestrum, & Deum meum, & Deum vestrum.
units.tr: 17 Jesus saith unto her, Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father; but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God.

units.la: 18 Venit Maria Magdalene annuntians discipulis quod vidisset Dominum, & quod ea sibi dixisset.
units.tr: 18 Mary Magdalene came and told the disciples that she had seen the Lord, and that he had spoken these things unto her.

units.la: Videtur hic gestus parum decorus, nam oportuit loquenti Angelo patientem ac reverentem aurem accommodare. Sed hoc, ut alia, ascribo dolori quo sic obstupefacta est mulier, ut quid ageret nihil penitus habuerit, prae Christo nihili fecerit omnia, quae vel vidit ipsa, vel audivit. Non dubito etiam quin secreta aliqua vis procedat a praesenti Domino, & mulierem converterit, & Angelis silentium iniunxerit. Christus enim Dominus est & hominum & Angelorum. Ipso praesente conversum sese homines, ac sistunt se coram eo, silent etiam Angeli. Iohannes Baptista ipso praesente siluit. Qui habet sponsam, sponsus est, amicus autem sponsi stat, & audit eum, gaudio gaudet propter vocem sponsi. Conspexit quidem Iesum stantem. Antea quidem conspexit Angelos Domini aduentantis tanquam eius praecursores: nunc autem eum conspicit ipsum Dominum. Qui quaerit Dominum,
units.tr: This gesture seems rather unseemly, for she ought to have given a patient and reverent ear to the angel as he spoke. But I ascribe this, as other things, to the sorrow by which the woman was so stunned that she had no idea what to do, and in the presence of Christ she made nothing of everything she had either seen or heard. I do not doubt either that some hidden power went forth from the Lord who was present, turning her round and imposing silence on the angels. For Christ is the Lord both of men and of angels. When he is present, men turn to him and stand before him, and the angels also fall silent. John the Baptist kept silent when Christ was present. He who has the bride is the bridegroom, but the friend of the bridegroom stands and hears him, and rejoices greatly because of the bridegroom's voice. She indeed saw Jesus standing. Before, she had seen the angels of the Lord who were coming, as his forerunners; now she sees the Lord himself. She who seeks the Lord

units.la: 13. Prima apparitio Christi post resurrectionem, nempe Mariae Magdalenae.
units.tr: 13. The first appearance of Christ after the resurrection, namely to Mary Magdalene.

units.la: Iohan. 3.29. Maria videt Iesum stantem. tandem conspecturus est ipsum Dominum. Medio autem loco obuij ei fiunt nuncij, precursores & legati, quos vult nos Dominus audire, tanquam ministros suos & dispensatores mysteriorum Dei. Tandem autem vel incogitantibus nobis superuenit ipse Dominus. Dixi supra Mariam & reliquas etiam mulieres, eo quod Angelos viderint, prælatas esse Apostolis omnibus. Nunc video Mariam prælatam esse & Apostolis & mulieribus aliis omnibus, hoc ipso quòd Dominum prima omnium cospexerit post resurrectionē ipsius. Prima enim vidit eum teste Marco: Arguit autem hoc Mariam imprimis & plusquam cæteros omnes, desiderio Domini tactam fuisse: priores enim desiderio Domini absentis, priores
units.tr: John 3.29. Mary sees Jesus standing. At last she is to see the Lord himself. Meanwhile, messengers, forerunners and envoys meet her, whom the Lord wishes us to hear as his ministers and stewards of the mysteries of God. At last, however, the Lord himself comes upon us when we are not thinking of him. I said above that Mary, and the other women too because they had seen the angels, were preferred to all the Apostles. Now I see that Mary was preferred both to the Apostles and to all the other women, in that she was the first of all to see the Lord after his resurrection. For she saw him first, according to Mark. This shows that Mary was touched more than all the others, and first, by desire for the Lord; for those who first longed for the absent Lord will be first to behold him present.

units.la: futuri sunt aspectu præsentis. Mulier, quid fles? Antea audiut Angelos, nunc audit vocem ipsius Domini: Antea vidit Dominum, nunc audit loquentem Dominum. Vide incrementum gratiæ. Sed quid audit? Mulier, quid fles? Alloquitur primum eam, vt ignotus ignotam, mulierem, non Mariam compellans. Item non dicit, Scio equidem te flere mea causa: scio te me quærere. Ergo prima facie non alloquitur eam familiariter, sed suspensam aliquandiu tenet eo fine vt gaudium ipsius tandem maius, plenissimumque euaderet. Nam Dominus etiam suos non vitur familiariter aliquanto tempore; eminus eos intuetur, eminus alloquitur. Id quod fit quantisper hic viuimus. Nunc enim per fidem incedimus, non autem per aspectum: & videmus in speculo & per ænigma. Hoc autem ideo facit vt suo repore cū dabitur eū presente cōuenire, eius præsentia & aspectu illo longè suauissimo, maiori cum gaudio & voluptate fruamur. Vult enim Dominus exerceri in hac vita fidem, patientiam, desiderium nostrum. Quanto autem maius est desiderium Domini absentis in hac vita, tanto maius auctiusque est gaudiū nostrum, ex præsenti in altera. Et nesciebat quòd Iesus. Ignoratiam istam ascribo stupori mulieris & præstrictis quasi oculis, vel dolore nimio, vel certè secreta aliqua vi & efficacia Domini, qui noluit se statim ab ea de facie cognosci, sed eam primùm probare & tentare voluit. Mariæ autem exemplo hoc obseruo offerentem sese nobis videndum Dominum in Euangelio suo, non statim à nobis cognosci: nam non minor caligo occupat nunc oculos mentis nostræ, quàm fuit ea quæ tum occupauit oculos Mariæ corporeos. Illa putans quòd hortulanus esset. Vt non potuit cognitum Dominum de facie, ita neque de voce eius vt oculi, sic aures quoque mulieri fuerunt obstructæ. Neque enim ista eius ignorantia qua Dominum præsentem & loquentem non cognouit, ascribenda est vel potius, vt sic dicam, faciei Domini, vel dissimulatæ & non vocis, verùm mulieris ipsius constitutioni, siue ea caligine ex dolore fuerit, siue ex virtute quadam Dei extraordinaria, præstringenti ipsi oculos. Tantùm hoc obseruo, Nos vt ad tempus executionis ad faciem Domini conspectam, ita ad temporis dispersionem obescimus ad vocem Domini auditam, sensibus nostris interea occupatis, imò ferè absorptis ab aliis terrestribus his ac mundanis.
units.tr: Woman, why do you weep? Before, she heard angels; now she hears the very voice of the Lord. Before, she saw the Lord; now she hears the Lord speaking. See the increase of grace. But what does she hear? Woman, why do you weep? He first addresses her as a stranger would address a stranger, calling her "woman," not Mary. Nor does he say, "I know indeed that you weep on my account; I know that you seek me." So at first sight he does not address her familiarly, but keeps her in suspense for a while, so that her joy at last might become greater and fuller. For the Lord also does not treat his own familiarly for some time; he looks upon them from afar and speaks to them from afar. This happens for as long as we live here. For now we walk by faith, not by sight, and we see in a mirror and in an enigma. He does this so that, when the time comes and we are given to meet him present, we may enjoy his presence and that most sweet sight with greater joy and delight. For the Lord wills that our faith, patience and longing be exercised in this life. And the greater our longing for the absent Lord in this life, the greater and more abundant will be our joy in his presence in the next. And she did not know that it was Jesus. I ascribe this ignorance to the woman's astonishment and to eyes as if dazzled, either by excessive grief or certainly by some hidden power and efficacy of the Lord, who did not wish to be recognised by her at once, but wished first to test and try her. From Mary's example I observe this: the Lord, offering himself to be seen in his Gospel, is not recognised by us at once. For no less a darkness now clouds the eyes of our mind than that which then clouded Mary's bodily eyes. Supposing that he was the gardener. As she could not recognise the Lord by his face, so neither could she by his voice; her ears, like her eyes, were closed to her. Nor is this ignorance of hers, by which she did not recognise the Lord when he was present and speaking, to be ascribed to the Lord's face, or rather, so to speak, to his disguised face and not to his voice, but to the woman's own condition, whether that darkness came from grief or from some extraordinary power of God dazzling her eyes. I observe only this: just as we are blinded to the time of execution when we see the face of the Lord, so we are blinded to the passing of time when we hear the voice of the Lord, our senses meanwhile being occupied, indeed almost swallowed up, by other earthly and worldly things.

units.la: Dialogus, Maria. Alloquitur eam nunc vna tantùm vocali selecta ea ac familiari, cùm de nomine compellet, vt pastor ouem suam. Nam pastor bonus, nominatim oues suas ad se vocat. Vocatio hæc quoque efficax: nam statim mulieri, aures, oculi, sensus deniq; omnes aperti sunt. Postquam nos Deus iam aliquandiu alloquutus est, tanquam sibi minus notos voce quasi perceptos, neque etiam adeo in nobis efficaci, tandem alloquitur nos efficaciter tanquam notos, & de nomine, & de corde, denique de actionibus omnibus. Sic Samaritanam illam primùm alloquutus est tanquam ignotam, deinde tanquam notam de actionibus & præsentibus præteritæ vitæ. Quare ne pigeat Dominum loquentem audire, etiamsi non statim per verbum suum in nobis efficax sit: nam vel vnica voce tandem, qua ipsi visum nos compellare, familiari videlicet ac efficaci, rem perficere conficere, nòsque efficaciter vocare. Conuersa illa dei, Rabboni. Hactenus Dominus vna voce mulierem compellauit: mulier vna vicissim voce respondit, & ea quàm selecta ac familiari, nempe qua decuit ouem respondere Pastori suo, vel discipulam magistro: voce denique efficacis vocationis indice. Nam tum demum efficax vocatio Domini, vt vt Dominus nos vocat, si nos vicissim respondeamus: vt, inquam, Dominus nos
units.tr: Dialogue: Mary. He now addresses her with a single voice, one that is chosen and familiar, when he calls her by name, as a shepherd calls his sheep. For the good shepherd calls his own sheep to himself by name. This call is also effective, for at once the woman's ears, eyes and indeed all her senses are opened. After God has for some time spoken to us, as to those less known to him, by a voice that is perceived but not yet effective in us, at last he addresses us effectively, as those known to him, both by name and by heart, and finally by all our actions. So he first addressed the Samaritan woman as a stranger, and then as one known to him, from the facts of her past life and present. Therefore let it not weary us to hear the Lord speaking, even if his word is not at once effective in us. For at last, by that one single voice with which he deigns to address us, familiar and effective, he accomplishes the matter and effectively calls us. Her turning to him: Rabboni. Hitherto the Lord has addressed the woman with one voice; in turn the woman answers with one voice, and a chosen and familiar one, namely the kind that becomes a sheep answering its shepherd, or a disciple answering her master. In short, it is a voice that marks an effective calling. For the calling of the Lord becomes effective only when, as the Lord calls us as his sheep known by name, we in turn answer him lovingly and reverently, as sheep in the Lord's fold or as pupils in his school.

units.la: Ingenium nostrum etiam in Domini schola. vocat, tanquam oues suas de nomine ipso notas, nos vi- cissim tanquam oues in ouili Domini, vel discipulin schola ipsius amanter ac reuerenter respondemus. Obseruamus hoc loco, quòd, quantisper Dominus nos tanquam ignotos alloquitur, tantisper nos ei tanquā ignoto alicui respondemus: vt discamus nihil posse nos nisi ipse nos praeueniat gratia sua: nisi ipse nos prior diligat, non posse nos eum diligere: nisi ipse nos prior cognoscat, non posse nos eum cognoscere: At nunc, inquit Paulus, cum cognoscatis Deum: Tum per correctionem subiungit: Imo, inquit, cum cognitisitis ab eo. Quo significat non posse nos cognoscere Dominum, nisi ipse prior nos cognoscat. Ne me tangito. Videtur hic Mariam accurrisse ista tim, vt exciperet vlnis & amplecteretur Dominū: Dominū vero subterfugisse ipsius amplexus, hac voce eā coercès, Ne me tangito: cui ratione suā annectit, hanc nimirum, Nondum enim ascendi ad Patrem meum. Res mira est, quod adeo nunc fugiat amplexus Mariae, cūm tamen paulò post, mulieres in vrbem redeuntes passus sit amplecti pedes suos, seséque ad pedes suos proiectas, adorare : item discipulos tangere se ac contrectare manibus: denique Thomam ipse inuitauerit, vt digitum inferret in cicatrices manuum ac lateris ipsius. Et haec ipsa quoque facta sunt ante ascensionem ipsius ad coelos, vt haec responsio videatur non satis valere, aut vim habere prohibendi Mariam ab amplexibus Domini. Respondeo primùm ex ratione subnexa à Domino, deinde ex mandato quod paulò post datum est Mariae. Rationis additae hic sensus est, quasi dicat, Maria, video te nimis addictam corporali praesentiae meae: nondum tempus amplectendi me aduenit: expecta paulisper donec ascendero ad Patrem meum, & in caelis gloriosus fuero. Tum quidem licebit tibi quantum voles me fide & spirituali amplexu complecti, mihiqué in aeternum adhaerescere. Addicta enim fuit magis quàm par erat praesentiae Domini corporali, cogitauitque sibi cum Christo etiamnum viuendum esse in terris his, post ipsius resurrectionem, sicut iam antea cum eo suauiter vixit. Christus igitur non passus est se tangi ab ea, donec meliora docuisset mulierem, & admonuisset eam de praesentia illa sua spirituali tactu {a}tactu spipituali, de vita denique illa sibi in cælis, non in terris, in posterum transfigenda. Posteaquam eam hæc docuisset, tum quidem ab ea vna cum aliis mulieribus passus est se tangi & contrectari, vt postea videbimus. Hæc vna est responsio. Altera colligitur ex legatione illa mulieri paulo post demandata, animus enim fuit mulierem ablegare ad discipulos cum mandatis: ideoque nelegatio hæc ab eo destinata impediretur vllis amplexibus, non passus est eam se amplecti prius, quàm legationem illam obiisset. Atque hæc altera est responsio ad propositam quæstionem. Quæ autem ex his quæ diximus obseruamus, hæc sunt, Paulus profesus suum illum in Christum amorem, ait, Coshringit nos charitas Christi: tum rationem addit, vt qui cum mortui essemus pro nobis mortuus sit: quasi dicat, Æquum est vt eum, qui nos tam vehementer amauit vicissim amemus. Postea docet quònam pacto sit illam suam erga Christum charitatem ostensurus, nempe per eandem illam vitam, quam beneficio mortis Christi accepit. Vinimus, inquit, ei, qui pro nobis mortuus est. Postremò definiens vitam illam quam victus fit impositum Christo: Posthac, inquit, neminem secundum carnem cognoscimus, id est, secundum carnalia ista terrestria ac peritura, quæ homines tanti faciunt: quin potius secundum spiritualem illam generationem, quà regenerationem vocant, & spiritualia illa, quæ eam comitantur, cognoscam homines. Addit, quod maius est, imò si Christum ipsum cognouimus secundum carnem, non amplius sic cognoscimus eum. Christum in terris humiliatum comitata sunt etiam carnalia quædam, atque ita quidem fieri oportuit. Dicit itaque Paulus distinguturum se inter Christum humiliatum, & Christum glorificatum: neq; amplius Christum iam glorificatum in cælis, in terribus & carnalibus his, quæ comitabantur necessario humiliatum eum in terris, se agnituum. Hæc de Paulo: cum eo nunc comparemus Mariam. Similis quidem & fuit Maria in charitate, atque in officiis charitatis: at in cultu Domini nondum Paulo similis: nam Maria adhuc Christum agnouit secundum carnem, & (vt sic dicam) carnaliter nimium de eo cogitauit: vt videas ipsius exemplo etiam eos, qui alioqui diligunt Dominum, errare in ipsius cultu, ac carnaliter & crassè nimis de eo cogitare. Cuiusmodi est Papisticus iste cultus hodierno die, nempe carnalis ac crassus, sapiens crassum illum ipsorum ac sensum carnalem. Neque enim Dominum in crassa imagine tantum colunt, sed monstrosam nescio quam praesentiam sibi fingunt corporis & sanguinis Domini in Sacramento Coenae. Verum cum Dominus non acceptat Mariae carnalem & crassum hunc cultum, quae tamen aliàs ipsi tantopere placuit, quomodo acceptúrus est tam crassum & carnale cultum e manu eorum, qui iam millies commonefacti sunt, se non docere nisi doctrinas, quae sunt inventa hominum? Maria quidem audiuit libenter docentem meliora ac rectiora. At isti, qua suntanimi obstinatione, ne fi quis hoc eos doceat millies, tamen non resipiscunt. Deinde observa quanta cum celeritate velit Dominus expediri negotium à se quodcunque commissum cuiquam, quum nolit mitsum, vel etiâ mittendum à se haerere in amplexibus cuiusquam, tantisperdum negotium expedierit: nolit in itinere, ne verbo quidem obuium quenquam salutare, si ea ratione mora aliqua nectatur. Servus Prophetae missus ab eo ad Schunamitidem, prohibitus est ne in itinere vel salutaret quenquam, vel etiam salutanti eum cuiquam respondet. Idem similiter prohibitum est septuaginta illis discipulis ab ipso Domino. Nolit denique nos in itinere, vel in dextram, vel in sinistram, vel etiam retro oculum flectere, siquidem id futurum sit nobis impedimento.
units.tr: Our wit also in the Lord's school. We observe here that, for as long as the Lord addresses us as strangers, for so long we answer him as one who is a stranger to us, so that we may learn that we cannot do anything unless he anticipates us by his grace; unless he first loves us, we cannot love him; unless he first knows us, we cannot know him. But now, says Paul, since you know God; and then by way of correction he adds: Or rather, he says, since you have been known by him. By this he signifies that we cannot know the Lord unless he first knows us. Do not touch me. Mary seems to have rushed forward to embrace the Lord and clasp him in her arms, but the Lord avoided her embrace, restraining her with these words, Do not touch me, to which he attaches his reason, namely, For I have not yet ascended to my Father. It is a remarkable thing that he now shuns Mary's embrace, when a little later he allowed the women returning to the city to embrace his feet and to fall at his feet and worship him; likewise he let the disciples touch and handle him with their hands; and finally he invited Thomas to put his finger into the wounds of his hands and side. And these things also happened before his ascension into heaven, so that this answer seems not to be sufficient, or to have force to forbid Mary from embracing the Lord. I answer first from the reason added by the Lord, and then from the command given to Mary a little later. The sense of the added reason is as if he were saying: Mary, I see that you are too much attached to my bodily presence; the time for embracing me has not yet come. Wait a little until I have ascended to my Father and have been glorified in heaven. Then indeed you will be free to embrace me as much as you wish, by faith and spiritual embrace, and to cling to me for ever. For she was more attached to the bodily presence of the Lord than was fitting, and she thought that she was still to live on earth with Christ after his resurrection, as she had sweetly lived with him before. Christ therefore did not allow himself to be touched by her until he had taught the woman better things and reminded her of that spiritual presence of his, which is touched by faith, and of the life that she was to live in future in heaven, not on earth. After he had taught her these things, then indeed he allowed himself to be touched and handled by her, together with the other women, as we shall see later. This is the first answer. The second is drawn from the errand given to the woman a little later. For his intention was to send her away to the disciples with a message; so that this errand, which he had appointed, should not be hindered by any embraces, he did not allow her to embrace him before she had carried out that errand. This is the second answer to the question proposed. As for what we observe from what we have said, these are the points. Paul, declaring his love for Christ, says, The love of Christ constrains us, and he adds the reason: because one died for all, therefore all died; as if to say, it is right that we in turn love him who loved us so intensely. Afterwards he teaches how he is to show that love of his for Christ, namely through the same life which he received by the benefit of Christ's death. We live, he says, for him who died for us. Lastly, defining that life which is laid upon those who have been conquered by Christ, he says: Henceforth we know no one according to the flesh, that is, according to those carnal, earthly and perishable things which men value so highly; rather, we know men according to that spiritual generation, which they call regeneration, and the spiritual things that accompany it. He adds what is greater: nay, even if we have known Christ according to the flesh, we no longer know him so. Certain carnal things accompanied Christ while he was humbled on earth, and indeed it had to be so. Paul therefore says that he will distinguish between Christ humbled and Christ glorified, and that he will no longer recognise the Christ now glorified in heaven by those earthly and carnal things which necessarily accompanied him while he was humbled on earth. So much for Paul; now let us compare Mary with him. Mary was indeed similar to him in love and in the duties of love, but not yet similar to Paul in the worship of the Lord, for Mary still knew Christ according to the flesh and, so to speak, thought of him too carnally. From her example you may see that even those who otherwise love the Lord go astray in his worship and think of him in a carnal and too crude way. Such is the Papistical worship of today, carnal and crude, savouring of that crude and carnal sense of theirs. For they do not merely worship the Lord in a crude image, but they imagine some monstrous presence, I know not what, of the body and blood of the Lord in the sacrament of the Lord's Supper. But if the Lord does not accept this carnal and crude worship from Mary, though otherwise it greatly pleased him, how will he accept such crude and carnal worship from the hands of those who have been warned a thousand times that they teach only the doctrines which are the inventions of men? Mary indeed listened gladly to one who taught better and more correct things. But these men, with their obstinate minds, do not repent, even if someone teaches them a thousand times. Next, observe with what speed the Lord wishes the business committed to anyone by him to be dispatched; he does not wish the one sent, or even the one about to be sent, by him to linger in anyone's embraces as long as the business is not finished. He does not wish one on the road to greet anyone even with a word, if some delay might be caused by this. The servant of the prophet, sent by him to the Shunammite woman, was forbidden to greet anyone on the way, or even to answer anyone who greeted him. The same thing was likewise forbidden to the seventy disciples by the Lord himself. Finally, he does not wish us on the road to turn our eye to right or left, or even backward, if that would be an impediment to us.

units.la: Paulus missus à Deo tanquam Apostolus, ita cucurrit & contendit ad metam, ut quae à tergo erant oblitus, scopum versus ferretur ad palmam supernae vocationis Dei in Christo Iesu.
units.tr: Paul, sent by God as an apostle, so ran and strove toward the goal, forgetting what lay behind him and pressing on toward the mark, for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus.

units.la: Sed proficiscere ad fratres. Sequitur negotium illud à Domino Mariae creditum. Diximus autea non vno modo mulieres viris, & Apostolis ipsis praelatas esse à Domino. 1. Quod revelatio iis sit facta resurrectionis Domini. 2. Quod per Angelos non per homines facta sit. At Maria & Apostolis & mulieribus aliis praelata est. 1. Quod Dominum post resurrectionem prima omnium conspexerit. 2. Quod revelatio ipsi primum facta sit ascensionis Domini ad caelos; quae quidem ulterior & superior quae dam
units.tr: But go to my brothers. There follows the commission which the Lord entrusted to Mary. I said earlier that the Lord set women above men and above the apostles themselves in more than one way. (1) Because the revelation of the Lord's resurrection was made to them; (2) because it was made through angels and not through men. Mary, however, was set above both the apostles and the other women: (1) because she was the first of all to see the Lord after his resurrection; (2) because the revelation of the Lord's ascension to the heavens was first made to her, which is a further and higher degree of his glorification;

units.la: Carnales de Christo glorificato cogitationes. dâ fuit glorisicationis Christi gradus.3. Quòd preco quasi facta sit & ministra ascensionis Domini ad alios missa, etiam ad Apostolos ipsos. Magna quidem fuit hæc gratia, qua mulieres honorauit Dominus præ viris, præsertim autem Mariam, quam Dominus possessam aliquando à septem dæmoniis, hoc est, ad inferos vsque detrusam nunc incælos erigit, supraque omnes alios euehit. Nam maximè humiliatus quisque eo quo visum est Domino tempore maximè exaltatur. Profitescere, inquit, ad fratres meos. Hic impletur proculdubiò Scriptura ea quæ habetur Ps.22.23. Annunciabo nomen tuum fratribus meis. Apostolus ad Hebræos huius appellationis tam blandæ ac familiaris causam designat, dum dicit, Et qui sanctificat, & qui sanctificantur ex vno sunt omnes: nempe communi natura humana: Quam ob causam non erubescit fratres ipsos vocare, dicens, Annunciabo nomen tuum fratribus meis. Ergo communio eiusdem naturæ, nempe humanæ, facit, vt fratres nos cognominet, neque erubescat nos fratres suos vocare etiam iam glorificatus, & in tantam sublimitatem euectus, nos, inquam, miseros peccatores, qui tanto ab eo distamus interuallo. Si quis, licet terræ filius, in superiorem aliquem locum euectus sit, tum quidem ei vilescit pater pauperculus, mater pauperacula, pauperculi & egeni cognati omnes. At Christo etiam glorificato, non vilescimus nos, si Christus nobis non vilescat. Non pudet cum nostri, nisi nos prius pudeat eius. Non abnegat nos coram Patre suo, priusquam nos abnegauerimus eum coram hominibus. Sed videamus ipsa legationis verba: Dic iis, Ascendo ad Patrem meum. Ad Illæ mulieres ab Angelis acceperunt reuelationem resurrectionis Domini cum Apostolis communicandam. At Maria ab ipso Domino accipit reuelationem ascensionis Domini, qui excellentior quidem est gloriæ ipsius gradus. Ministri siue Angeli, siue homines à Domino missi, reuelant de eo aliquid, sæpe etiam magna. At vero Dominus ipse, cùm ad nos propius accedit, maiorem lucem ac reuelationem secum affert, quàm quæ allata fuit à ministris. Sic in primo aduentu maiorem reuelationem attulit, quàm quæ allata est ante cum vel à Prophetis, vel ab Iohanne Baptista. Sic in secundo aduentu redibit cum maiori clarioríque lucc ac reuelatione, quàm vnquam antehac visa est vel allata, Difficulter nunc credimus etiam paruis: at tunc magna videbimus, & quæ nunquam oculus vidit, vel auris audiuit, vel ingressa sunt in cor hominis. Sed expendamus verba: Ascendo, inquit. Verbum hoc subinnuit desertionem aliquam fratrum & discipulorum, quos post se relicturus fuit in mundo, ac proinde oportuit illud triste esse & ingratū discipulis. Sed quod addit postremo, ad Patrem vestrum, Deum vestrum, id magis eos recreare oportuit & consolari: importat enim non tantum ipsi, quòd ascendat, sed etiam discipulis suis: cùm discipulis quoque gloria illa paterna communicanda fuerit. Nam hæc causa est cur communicetur nobis gloria Dei, quod nimirum Christus iam ascenderit ad Patrem nostrū & Deum nostrum. Atque hic quidem ordo est quo communicatur nobis gloria Dei. Primùm Christus ipse post ascensum suum in cælos, implebitur omni gloria: deinde nos ex eius plenitudine accipimus omnes. Ordinis autem ratio est, quia primùm Deus est Pater Christi & Deus Christi. Ideo gloria primogenito prius communicanda est: deinde per Christum & primogenitum est Pater noster, & Deus noster: est autem, vt hoc dicamus obiter, Pater Christi, vt Christus est Dei filius ab æterno à Patre genitus. Est verò Deus Christi, vt est homo in tempore factus. Hæc igitur verba inferunt duas Christi naturas in vna persona existentes, diuinam & humanam. Iam vt in summa dicam, oportuit nuncium hoc de Christi ascensione in cælos efficax in discipulis esse ad ipsos supra omnes cælos euehendos, saltem quoad animos, si non quoad ipsorum corpora. Venit Maria Magdalene. Passio est Maria se ad tempus diuelli à Christo, vt postea eo maiori cum gaudio frueretur. Sic nos oportuit æqui bonique consulere, quòd peregrinemur à Domino ad tempus, ex voluntate ipsius, vt postea eo in æternum fruamur maiori cum voluptate & gaudio. Maria autem interea temporis dum abfuit à Domino occupata fuit in annunciando aliis Domino. Sic & nos oportet dum peregrè agimus à Domino, in Domini negotiis occupatos esse, vt cùm reuersus fuerit Dominus, & nos in occursum ipsius rapti captifuerimus, ipsi simus acceptiores. Marcus in suo Euangelio narrat Mariam superuenisse discipulis flenti-bus & lugentibus.Fletus hic & luctus, etsi inanis fuerit, & absque iusta causa,tamen non plane reprehendendus, quia hauddubie profectus est ex amore & desiderio Domini. Semen alioqui bonum potest exerere se in effectis non ita bonis,ac vitiari quodammodo imperfectionibus naturæ huius,vt ignorantia, vt obliuione, vt incredulitate quibus vitiatum est bonum illud in discipulis Christi semen. Nam quia primum ignari fuerunt scripturarum,& obliti prædictionis Domini, denique dissi si annunciationi resurrectionis ipsius : ideo amor Domini erupit in luctum ac fletum quendam inanem. Sed videamus effectum sermonis & annuntiationis Mariæ.
units.tr: carnal thoughts about the glorified Christ. (3) because she was, as it were, made a herald and minister of the Lord's ascension, sent to others, even to the apostles themselves. This was indeed a great grace, by which the Lord honoured women above men, and Mary especially, whom the Lord, once possessed by seven demons, that is, thrust down even to the depths, now raises up into heaven and lifts above all others. For each one who is most humbled is most exalted at the time the Lord sees fit. Go and tell, he says, my brothers. Here, without doubt, is fulfilled the Scripture found at Ps. 22.23: I will declare your name to my brothers. The apostle to the Hebrews sets out the reason for this so gentle and familiar a name, when he says: For both he who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are all of one, namely of one common human nature: For which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren, saying, I will declare your name unto my brethren. So it is the sharing of the same nature, namely the human, that makes him call us brothers, and he is not ashamed to call us his brothers even now that he is glorified and raised to such exalted height; us, I say, wretched sinners, who are so far distant from him. If someone, though a son of the earth, is raised to some higher place, then his poor father, his poor mother, and all his poor and needy relations become cheap in his eyes. But Christ, even glorified, does not despise us, provided that we do not despise him. He is not ashamed of us unless we are first ashamed of him. He does not disown us before his Father until we have disowned him before men. But let us look at the words of the commission itself: Say to them, I ascend to my Father. Those women received from the angels the revelation of the Lord's resurrection to be shared with the apostles. But Mary receives from the Lord himself the revelation of his ascension, which is indeed a more excellent degree of his glory. Ministers, whether angels or men sent by the Lord, reveal something of him, often even great things. But the Lord himself, when he draws nearer to us, brings with him a greater light and revelation than that which was brought by ministers. So at his first coming he brought a greater revelation than that which had been given before, either by the prophets or by John the Baptist. So at his second coming he will return with a greater and clearer light and revelation than has ever been seen or brought before. Now we believe with difficulty even small things; then we shall see great things, and things which eye has not seen, nor ear heard, nor which have entered into the heart of man. But let us weigh the words: I ascend, he says. This word hints at a certain desertion of the brothers and disciples, whom he was going to leave behind in the world, and therefore that news had to be sad and unwelcome to the disciples. But what he adds last, to your Father, your God, ought rather to refresh and console them; for it concerns not only himself, that he ascends, but also his disciples, since that paternal glory was to be shared with the disciples too. For this is the reason why the glory of God is communicated to us: namely, that Christ has now ascended to our Father and our God. And this is indeed the order by which the glory of God is communicated to us. First Christ himself, after his ascent into the heavens, will be filled with all glory; then we all receive from his fullness. The reason of the order is that God is first the Father of Christ and the God of Christ. Therefore glory must first be communicated to the firstborn; then through Christ and the firstborn he is our Father and our God. He is, to say this in passing, the Father of Christ insofar as Christ is the Son of God, begotten of the Father from eternity; and he is the God of Christ insofar as he was made man in time. These words therefore imply the two natures of Christ existing in one person, the divine and the human. Now, to sum up, the news of Christ's ascension into the heavens had to be effective in the disciples, to lift them above all the heavens, at least in their minds, if not in their bodies. Mary Magdalene came. Passio is that Mary was for a time torn away from Christ, so that afterwards she might enjoy him with greater joy. So we too ought to accept with equanimity and goodwill that we are sojourners away from the Lord for a time, by his will, so that afterwards we may enjoy him for ever with greater delight and joy. Meanwhile Mary, while she was absent from the Lord, was occupied in announcing the Lord to others. So we too ought, while we are away from the Lord on our pilgrimage, to be occupied in the Lord's business, so that when the Lord returns, and we are caught up to meet him, we may be the more acceptable to him. Mark, in his Gospel, relates that Mary came upon the disciples while they were weeping and mourning. This weeping and mourning, though it was vain and without just cause, is nevertheless not wholly to be blamed, because it certainly arose from love and longing for the Lord. Otherwise a good seed can sprout in effects that are not so good, and be somehow marred by imperfections of nature, such as ignorance, forgetfulness, and unbelief, by which that good seed in the disciples of Christ was spoiled. For since at first they were ignorant of the Scriptures, and had forgotten the Lord's prediction, and finally were unwilling to believe the announcement of his resurrection, therefore their love for the Lord broke out into a certain vain grief and weeping. But let us see the effect of Mary's word and announcement.

units.la: Illi, inquit Marcus, cum audissent eum viuere, & conspectum fuisse ab eo, non crediderunt. Mira est discipulorum pertinacia in incredulitate sua, & illud plane suo exemplo nos docent, quam difficile sit per naturam homini credere articulo resurrectionis mortuorum: nempe quod qui semel mortuus est,& vita hac defunctus, possit ad vitam reuocari. Quod quidem iis qui sapientiores sunt secundum carnem difficilius est creditu, quàm iis qui sapientiæ carnis non ita confidunt, hoc est, viris quàm mulieribus. Animalis enim homo nō capax est eorum quæ sunt Spiritus Dei: sunt enim illi stultitia. Dum hæc geruntur aliæ mulieres rursus ad monumentum redeunt,ac digredientibus, prorsusque ignaris eius quod accidisset Magdalena, Iesus occurrit easque salutat. Hæc historia habetur verbis proximè sequentibus.
units.tr: When they heard, says Mark, that he was alive and had been seen by her, they did not believe.
