units.tr: Unless the Lord multiplied that grace of his toward us, and, when we grew slack in our course and calling, drew us after him by taking hold of us as if with an outstretched hand, it could by no means happen that we would persevere to the end, having been abandoned by him.

units.la: Exit ergo sermo. Hactenus fuit ille sermo Petri & Domini mutuus. Nunc proxime refert Iohannes responsum illud Domini perperam & siniistre interpretatum fuisse a discipulis. Domini quidem responsio simplex fuit, neque ullam ambiguitatem in se habuit: nihil enim ipse de Iohanne, deque ipsius vel vita, vel morte. At ideo hi interpretati sunt verba Domini, ac si Iohannem non moriturum dixisset. Illud enim manere quod dictum a Domino, interpretati sunt, non mori, usque ad adventum Domini ipsiusque reditum: ut videas quam pronum sit ac proprie humanum ingenium ad siniistre interpretandum verba Dei, & peruertendum mentem Spiritus sancti in scripturis loquentis: cum enim Apostoli Christi tam educati in schola ipsius, & eo tam familiariter praesente usi, tamen ipsius verba detorserint in sensum nō suum: quis miretur hominès hodierno die, quotidie idem facere? verum culpa est non quidem vobi Dei, & Scripturæ sacræ, quòd ipsa sit ambigua, flexiloqua, obscura, vt isti blasphemant: verum culpa est partim cæcitatis mentis eorum, partim est peruersitatis voluntatis & cordis eorum malitiæ. Vel enim non vident (quæ est naturæ ista cæcitas) mentem ipsam Domini: vel si videant eam, nolunt tamen videre; quæ est cordis duritiès & malitia. Indocti enim parùmque stabiles detorquent Scripturas sacras suo ipsorum exitio. Et, si tectum sit Euangelium, tectum est iis qui pereunt: quibus Deus huius seculi excæcauit mentes, &c. Rursus nota quâ celeriter sparsum sit hoc mendacium & locum sibi sumpserit in mentibus discipulorum: vt videas quàm citò quâ multi imbibant mendacia, fabulas, hæreses: quia scilicet natura tam sumus capaces eorum. Sed postquam iam iuxta promissionem Domini extra ordinem in die Pentecostes illuminati sunt discipuli, & datus est Spiritus ille, qui suggessit eis ea omnia, simulque verum eorum omnium sensum, quæ iam viua voce tradidisset Christus. Vide Iohann. 14. 26. Posteaquam, inquam, hæc iam facta sunt, sepultum est mendacium illud de Iohanne, & rei veritas omnibus innotuit. In regno autem Antichristi non solùm hæc fabula, sed & infinitæ vanitates & figmenta, etiam ipsarum prophanarum gentium, quæ in aduentu Domini sepulta sunt, ex inferis iunt reuocata. Nam ex fabulis, ex superstitionibus gentium, ex ritibus Iudæorum iam per Christum abolitis, religio Papisticaferè tota est confusa. De Iohanne autem eiusque morte, qui velit legat fabulosa, in eorum, quæ vocantur, Legendis. Hic est discipulus. Occasione proximi sermonis, qui de ipso fuit, concludit hoc suum Euangelium. In conclusione declarat, quinam is fuerat de quo sermo tum fuit, nempe discipulus ille idem, qui testatur hæc omnia, eáq; scripto prodidit: hoc dum facit claudit Euangelium suum, ipsúmque quasi obsignat. Primùm observuo ex eo quod dicit Iohannes se & testari, & scripsisse hæc, ipsum non vno tantùm modo testatum fuisse veritatem illam, quæ est in Christo Iesu. Et quidem non vno modo testatum facimus Euangelium Christi, ipsiúsque veritatem. Testimonium monium de veritate perhibemus verbo, testamur quo-que eandem scripto. Cum igitur quo plura sunt de veri-tate testimonia, eo maior redunder Deo gloria, conan-dum nobis est, vt omnibus quibus possumus modis re-stratam faciamus mundo Euangelij Christi veritatem, verbo, scripto, confessione oris, etsi ita opus sit, effuso e-tiam sanguine nostro. Sed hoc nobis hic praecipue no-tandum est, Iohannem postea quàm historiam suam con-texuisset, & conscripsisset, tandem eam obsignare, affixo quasi in eam sigillo suo. Hoc & nobis quasi faciendum est: postquam enim Christum iam praedicauimus, ser-monem illum nostrum sigillo quasi nostro oportet ob-signare: & si ita opus sit, etiam sanguine nostro, Paulus postquam Philippensibus praedicasset Christum, eósque ad fidem adduxisset, scripsit ad eos gaudere se & gratula-ri, si super hostia sacrificióque fidei eorum pro libamen-to offeratur: nempe ad obsignandum eorum fidem, pari-terque doctrinam iis à se iam traditam. Summus verum te-stimonium. Haec est causa cur obsignet Euangelium suum: nempe πληροφορία & plena persuasio veritatis ipsius. Hinc ista obsignatio. Qui habet παῤῥησίαν ad obsignandum Euangelium à se praedicatum, is est solus qui habet πληροφορίαν. Quare ei qui Christū praedicat studendum est plerophoria, vt possit loqui cum certa persuasione multa, id quod dixit Apostolus: vt possit etiam veritatem à se praedicatam etiam sanguine suo, si ita opus sit, obsignare. Sunt autem & alia multa. Occupatio: an omnia quaecunque à Christo facta sunt à te sunt scripta? hoc enim obiici potuit à curioso aliquo. Respondet Iohannes, Non omnia quidem quae fecit Dominus, à se scripta esse: neque enim fuisse se scribere ea omnia, neque etiam potuisse. Nā, vniversus quidem mundus non posset capere eos, qui sigillatim scriberentur libros. Nota primum ingenium hominum, quàm curiosum immoderatumque sit. Postquam enim omnia sunt perscripta ab Euangelistis, Apostolis & Prophetis, non contentum iis, quaeret demum, nihil superesset praeterea? Quod cum satis sciat diabolus ideo in regno Antichristi suggessit praeter scripta Prophetica & Apostolica, infinita mendacia, quae ipsi vocant traditiones diuinas, Apostolicas, Ecclesiasticas, vt
units.tr: Exit ergo sermo. Up to this point that was the mutual exchange between Peter and the Lord. Now John reports that the Lord's reply was misinterpreted and taken in the wrong sense by the disciples. The Lord's answer was simple and contained no ambiguity: he said nothing about John, or about John's life or death. But these men interpreted the Lord's words as if he had said that John would not die. They took the word manere (to remain), which the Lord had used, to mean not to die until the coming and return of the Lord. See how prone and naturally inclined the human mind is to take God's words in a perverse sense and to twist the mind of the Holy Spirit speaking in the Scriptures. For if the apostles of Christ, so trained in his school and so familiarly in his presence, nonetheless twisted his words into a sense not his own, who would be surprised that men today do the same every day? The fault lies not in the Word of God and the holy Scripture, as if it were ambiguous, ambiguous in its wording and obscure, as these blasphemers claim. The fault lies partly in the blindness of their minds and partly in the perversity of their will and heart and the malice of their heart. For either they do not see the Lord's mind (such is the blindness of nature), or if they do see it, they refuse to see it; and that is the hardness and malice of the heart. For the unlearned and unstable twist the holy Scriptures to their own destruction. And if the gospel is veiled, it is veiled to those who perish, whose minds the god of this world has blinded, and so on. Note again how quickly this lie spread and took hold in the minds of the disciples, so that you may see how quickly and how readily many drink in lies, fables and heresies, because we are by nature so receptive to them. But after the disciples were enlightened in the manner promised by the Lord, outside the ordinary course, on the day of Pentecost, and that Spirit was given who suggested to them all those things, and at the same time the true sense of all the things that Christ had taught them by living voice (see John 14:26), then, I say, once these things had been done, that lie about John was buried and the truth of the matter became known to all. But in the kingdom of Antichrist not only this fable but also endless vanities and fictions, even those of the profane nations which were buried at the coming of the Lord, have been called back up from the dead. For the Papist religion is almost wholly confused out of fables, out of the superstitions of the nations, and out of the rites of the Jews already abolished through Christ. As for John and his death, whoever wishes may read the fabulous accounts in what are called the Legends. This is the disciple. On the occasion of the preceding saying, which concerned him, he concludes his gospel. In the conclusion he declares who that man was about whom the saying then concerned, namely that same disciple who bears witness to all these things and has delivered them in writing; in doing this he closes his Gospel and, as it were, seals it. First I observe from what John says, that he both bears witness and has written these things, that he did not bear witness to that truth which is in Christ Jesus in one way only. Indeed we do not bear witness to the Gospel of Christ and its truth in only one way. We bear testimony to the truth by the spoken word, and we also attest the same in writing. Therefore, since the more testimonies there are to the truth, the greater the glory that redounds to God, we must strive to make the truth of the Gospel of Christ known to the world by every means we can: by word, by writing, by confession of the mouth, and even, if so required, by shedding our blood. But here we must especially note that John, after he had woven together and written his history, finally sealed it, as it were affixing his own seal to it. We too ought to do the same: for after we have preached Christ, we ought to seal that our preaching, as with our own seal, and if need be, even with our blood. Paul, after he had preached Christ to the Philippians and brought them to faith, wrote to them that he rejoiced and congratulated them, if he were to be offered as a libation upon the sacrifice and offering of their faith; namely, to seal their faith and likewise the teaching which he had already delivered to them. His testimony is true. This is the reason why he seals his Gospel: namely the plerophoria [πληροφορία] and full persuasion of its truth. Hence this sealing. He who has parrhesia [παῤῥησίαν], boldness, to seal the Gospel he has preached, is the only one who has plerophoria [πληροφορία], full assurance. Therefore whoever preaches Christ must strive for full assurance, so that he may speak many things with certain persuasion, as the Apostle said, and so that he may seal with his blood, if so required, the truth he has preached. There are also many other things. An objection: are all the things that were done by Christ written by you? For some curious person might have objected this. John replies that he did not write down all the things the Lord did, for he neither was able to write them all, nor could he have done so. For the whole world could not contain the books that would be written one by one. Note first how curious and immoderate the human mind is. For after all things have been fully written down by the evangelists, apostles and prophets, is it not discontented with these and asks finally whether anything else remains? Since the devil knows this well, in the kingdom of Antichrist he has suggested, besides the prophetic and apostolic writings, endless lies, which they call divine, apostolic and ecclesiastical traditions, so that

units.la: EEcc nemo iam debeat ignorare religionem Pontificiam co-paratam esse non ad fidem & salutem hominum, sed ad curiositatem & immoderatum appetitum. Rursus re-sponsione Iohannis discimus non modo veteres illos Prophetas & Apostolos, quorum opera vsus est Spiritus sanctus ad scribendum utrumque illud Testamentum, verum etiam eorum exemplo pios quosque & sanctos homines oportere modum seruare in loquendo & in scribendo, de iis quae ad religionem & cultum Dei pertinent. Nam veteres illi sancti viri in scribendo duo respexerunt, primum infinitam illam Dei maiestatem & immensitatem eorum, quae de Deo, de Christo scribi potuerunt: deinde modulum non solum ingenij, sed etiam fidei nostrae qui non sumus capaces eorum omnium, quae possunt scribi. Quare pennam suam Dei voluntate attemperarunt ad animum fidemque nostram: & deleetu habito scripserunt ea quae Spiritui sancto videbantur sufficere ad fidem salutemque nostram: infinita enim & immensa illa, si scripta fuissent omnia, obruissent & memoriam, mentem & fidem humanam. Hodierno enim die tristis experientia satis probat, Antichristum obruere mundum inventionibus & non scriptis illis veritatibus, quas vocant, quarum nullus vnquam finis est aut modus. Sed hic non est praetermittenda phrasis, qua hoc loco vtitur Euangelista: cum dicit mundum non posse capere omnes qui scriberentur libros: profecto enim phrasis haec non tam hyperbolica est, quam balbutiens ad captum nostrum. In re enim infinita & incomprehensibili balbutit nobiscum Spiritus sanctus, & nostro more loquitur. Iohannes enim dum ita loqueretur, intuitus est infinitam illam abyssum maiestatis diuinae quae est in Christo, quaeque est in operibus ipsius: quae non tantum omnes sensus hominum, sed & terram, & coelos ipsos absorberet. Volens itaque illam immensitatem exprimere aliquo certe modo, nimirum eo quem nos capere possemus. Hic mundus, inquit, totus non posset capere libros, qui scriberentur: quo quidem significatur Christum cum operibus suis omnibus describi non potuisse a quoquam pro dignitate sua, & amplitudine illius maiestatis, quam ne totus quidem mundus potest capere.
units.tr: Now no one should be ignorant that the Papist religion has been devised not for the faith and salvation of men but for curiosity and immoderate appetite. Again, from John's reply we learn that not only the ancient prophets and apostles, through whose work the Holy Spirit used to write both Testaments, but also, following their example, all pious and holy men ought to observe moderation in speaking and writing about those things which pertain to religion and the worship of God. For those ancient holy men, in writing, had regard to two things: first, the infinite majesty and immensity of God and of all that could be written about God and Christ; second, the measure not only of our intellect but also of our faith, since we are not capable of all the things that could be written. Therefore they tempered their pen, by God's will, to our mind and faith, and, having made a selection, wrote those things which the Holy Spirit judged sufficient for our faith and salvation. For if all those infinite and immense things had been written, they would have overwhelmed both the memory, the mind and the faith of man. Indeed the sad experience of today amply proves that Antichrist overwhelms the world with inventions and with those so-called truths that were not written, and of which there is never any end or limit. But here we must not pass over the expression which the evangelist uses in this place, when he says that the world could not contain the books that would be written. For this phrase is not so much hyperbole as a stammering adapted to our capacity. For the Holy Spirit, dealing with a matter infinite and incomprehensible, stammers with us and speaks in our manner. For John, while speaking thus, had in view that infinite abyss of divine majesty which is in Christ and in his works, which would absorb not only all the senses of men but the earth and heavens themselves. Wishing therefore to express that immensity in some way that we could grasp, he says: the whole world, he says, could not contain the books that would be written. By this is signified that Christ with all his works could not be described by anyone in a manner worthy of his dignity and of the greatness of that majesty, which not even the whole world can contain.

units.la: Vide quae in Iohannes c. 21. cap. 20. Ver. 31. capere. Nam hoc semel sciendum est, hanc Scripturam sacram, quæ extat de maiestate illa, infinitis partibus inferiorem esse ea ipsa maiestate de qua loquitur, & Spiritum Dei sanctum nobiscum de ea tantùm balbutire. Neque enim vnquâ possunt sublimia, grandia & magnifica satis verba inueniri à quoquam, quibus exprimatur maiestas illa incomprehensibilis. Atque huc usque prosequuti sumus Historiam Iohannis nostri Euangelicam. Nunc autem reliquam resurrectionis Christi historiam persequemur, vt eam narrant alij Euangelistæ: quam etiam Iohannes ab aliis perscriptam esse, satis cognouit: ideóque de industria eam ipse omisit amandauitque lectorem ad alios Euangelistas. Nos itaque ex aliis eam persequemur.
units.tr: See what is said on John 20, verse 31 (the word "contain"). This must be known once for all: this holy Scripture, which speaks of that majesty, is infinitely inferior to the majesty itself of which it speaks, and the Holy Spirit with us stammers only a little about it. For no one can ever find words lofty, grand and magnificent enough to express that incomprehensible majesty. So far we have followed the Gospel history of our John. Now we shall pursue the rest of the history of Christ's resurrection as the other Evangelists tell it. John knew well that others had already written it, and so he deliberately left it out and sent his reader to the other Evangelists. We shall therefore follow it from them. ## Matthew 28.

units.la: Matthæi 28.
16 Vndecim autem illi discipuli profecti sunt in Galilæam, in montem vbi constituerat eis Iesus.
units.tr: 16 Now the eleven disciples went away into Galilee, to the mountain where Jesus had appointed them.

units.la: 17 Et cùm vidissent eum, adorauerunt eum: quidam autem dubitauerunt.
units.tr: 17 And when they saw him, they worshipped him; but some doubted.

units.la: 18 Et cùm accessisset ad eos Iesus, loquutus est eis, dicens, Data est mihi omnis potestas in cælo & in terra.
units.tr: 18 And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying: All power is given to me in heaven and on earth.

units.la: 19 Profecti ergo docete omnes gentes, baptizantes eos in nomine Patris & Filij & Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: 19 Go therefore and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

units.la: 20 Docentes eos seruare omnia quæcunque mandaui vobis: & ecce ego vobiscum sum omnibus diebus usque ad consummationem seculi.
units.tr: 20 Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you; and behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age. ## Mark 16.

units.la: Marci 16.
15 Et dixit eis, Profecti in mundum universum, prædicate Euangelium omni creaturæ.
units.tr: 15 And he said to them: Go into all the world and preach the gospel to every creature.

units.la: 16 Qui crediderit, & baptizatus fuerit, seruabitur: qui verò non crediderit, condemnabitur.
units.tr: 16 He who believes and is baptized will be saved; but he who does not believe will be condemned.

units.la: 17 Signa autem eos qui crediderint, hæc consequentur, per nomen meum dæmonia eiicient: linguis loquentur.
units.tr: 17 And these signs will follow those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new tongues.

units.la: Ecc ij
units.tr: Ecc ij

units.la: 18 Serpentes tollent, & si quid lethale biberint, nequaquam nocebit iis : aegrotis manus imponent, & bene habebunt.
units.tr: 18 They will take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it will by no means harm them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will be well.

units.la: Pauca praeterea habent de resurrectione Domini Matthaeus & Marcus. Habent illi aliam praeteritam apparitionem Christi, quam nos tanquam nonam praecedentibus illis annumeramus. Primum enim omnium apparuit Dominus Magdalenae. 2. Aliis mulieribus. 3. Duobus discipulis, qui in vicum Emmaun-tem profecti sunt. 4. Petro. 5. Iacobo. De hinc illae tres apparitiones generales magis, quantum meminit Iohannes in historia sua. Haec igitur quam habent Matthaeus & Marcus nona est numero. Sic autem habet historia. Primum conueniunt vndecim discipuli, & vna cum iis, vt videtur, complures alij. Nam hoc tempore, vt verisimile est, apparuit Christus amplius quam quingentis fratribus: cuius quidem apparitionis meminit Paulus, primae ad Corinthios 15. 6. Tempus autem apparitionis, & locus, videntur a Domino praestituta ac praescripta esse discipulis ministerio mulierum, quibus mandauit Dominus supra, vt haec quasi comitia indicerent discipulis suis. Conueniunt igitur in vnum ex praescriptione Domini: Dominus autem sistit se iis praesentem ex pacto suo.
units.tr: Matthew and Mark have little else about the Lord's resurrection. They have another earlier appearance of Christ, which we count as the ninth, after the preceding ones. For first of all the Lord appeared to Magdalene; (2) to the other women; (3) to the two disciples who went away to the village of Emmaus; (4) to Peter; (5) to James. After these come the three general appearances, as John recalls in his history. So the one that Matthew and Mark have is ninth in number. The history goes like this. First the eleven disciples gather, and with them, as it seems, many others. For at this time, as is likely, Christ appeared to more than five hundred brethren, a appearance Paul recalls in 1 Corinthians 15. The time and place of the appearance seem to have been fixed and prescribed by the Lord for the disciples through the ministry of the women, to whom the Lord had earlier entrusted the task of announcing this meeting to his disciples. So they gather together at the Lord's appointment, and the Lord presents himself to them by his promise.

units.la: Nota igitur, Dominum, qui praecipit haec comitia Ecclesiae suae, promittitque iis praesentiam suam, sistere se praesentem suis, etsi non corporaliter, vt fecit in his comitiis discipulorum suorum, tamen spiritualiter. Neque etiam minus efficax est eius praesentia in suis nunc, quam fuit ea tum olim. Id quod pij reipsa in se sentiunt per gaudium hoc Spiritus sancti, & per pacem hanc tantam conscientiarum: quae profecto non posset sentiri, nisi in Spiritu suo praesens esset Dominus.
units.tr: Note, then, that the Lord, who commands this assembly of his Church and promises them his presence, presents himself to his people, though not bodily as he did at this gathering of his disciples, yet spiritually. Nor is his presence now any less effective among his people than it was then. Godly people feel this in themselves in fact, through this joy of the Holy Spirit and this great peace of conscience; which certainly could not be felt unless the Lord were present in his Spirit.

units.la: Adorarunt eum. Haec sunt quae sequuntur, praesentiam illam & apparitionem Domini: primum adoratio, deinde communicatio. Appropinquantem igitur adorant, id quod arguit ipsum, cum magna gloria, ab iis hoc tempore conspectum esse. Praesentia enim Domini gloriae requirit adorationem nostram.
units.tr: They worshipped him. These are the things that follow that presence and appearance of the Lord: first worship, then fellowship. So they worship him as he approaches, which shows that he was seen by them at this time with great glory. For the presence of the Lord calls for our worship because of his glory.

units.la: At, inquies, in coetibus sanctorum, quid est quod nunc cernimus? Discipuli olim viderunt oculis corporeis gloriosum Dominum: at nos nihil his oculis intuemur? Vides ac intueris Dominum in verbo suo, crucifixum primum, deinde glorificatum: vides, inquam, eum oculis mentis & fidei. Qui autem non adorabit Dominum in verbo suo praesentem, profecto is non adoraturus est eum tum cum coram sistet se: & qui in hoc mundo non adorant eum, quem intuentur in hoc quasi speculo Euangelii, profecto ij in altero seculo nunquam sunt eum adoraturi. Quid videt idiota ille, quem Paulus fingit ingredi in coetum, in quo sunt plures qui prophetant, & ingressum iam procidere in faciem & adorare? Quid, inquam, videt idiota ille tum cum adoravit, & testatus est Deum in omnibus prophetis esse? Procul dubio lux illa verbi Euangelici affulsit menti eius, & Christus stitit se praesentem oculis fidei: idipsum quod nunc contingit piis & fidelibus quibusque, dum coetibus Ecclesiasticis intersunt hoc ipso die. Quare in coetibus semper adorandum est, & sedendum cum reverentia, ad excipiendum animis nostris illum Christi Spiritum sanctum, quem vna cum verbo Euangelij praedicato offert nobis omnibus. Nota deinde efficaciam illam praesentiae gloriae Christi incurvare ac flectere simul animas & corpora hominum. Hinc dixit Paulus ad nomen Iesu omne genu se flectere caelestium, terrestrium ac subterraneorum. Ea enim est ipsius sublimitas in quam est euectus, & quidem efficax in res creatas omnes sublimitas, vt eas vel flectat suaviter, vel frangat violenter. Hinc sunt illi horrores diabolorum & improborum quorumcunque hominum: hinc reverentia illa Angelorum, beatorum & hominum piorum, quoties vel loquuntur, vel audiunt quicquam de ipso, ipsiusque tanta illa sublimitate.
units.tr: But, you will say, in the assemblies of the saints, what is it that we now see? The disciples once saw the glorious Lord with their bodily eyes; but we look upon nothing with those eyes? You see and gaze upon the Lord in his word, crucified first and then glorified: you see him, I say, with the eyes of the mind and of faith. But whoever does not worship the Lord present in his word will certainly not worship him when he stands before us; and those who do not worship in this world him whom they behold in this mirror, as it were, of the Gospel, will certainly never worship him in the other age. What did that outsider see, whom Paul imagines coming into an assembly in which several are prophesying, and who, on entering, falls on his face and worships? What, I say, did that outsider see when he worshipped and bore witness that God is in all the prophets? Without doubt the light of the Gospel word shone upon his mind, and Christ presented himself to the eyes of faith: the same thing that now happens to all the pious and faithful, while they are present at the church assemblies on this day. Therefore in the assemblies we must always worship, and sit with reverence, so as to receive into our souls that Spirit of Christ, the Holy Spirit, whom he offers to us all together with the preached word of the Gospel. Notice next that efficacy of the presence of Christ's glory, which bends and turns both the souls and the bodies of men. Hence Paul said that at the name of Jesus every knee of those in heaven, on earth and under the earth shall bow. For this is his sublimity into which he has been exalted, and indeed a sublimity efficacious over all created things, so that it either gently bends them or violently breaks them. Hence come those terrors of devils and of all wicked men; hence that reverence of angels, of the blessed and of pious men, whenever they speak or hear anything about him and about his so great sublimity.

units.la: Quidam autem dubitarunt. Nempe ex iis ipsis, qui tum eum adorarunt, vt scias quibus cum dubitationibus cultus nostri, & preces nostrae sint coniunctae, & ex quibus difficultatibus tandem eluctentur. Causa autem, quae monuit eos ad dubitandum, eadem fortasse fuit, quae monuit eos ad adorandum: nempe insolita illa Domini Christum.
units.tr: Some, however, doubted. Namely, some of those very men who then worshipped him, so that you may know with what doubts our worship and our prayers are joined, and from what difficulties they at last struggle free. The cause, moreover, which prompted them to doubt was perhaps the same that prompted them to worship: namely, that unaccustomed majesty and glory of the Lord Christ, which they could not even have expected.

units.la: EEee iij maiestas & gloria, quantam ne expectare quidé pote-runt. Ea enim nunc est Christi gloria, sedentis ad dexteram maiestatis illius, vt si eam daretur nobis praesentem videre ac intueri, quae est corruptela naturae nostrae, dubitaremus an is Christus ille esset de quo audiuimus in Euangelio. Neque hic silendum quanta cum difficultate fides habeatur, articulo illi qui est de resurrectione corporum nostrorum. Verum non magis difficilis est, quàm necessarius creditu: ideóque Dominus commoratus est in terris quadraginta dies totos, perpetuò fidem faciens resurrectionis suae.
units.tr: For such now is the glory of Christ, seated at the right hand of that majesty, that if we were given to see and gaze upon him present, which is the corruption of our nature, we would doubt whether he is that Christ of whom we heard in the Gospel. Nor should we pass over here how great a difficulty faith meets with in the article concerning the resurrection of our bodies. Yet it is no less difficult than it is necessary to believe; and therefore the Lord remained on earth for forty whole days, continually giving proof of his resurrection.

units.la: Et accedens. Propius ad eos accedit, tum vt omnem scrupulum eximeret, ex animis eorum, tum vt maiori cum efficacia ac fructu eos doceret. Sine dubio dum propius admouit oculis eorum corporalem suam praesentiam, interea insinuauit se per Spiritum suum in animos eorum ad hoc vt essent ij θεοδίδακτοι. Dominus in quibus vult efficax esse per verbum suum, propius ad eos per Spiritum suum accedit. In quibus autem non vult esse efficax, tantùm eminus ostendit eis potentiã & gloriam suam. Data est mihi omnis authoritas. Praefationem potestatis & authoritatis illius suae, praemittit legationi & Apostolatui eorum, simul & mandatis, quae vs daturus erat: ad hoc vt intuentes potestatem illam infinitam, ex qua profectum est ministerium & Apostolatus eorum, legationem & Apostolatu suum iam obirent cum fiducia & libertate animi simul & oris, scientes nimirum se habere vindicem eum, qui Dominus sit caelorum & terrae. Nota igitur, Ministerium hoc, etsi tantum famulitium quoddam sit, in Ecclesia Dei, non dominium, tamen fundatum esse in potestate quadam plusquam regia. Vult autem Dominus tam Ministros ipsos, quàm populum ac auditores, habere oculos suos perpetuò elevatos ad potestatem illam ex qua profectum est ministerium hoc, vt & illi cū fiducia & libertate ministrent, & hi non offendantur, abiecta ista & vili in speciem ministerij facie, Euangelij praedicati maiestatem non ex externa ministerij specie, verum ex potestate illa Domini infinita metientes. Tum hoc obseruandum potestatem hanc non modo in coelis esse dicit, sed in terris quoque. que. Interea data potestatem dicit vt Apostoli, & omnino Ecclesiæ omnes Ministri habeant potestatem & authoritatem in qua assiduè recumbat interea, dum in terris his obeunt munus suum, & luctantur cum ingrato isto mundo, cum diabolo, cum peccato. In coelis datam sibi dicit authoritatem, vt Apostoli & Ecclesiæ Ministri expectent post iam obitum illud munus suum, & tot labores exantlatos, tandem requiem illã coelestem, in qua futurum est vt securi conquiescant, cum Domino & rege suo in æternum. Paulus, Si in hac solùm vita, inquit, speramus in Christum omnium hominum miserrimi sumus. Quo significat, quod si tantum esset potestas Domini ea in qua, in hac duntaxat vita conquiescceremus, profectò pessimè nobiscum ageretur. Sed paulò diligentius observanda nobis est hæc Domini potestas, ecquænam ea sit: filij Dei potestas est, primùm ea ipsa gloria quam habuit cum Patre, ante iacta mundi fundamenta, Glorifica me, inquit, Pater, apud temetipsum ea gloria quam habui apud te, antequam hic mundus exisseret. Deinde potestas filij Dei est ea quam in carne acquisiuit, cum sese filius Dei exinaniret assumpta serui forma, in qua obediens factus est Patri ad mortem, mortè autem crucis. Propterea, inquit, extulit eum Pater in summam sublimitatem, &c. In quibus verbis habes acquisitam illam Mediatoris potestatem, quæ & hoc loco intelligenda est: nam ex hac potestate est Euangelium, ex hac est ministerium: ex hac denique est salus mundi: nempe ex potestate illa filij Dei, quam sibi in carne nostra acquisiuit. Potestas enim filij Dei illa, quam ab æterno cum Patre habuit, absque carne non prodesset peccatoribus ad vitam æternam.
units.tr: And drawing near. He draws nearer to them, both to remove every scruple from their minds and to teach them with greater efficacy and profit. Without doubt, while he brought his bodily presence nearer to their eyes, he at the same time insinuated himself through his Spirit into their minds, so that they might be taught by God [θεοδίδακτοι]. Where the Lord wills to be effective through his word, he draws near to them through his Spirit. But where he does not will to be effective, he only shows them his power and glory from afar. All authority has been given to me. He sets down the preface of his authority, placing it before their commission and apostleship, together with the commands he was about to give them: so that, looking upon that infinite power from which their ministry and apostleship proceed, they might now carry out their embassy and apostleship with confidence and freedom of mind and of speech, knowing that they have as their defender him who is Lord of heaven and earth. Note, therefore, that this ministry, though in the Church of God it is only a certain service and not lordship, is nevertheless founded upon a power more than kingly. Moreover the Lord wills both the ministers themselves and the people and hearers to keep their eyes always lifted to that power from which this ministry proceeds: so that the ministers may serve with confidence and freedom, and the hearers may not take offence at the lowly and mean appearance of the ministry, measuring the majesty of the preached Gospel not by the external appearance of the ministry but by that infinite power of the Lord. Further, it is to be observed that he says this power is not only in heaven but also on earth. Meanwhile he says the power has been given so that the apostles, and indeed all the ministers of the Church, may have a power and authority on which they may constantly rely while on earth they carry out their task and struggle with this ungrateful world, with the devil, and with sin. He says authority has been given to them in heaven, so that the apostles and ministers of the Church may await, after the completion of that task and the many labours undergone, at last that heavenly rest in which they will be able to rest securely with their Lord and King for ever. Paul says: If in this life only we hope in Christ, we are of all men most miserable [1 Cor. 15.19]. By this he means that if the power of the Lord were only that in which we rest in this life alone, things would go very badly for us indeed. But we must observe this power of the Lord more carefully, and ask what it is: it is the power of the Son of God, first that very glory which he had with the Father before the foundations of the world were laid: Glorify me, Father, with yourself, with that glory which I had with you before the world existed [John 17.5]. Next, the power of the Son of God is that which he acquired in the flesh, when the Son of God emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, in which he became obedient to the Father unto death, even the death of the cross. Therefore, he says, the Father exalted him to the highest place, etc. In these words you have that power of the Mediator which has been acquired, and which must be understood also in this place: for from this power comes the Gospel, from this comes the ministry, and from this finally comes the salvation of the world; namely, from that power of the Son of God which he acquired for himself in our flesh. For that power of the Son of God which he had from eternity with the Father would not, without the flesh, profit sinners unto eternal life.

units.la: Profecti Hactenus præfatio fuit, nunc sequitur eorum allegatio, & ministerii siue Apostolatus commendatio.
units.tr: Setting out So far this has been the preface; now comes their commission, and the commendation of the ministry or apostolate.

units.la: 1. Proficiscimini, ait, exite etiam extra Iudææ terminos.
units.tr: 1. Go, he says, and go out even beyond the borders of Judea.

units.la: 2. Docete, prædicate Euangelium. 3. Baptizate, obsignate symbolo Baptismi Euangelium à vobis prædicatum. Ad quos autem proficiscendum sit, quinam docendi, quinam baptizandi sint admonet. Nempe gentes omnes, omnis creatura. q.d. Potestas mea patet ad omne creaturam, ad omnes gentes, non ad Iudæos solùm: itaque Euangelium meum & ministerium illud vestrum, quo quidé propagatur ad omnes illa mea potestas, ad omnes mortales pariter sese extendat. Nota primùm, Apostolatum olim demandatum discipulis, non fuisse honoris inanem aliquem titulum, verùm munus operosum : ut ridiculum iam sit existimare istos otiosos ventres, Apostolorū successores esse, sicuti ipsi vèditàt hodierno die.
units.tr: 2. Teach, preach the Gospel. 3. Baptize, sealing with the sign of Baptism the Gospel preached by you. He indicates both where they are to go and who is to be taught and baptized: all nations, every creature. As if to say: my power extends to every creature and to all nations, not to the Jews alone; so let your ministry, by which my power is spread abroad, reach equally to all mortals. Note first that the apostolate once committed to the disciples was not an empty title of honour but a laborious office. So it is ridiculous now to think that those idle bellies are the successors of the Apostles, as they boast today.

units.la: Nota deinde, duas partes esse ministerij, prædicationem verbi & administrationem Sacramenti : nihil enim hic audimus de sacerdotio, aut immolatione vel cruēta vel incruenta: vt stultum sit credere aliud esse sacerdotium in Ecclesia Christi, præter id quod destinatum est ad immolandas Deo animas hominum spirituali illo verbi Dei gladio.
units.tr: Note next that the ministry has two parts: the preaching of the Word and the administration of the Sacrament. For we hear nothing here about a priesthood, or about sacrifice, either bloody or unbloody. So it is foolish to believe that there is any other priesthood in the Church of Christ, besides that which is appointed to offer up the souls of men to God with that spiritual sword of the Word of God.

units.la: Nota tertiò, non aliis atque aliis, sed eisdem duas has ministerij partes concreditas esse, & prædicationem verbi, & administrationem Baptismi: vt necesse sit prophanari Sacramentum Baptismi, si non ministredur ab eo, qui habeat quoque potestatem prædicandi Euangelium, hoc est à priuato aliquo viro, nedum muliercula. Nota quartò, quo ordine ministretur Baptisma : nempe non nisi prædicato iam prius Euangelio, & promulgato fœdere gratuito : cuius quidem Baptisma sigillum quoddam est. Quorsum enim signaculum, si nihil sit quod obsignes? Quare Baptisma, sine doctrina fœderis progrediente, inutile est ac mortuum elementum.In nomine. Hoc est in potestate ac authoritate Patris, Filij, & Spiritus sancti.
units.tr: Note thirdly that these two parts of the ministry, the preaching of the Word and the administration of Baptism, are entrusted not to different people but to the same people. So the sacrament of Baptism would be profaned if it were not administered by one who also has the power to preach the Gospel, that is, by some private man, let alone a mere woman. Note fourthly the order in which Baptism is administered: namely, not until the Gospel has first been preached and the free covenant proclaimed, of which Baptism itself is a kind of seal. For why a signet if there is nothing to seal? Therefore Baptism without the teaching of the covenant going before is useless and a dead element. In the name. That is, in the power and authority of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.

units.la: Nota igitur, efficaciam Baptismi esse à potestate non quidem Ministri, non verborum, vt vocant, in Baptismo operatoriorum : sed solius Dei. Quare baptizatum oportet oculos ad cœlos & Deum sublatos habere. Nota deinde, non dicit in genere in nomine Dei, sed distinctè, in nomine Patris, Filij, & Spiritus sancti. Ergo baptizatum oportet intueri Deum in trinitate, vel tres personas in Deitate.
units.tr: Note, then, that the efficacy of Baptism comes not from the power of the minister, nor from the so-called words operating in Baptism, but from God alone. So the one baptized must have his eyes lifted up to heaven and to God. Note next that he does not say in general "in the name of God," but distinctly, "in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit." Therefore the one baptized must look upon God in the Trinity, or the three persons in the Godhead.

units.la: Fides enim est distincta Dei notitia atque apprehensio: quisquis enim verè ac solidè credit in Deum, is sentit omne bonum primùm manare à Patre tanquam fonte, per Filium Mediatorem, & per Spiritum sanctum operatorem. Illud postremò addam, Non leges in tota veteri Scriptura tam claram ac perspicuam hanc personarum in Deitate distinctionem : vt scias Iesum ChriChristum Dei filium, primum omnium in mundū intulisse distinctam Dei cognitionem, & distinctè nominasse Patrem, Filium, & Spiritum sanctum. Patribus sub veteri Testamento ante Christi in carne manifestationem, cognitus aliquo modo fuit Deus in Trinitate, sed confusior fuit illa cognitio, si coparetur cum ea cognitione, quam Christus in aduentu suo in mundum intulit. Potissimum autem cum Christus iam resurrexisset ex mortuis & glorificatus esset, extitit haec distincta Trinitatis cognitio. Christus enim iam glorificatus, potissimum est imago iacōspicui Dei, & splēdor glorię ipsius, & character persōnæ ipsius. A Christo autem glorificato procedit operatio illa Spiritus sancti efficax. Quare ex Christi regno & gloria emersit potissimum distincta haec Trinitatis notitia. Docentes eos feruare. Restringit doctrinam abiis praedicandā ad ea quę ipse Christus prior docuerit Iohan. 14.26. Promittit primum Spiritum qui docturus sit omnia, tum restringit ea omnia, ad ea quæ ipse prior docuerit: Suggeret, inquit, omnia, quæ dixi vobis. Nunc restringit praedicationem Apostolorū ad ea, quæ ipse prior docuerit. Hinc sequitur fundamentum, regulam, & mensuram omnis veræ doctrinæ, esse doctrinam ipsius Christi, quam ipse tum tradidit cum commorarentur inter nos. Hanc regulam seruauit Spiritus ipse Christi, quem ipse discedens reliquit post se Ecclesiæ suæ: hac regulam seruarunt Apostoli, qui nihil docuerunt nisi id quod iam intus eos docuerat Spiritus ille Dei, qui rursus nihil docuerat, nisi quod iam ante se docuerat ipse filius Dei Iesus Christus. Quare doctrina & Spiritus sancti, & Apostolorū, à Christo doctore primum profecta est tota. Quæritur an pastores & doctores, qui in Ecclesia Christi sequuti sunt Apostolos, An hi, inquā, omnes tantum ea tradiderunt, quæ ipse Christus prior tradidit? Respondeo, ita in regno Antichristi aberrasse eos à fundamento illo, & regula veritatis à Christo posita, atque etiam Spiritu illo veritatis, qui ducit nos in omnē veritatem, ut pro doctrina Christi & Spiritus ipsius, non cessent obtrudere traditiones, nugas, ac sua ipsorum deliria. Quare admonendi sunt auditores, ut nihil audiant & recipiant ipsi, nisi quod conforme sit fundamento illo.
units.tr: For faith is a distinct knowledge and apprehension of God; whoever truly and firmly believes in God perceives that every good comes first from the Father as from a fountain, through the Son as Mediator, and by the Holy Spirit as the one who works it. Last, I will add this: you will not find in all the Old Testament so clear and plain a distinction of persons in the Godhead. So you may know that Jesus Christ, the Son of God, first of all brought into the world a distinct knowledge of God, and named distinctly the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Under the Old Testament, before the manifestation of Christ in the flesh, the Fathers knew God in some way as a Trinity, but that knowledge was more confused when compared with the knowledge which Christ brought into the world at his coming. Chiefly, however, when Christ had already risen from the dead and been glorified, this distinct knowledge of the Trinity came forth. For Christ, now glorified, is above all the image of the invisible God, and the brightness of his glory, and the express character of his person. And from the glorified Christ proceeds that effectual work of the Holy Spirit. Therefore it was chiefly out of the kingdom and glory of Christ that this distinct knowledge of the Trinity arose. Teaching them to observe. He restricts the doctrine to be preached by them to what Christ himself first taught (John 14.26). He first promises the Spirit who is to teach all things, and then restricts all those things to what Christ himself first taught: He will bring to your remembrance, he says, all things that I have said to you. Now he restricts the preaching of the Apostles to what he himself first taught. Hence it follows that the foundation, rule and measure of all true doctrine is the doctrine of Christ himself, which he delivered while he dwelt among us. The Spirit of Christ, whom he left behind after his departure for his Church, kept this rule; the Apostles kept this rule, teaching nothing except what that Spirit of God had already taught them inwardly, and that Spirit in turn taught nothing except what the Son of God, Jesus Christ, had already taught before. Therefore the whole doctrine, both of the Holy Spirit and of the Apostles, came in the first place from Christ the Teacher. It is asked whether the ministers and teachers who followed the Apostles in the Church of Christ have all delivered only what Christ himself first delivered. I answer: no; in the kingdom of Antichrist they have strayed from that foundation and rule laid down by Christ, and also from that Spirit of truth who leads us into all truth, so that, in place of the doctrine of Christ and of his Spirit, they do not cease to thrust upon us traditions, trifles, and their own delusions. Therefore the hearers must be warned to accept and receive nothing except what agrees with that foundation.

units.la: Distincta cognitio Dei a Christo nobis allata.
units.tr: The distinct knowledge of God brought to us by Christ.

units.la: Doctrinae Ecclesiis Christianis proponendae summa.
units.tr: The sum of the doctrine to be set before the Christian Churches.

units.la: Fundamentum, regula, mensura doctrinae orthodoxae.
units.tr: The foundation, rule and measure of orthodox doctrine.

units.la: Post Christum. Apostolos & Apostolicos viros, quid alii multi Ecclesiis propo-suerint. doctrinæ Christi ipsius. At,inquies,quomodo id resciemus? Respondeo primùm,rescicmus per Spiritum sanctum, qui nihil nos docebit, nisi quod iam docuit ipse Dominus. Quare seriò ipse à nobis inuocandus est ad hoc,vt velit nos illuminare atque regere:deinde resciemus id per Scripturam Propheticam & Apostolicam,in qua neque plùs, neque minùs doctrinæ veritatis traditum est,quam docuerat ipse Dominus.
units.tr: After Christ: what the Apostles and Apostolic men proposed to the Churches, and what many others since have proposed, is the doctrine of Christ himself. But, you will say, how shall we know this? I answer, first, we know it through the Holy Spirit, who will teach us nothing except what the Lord himself has already taught. Therefore he must be earnestly called upon by us, that he may be willing to enlighten and guide us. Then we shall know it through Prophetic and Apostolic Scripture, in which no more and no less of the doctrine of truth is delivered than the Lord himself taught.

units.la: Qui crediderit. Hactenus dedit discipulis suis mandatū exeundi, prædicandi & baptizandi. Nunc autē promissionem facit iis omnibus quotquot ad prædicationem eorum essent credituri, & baptismum eorum recepturi. Promissio autem est salutis & vitæ æternæ, simul autem denunciatio est aduersus eos omnes quicunq; non credituri essent eorū prædicationi. Aduersus hos igitur denunciat dānationem & mortem æternā. Nota igitur primùm:quemadmodū Apostolatus & omnino ministerium procedit ex potestate illa,quę impler cœlos pariter & terrā: ita inefficax esse non potest hoc ministerium,verùm necesse est afferat vel vitā vel mortem: vitā credentibus, mortem non credentibus. Vnde Paulus dixit se semper triumphare,ac victorē esse, Christiquę bonā flagrātiam esse Deo,& in iis qui seruantur, & in iis qui pereunt: In ijs qui seruantur, odorem vitæ ad vitam: in ijs qui pereunt odorem mortis ad mortem. Quibus verbis designauit efficaciam Euangelij prædicati, quæ sit in quouis genere hominum. Deinde obseruo his verbis, fidem, iustitiam, salutem,& omnino Dei gratiam quodam modo alligatam esse ministerio huic, adeo vt quisquis velit se subiicere ministerio, is consequuturus sit fidem, iustitiam, vitam. Contrà verò, qui ministerium contempserit, neque fidem, neque iustitiam, neque salutem sit consequuturus. At, inquis, gratia Dei externis istis non est alligANDA? concedo, non sic alligatam esse gratiam ordinariis istis mediis & externis adiumentis, vt Deus iis operitur extra ordinem in iis, in quibus ipsi visum est sic operari. Sed interea id certum est eum qui neglexerit vel contempserit media hæc ordinata à Deo, gratia Dei frustratum iri. Fides est ex auditu, auditus autem est verbi prædicati. Romi o. vers. 14. Tertiò nota prædclarum quoddam fidei effectum: nempe salutem, vitamque æternam. Quod quidem non sic accipiendum est, quasi virtute ac merito fidei suæ, quis servetur: verum virtuti illi ac merito Christi, quæ fide apprehendimus effectum hoc tantum est tribuendum. In Christo enim hæc vita residet, adeo plena & copiosa, vt non citius eum fide recipiamus, quàm vita ista, ex eo in nos redundet. In eo tanta lux habitat, vt quam primum ad eum propius accedimus, irradiet nos ipse luce illa sua. Tanta deniq; in eo gloria est, vt dum intuemur eum in speculo hoc Euangelij sui, transformemur in eandem imaginem ex gloria in gloriam. Hoc totum tribuitur efficaciæ Christi. Transformabit hoc, inquit Apostolus, corpus humile, vt conforme fiat glorioso suo corpori per efficacitatē, qua etiam poterit sibi subiicere omnia. Obserua quarto loco in promissione Baptismum cum fide, hoc est Christo fide apprehensō coiunctum esse, non quidem vt causam salutis, aut etiam immediatam aliquā causam: verum vt testimonium ipsius causæ necessarium, adeo vt, qui hanc Baptismi tesseram ac notam passus fuerit sibi insculpi, eamque contempserit, non sit ipse salutem consequuturus. Dico igitur Baptismum necessariū esse ad salutem, secundum quid, hoc est, vt sic dicā, in casu neglectus, vel contemptus: simpliciter vero & extra casum contemptus nōn esse ad salutem necessarium, adeo vt sine eo nō possit quis seruari. Potest enim quis Christo inseri, & per Christum seruari etiam sine Baptismi symbolo. Gratia enim Dei non est sic alligata externis istis adiumentis & ordinariis mediis, vt nequeat Deus hominem sine his seruare omnino: cum ordinariorum mediorū non carentia, vt sic dicam, nuda, verūm neglectus & conceptus priuet hominē Dei gratia. Videtur ad ostendendum nō esse simplicē baptismi necessitatem ad salutem nostrā. Spiritus sanctus in denunciatione ea quę promissionem sequitur de industria nō meminisse Baptismi. Ait enim, qui non crediderit damnabitur. Nihil hic loquitur de Baptismo. Obseruo quinto loco in denunciatione, quidnā per negationem fidei intelligat, dum dicit, Qui non crediderit. Sub negatione igitur ista includit primum quęcunque peccata in legem moralem admittuntur, vt ori-
units.tr: Whoever believes. Hitherto he has given his disciples the commission to go out, preach and baptize. Now he makes a promise to all who would believe their preaching and receive their baptism. The promise is of salvation and eternal life; at the same time there is a denunciation against all who would not believe their preaching. Against these, therefore, he denounces condemnation and eternal death. Note first: just as the apostolate, and indeed the whole ministry, proceeds from that power which fills heaven and earth alike, so this ministry cannot be ineffective, but must bring either life or death: life to believers, death to unbelievers. Hence Paul said that he always triumphs and is victorious, and that the good savour of Christ is to God both among those who are saved and among those who perish: among those who are saved, the savour of life unto life; among those who perish, the savour of death unto death. By these words he marked out the efficacy of the preached Gospel, which is found in every kind of man. Next I observe from these words that faith, righteousness, salvation, and in short the grace of God, are in some sense bound to this ministry, so that whoever is willing to submit himself to the ministry will obtain faith, righteousness and life. On the contrary, whoever despises the ministry will obtain neither faith, nor righteousness, nor salvation. "But," you say, "is the grace of God not bound to these external things?" I concede that grace is not so bound to these ordinary means and external helps that God cannot work outside the ordinary way in those in whom it has pleased him to work so. Yet meanwhile this is certain: whoever neglects or despises these means ordained by God will be cheated of the grace of God. Faith is from hearing, and hearing is through the preached word (Rom. 10.14). Thirdly, note a notable effect of faith: namely, salvation and eternal life. This is not to be understood as if anyone is saved by the power and merit of his own faith; rather this effect is to be attributed only to that power and merit of Christ which we apprehend by faith. For in Christ this life dwells, so full and abundant that the moment we receive him by faith, that life overflows into us from him. In him so great a light dwells that as soon as we draw nearer to him he shines upon us with that light of his. Finally, in him there is so great a glory that, while we gaze on him in the mirror of his Gospel, we are transformed into the same image from glory to glory (2 Cor. 3.18; 4.6). All this is ascribed to the efficacy of Christ. He will transform this, says the Apostle, our lowly body, to be conformed to his glorious body, by the working by which he is able even to subject all things to himself (Phil. 3.21). Fourthly, observe in the promise that Baptism is joined with faith, that is, with Christ apprehended by faith, not indeed as the cause of salvation, or even as some immediate cause, but as a necessary testimony of that cause; so that whoever has suffered this token and mark of Baptism to be engraved on him, and has despised it, will not obtain salvation. I say therefore that Baptism is necessary to salvation in a qualified sense, that is, so to speak, in case of neglect or contempt; but simply, and apart from the case of contempt, it is not necessary to salvation, so that no one can be saved without it. For a man may be grafted into Christ, and saved through Christ, even without the sign of Baptism. For the grace of God is not so bound to these external helps and ordinary means that God cannot save a man altogether without them; for it is not the lack of ordinary means, as it were bare, but neglect and contempt, that deprives a man of the grace of God. This seems to show that the necessity of Baptism for our salvation is not simple. The Holy Spirit, in the denunciation that follows the promise, deliberately made no mention of Baptism. For he says, "whoever does not believe will be condemned." Here he says nothing about Baptism. Fifthly, observe in the denunciation what he means by the denial of faith, when he says, whoever does not believe. Under this denial he first includes all the sins that are committed against the moral law, both original sin and all actual sins; which, unless they are in Christ, from whom alone is the remission of all these, all remain unabolished and will themselves bring about condemnation.

units.la: 2. Corinth. 4. 6. & 3. 18. Philip. 3. 21. ginale peccatum, vt actualia omnia, quæ si non sint in Christum, ex qua sola est omnium istorum remissio, hęc omnia adhuc manent nō abolita, & damnationē ipsa dem procurabunt: deinde in negatione ista fidei intelligit rebellionem illā & infidelitatem qua homines oblatam gratis à Deo gratiā reiiciunt contĕptim, quod quidē peccatum est omniū longè maximū atq; grauissimū. Ex quo sequitur, nō vulgaris aliqua dominatio, verùm damnatio lōgè grauissima.Qui non credit iam condemnatus est. His verbis significat tum præsentem tum grauissimā condemnationem. Ratio addita est à rebellione, quæ fit aduersus maiestatem illam vnigeniti filij Dei, quia, inquit, non crediderit in nomen vnigeniti filij Dei.
units.tr: 2. Corinth. 4. 6. & 3. 18. Philip. 3. 21. Original sin, like all actual sins, remains unabolished unless it is in Christ, from whom alone all these are remitted, and these sins will themselves procure damnation. Then, in this negation of faith, he understands that rebellion and unbelief by which people contemptuously reject the grace of God, offered freely; this sin is by far the greatest and most grievous of all. From this it follows that the damnation is not some ordinary dominion but a most grievous damnation. He who does not believe is already condemned. By these words he signifies both a present and a most grievous condemnation. The reason is added from the rebellion, which is directed against the majesty of the only-begotten Son of God, because, he says, the man has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.

units.la: Signa autem eos. Hęc altera est promissio, qua ad credendum homines allicit, nempe promissio fidei miraculosę & donorum Spiritus sancti miraculosorum. Promissio autem hęc neque patet ad omnes & singulos fideles, neque extenditur ad omnia tempora & ætates. Verùm restringenda est ad certos quosdam, quibus visum est Domino impertiri donum hoc miraculorum, & ad certum tempus, nempe, prima illa tempora in quibus Euangelium, quod mundo prius inauditum erat, confirmari necesse fuit. Neque est quod iactitent Pontificij miracula quotidie edi in Ecclesia sua: sunt enim procul dubio ea, quę prędixit Christus ipse primùm in aduentu Antichristi edenda; Matth. 24.24. Deinde quę dixit Paulus 2. Thess. 2.9. signa esse & prodigia mendacia, efficacia tamen in iis, qui amorem veritatis non recipiunt. Sed de his hactenus obseruo, priori loco promissa est hominibus salus, quod quidem miraculum est longè maximum. Posteriori verò loco, promittuntur alia miracula, vt notę totidem & signa futurę illius salutis, quod dixi miraculum esse omnium maximum. Quòd autem omnia hæc, quæ edebantur, primis illis temporibus miracula totidem signa erant salutis, apparet ex illis verbis Christi. Vt autem sciatis, inquit, filium hominis authoritatem habere in terra remittendi peccata, Paralyticum illum sanitati restituam. Dixit enim Paralytico, Surge, tolle lectum tuum, & abi domum. Ergo miraculum illud sanationis tanquā argumentum fuit maioris gratiæ nempe remissionis peccatorum & salutis æternæ. Obseruo igitur, nunquam esse fidem sine miraculo, si nō tali, qualia erant quæ primis illis temporibus edebantur: at certè non sine miraculo regenerationis & salutis. Hancque salutem magis admirandam esse quàm omnia illa miracula satis docuit ipse Dominus, cùm septuaginta illos discipulos reuersos iam & gaudentes miraculis in ipsius nomine à se editis, sic castigauit, Gaudete, inquiens, potius, quòd nomina vestra cælis sunt inscripta. Et Petrus dicit ex gentibus homines cùm non viderent eos qui primis illis temporibus conuerfierant ad Christum, more solito ad eandem luxus profusionem concurrere, dicit, in quam eos visos esse sibi peregrinari, hoc est, supra modum esse obstupefactos: neque id quidem iniuria. Nam qui serio conuersus est & renatus is miraculum est orbis. Notandum autem hic signa & miracula non sequi simpliciter fidem illam quam iustificantem vocat, sed in videndis miraculis opus esse alia præterea fide, quam miraculosam vocant: quæ nihil aliud est quàm speciale quoddam & extraordinarium donum Spiritus sancti, quo fiebat vt primis illis temporibus ex fidelibus aliquot derent miracula. Fides autem hæc nitebatur specialibus promissionibus, certis quibusdam extra ordinem factis à Deo. Hoc obseruo propter aduersarios, qui non aliam fidem miraculorum esse censent, quàm hàc quam dicimus iustificantem.
units.tr: Signs will accompany those who believe. This is the second promise, by which he draws people to believe, namely the promise of miraculous faith and of the miraculous gifts of the Holy Spirit. But this promise does not extend to all and each of the faithful, nor to all times and ages. Rather it must be restricted to certain persons, to whom the Lord was pleased to grant this gift of miracles, and to a certain time, namely those first times in which the Gospel, previously unheard of in the world, had to be confirmed. Nor have the Papists any reason to boast that miracles are wrought daily in their Church: for these are without doubt the things Christ himself foretold would be wrought at the coming of Antichrist (Matth. 24.24), and which Paul called lying signs and wonders (2 Thess. 2.9), yet effective among those who do not receive the love of the truth. But so much for these matters. I observe that in the first place salvation is promised to people, which is indeed by far the greatest miracle. In the second place, other miracles are promised, as so many marks and signs of that salvation, which I said was the greatest of all miracles. That all these miracles which were then performed were so many signs of salvation appears from those words of Christ: But that you may know, he says, that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins, I will restore the paralytic to health. For he said to the paralytic, Rise, take up your bed, and go home. Therefore that miracle of healing was, as it were, a proof of a greater grace, namely the remission of sins and eternal salvation. I observe, then, that there is never faith without a miracle, if not of the kind that were performed in those first times, yet certainly not without the miracle of regeneration and salvation. And the Lord himself has sufficiently taught that this salvation is more to be wondered at than all those miracles, when he rebuked the seventy disciples who returned already rejoicing in the miracles they had performed in his name: Rejoice rather, he said, that your names are written in heaven. And Peter says that when the Gentiles did not see those who had been converted to Christ in the first times running, as usual, to the same excess of revelry, they were astonished at this, that is, they were amazed beyond measure; and not without reason. For whoever is truly converted and born again is a miracle of the world. It must be noted here that signs and miracles do not simply follow that faith which he calls justifying, but that in seeing miracles there is needed another faith besides, which they call miraculous: this is nothing other than a special and extraordinary gift of the Holy Spirit, by which it came about that in those first times some of the faithful performed miracles. This faith rested on special promises, certain things done beyond the ordinary course by God. I observe this on account of our opponents, who think that the faith of miracles is no other than that justifying faith which we speak of.

units.la: Et ecce ego vobiscum sum. Hac promissione facta discipulis suis profecturis in vniuersum mundum ex mandato Domini, claudit Christus sermonem suum. Quemadmodum igitur in exordio sermonis sui erexit eorum animos ad obeundam tam difficilem legationem, demonstrata illa potestate & authoritate sua omnia & cœlos & terram occupante: Ita nunc concludit orationem sua facta promissione præsentiæ tantæ illius potestatis. Ego, inquit, q.d. Ego, cui data est omnis illa potestas in cælis & in terra: Ego, inquam, ero vobiscum cum omnia mea potestate. Emphasis enim est in pronomine Ego. Promittit, etiam, hanc præsentiam sui, non ad tempus tantum duraturam, verum permansuram in secula. Tertio promittit præsentiam, non quæ futura sit certis & statis duntaxat temporibus, sed quæ futura sit sine termissione, omnibus, inquit, diebus: ne vno quidē die excepto. Vide igitur quàm præclara sit & plena consolatio nis hæc promissio. Et ecce ego vobiscum sum. Promissio est potentiæ infinitæ primum, deinde, quæ iis præsens futura sit. Tertiò, futura præsens nõ ad certum aliquod tempus, verùm in seculum. Quartò, futura præsens in seculum non statis diebus, sed absque intermissione aliqua. Hæc autem promissio habet conditionem quæ immediatò præcessit. Si discipuli docturi sint homines seruare ea omnia, quæ ab ipso sunt eis prius iam tradita: ea, inquam, omnia & non alia præter ea. Hæc promissio ad ministerium hoc, quod nunc est pertinet: Ait enim, ero vobiscũ in seculum. At Apostoli Christi iam mortui sunt: ergo promissio hæc facta est Ministris Ecclesiæ & Apostolorum successoribus, qui mansuri sunt in Ecclesia ad Christi reditum usque. Minister igitur quicunque bona fide facit officium suum, docétque ea quæ Christus docuit & omnia & sola: & docet ea diligenter ac sincerè: Hic, inquam, habet fiduciæ & lætitiæ non paruam materiam ex tanta promissione. Tantùm ipse videat ut faciat officium suum, attendat ad doctrinam, permittat cætera promissæ huic præsentiæ Domini sui, qui eum nullo vnquam tempore est derelicturus. Vt autem Ministro attendendũ, vt fungatur bona fide officio suo: ita interest populi videre vt nullo modo sinat se abstrahi ab officio suo, fideliter & diligenter faciendo, neque implicari negotiis vitæ huius. 2. Timoth. 2. 4. Sic enim fit vt præsentia Dei retineatur in populo. Nam præsentia, quam habet Minister, ea quoque fruitur populus: & benedictio Ministri, est benedictio populi. Contraque maledictio Ministri, maledictio pariter est populi, præsertim eius qui contemptui habet ministerium. De Pontificiis, ut hoc postremò dicam, si aduertant promissionem præsentiæ Domini, hic non fieri nisi certa quadam conditione, nempe si ipsi doceant, quæ Christus docuit omnia & sola, non concludent profectò ex hoc loco & promissione ista Ecclesiam suam non sic deseri vnquà à Domino vt erret. Non seruata enim cõditione ea, quæ præposita est, quæ quæso fiducia potest esse promissæ illius præsentiæ. Quòd autem non seruetur in Ecclesia pontificia illa conditio, & quantum exulet ab illa Antichristi sede spiritus veritatis, & vera Christi doctrina, doctrinis hominum & figmentis cerebri humani in eius locum suffectis iam manifestius est, quàm vt illa indigeat declaratione.
units.tr: And behold, I am with you. With this promise made to his disciples, who were about to go into the whole world at the Lord's command, Christ closes his discourse. Just as at the beginning of his discourse he raised their spirits to undertake so difficult an embassy, by displaying that power and authority of his which occupies heaven and earth, so now he concludes his speech by making the promise of the presence of that great power. I, he says, as if to say: I, to whom all that power in heaven and on earth has been given: I, I say, will be with you with all my power. For the emphasis lies on the pronoun I. He also promises that this presence of his will not last only for a time but will remain forever. Thirdly, he promises a presence not to be in force only at certain fixed times, but one that will be without interruption: all, he says, days, not even one day excepted. See, then, how bright and full of consolation this promise is. And behold, I am with you. The promise is, first, of infinite power, and then of its being present with them. Thirdly, a presence to be not for some particular time but for the age. Fourthly, a presence to be for the age, not on fixed days but without any interruption. This promise has the condition which immediately precedes it: if the disciples are to teach people to observe all those things which have already been handed down to them by him: all of them, I say, and no others besides these. This promise pertains to the ministry which now exists: for he says, I will be with you unto the age. But Christ's apostles are now dead; therefore this promise has been made to the ministers of the Church and to the successors of the apostles, who are to remain in the Church until Christ's return. Therefore any minister who in good faith performs his office, and teaches all and only the things that Christ taught, and teaches them diligently and sincerely, has, I say, no small matter of confidence and joy from so great a promise. Let him only see to it that he does his office, attend to the doctrine, and leave the rest to the promised presence of his Lord, who will never at any time forsake him. And just as the minister must take care to discharge his office in good faith, so it is in the interest of the people to see that they in no way allow him to be drawn away from his office, by diligently and faithfully performing it, nor entangled in the affairs of this life (2 Tim. 2.4). For in this way the presence of God is kept among the people. For the presence which the minister has, the people also enjoy; and the blessing of the minister is the blessing of the people. Conversely, the curse of the minister is equally the curse of the people, especially of those who hold the ministry in contempt. As to the Papists, to say this last point: if they considered the promise of the Lord's presence, that it is not made here except under a certain condition, namely if they themselves teach all and only the things that Christ taught, they would certainly not conclude from this passage and this promise that their Church is so little forsaken by the Lord that it cannot err. For if the condition set down is not observed, what confidence, I ask, can there be in that promised presence? That this condition is not observed in the Papist Church, and how far the Spirit of truth and the true doctrine of Christ are absent from that seat of Antichrist, with human doctrines and figments of the human brain having been put in their place, is now too manifest to need any demonstration.

units.la: Marci 16.
units.tr: Mark 16.

units.la: 19 Dominus igitur postquam loquutus fuisset eis, Sursum receptus est in cælum & sedet ad dextram Dei.
units.tr: 19 So then the Lord, after he had spoken to them, was received up into heaven and sitteth at the right hand of God.

units.la: 20 Illi verò profecti prædicarunt vbique Domino cooperante, & sermonem eorum confirmante, per signa subsequentia.
units.tr: 20 And they went forth and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word with the signs that followed.

units.la: Lucæ 24.
units.tr: Luke 24.

units.la: 50 Eduxit autem eos foras ad Bethaniam vsque, & sublatis manibus benedixit eis.
units.tr: 50 And he led them out as far as Bethany, and lifting up his hands he blessed them.

units.la: 51 Et factum est vt dum ipse benediceret eis, disiunctus est ab eis, & sursum ferebatur in cælum.
units.tr: 51 And it came to pass, while he blessed them, that he was parted from them and was carried up into heaven.

units.la: 52 Ipsi autem adorato eo reuersi sunt Hierosolymam cum gaudio magno.
units.tr: 52 And they worshipped him, and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.

units.la: 53 Erantque omni tempore in templo, laudantes & benedicentes Deo, AMEN.
units.tr: 53 And they were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.

units.la: Actorum 1.
units.tr: Acts 1.

units.la: 6 Cū igitur illi convenissent, interrogarunt eū, dicentes: Domine num hoc tempore restitues regnū Israëli?
units.tr: 6 When therefore they were come together, they asked him, saying: Lord, wilt thou at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?

units.la: 7 Dixit autem ad illos, Non est vestrum noscere tempora aut opportunitates quas Pater in sua ipsius potestate posuit:
units.tr: 7 And he said to them, It is not for you to know the times or the seasons, which the Father hath put in his own power.

units.la: 8 Sed recipietis virtutem Spiritus sancti, postquam superuenerit in vos, eritisque mihi testes, & in Ierosolymis, & in tota Iudæa & Samaria, & vsque ad vltimas terras.
units.tr: 8 But you shall receive the power of the Holy Spirit, when he is come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and even to the uttermost parts of the earth.

units.la: 9 Et cùm hæc dixisset, aspicientibus ipsis elevatus est: & nubes suscepit eum ab oculis eorum.
units.tr: 9 And when he had said these things, while they looked on, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.

units.la: 10 Et cùm essent intentis in cælum oculis, eo prosiciscente, Ecce viri duo astiterunt illis albo vestitu:
units.tr: 10 And while they were looking steadfastly towards heaven as he went up, behold, two men stood by them in white apparel,

units.la: 11 Qui & dixerunt, Viri Galilaei quid statis intuentes in coelum? Hic Iesus, qui sursum receptus est a vobis in coelum, sic veniet quemadmodum conspexistis eum proficiscentem in coelum.
units.tr: 11 Who also said: Ye men of Galilee, why stand you looking up to heaven? This Jesus, who is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, as you have seen him going into heaven.

units.la: 12 Tunc reversi sunt Hierosolymam, a Monte qui vocatur Oliveti, qui est prope Hierosolymam, distans uno itinere Sabbathi.
units.tr: 12 Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, about a Sabbath day's journey away.

units.la: 13 Et cum introissent, ascenderunt in coenaculum ubi commorabatur & Petrus, & Iacobus, & Iohannes, & Andreas, Philippus & Thomas, Bartholomaeus & Matthaeus, Iacobus filius Alphaei, & Simon Zelotes, & Iudas Iacobi frater.
units.tr: 13 And when they were come in, they went up into the upper room where they were staying: Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon the Zealot, and Judas the brother of James.

units.la: 14 Hi omnes perdurabant concorditer, in oratione & deprecatione cum uxoribus & Maria matre Iesu, & cum ipsius fratribus.
units.tr: 14 All these continued together in prayer and supplication, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.

units.la: SEquitur historia ascensionis Domini, de qua Matthaeus nihil, Iohannes nihil habet in Euangelio suo: Marcus in Euangelio suo aliquid, Lucas vero aliquid in Euangelio suo. In Actis vero Apostolorum idem Lucas historiam fusius conscripsit. primum ergo, ut ad rem veniamus, ait Lucas, Eduxit eos foras Bethaniam. Non iuerunt eo sua sponte, sed educti sunt Hierosolymis ad conspiciendam tantam gloriam, & participandu tanta gratia. Nemo enim sua sponte vadit participatu gratia, verum necesse est eo deducamur omnes. Dominus autem ipse est, qui eduxit: deducamur a Domino necesse est. Nemo potest venire ad me, nisi Pater qui misit me traxerit eum: Iohan. 6.44. Qui autem educti sunt, fuerunt ij quidem discipuli. Non omnes autem vocati sunt ad id spectaculi, verum familiares aliquot, qui imprimis Domino chari erat. Pauci enim sunt quos deducit omnino Dominus, verum hoc tempore, non nisi paucos oculatos testes ascensionis suae visum est ipsi admittere. Malebat enim mundo & hominum vulgo innotescere sua ascensione per auditu quam per visum. Arridet enim Domino fides ea quae est ex auditu: & beari sunt, inquit, qui cum nō viderint, credunt tamen. Iohan. 20. 29. Obseruo hoc discriminis fuisse inter crucifixionē & resurrectionē atque ascensionē ipsius: Cum Dominus crucifigeretur, aderant promiscuè Iudæi, & Gentes omnes eo confluebant ex omni loco. At vero gloriosæ Resurrectionis non nisi paucos, & eos quidem discipulos suos ac familiares voluit testes esse. Ascensionis similiter non nisi paucos testes esse voluit, & eos quoque discipulos suos ac familiares. Maluit enim gloriam suam aliis innotescere per prædicationem Euangelij, quàm per præsentē intuitum. Ex hoc discrimine discendum, quòd ignominia Christi exponatur omnibus promiscuè inspicienda, gloria verò non nisi paucis aliquot, & iis qui seruantur.
units.tr: The story of the Lord's ascension follows, of which Matthew says nothing, and John nothing in his Gospel; Mark says something in his Gospel, and Luke something in his Gospel. In the Acts of the Apostles the same Luke has written the history more fully. First, then, to come to the matter, Luke says: He led them out as far as Bethany. They did not go there of their own accord, but were led out from Jerusalem to behold so great a glory and to share in so great a grace. For no one goes of his own accord to share in grace; rather we must all be led there. But it is the Lord himself who leads us out: we must necessarily be drawn by the Lord. No man can come to me, except the Father who sent me draw him (John 6:44). Those who were led out were indeed disciples, but not all were called to that sight; only some close friends, who were especially dear to the Lord. For few are those whom the Lord leads altogether, and at this time it pleased him to admit only a few eyewitnesses of his ascension. For he preferred that his ascension become known to the world and to the common people by hearing rather than by sight. For the faith that comes from hearing pleases the Lord: and blessed are they, he says, who have not seen and yet have believed (John 20:29). I observe that there was this difference between his crucifixion and his resurrection and ascension: when the Lord was crucified, Jews of every sort were present, and Gentiles flocked to it from every place. But he willed that there be only a few witnesses to his glorious resurrection, and these indeed his disciples and friends. Likewise he willed that there be only a few witnesses to his ascension, and these too his disciples and friends. For he preferred that his glory become known to others through the preaching of the Gospel rather than through present sight. From this difference we are to learn that the shame of Christ is set forth to be viewed indiscriminately by all, but his glory only to a few, and those who are kept for it.

units.la: Educit eos Bethaniam vsque. Ad montem scilicet Oliueti, qui erat propè Hierusalem, distans itinere Sabbathi. Hunc locum ex propositio delegit, vt eo ipso in loco triumphum suum adornaret, & ex eo solium illud suum cœlestē conscenderet: in quo loco prius cum morte luctatus est, captus est, & ex quo abductus est ad ignominiosam crucem. Oportet enim (vt in genere dicam) Dominum glorificari, in eodem loco, in quo ignominia prius affectus est.
units.tr: He led them out as far as Bethany. That is, to the Mount of Olives, which was near Jerusalem, about a Sabbath day's journey away. He chose this place on purpose, so that in this very place he might prepare his triumph, and from it ascend to that heavenly throne of his; in the place where he had previously struggled with death, was seized, and from which he was led away to the shameful cross. For it is fitting (to speak in general terms) that the Lord be glorified in the same place where he was previously subjected to shame.

units.la: Sequitur deinde communicatio, habita paulò ante ascensionem inter Dominum & discipulos suos, ea nimirum quæ habetur Act. 1. 6. Postea quam enim convenissent illi vna in montem qui dicebatur Oliueti, interrogant eum discipuli, Domine, an restitues hoc tempore regnum Israeli? Fortasse enim tum de regno illo cœlesti aliquid loquebatur Dominus, ex quo quidem sermone arrepta est occasio huius quæstionis: in qua profectò quæstione non uno modo peccatum est.
units.tr: Next follows the conversation held a little before the ascension between the Lord and his disciples, namely the one recorded in Acts 1:6. For after they had come together on the mount called Olivet, the disciples ask him: Lord, wilt thou at this time restore the kingdom to Israel? For perhaps the Lord was then speaking of that heavenly kingdom, and from his words this question took its occasion; and certainly in this question they sinned in more than one way.

units.la: Peccatum est in curiositate, vt apparet ex responsione Domini. 2. Etiam adhuc somniarunt discipuli de regno nescio quo terrestri. 3. Voluerunt regnare & triumphare antequam certassent.
